Parameters of braced_excavation
ParameterTypeDescription
excavation_depthfloatrequiredExcavation depth (m).
layersarrayrequiredArray of soil-layer dicts, top down: {thickness (m, required), unit_weight (kN/m3, required), friction_angle (deg, default 30), cohesion (kPa, default 0), soil_type ('sand' or 'clay', also 'soft_clay' or 'stiff_clay'; REQUIRED on each layer above the excavation base, refused if missing)}. soil_type picks the Terzaghi-Peck apparent-pressure envelope: the one for sands where sand is the thicker over the excavation depth, else the one for clays, soft to medium or stiff fissured by the average N = gamma*H/cu over the excavation depth (> 4 soft). The embedment below the excavation uses each layer's own phi and c. The last layer continues below its thickness.
supportsarrayoptionalSupport levels [{depth (m), support_type ('strut' or 'anchor'), spacing (m), angle_deg}].
surchargefloatoptionalSurface surcharge (kPa); added to the envelope as Ka*q (sand) or q (clay). default: 10.0
gwt_depthfloatoptionalGroundwater depth behind the wall (m); water pressure is added for sand envelopes.
gwt_depth_excavationfloatoptionalGroundwater depth on the excavation side (m from top of wall), never above the excavation base. Default: same as gwt_depth.
FOS_passivefloatoptionalEmbedment FS, MR = FS*MD about the lowest support (Caltrans uses 1.3). default: 1.5
embedment_increasefloatoptionalMultiplier on the free-earth-support embedment. default: 1.0
support_load_methodstroptionalHow the support loads and span moments are taken: 'hinge' (default) = the Caltrans Trenching and Shoring Manual's hinge method (Sec. 8-4.02, Fig. 8-7, p. 8-10; Example 8-2): the load above the first support to it, its moment M1 there carried by the span below (T1L = P/2 + M1/L, T2U = P/2 - M1/L), simple spans between supports, and the lowest support's load from below by free earth support about it (FS = 1; one support: the whole wall about it); 'hinge_subgrade' = GEC-4's hinge method (Fig. 38, p. 79): the same above, simple spans down to the excavation base, which takes a subgrade reaction R; 'simple_spans' = UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-54 (p. 257): simple spans between supports, the span below the lowest support a cantilever on it (UFC's 80 % moment reduction not applied). Choices give the other methods' loads. allowed: hinge, hinge_subgrade, simple_spans default: "hinge"
stiff_clay_coefficientfloatoptionalThe stiff clay envelope's ordinate as a multiple of gamma H, 0.2 to 0.4: 0.4 (default) per UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-53 (p. 256, internally supported walls, N0 <= 4); 0.2 'when movements are minimal and the construction period is short' (UFC); the Caltrans Trenching and Shoring Manual (Eq. 8-3-2, p. 8-5) leaves it between 0.2 and 0.4 to judgment. Read for stiff fissured clay (N <= 4) and, for 4 < N < 6, as the ordinate soft clay must reach (Caltrans Sec. 8-3.02: the larger of the two). default: 0.4
passive_theorystroptionalThe passive coefficient below the excavation: 'rankine' (default) = Rankine's Kp, no wall friction, as the Caltrans Trenching and Shoring Manual's examples take it where the wall friction is zero (pp. 7-18, 7-27), with its note that Rankine 'tends to underestimate the passive earth pressure' and Sec. 4-6 (p. 4-28): Rankine 'should not be used ... because it does not account for wall friction'; 'log_spiral' (or 'caquot_kerisel', the same) = the log-spiral Kp of log_spiral_source at passive_wall_friction_deg in each layer below the excavation. Choices give the other theory's Kp and embedment. allowed: rankine, log_spiral, caquot_kerisel also read as: logspiral = log_spiral, log-spiral = log_spiral default: "rankine"
log_spiral_sourcestroptionalWith passive_theory 'log_spiral', the printed source of Kp, as earth_pressure_coefficient takes it: 'ufc_3_220_20' (default) = UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 4-12 (p. 191), its log-spiral Kp for a vertical face and level ground at any wall friction; 'caquot_kerisel_1948' = the Caltrans Trenching and Shoring Manual Fig. 4-20 chart (its Example 8-1), and 'dm7_2_eq_4_12' = UFC Eq. 4-12 by name, both needing passive_wall_friction_deg given; 'dm7_2_fig_4_12' / 'dm7_2_fig_4_13' = UFC's charts, drawn for delta/phi' 0.66 only. allowed: ufc_3_220_20, caquot_kerisel_1948, dm7_2_eq_4_12, dm7_2_fig_4_12, dm7_2_fig_4_13 default: "ufc_3_220_20"
passive_wall_friction_degfloatoptionalWith passive_theory 'log_spiral', the wall friction delta (deg) in every layer below the excavation, at most its phi': the engineer's call (UFC 3-220-20 Table 4-1, p. 184; Caltrans Example 8-1 takes 15 deg on phi 30). Left out: delta/phi' = 0.66 (UFC p. 191, 'a common assumption') in a layer without cohesion, none in a layer with cohesion (UFC Fig. 4-37 step 1, p. 237: 'Passive pressures for clean coarse grained soils include wall friction'; in other soils it ignores wall friction); refused with 'caquot_kerisel_1948' or 'dm7_2_eq_4_12', which need it given (Caltrans p. 4-29: 'Given delta'). For soldier piles in coarse-grained soil UFC p. 249 takes KP 'without wall friction': give 0.
FyfloatoptionalSteel yield strength (MPa) for section sizing. default: 345.0
Fb_ratiofloatoptionalAllowable bending stress / Fy for the required section: 0.60 (default) as the Caltrans Trenching and Shoring Manual's examples take it (Example 7-3, p. 7-43; Example 8-1); GEC-4 (p. 81) recommends 0.55 for permanent walls and temporary walls that are critical; 0.66 the Caltrans railroad example (p. 9-20). Choices give the section at each. default: 0.6

Applicability limits & conventions
  • The apparent-pressure envelopes, anchor loads and moments reproduce the worked examples (V-016, Caltrans Ex 8-2); the embedment below the lowest support is free earth support about it (Caltrans T&S 8-4).
  • Where no moment balance exists within six times the excavation depth, the free-earth solution returns no embedment (and nothing computed from it) with a plain note, never a depth without a solution.

4.3.3 retaining_walls — Retaining walls (cantilever & MSE)

Problems it solves

Cantilever (semi-gravity) concrete retaining walls and mechanically-stabilized-earth (MSE) walls: external stability (sliding, overturning, bearing, eccentricity) and MSE internal stability (reinforcement tension and pullout), by ASD and LRFD.

Methods & theories implemented
  • Cantilever-wall stability: the active thrust on the vertical plane through the back of the heel, by Rankine or Coulomb with δ = β on that plane (FHWA NHI-06-089 p. 10-20, Ex 10-3), no tension in a cohesive backfill (UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-5 Note A); sliding by GEC-6 Eqs. 5-38 to 5-40 (FS 2.0 when passive is counted, UFC Sec. 4-5.1.3); e within B/6 on soil and B/4 on rock; bearing as the uniform qeq = V/(B − 2e) against a given allowable pressure for B′ (GEC-6 Eq. 6-6, Sec. 6.4.2), or the trapezoid’s qmax on rock; an optional water table behind the wall with uplift on the base (UFC Sec. 4-4.1; EM 1110-2-2104 para. E-12).
  • MSE walls by GEC-11’s Simplified Method: external stability (sliding, also on the lowest geosynthetic sheet; eccentricity; bearing on L − 2e) and internal Kr/Ka (Fig. 4-10) and F* pullout for steel strips, bar mats and welded grids and for geogrids and geotextiles (F* = 2/3 tan φ, Eq. 3-8); the bilinear surface for inextensible and the linear one for extensible reinforcement (Fig. 4-9); level, sloping or broken backslopes and a face battered 10° or more (Vol I p. 4-15, Eq. 4-26).
  • AASHTO/GEC-11 LRFD external stability — Strength I max/min + Service I load-factor combinations, live-load exclusions, and per-mode capacity/demand ratios.
  • References: FHWA GEC-11 (FHWA-NHI-10-024 Vol I, NHI-10-025 Vol II); AASHTO LRFD; FHWA GEC-6; FHWA NHI-06-089; UFC 3-220-20; validated against GEC-11 Ex E4/E7 (V-009/V-010/V-011) and, for the cantilever, UFC 3-220-20 App. B-1 and NHI-06-089 Ex 10-3 (V-061).

Parameters of cantilever_wall
ParameterTypeDescription
wall_heightfloatrequiredTOTAL wall height H (m), measured from the UNDERSIDE of the base slab (footing) to the top of the stem: H = base_thickness + stem height. The active thrust acts over H on the vertical plane through the back of the heel. If you know the height retained above the top of the footing, add base_thickness (4.0 m retained on a 0.5 m footing is wall_height 4.5).
gamma_backfillfloatrequiredBackfill unit weight (kN/m3).
phi_backfillfloatrequiredBackfill friction angle (degrees).
base_widthfloatoptionalBase width (m). Auto-sized if omitted.
toe_lengthfloatoptionalToe length (m). Auto-sized if omitted.
stem_thickness_topfloatoptionalStem thickness at top (m). default: 0.3
stem_thickness_basefloatoptionalStem thickness at base (m).
base_thicknessfloatoptionalBase slab thickness (m). Auto-sized if omitted: H/10 (FHWA NHI-06-089 Fig. 10-16(a), p. 10-38: H/12 to H/10).
stem_batterstroptionalWhich face of a tapered stem (thicker at its base than at its top) is battered. 'back' (default): the front face vertical, the backfill over the battered back counted as resisting weight. 'front': the back face vertical, as UFC 3-220-20 App. B-1 Fig. B-2 (p. 598) and FHWA NHI-06-089 Fig. 10-16(a) and Example 10-3 (p. 10-52) draw it. allowed: back, front default: "back"
embedment_depthfloatoptionalDepth of the underside of the base below the ground in front of the wall, Df (m), 0 to wall_height. Left out: the base thickness, the ground in front at the top of the base. Deeper, the soil over the toe counts as resisting weight (UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-27, p. 220: 'Weight includes ... weight of soil above footing'; App. B-1.3, p. 599), at gamma_foundation, and include_passive's passive resistance acts over Df.
has_shear_keybooloptionalInclude a shear key below the base (with key_depth). It acts only with include_passive: the sliding check then takes the passive resistance over the depth of the key only, from the underside of the base (depth embedment_depth below the ground in front) to the bottom of the key (embedment_depth + key_depth), the trapezoid UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-29 draws below the toe (p. 224: 'the passive pressure is applied only along the depth of the key and not along the entire burial depth of the wall'; GEC-6 Fig. 5-22 likewise), in place of the passive over the embedment; with the undrained rule it counts cu, as GEC-6 Eq. 5-41 (p. 101) counts Pp in front of the key. GEC-6 Sec. 5.4 (pp. 100-101): keys in granular soils 'are not very efficient in developing passive pressures'; its key method is for stiff, overconsolidated clays and soft rock. UFC: 'it is also prudent to consider some amount of future excavation in front of the wall'. default: false
key_depthfloatoptionalShear key depth below the underside of the base slab (m). default: 0.0
surchargefloatoptionalUniform LIVE-load surcharge on the backfill (kPa), e.g. traffic. Its thrust K*q*H drives every check. Over the heel it is NOT a resisting force in sliding, overturning or the eccentricity check by default (live_load_resists), and it does load the base in the bearing pressures (surcharge_in_bearing). A pavement or slab is not a surcharge here: model it as retained soil up to the ground surface (it then rests on the heel and resists like the backfill). Any other surcharge is transient live load: its thrust counts in every check, but its weight over the heel does not resist sliding or overturning. A permanent load you want carried as a surcharge goes in dead_load_surcharge. default: 0.0
dead_load_surchargefloatoptionalUniform DEAD-load (permanent) surcharge on the backfill (kPa), a permanent load that is not part of the retained soil (FHWA NHI-06-089 Sec. 10.4.2). Pavements and slabs are normally modelled as retained soil up to the ground surface instead. Its thrust drives every check, added to the live load's. Over the heel it is not a resisting force by default (dead_load_resists=true counts it as resisting weight in sliding and overturning); it loads the base in the bearing pressures (surcharge_in_bearing). default: 0.0
live_load_resistsbooloptionalCount the live-load surcharge over the heel (and its share of a sloped or Coulomb thrust's vertical component) as a resisting force in sliding, overturning and the eccentricity check. Default false: FHWA NHI-06-089 Sec. 10.5.5 (p. 10-43), 'the live load surcharge is not considered as a stabilizing force over the heel of the wall when sliding resistance is being checked'; UFC 3-220-20 App. B-1.2 (p. 597), 'For overturning and sliding checks, it is assumed that the traffic pressure does not act over the wall heel'. true = the free body with the load over the heel, which none of these references uses for a live load. The result's choices say which was used. default: false
dead_load_resistsbooloptionalCount the dead-load surcharge over the heel as a resisting force in sliding, overturning and the eccentricity check. Default false: FHWA NHI-06-089 Sec. 10.5.3 (p. 10-41), for CIP semi-gravity walls the surcharge loads are 'conservatively neglected within the width of the base slab since they contribute to overturning and sliding resistance'. true = counted as a permanent load: GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-22 (AASHTO), loads that increase sliding resistance are included 'only if those loads are permanent'. default: false
surcharge_in_bearingbooloptionalCount the surcharges over the heel in the bearing pressures (q_toe, q_heel, FOS_bearing). Default true: UFC 3-220-20 App. B-1.6 (p. 602), 'it is conservative to include the surcharge over the heel of the wall, if this is possible to occur, in the bearing capacity check'; GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-26. false = the surcharge taken as located behind the heel (NHI-06-089 p. 10-41). default: true
backfill_slopefloatoptionalBackfill slope angle (degrees), rising away from the wall. A backfill descending away from the wall (below 0) is refused. default: 0.0
c_backfillfloatoptionalBackfill cohesion (kPa). The active pressure Ka sigma_v - 2 c sqrt(Ka) is taken as zero where it is negative, the tension zone (UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-5 Note A; FHWA NHI-06-089 p. 10-15); the result's choices give the thrust with c neglected and with NHI's minimum active pressure of 5z kN/m2 beside it. default: 0.0
phi_foundationfloatoptionalFoundation soil friction angle (deg), FULL value — the sliding check applies delta_b = (2/3)*phi_foundation INTERNALLY. Do NOT pre-reduce (passing 2/3*phi here double-counts the reduction). To set the base friction angle directly, use delta_base instead. Defaults to phi_backfill. phi_foundation = 0 gives an undrained strength (c_foundation = cu): sliding_cohesion then defaults to 'undrained'.
c_foundationfloatoptionalFoundation soil cohesion (kPa), FULL value, no 2/3 factor. The sliding check counts it by sliding_cohesion: NOT at all with 'drained' (the default unless phi_foundation is 0), as the undrained shear strength cu with 'undrained' (ca = cu) or 'friction_plus_adhesion' (Ca from UFC 3-220-20 Table 4-1). To set the adhesion directly, use base_adhesion. default: 0.0
sliding_cohesionstroptionalHow the sliding check counts the foundation soil's cohesion, by the rule a reference prints. Default depends on phi_foundation: 'undrained' when phi_foundation is 0 (c_foundation is then cu), else 'drained'. 'drained': R = V tan delta_b, c_foundation NOT counted (GEC-6 Sec. 5.4 Eq. 5-38, p. 100: 'Equations 5-38 and 5-39 should not be combined for use at the same time'; EN 1997-1 6.5.3(10): 'Any effective cohesion c' should be neglected'). 'undrained': R = ca B alone, no friction, ca = c_foundation taken as the undrained shear strength cu, or base_adhesion (GEC-6 Eq. 5-39: 'ca is typically taken as equal to the undrained shear strength'). 'friction_plus_adhesion': R = V tan delta_b + Ca Be, Ca from UFC 3-220-20 Table 4-1 (p. 184) at c_foundation taken as the undrained shear strength (up to 191.5 kPa), or base_adhesion; Be = B - 2e, the effective base width (UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-27 and Sec. 4-5.1.3, p. 223, which adds that the minimum FS 'may also need to be increased when base adhesion is included'). The result's choices give the rule used, its basis and each other rule's FOS_sliding on the same wall. allowed: drained, undrained, friction_plus_adhesion
delta_basefloatoptionalBase interface friction angle delta_b (deg), used DIRECTLY in the sliding check with NO 2/3 factor. Overrides the (2/3)*phi_foundation default. delta_b = phi_foundation for concrete cast against the ground (GEC-6 Sec. 5.4, p. 99: tan delta 'will be equal to the tangent of the friction angle (tan phi) for the soil supporting the footing'). The result's choices state the delta_b used, its basis and the other reading. Refused with sliding_cohesion 'undrained', which counts no friction.
base_adhesionfloatoptionalBase adhesion ca (kPa), used DIRECTLY with sliding_cohesion 'undrained' (in place of cu) or 'friction_plus_adhesion' (in place of the UFC 3-220-20 Table 4-1 value). Refused with 'drained', which counts no adhesion: give sliding_cohesion with it.
include_passivebooloptionalInclude passive resistance in front of the wall in the sliding check (Rankine's Kp unless passive_theory says otherwise; UFC 3-220-20 p. 219: 'typically ignored', and with it considered FSL >= 2.0, Fig. 4-27, so FOS_sliding_required then defaults to 2.0), acting over the embedment, from the ground in front to the underside of the base (embedment_depth, default the base thickness), or with has_shear_key over the depth of the key only (from embedment_depth to embedment_depth + key_depth below the ground in front, UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-29). With the undrained rule it counts the foundation's cu, Kp sigma_v + 2 cu sqrt(Kp) (UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 4-7, p. 178, and p. 181); with the other rules c_foundation is not counted in it (p. 179). default: false
gamma_foundationfloatoptionalFoundation soil unit weight (kN/m3): the passive resistance in front of the wall and the soil over the toe (embedment_depth below the top of the base). Defaults to gamma_backfill.
passive_theorystroptionalWith include_passive, the passive coefficient in front of the wall: 'rankine' (default) = Rankine's Kp, no wall friction; 'log_spiral' (or 'caquot_kerisel', the same) = the log-spiral Kp of log_spiral_source at passive_wall_friction_deg. UFC 3-220-20 (Sec. 4-5.1, Figs. 4-27 and 4-29, pp. 219-224) names no theory for it; choices give the other theory's Kp and FOS_sliding and the FOS with no passive. allowed: rankine, log_spiral, caquot_kerisel also read as: logspiral = log_spiral, log-spiral = log_spiral default: "rankine"
log_spiral_sourcestroptionalWith passive_theory 'log_spiral', the printed source of Kp, as earth_pressure_coefficient takes it: 'ufc_3_220_20' (default) = UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 4-12 (p. 191), its log-spiral Kp for a vertical face and level ground at any wall friction; 'caquot_kerisel_1948' = the Caltrans Trenching and Shoring Manual Fig. 4-20 chart, and 'dm7_2_eq_4_12' = UFC Eq. 4-12 by name, both needing passive_wall_friction_deg given; 'dm7_2_fig_4_12' / 'dm7_2_fig_4_13' = UFC's charts, drawn for delta/phi' 0.66 only. allowed: ufc_3_220_20, caquot_kerisel_1948, dm7_2_eq_4_12, dm7_2_fig_4_12, dm7_2_fig_4_13 default: "ufc_3_220_20"
passive_wall_friction_degfloatoptionalWith passive_theory 'log_spiral', the wall friction delta in front of the wall (deg), 0 to phi_foundation: the engineer's call (UFC 3-220-20 Table 4-1, p. 184). Left out: delta/phi' = 0.66 (UFC p. 191, 'a common assumption'); refused with 'caquot_kerisel_1948' or 'dm7_2_eq_4_12', which need it given (Caltrans p. 4-29: 'Given delta').
q_allowablefloatoptionalAllowable bearing pressure (kPa) for the bearing check. On soil (bearing_pressure 'uniform', the default) it is compared with q_eq = V/(B - 2e), the uniform pressure over the effective width B' = B - 2e, so give the allowable bearing pressure for B' (GEC-6 Sec. 6.4.2, p. 119: 'Bf in Equation 5-14 may be replaced by B'f'); with 'linear' (the default with founded_on_rock), with the larger edge pressure. Without it the bearing check is NOT RUN: FOS_bearing and passes_bearing are null and checks_not_run lists 'bearing' (q_toe / q_heel are still reported).
gamma_concretefloatoptionalConcrete unit weight (kN/m3). Default 23.6, 150 pcf, as UFC 3-220-20 App. B-1.3 (p. 599) and FHWA NHI-06-089 Example 10-3 (p. 10-53) take it. default: 23.6
FOS_sliding_requiredfloatoptionalRequired sliding FOS; the check passes at or above it. Default depends on include_passive: 1.5 (GEC-6 Eq. 5-40, p. 100; UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-27; FHWA NHI-06-089 Fig. 10-17), 2.0 with the passive resistance counted (UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-27, p. 220, and Sec. 4-5.1.3, p. 223: 'If passive resistance is included, the minimum FSL should be increased to 2.0'). The result's choices say which was taken.
FOS_overturning_requiredfloatoptionalRequired overturning FOS; the check passes at or above it. Default depends on founded_on_rock: 2.0 on soil, 1.5 on rock (FHWA NHI-06-089 Sec. 10.5.5, p. 10-44: 'approximately of 2.0 for soils and 1.5 for rocks'; GEC-6 Sec. 7.3, p. 124: 'greater than about 2.0 for permanent dead loads'). UFC 3-220-20 Sec. 4-5.1.2 (p. 223) asks FOT >= 1.5 for any wall.
pressure_methodstroptionalEarth pressure theory. The active thrust acts on the vertical plane through the back of the heel. 'rankine' (default): the thrust parallel to the backfill slope. 'coulomb': Coulomb's Ka (UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 4-10) at the wall friction on that plane, wall_friction_deg, by default the backfill slope (FHWA NHI-06-089 p. 10-20 and Example 10-3; delta = 0 behind level backfill). At that default Coulomb's Ka on a vertical plane is Rankine's (sloped) Ka, the same thrust (NHI Example 10-3's 0.35 at phi 30, beta 10 is both), so 'coulomb' changes the result only with wall_friction_deg given. allowed: rankine, coulomb default: "rankine"
wall_friction_degfloatoptionalWall friction delta on the vertical plane through the back of the heel (deg), with pressure_method 'coulomb', 0 to phi_backfill. Left out: the backfill slope (FHWA NHI-06-089 p. 10-20: on that plane 'there is soil-to-soil contact ... it is generally conservative to assume that the earth pressure is parallel to the slope of the backfill'). Refused with 'rankine'. The result's choices give the delta used and the other reading's Ka.
interface_gap_possiblebooloptionalWhether water or air can reach the base-clay interface. With sliding_cohesion 'undrained' (an undrained clay under the base) the base resistance is then held to 0.4 V (EN 1997-1 Sec. 6.5.3(12)P, Eq. 6.5, p. 65). GEC-6 and UFC 3-220-20 print no such limit. Refused with the other rules. The result's choices give FOS_sliding under the other reading. default: false
founded_on_rockbooloptionalWhether the wall is founded on rock. On rock the eccentricity limit is B/4, the middle half, in place of B/6 (GEC-6 Sec. 6.4.1, p. 119; UFC 3-220-20 Sec. 4-5.1.2, p. 223; FHWA NHI-06-089 Fig. 10-17), FOS_overturning_required defaults to 1.5 and bearing_pressure to 'linear'. default: false
water_table_depthfloatoptionalDepth of a level water table behind the wall below the top of the backfill at the stem (m), 0 or more (0 = water at the top of the backfill). Left out: no water table, the backfill drained (FHWA NHI-06-089 Sec. 10.5.3, p. 10-41: 'If adequate drainage measures are provided, the hydrostatic pressure due to groundwater behind the wall generally need not be considered. However, hydrostatic pressure must be considered for portions of the wall below the level of the weep holes unless a deeper drainage system is provided behind the base of the wall'). Given: below it the earth pressure is on the buoyant unit weight gamma_sat - gamma_w and the water pressure gamma_w z is added, horizontal (UFC 3-220-20 Sec. 4-4.1 and Fig. 4-16(a), pp. 199-202; FHWA NHI-06-089 Fig. 10-12, p. 10-27: 'should consider the greatest unbalanced water head anticipated'); the water pressure under the base (base_uplift) comes off V in sliding and adds to the overturning moment. In front of the wall no water is taken above the underside of the base. At or below the underside of the base (wall_height or deeper) it changes nothing. The result's choices give the drained backfill's FOS beside it.
gamma_sat_backfillfloatoptionalWith water_table_depth, the backfill's saturated unit weight below the water table (kN/m3), more than gamma_w (9.81). Left out: gamma_backfill, as UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-16(a) (p. 202) takes gamma 125 pcf above the water table and gamma_b 62.5 pcf below it; against a larger gamma_sat that errs on the safe side for sliding and overturning where the heel carries soil below the water table, on the unsafe side for the bearing pressures and a wall with little or no heel. Refused without water_table_depth.
base_upliftstroptionalWith water_table_depth, the water pressure under the base (uplift), h_w being the water's height above the underside of the base: 'linear' (default) = gamma_w h_w at the heel to 0 at the toe, no water in front of the wall, a straight line between the heads at the heel and the toe as EM 1110-2-2104 para. E-12 (p. 115) prints a wall's uplift; 'uniform' = gamma_w h_w under the whole base, the same head at both (EM 1110-2-2104 para. E-12, p. 116; UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 5-40, p. 346, a structure below the water table). The uplift comes off V in sliding and its moment about the toe adds to the overturning moment (the choices give the FOS with it taken off the stabilizing moment instead, and the other distribution's). Refused without water_table_depth. allowed: linear, uniform default: "linear"
uplift_in_bearingbooloptionalWith water_table_depth, count the uplift in the bearing pressures (q_toe, q_heel, q_eq, FOS_bearing). Default false: UFC 3-220-20 Sec. 5-3.2 (p. 292), 'Uplift is present on the base of the foundation when the groundwater table is above the bearing elevation. Its effect on the bearing pressure can be conservatively ignored unless sliding or uplift is a concern', on the safe side while the resultant is in the middle third (e <= B/6). true = the effective pressure under the base, the weights less the uplift (EN 1997-1 Sec. 6.5.2.1(3)P, p. 63: 'Water pressures not caused by the foundation load shall be included as actions'). Give q_allowable for the water table at that level (GEC-6 Sec. 5.2.3.2, p. 56). Refused without water_table_depth. default: false
bearing_pressurestroptionalThe bearing pressure compared with q_allowable. Default depends on founded_on_rock: 'uniform' on soil, 'linear' on rock. 'uniform' (the default on soil): q_eq = V / B', B' = B - 2e (GEC-6 Eq. 6-6 and Sec. 6.4.2, p. 119; FHWA NHI-06-089 Fig. 10-17: 'Use uniform stress, qeq, for soils'; UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 4-27 and Sec. 4-5.1.4, p. 224, for soil that is 'relatively ductile'). 'linear' (the default with founded_on_rock): the larger edge pressure of the trapezoid or triangle, q_toe or q_heel (UFC Sec. 4-5.1.4: 'For more brittle materials, such as rock and sensitive clays'; FHWA NHI-06-089 Fig. 10-17). The result's choices give the other pressure's FOS_bearing. allowed: uniform, linear
Worked example

Ask → A 6 m cantilever retaining wall on φ=32° backfill with a 12 kPa surcharge — check sliding, overturning, and bearing.

call_agent(
    agent_name='retaining_walls',
    method='cantilever_wall',
    parameters={
        "wall_height": 6.0,
        "gamma_backfill": 18.0,
        "phi_backfill": 32.0,
        "surcharge": 12.0,
        "q_allowable": 250.0
    },
)
Representative output (real, from the shipped code)
verdict: FAILS: sliding (FOS 1.14 < 1.50 required). Passes: overturning (FOS 2.69 >= 2.00 required); bearing (q_eq 142.8 kPa <= q_allowable 250.0 kPa, FOS 1.75); eccentricity (resultant within the middle third: e = 0.537 m <= B/6 = 0.600 m).
checks_failed: [1 entries]
checks_not_run: [0 entries]
all_checks_pass: False
FOS_sliding: 1.143
FOS_overturning: 2.695
FOS_bearing: 1.751
FOS_sliding_required: 1.5
FOS_overturning_required: 2.0
passes_sliding: False
passes_overturning: True
passes_bearing: True
bearing_checked: True
q_allowable_kPa: 250.0
… (additional fields in the full result dict)

Here the auto-sized base fails sliding (FOS 1.14 < 1.5) — exactly the kind of check-and-revise loop the toolkit is built for.

Applicability limits & conventions
  • MSE external stability is an ASD factor-of-safety check (mse_wall) or an LRFD capacity/demand check (mse_lrfd_external_stability; in the library analyze_mse_wall(lrfd_external=True) runs both). The LRFD check and a broken backslope take a vertical face only. The MSE checks have no water table (the cantilever wall has one).

4.3.4 ground_improvement — Ground improvement

Problems it solves

Improving weak ground before it is loaded: aggregate piers and stone columns, prefabricated vertical (wick) drains, surcharge preloading, and vibro-compaction — the settlement reduction, capacity increase, and time to consolidate.

Methods & theories implemented
  • Aggregate piers / stone columns: area-replacement ratio, equal-strain settlement-reduction factor, composite modulus, and the settlement ratio off GEC-13 Fig. 5-21 (weighted modulus, Balaam, and the Priebe curve as GEC-13 prints it, φ = 37.5°; no Priebe formula).
  • Radial consolidation for PVDs by GEC-13 Eq. 2-1 with F(n) = ln(n) − 0.75 (Eq. 2-2), a 2.5 in drain and smear ignored by default (GEC-13 p. 2-35; smear optional by UFC 3-220-10 Eq. 5-25; well resistance not modelled, GEC-13 p. 2-36), combined with vertical drainage by Carrillo (UFC 3-220-10 Eq. 5-27); drain-spacing design.
  • Surcharge preloading; vibro-compaction feasibility by GEC-13's fines limits (p. 4-65) and SPT N (Table 4-8), with the probe spacing for a target relative density off GEC-13 Fig. 4-34.
  • References: FHWA GEC-13 (ground-modification manual); UFC 3-220-10 (2026); validated V-018/V-019/V-020.
Agent-callable methods (from the shipped registry)
Aggregate Piers
MethodWhat it doesParams
aggregate_piersAggregate pier (stone column) design: settlement reduction, capacity increase.10
priebe_improvement_factorStone columns: the settlement ratio off the Priebe curve GEC-13 prints, Fig. 5-21 curve (4), phi = 37.5 deg (p. 5-36), which GEC-13 calls the upper bound, for preliminary estimates (p. 5-37).1
General
MethodWhat it doesParams
feasibilityGround improvement method feasibility screening.13
Surcharge
MethodWhat it doesParams

Vibro Compaction
MethodWhat it doesParams
vibro_compactionVibro compaction (vibroflotation) feasibility by GEC-13 Ch. 4 (fines content, SPT N by Table 4-8), and the probe spacing for a target relative density off GEC-13 Fig. 4-34.4
Wick Drains
MethodWhat it doesParams
wick_drainsPrefabricated vertical drain (PVD) consolidation: radial by GEC-13 Eq. 2-1 with F(n) = ln(n) - 0.75 (Eq. 2-2), well resistance not modelled (GEC-13 p. 2-36: 'rarely significant'), combined with vertical drainage by Carrillo (UFC 3-220-10 Eq. 5-27).10
design_drain_spacingFind required drain spacing for a target combined (vertical and radial) consolidation in a target time, by GEC-13 Eq. 2-1 and Carrillo (UFC 3-220-10 Eq. 5-27). GEC-13 p. 2-33 gives typical spacings of 3 to 5 ft in homogeneous clays, 4 to 6 ft in silty clays, 5 to 6.5 ft in coarser soils for about 90 percent consolidation in 3 to 4 months.10
Parameters of aggregate_piers
ParameterTypeDescription
column_diameterfloatrequiredPier column diameter (m).
spacingfloatrequiredCenter-to-center spacing (m). Alternatively give area_replacement_ratio (As/A, 0.1-0.35 typical) and spacing is back-calculated.
area_replacement_ratiofloatoptionalArea replacement ratio As/A (0.1-0.35 typical). Used to compute spacing when spacing is not given.
patternstroptionalInstallation pattern. allowed: triangular, square default: "triangular"
E_soilfloatoptionalSurrounding soil modulus (kPa). With settlement_method 'stress_ratio', used only for the composite modulus E_comp = E_soil*[1 + as*(n-1)]; the GEC-13 Fig. 5-21 methods need it given, for E_c/E_s. default: 5000.0
nfloatoptionalStress concentration ratio sigma_c/sigma_s; sets the improved bearing and, with settlement_method 'stress_ratio', the settlement reduction factor. GEC-13 for stone columns: measured 'between 2.0 and 5.0' (p. 5-31), and 'For preliminary design, a ratio of 2.5 is often conservatively used for stability and bearing resistance calculations' (p. 5-32); for rammed aggregate piers 5 to 10 under flexible embankment loading and 10 under rigid footings (p. 5-43); 'stress concentration ratios range from 4 to 45 for rigid footings' (p. 5-45). default: 5.0
settlement_methodstroptionalHow the settlement over the columns is worked out. 'stress_ratio' (default): SRF = 1/[1 + as*(n-1)] from n. The others give the settlement ratio (settlement without columns / with them; GEC-13 p. 5-36 prints it as 'n', which is not the stress ratio n) by E_c/E_s off GEC-13 Fig. 5-21, and need E_column and E_soil: 'weighted_modulus' (curve 2, settlement ratio = 1 + as*(E_c/E_s - 1), any E_c/E_s); 'balaam_rigid' (curves 5b, 5c: E_c/E_s 5 to 10, A/A_c 1.75 to 9); 'balaam_flexible' (curve 5a: E_c/E_s = 10, A/A_c 1.5 to 8.5). GEC-13 p. 5-37: the FHWA (1983) Equilibrium Method, 'roughly equivalent to the Balaam relationships', 'represents an average or lower bound estimate suitable for preliminary analyses'; the Priebe curve (priebe_improvement_factor) 'the upper bound effectiveness'. allowed: stress_ratio, weighted_modulus, balaam_rigid, balaam_flexible default: "stress_ratio"
E_columnfloatoptionalAggregate column modulus E_c (kPa), with E_soil, for the settlement_method 'weighted_modulus', 'balaam_rigid' or 'balaam_flexible' (E_c/E_s, GEC-13 Fig. 5-21). Refused with 'stress_ratio', which takes n instead. Alias: column_modulus.
q_unreinforcedfloatoptionalUnreinforced bearing capacity (kPa). 0 = not computed. default: 0.0
S_unreinforcedfloatoptionalUnreinforced settlement (mm). 0 = not computed. default: 0.0
Worked example

Ask → 0.76 m aggregate piers on a 1.5 m triangular grid under soft ground — what settlement reduction and bearing improvement do they buy?

call_agent(
    agent_name='ground_improvement',
    method='aggregate_piers',
    parameters={
        "column_diameter": 0.76,
        "spacing": 1.5,
        "pattern": "triangular",
        "E_soil": 8000.0,
        "S_unreinforced": 100.0,
        "q_unreinforced": 150.0
    },
)

Applicability limits & conventions
  • Aggregate-pier settlement uses the equal-strain settlement-reduction model, not the GEC-13 stiffness-modulus (kg) two-layer method (V-018); the Priebe curve is GEC-13's, drawn for φ = 37.5° only and read at A/Ac 1.6 to 8, and depends on the area-ratio convention supplied (V-019).

4.4 Slope stability & continuum FEM

Will the slope stand? Limit-equilibrium factors of safety and a full 2D finite-element stress/deformation and strength-reduction engine.

4.4.1 slope_stability — Slope stability

Problems it solves

Will the slope stand? The factor of safety of an earth or rock slope against sliding — for a specified surface or the critical one found by search — under drained or undrained conditions, groundwater, surcharge, seismicity, reinforcement, and rapid drawdown, and its probabilistic FOS.

Methods & theories implemented
  • Methods of slices: Ordinary/Fellenius, Bishop simplified (1955), Janbu (corrected), Spencer (1967), Morgenstern–Price, and the rigorous GLE (Fredlund–Krahn) with interslice-force functions.
  • Critical-surface search: circular centre-grid with the best centres refined, entry–exit arcs, random noncircular polylines with differential-evolution / PSO refinement, and weak-layer search; then small circles through each face’s toe and, wherever c′ = 0 soil forms a face, shallow planar surfaces parallel to it. Every trial surface carries the reinforcement it crosses; the result names the governing surface, each family’s minimum and the reinforcement crossing it, and warns when the governing circle ends at a profile end (the profile is then carried on level and the lower FOS reported).
  • Advanced per-layer strength models (the layer strength_model selector): Mohr–Coulomb (default), SHANSEP undrained-strength-ratio (su = S·OCRm·σ′v, with a su,min floor), Generalized Hoek–Brown for rock (σci, GSI, mi, D), and anisotropic undrained strength (su active / DSS / passive by the slice base’s inclination, Casagrande–Carrillo).
  • Reinforcement crossing the slip surface: soil nails (pullout + bar-tension capacity, FHWA GEC-7), tieback anchors (allowable tension when the bond zone crosses the surface), horizontal geosynthetic layers, and Ito & Matsui (1975) stabilizing piles, applied in every method as Wright & Duncan (1991) apply them: active (the default; the support reduces the driving force) or passive (the support is added to the resisting force and so divided by F); plus ponded water, tension cracks, and pseudo-static kh.
  • Seismic displacement (the yield coefficient ky, Newmark sliding block on a record, the Jibson 2007 and Bray & Travasarou 2007 regressions), rapid drawdown (USACE 2-stage, Lowe–Karafiath 2-stage, Duncan–Wright–Wong 3-stage; on one surface or by search), infinite-slope FOS, and probabilistic FOS (FOSM and Monte Carlo).
  • References: Fredlund & Krahn (1977); Bishop (1955); Spencer (1967); Janbu; Duncan, Wright & Brandon (2014); Ito & Matsui (1975); Jibson (2007); validated vs Fredlund–Krahn / ACADS / Duncan / Slide2 (VALIDATION.md, V-015/V-026…V-040).
Agent-callable methods (from the shipped registry)
Slope Stability
MethodWhat it doesParams
analyze_slopeAnalyze ONE specified slip surface (Fellenius/Bishop/Janbu+f0/Spencer/Morgenstern-Price/GLE). Requires a trial circle (xc/yc/radius) or slip_points. If you do NOT already have a specific trial surface, use search_critical_surface instead — it auto-finds the critical surface and avoids 'circle does not intersect the ground surface' errors. Supports reinforcement (nails/anchors/geosynthetics), ponded water (auto), SHANSEP and Hoek-Brown layer strengths, pseudo-static kh, tension cracks.29
compare_methods_tableRun ALL limit-equilibrium methods (OMS, Bishop, Janbu uncorr/corr, Spencer, Morgenstern-Price) on ONE slip surface and return a side-by-side FOS table (Fredlund & Krahn 1977 style method comparison).26
infinite_slope_fosInfinite-slope (planar translational) factor of safety in closed form (Duncan-Wright): FOS = [c' + (gamma*z*cos^2(beta) - u)*tan(phi')] / (gamma*z*sin(beta)cos(beta)). For the shallow surface-parallel failure mechanism; the depth cancels for cohesionless soil (FOS = tan(phi')/tan(beta) dry, or gamma'/gamma that for seepage at the surface). Use analyze_slope/search_critical_surface for circular/noncircular mechanisms.9
rapid_drawdown_fosRapid-drawdown FOS on a SPECIFIED slip surface: USACE/Army-Corps 2-stage, Lowe-Karafiath 2-stage, or Duncan-Wright-Wong 3-stage. Low-permeability layers respond undrained after fast reservoir drawdown; give them the total-stress R-envelope (soil_layers[].R_c, R_phi) alongside c_prime/phi (R_phi=null => free-draining). Stage 1 = full-pool effective stresses; stage 2 = undrained strength from the R and effective envelopes (Kc-interpolated for Lowe-Karafiath and 3-stage); stage 3 (3-stage only) substitutes the drained strength where lower; final FOS is solved at the drawn-down pool.31
search_rapid_drawdownSEARCH for the critical (minimum-FOS) slip surface under RAPID-DRAWDOWN strengths (Corps 2-stage / Lowe-Karafiath 2-stage / Duncan-Wright-Wong 3-stage). Like search_critical_surface but the per-trial FOS is the rapid-drawdown solve; supports circular and noncircular searches. Use this (not rapid_drawdown_fos) when you do NOT already have a specific trial surface. Low-permeability layers need the R-envelope (soil_layers[].R_c, R_phi).38
yield_accelerationYield (critical) seismic coefficient ky for a SPECIFIED slip surface: the horizontal pseudo-static coefficient kh at which the factor of safety = 1.0 (Newmark critical acceleration, ay = ky*g). Found by bisection on the module's pseudo-static FOS. Feed ky into newmark_displacement or newmark_jibson2007. Provide the surface as xc/yc/radius or slip_points.26
newmark_displacementNewmark rigid-block permanent DOWNSLOPE displacement by double integration of an earthquake acceleration time history against the yield coefficient ky (no upslope rebound). polarity='downslope' (default) is the standard Newmark/Jibson single-block convention (only the destabilizing polarity drives the block); 'rectified' uses the absolute record so both polarities drive it (conservative, ~2x for a symmetric record). Get ky from yield_acceleration. For a quick estimate without a record, use newmark_jibson2007.5
newmark_jibson2007Jibson (2007) regression estimate of Newmark displacement from the critical-acceleration ratio ky/amax (Eq. 6): log10 D[cm] = 0.215 + log10[(1-ky/amax)^2.341 (ky/amax)^-1.438], sigma=0.51 log10. Needs no time history; requires 0 < ky < amax.2
bray_travasarou_2007Bray & Travasarou (2007) simplified seismic DEVIATORIC slope displacement — a fully-coupled stick-slip sliding-block regression that captures sliding-mass flexibility (via the fundamental period Ts) and spectral demand at 1.5*Ts, which the rigid-block Jibson/integration models don't. Returns P(D=0) (prob. of negligible <=1 cm displacement) and the median non-zero displacement (16/84% via sigma_ln=0.66). A period-dependent cross-check for Jibson.5
search_critical_surfaceSearch for the critical slip surface (minimum FOS): circular centre-grid, entry-exit arcs, random noncircular polylines, differential-evolution noncircular refinement, PSO, or weak-layer-biased search.35
fosm_fosFOSM / Taylor-series reliability of the FOS on a fixed slip surface (Duncan 2000): central finite differences at +/- 1 sigma per variable -> COV_F, beta (normal + lognormal), probability of failure, per-variable variance contributions. Supports both independent per-layer scalar variables AND a correlated depth-varying su-gradient law (see 'variables').28
monte_carlo_fosMonte Carlo FOS distribution on a fixed slip surface (optionally re-searching the critical surface per realization): samples layer parameters (normal/lognormal), returns pf, FOS statistics and histogram.32
Parameters of search_critical_surface
ParameterTypeDescription
surface_pointsarrayrequiredGround surface as [[x,y], ...] array (x increasing).
soil_layersarrayrequiredArray of soil-layer dicts: {top_elevation, bottom_elevation, gamma (all required); name, gamma_sat, phi, c_prime, cu, analysis_mode ('drained'|'undrained'), ru optional; bottom_boundary_points and top_boundary_points ([[x,z],...], sorted by x) optional, a sloping bottom or top in place of the flat elevation}. Per-layer strength_model: 'mohr_coulomb' (default), 'shansep' (su = shansep_S ocr^shansep_m sigma'_v; fields shansep_S, shansep_m, ocr, su_min) 'hoek_brown' (Generalized Hoek-Brown; fields hb_sigci kPa, hb_gsi, hb_mi, hb_D) or 'anisotropic' (undrained su varies with the slice-base inclination alpha; fields su_active [kPa, ACTIVE/crest zone, alpha>=+45deg], su_dss [direct simple shear, alpha=0], su_passive [PASSIVE/toe zone, alpha<=-45deg] — su_active>=su_dss>=su_passive for K>1 clays; Casagrande-Carrillo sin(2alpha) interpolation; standard toe-at-low-x slope). For rapid_drawdown_fos, low-permeability layers also take the total-stress R-envelope R_c (kPa) and R_phi (deg); R_phi omitted/null => free-draining. One material per point: where two layers cover the same ground the one listed FIRST holds it, for weight and strength (reported in layer_overlaps); ground above the deepest layer's bottom that no layer covers is refused.
gwt_pointsarrayoptionalGroundwater table [[x,y],...]. If above the ground surface, ponded water is auto-detected (water weight + horizontal hydrostatic thrust applied as external loads).
khfloatoptionalHorizontal pseudo-static seismic coefficient (acts on soil weight only). default: 0.0
surchargefloatoptionalVertical surcharge (kPa). A single loaded zone; use 'surcharges' for several distinct loaded areas. default: 0.0
surcharge_x_rangearrayoptional[x_start, x_end] extent of the single 'surcharge'.
surchargesarrayoptionalSeveral distinct surcharge zones (bench + crest loads, etc.): [{pressure kPa, x_start, x_end}, ...]. Each zone's pressure is summed at any x it covers, ON TOP OF the single 'surcharge'/'surcharge_x_range'. Represent a linearly-varying (trapezoidal) load as its mean uniform pressure or as several thin zones.
tension_crack_depthfloatoptionalTension crack depth at the crest (m). default: 0.0
tension_crack_water_depthfloatoptionalWater depth in the tension crack (m). default: 0.0
tension_crack_sidestroptionalWhich crest end the tension crack is on: 'entry' (default, low-x / slip-surface entry) or 'exit' (high-x). Put it on whichever side the crest is on; no need to mirror the slope. allowed: entry, exit default: "entry"
tension_crack_modelstroptionalTension-crack mechanism: 'strength' (default) keeps the cracked wedge as zero-shear-strength driving soil; 'truncation' removes it from the sliding mass (mass ends at the vertical crack face, as Slide2/UTEXAS do). Truncation is less conservative. allowed: strength, truncation default: "strength"
reverse_curvaturestroptionalA circle whose centre is below the ground where it comes out would turn back above its centre (Slide2: reverse curvature). 'tension_crack' (default, as Slide2) closes it with a dry vertical crack; 'discard' drops such circles from searches. allowed: tension_crack, discard default: "tension_crack"
pore_pressure_pointsarrayoptionalDiscrete pore-pressure field as [[x, z, u], ...] triples (u in kPa) -- a flow-net / TIN sampling. When given, the base pore pressure at each slice is interpolated from this field (linear on the Delaunay triangulation, nearest-node fallback outside the hull, suction clamped to 0), OVERRIDING the gwt_points piezometric line and per-layer ru. The ponded-water buttress still comes from gwt_points, so set BOTH for a reservoir over a flow-net field.
nailsarrayoptionalSoil nails (per metre of slope run): [{x_head, z_head, length required; inclination deg below horizontal=15, bar_diameter mm=25, drill_hole_diameter mm=150, fy MPa=420, bond_stress kPa=100, spacing_h m=1.5, support_convention}]. Capacity = min(pullout behind slip surface, bar tensile)/spacing_h (FHWA GEC-7).
anchorsarrayoptionalTieback anchors: [{x_head, z_head, length, T_allow kN/m required; inclination=15, support_convention}]. Full T_allow applied when the bond zone crosses the slip surface.
geosyntheticsarrayoptionalHorizontal geosynthetic layers: [{elevation, T_allow kN/m required; x_start, x_end, support_convention optional}]. Every support (nails, anchors, geosynthetics, piles) acts at the base of the slice it crosses (Wright & Duncan 1991). support_convention: 'active' (default; Duncan & Wright Method A / Slide2 Active: the force is not divided by F and reduces the driving side -- give the ALLOWABLE force) or 'passive' (Method B / Slide2 Passive: divided by F with the soil strength -- give the ULTIMATE force; lower FOS for the same force). All methods.
stabilizing_pilesarrayoptionalSingle-row stabilizing/micro piles crossing the slope (Ito & Matsui 1975 or a specified shear): [{x required; spacing m=1.0 (D1); z_head, z_toe optional}]. Set the resistance EITHER by shear_capacity (kN per pile; per-metre force = shear_capacity/spacing) OR ito_matsui=true with diameter (m; D2=spacing-diameter) and optional c/phi/gamma (default: soil layer) giving the Ito-Matsui plastic lateral force integrated from head to slip surface. force_direction 'horizontal' (default) or 'normal'. support_convention 'active' (default) or 'passive' as for geosynthetics. Stabilizing force at the slip crossing.
reinforcement_forcefloatoptionalSingle equivalent horizontal reinforcement force (kN/m). Simpler alternative to nails/anchors. default: 0.0
reinforcement_elevationfloatoptionalElevation of the equivalent reinforcement force (m).
surface_typestroptionalSearch strategy. 'entry_exit' grids circular arcs between entry/exit windows; 'noncircular_de' refines random polylines with scipy differential evolution. allowed: circular, entry_exit, noncircular, noncircular_de, pso, weak_layer default: "circular"
methodstroptionalLimit-equilibrium method (noncircular searches use spencer when 'bishop' is requested). Cost per trial surface, measured on four pinned slopes: fellenius about the same as bishop, janbu about twice bishop, and spencer, morgenstern_price and gle each about 30 to 40 times bishop at 30 slices and 40 to 70 times at 60 slices. A whole search costs less than that ratio where it scans with Bishop (the centre grid's refinement, the toe circles): the default 10 x 10 centre grid took 2-3 s with bishop and 14-16 s with spencer, a 10 x 10 or 12 x 12 entry_exit grid 2 s and 60-70 s, a 30 x 30 entry_exit grid at 60 slices 21 s and 972 s; the noncircular searches, scored with Spencer at their defaults (500 trials, 5 points), took 6-7 s (noncircular), 3-7 s (weak_layer) and 10-12 s (noncircular_de), 41 s where differential evolution scored 2,325 surfaces (development laptop; the app's host up to twice as long). On the circles of these slopes bishop and spencer gave FOS within 0.3 % of each other. Which method to use is the engineer's call; bishop_screen keeps the method and scans with Bishop. allowed: fellenius, bishop, janbu, spencer, morgenstern_price, gle default: "bishop"
x_rangearrayoptional[xmin, xmax] for circle center search.
y_rangearrayoptional[ymin, ymax] for circle center search.
x_entry_rangearrayoptional[xmin, xmax] window for the slip surface's ENTRY: its low-x end, whichever way the slope faces (the toe side of a slope rising to the right, the crest side of one falling to the right).
x_exit_rangearrayoptional[xmin, xmax] window for the slip surface's EXIT: its high-x end. Windows given the other way round (entry wholly right of exit) are swapped, and the result's warnings say so.
nxintoptionalGrid divisions in x (or entry divisions for entry_exit). default: 10
nyintoptionalGrid divisions in y (or exit divisions for entry_exit). default: 10
n_trialsintoptionalRandom trials for noncircular searches. default: 500
n_pointsintoptionalPolyline vertices for noncircular searches. default: 5
n_slicesintoptionalNumber of slices per trial. default: 30
seedintoptionalRandom seed for reproducible noncircular/PSO/DE searches.
time_budget_sfloatoptionalTime budget of the whole search in seconds (at most 600). The main search scores its centres or entry/exit pairs coarse first and stops at 80 % of the budget; the result is then the lowest surface found, and warnings and search_ranges.time_budget say what was scored of how many, at what spacing, the run time projected for the whole search, and what was not run. Raise it for a long search you mean to wait for. default: 180.0
bishop_screenbooloptionalcircular and entry_exit searches with spencer / morgenstern_price / gle: score every centre or pair with Bishop's simplified method, then re-score the lowest (at least 10, every one within 5 % of the lowest, at most 30) with the method itself; the reported FOS is the method's own. On four pinned slopes it found the same surfaces and FOS as the unscreened search in 35-60 % of the time on the default centre grid, 15-30 % on 10 x 10 and 12 x 12 entry_exit grids and 3 % on a 30 x 30 entry_exit grid at 60 slices (33 s against 972 s). Not applied where supports are modelled; noncircular searches are not screened. default: false
m_alpha_rulestroptionalWhich slices the m_alpha < 0.2 check looks at (every search leaves out a surface that fails it, as Slide2 does with its 'Check malpha < 0.2' setting on). 'frictional': slices with phi' > 0; on a phi' = 0 slice m_alpha = cos(a) does not change the FOS, so leaving such a surface out only raises the minimum. 'every_slice': every slice, as Slide2 checks. allowed: frictional, every_slice default: "frictional"
tolfloatoptionalConvergence tolerance for the iterative methods. default: 0.0001

2,300 trial surfaces were evaluated: the entry–exit arcs, then small circles through the toe and circles a little above it. A toe circle governs (FOS 1.583); the entry–exit arcs’ minimum is 1.587.

Applicability limits & conventions
  • Pore pressure is a piezometric surface, per-layer ru, or scattered (x, z, u) points (pore_pressure_points) interpolated linearly on their Delaunay triangulation, with suction set to zero. The ACADS 5 / Slide2 #10 flow net could not be pinned: Fig. 10.2’s grid values did not survive the text extraction, and they are not invented (V-029).
  • A tension crack sits at the entry side (default) or the exit side (tension_crack_side). By default the cracked wedge is kept as zero-strength driving soil with the full hydrostatic thrust, which is conservative. tension_crack_model='truncation' removes the wedge from the sliding mass, as Slide2 does, and reproduces ACADS 1(b) within 0.5 % (V-026).
  • When a rigorous method finds no solution on a surface that supports cross, the result gives no FOS for that method and says so, rather than an unreinforced value.

4.4.2 fem2d — 2D finite-element analysis (fem2d)

Problems it solves

When limit equilibrium is not enough: a full 2D plane-strain finite-element engine for stress and deformation of soil masses, slope stability by strength reduction, bearing collapse, excavation unloading, seepage, and coupled consolidation — with structural beam members for walls.

Methods & theories implemented
  • Elements: T6 quadratic triangle (default, collapse-accurate), CST, Q4, and 2-node Euler–Bernoulli beams.
  • Constitutive models: linear elastic, Mohr–Coulomb (3D-principal return mapping, non-associated flow), and Hardening Soil (Schanz, Vermeer & Bonnier 1999).
  • Strength-reduction method for slope FOS (Griffiths & Lane 1999), within 2 % across meshes once four or more elements span the slope; staged construction, with movements reported per stage and counted from the end of the in-situ stage; initial-stress relaxation for tunnels/cavities.
  • Footing capacity (fem2d_footing_capacity): a strip footing loaded to collapse, the soil’s weight applied first and a surcharge beside the footing held while the footing pressure rises. A flexible footing (the default) reads Prandtl’s (2 + π)c within about 2 %; on a frictional soil its qult is a lower bound that more iterations raise, and with no surcharge on a cohesionless soil it is set by the mesh (both warned). footing='rigid' is offered but reads high on the clay check and gives no mesh-converged value on a frictional soil; mesh='graded' is for φ = 0 clay only.
  • Staged excavation (analyze_excavation): half of a symmetric excavation, in-situ stresses by K0, then one stage per lift that removes the soil and releases the forces it carried; the wall is wished in place and each strut installed stress-free when the dig reaches it. Below the water table the excavation is dewatered by default, with steady seepage under the wall (excavation_water: 'dewatered', or 'full' / 'level'); the result gives each stage, the wall’s largest moment and shear with their depths, the net water pressure and the upward gradient in front of the wall. Benchmarked against the USS Steel Sheet Piling Design Manual’s cantilever in granular soil (Mmax within 3 %).
  • Steady seepage (Laplace equation, CST elements) and Biot consolidation (staggered, and a monolithic Taylor–Hood u–p scheme); PLAXIS-style calc-package plots.
  • References: Griffiths & Lane (1999); de Souza Neto et al. (2008); Clausen et al. (2006); Schanz et al. (1999); validated vs Griffiths–Lane, the Prandtl solution (~2%), and Itasca FLAC (VALIDATION.md, V-023/V-024).
Agent-callable methods (from the shipped registry)
FEM 2D
MethodWhat it doesParams
fem2d_hs_parametersEstimate HS/HSsmall model parameters for sand from relative density (Brinkgreve et al. 2010).1
fem2d_gravityElastic gravity analysis of a rectangular soil column (plane strain FEM).8
fem2d_foundationElastic strip foundation analysis on a half-space (plane strain FEM).9
fem2d_footing_capacityUltimate bearing capacity of a strip footing by FEM (plane-strain, the FE analogue of a bearing-capacity calc): footing='flexible' (default) ramps a uniform pressure to collapse, validated vs Prandtl Nc=5.14; footing='rigid' pushes the footing down as one body (GEC-6 p. 55: Eq. 5-7 assumes a rigid footing) and reads q from the reactions, but the Prandtl clay check read high and fell as the mesh was refined (348, 306 kPa on uniform 20x10, 40x20, 288, 273 on graded ones, vs 257), and for c-phi and c = 0 no mesh-converged value was found. On a frictional soil the flexible q_ult is a lower bound that a larger max_iter can raise (a warning says so). Use element_type='t6' (CST locks and never collapses).22

fem2d_local_fosLocal (pointwise) factor-of-safety map for a slope: runs the SRM then evaluates local_FOS = Mohr-Coulomb available shear / mobilized shear at each element using the ORIGINAL strengths. At the critical SRF the minimum local FOS ~ the global SRM FOS and the low-FOS band is the failure mass. Returns summary stats (the full field is for plotting).20
fem2d_excavationStaged excavation in front of an embedded wall (plane strain FEM): in-situ K0 stresses, then lifts with struts installed as the excavation reaches them; half of a symmetric excavation.23
fem2d_seepageSteady-state seepage analysis (Laplace equation, CST elements).6
fem2d_consolidationCoupled Biot consolidation analysis (settlement + pore pressure dissipation).17
fem2d_stagedStaged construction analysis (multi-phase, activate/deactivate soil groups and beams); reports each stage's own movement, the cumulative movement and the movement since a reference stage.12

The SRF at which the Newton solve stops converging is the FEM factor of safety; T6 quadratic elements are used by default.

Applicability limits & conventions
  • CST elements lock in plastic collapse (Prandtl Nc overshoots) — use T6 for collapse/FOS work; CST is for elastic/seepage/Biot only.
  • It is a research-grade solver, not a substitute for a commercial FE package under QA; a far-field boundary must be placed far enough to avoid truncation error. The strength reduction warns when the mesh has too few elements across the slope, and when φ = 0 soil lies below the toe with level ground shorter than 1.5 times its depth (a deep circle cannot form). By default over such soil the model carries the level ground to twice that depth each side, so Taylor’s deep circle can form (a slightly higher FOS than the narrower model and about twice the run time); x_extend sets the margins, one number or a (left, right) pair. An undrained layer with Poisson’s ratio below 0.45 is warned: use 0.49.

4.5 Seismic & liquefaction

Site response, seismic earth pressures, liquefaction triggering, and ground-motion processing.

4.5.1 seismic_geotech — Seismic geotechnics

Problems it solves

Site seismic geotechnics: the AASHTO seismic site class and site factors as FHWA GEC-12 reprints them, Mononobe–Okabe seismic earth pressures on walls, SPT liquefaction triggering, post-liquefaction residual strength, and small-strain shear modulus and modulus reduction.

Methods & theories implemented
  • AASHTO site class (GEC-12 Vol I Table 7-26) from Vs30, N-bar (field N, at most 100 blows/ft) or su-bar over the upper 30 m; site factors Fa/Fv (Tables 7-28, 7-29) and, when PGA is given, Fpga (Table 7-27) and As = Fpga·PGA (Eq. 7-78); SDS, SD1 (Eq. 7-79). Site Class F and Class E by soft-clay thickness are not checked.
  • Mononobe–Okabe KAE (UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 4-15) with battered walls and sloping backfill, the seismic thrust and its increment ΔPAE at 0.6 H; KPE (FHWA GEC-4 Eq. 44) on its own wall friction, 0.4φ unless given (UFC Fig. 4-8’s limit for a planar passive wedge).
  • SPT liquefaction triggering by the NCEER / Youd et al. (2001) simplified procedure, CSR and rd as FHWA GEC-13 Eq. 5-9 prints them; residual strength by Seed & Harder (1990) (default) or Idriss & Boulanger (2007) read off GEC-12 Fig. 7-78, with void redistribution “significant” or “negligible”.
  • Gmax from Vs, CPT (Rix & Stokoe; Mayne & Rix), Hardin (1978) or Andersen (2015), and Ishibashi & Zhang (1993) modulus reduction and damping (FHWA GEC-5 Ch. 8 for the first three).
  • References: FHWA GEC-12 Vol I (FHWA-NHI-16-009) Sec. 7.4.2.1, after AASHTO (2014); UFC 3-220-20 Sec. 4-4.4.1; FHWA GEC-4 Eq. 44; FHWA GEC-13 Eq. 5-9; NCEER (1997) / Youd et al. (2001); Idriss & Boulanger (2007) as GEC-12 Fig. 7-78 prints it; FHWA GEC-5 Ch. 8. Validated against GEC-11 Example E7 (V-011, KAE within 0.06%; V-062, site factor and kmax).

Parameters of seismic_earth_pressure
ParameterTypeDescription
phifloatrequiredFriction angle (degrees).
khfloatrequiredHorizontal seismic coefficient.
kvfloatoptionalVertical seismic coefficient (positive upward). Enters KAE through the seismic angle psi = atan(kh/(1-kv)) (UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 4-15) and, with gamma and H, the thrust PAE = (gamma H^2/2)(1-kv) KAE (Eq. 4-16). default: 0.0
deltafloatoptionalWall friction angle (deg). Defaults to 2/3 phi.
betafloatoptionalWall back face batter from vertical (degrees), positive when the back face leans toward the backfill (lowers KAE). UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 4-15 and Fig. 4-8 measure their theta the other way: theta = -beta. default: 0.0
ifloatoptionalBackfill slope angle (degrees); UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 4-15's beta. default: 0.0
include_passivebooloptionalAlso return KPE (passive seismic coefficient, GEC-4 Eq. 44). default: false
delta_passivefloatoptionalWall friction angle behind KPE (deg). Not given: 0.4 phi, the most UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-8 (p. 187) allows a planar (Coulomb) passive wedge ("unconservative for delta/phi' > 0.4"); FHWA NHI-06-089 p. 10-19 finds a planar passive wedge unreliable above phi'/3 and recommends log-spiral charts, with which its p. 10-17 maximum of phi/2 goes. Above 0.4 phi the result warns.
gammafloatoptionalSoil unit weight (kN/m3) for force calculation.
HfloatoptionalWall height (m) for force calculation.
KAfloatoptionalStatic active coefficient behind PA and delta-PAE. Not given: Rankine Ka from phi (vertical wall, level backfill, no wall friction).
Worked example

Ask → For a 6 m wall on φ=30° backfill with a horizontal seismic coefficient kh=0.2, what are the Mononobe–Okabe active and passive coefficients and the seismic thrust?

call_agent(
    agent_name='seismic_geotech',
    method='seismic_earth_pressure',
    parameters={
        "phi": 30.0,
        "kh": 0.2,
        "kv": 0.0,
        "delta": 20.0,
        "gamma": 18.0,
        "H": 6.0,
        "include_passive": true
    },
)

Applicability limits & conventions
  • Its SPT procedure is the NCEER/Youd-2001 method (for code-compliance work); the default unified liquefaction tool uses Boulanger & Idriss (2014) — choose per the citation you need.

4.5.2 liquefaction — Liquefaction (unified tool)

Problems it solves

The single, discoverable liquefaction-triggering tool: is the ground liquefiable, and what is the factor of safety by depth — from SPT or CPT data, by the method your work requires.

Methods & theories implemented
  • Auto-routes by input type and method: CPT (qc/fs) → Boulanger & Idriss (2014) via liquepy, with LPI / LSN / LDI indices.
  • SPT (N160) → Boulanger & Idriss (2014) by default, or NCEER / Youd et al. (2001) via method='nceer2001' for code-compliance work.
  • References: Boulanger & Idriss (2014); NCEER (1997) / Youd et al. (2001).

4.5.3 liquepy — Liquefaction building blocks (liquepy)

Problems it solves

Direct access to the Boulanger & Idriss (2014) liquefaction building blocks and field correlations, wrapping the liquepy library — for when you want the individual CRR/CSR/MSF/Kσ terms rather than the unified tool.

Methods & theories implemented
  • B&I-2014 CPT triggering (packaged run_bi2014) with LPI/LSN/LDI.
  • B&I-2014 SPT triggering composed from the module-level building blocks (CRRM7.5, rd, CSR, Kσ) plus the SPT fines correction and MSF.
  • CPT field correlations: Vs (McGann 2015, Robertson 2009 or Andrus 2007), Dr, su/σ′v, permeability and Ic profiles.
  • References: Boulanger & Idriss (2014); the liquepy library (installed with the app).

4.5.4 opensees — Nonlinear site response & PM4Sand (OpenSees)

Problems it solves

Nonlinear finite-element site response and element-test simulation, wrapping OpenSeesPy: cyclic direct-simple-shear behaviour of liquefiable sand and one-dimensional ground response.

Methods & theories implemented
  • PM4Sand cyclic DSS element tests (stress path, pore-pressure generation).
  • One-dimensional nonlinear site response (soil column, base motion), run in a separate process with a time limit (time_limit_s, default 600 s).
  • References: PM4Sand (Boulanger & Ziotopoulou); the OpenSeesPy library. Site response is checked against the OpenSees wiki’s layered soil column (total stress, McGann & Arduino) and the OpenSeesPy effective-stress example, Kramer (1996) §7.2’s uniform damped layer on elastic rock, and pyStrata. OpenSeesPy is installed with the app.

  • A wrapper around OpenSeesPy — model fidelity and convergence follow OpenSees; a heavy optional dependency.

4.5.5 pystrata — Equivalent-linear site response (pyStrata)

Problems it solves

One-dimensional equivalent-linear site response (a SHAKE-type analysis): amplification of a base motion through a layered soil column to a surface spectrum and profiles of peak strain and acceleration.

Methods & theories implemented
  • Equivalent-linear and linear-elastic 1D response, wrapping pyStrata.
  • Modulus-reduction/damping curves: Darendeli (2001), Menq (2003), or custom.
  • References: the pyStrata library; Darendeli (2001); Menq (2003). pyStrata is installed with the app (0.5 on Python 3.12, 0.6 on Python 3.13).

4.5.6 seismic_signals — Ground-motion signal processing

Problems it solves

Ground-motion signal processing: response spectra, intensity measures, and rotated components from an acceleration record — the quantities behind a seismic demand.

Methods & theories implemented
  • Response spectra by Nigam and Jennings (1969), in sub-steps at short periods (the OpenSees site response's code); bandpass filtering and baseline correction, PGV and PGD (eqsig); rotated-component spectra RotD0/RotD50/RotD100 (Boore 2010) from the same time-domain oscillator responses; Arias intensity, significant duration, and other intensity measures.
  • References: Nigam and Jennings (1969); Boore (2010); the eqsig library (installed with the app).
Agent-callable methods (from the shipped registry)
Seismic Signals
MethodWhat it doesParams
response_spectrumCompute the response spectrum, every period by Nigam and Jennings (1969): the record linear between samples, in sub-steps of at most a twentieth of the period, the peak read between samples (the OpenSees site response uses the same code).6
intensity_measuresCompute earthquake intensity measures (Arias intensity, CAV, significant duration).6
rotd_spectrumCompute rotated spectral acceleration (RotD0/RotD50/RotD100 or any percentile) from two horizontal components (Boore 2010): each component's oscillator response by Nigam and Jennings (1969), the record linear between samples, rotated through 0-179 deg, the peak at each angle read between samples. RotD100 of a component paired with zeros is that component's response_spectrum.8
signal_processingBandpass filtering and/or baseline correction of acceleration time history.6

4.6 Site characterization & geostatistics

Turning borings, cones, and lab data into a modelled ground — parse, visualize, correlate, and interpolate.

4.6.1 subsurface — Subsurface data I/O (DIGGS / GEF / AGS4)

Problems it solves

Getting field and lab data into a modelled ground: parse and validate DIGGS, GEF/BRO-XML CPT, and AGS4 files, visualize parameters against depth, and compute trend statistics — the ingest side of characterization.

Methods & theories implemented
  • DIGGS parser (18 test types) with Plotly parameter-vs-depth, Atterberg, plan-view and trend plots; the plan view labels its axes from the stated coordinate system.
  • DIGGS 2.6 writer (write_diggs) for logs and lab results read off a report: records given inline or as saved JSON files, checked against the schema and read back, with cross-checks (lab links, drives against sample intervals, readings below the hole’s depth) that never change a value; groundwater not encountered is never written as a level, an unknown position is never written as 0, and a printed refusal is kept as one.
  • Folded format adapters: GEF/BRO-XML CPT and borehole parsing (pygef), AGS4 read/validate (python-ags4; an optional extra, [ags4], since 5.34.0), and DIGGS schema/dictionary validation (pydiggs).
  • References: the DIGGS, GEF, and AGS4 standards; pygef / python-ags4 / pydiggs. GEF/BRO-XML parsing is installed with the app; AGS4 read/validate needs the [ags4] extra and DIGGS schema/dictionary validation the [pydiggs] extra.
