4.6.2 gstools — Geostatistics (kriging, random fields & conditional simulation)

Problems it solves

Geostatistics for spatially variable ground: fit a variogram to scattered data, krige a property between borings, generate correlated random fields for spatial-variability studies, and find the probability that a TOTAL over a footprint exceeds a value — the volume of rock above an excavation level, the area where soft soil runs below a level — by conditional simulation.

Methods & theories implemented
  • Variogram estimation and model fitting; ordinary/simple/universal kriging (the smoothed best estimate between points, with the kriged surface’s totals over plan polygons and Gaussian pointwise expectations; a large grid goes to a CSV); unconditional random-field generation, wrapping GSTools.
  • Conditional simulation: many realizations that honour the observations, by conditioning by kriging (Journel & Huijbregts 1978; Chilès & Delfiner 2012 §7.3.1), each integrated over plan polygons and levels on the same realizations: mean, percentiles, the chance of any encounter, an exceedance table with standard errors, a convergence table, CSV files, an exceedance curve and a plan map of P(z > level). GSTools’ CondSRF is offered to reproduce a CondSRF notebook; it spreads totals too widely, so it is not the default.
  • References: the GSTools library (Müller et al.). Installed with the app (no extra needed).
Agent-callable methods (from the shipped registry)
Geostatistics
MethodWhat it doesParams
krigingKriging (ordinary/simple/universal): ONE smoothed best estimate of a property between points -- the mean surface and its kriging variance. It understates the spread and cannot give the probability of a total over an area (use conditional_simulation).28
variogramEstimate and fit an empirical variogram from spatial data (sill, range, nugget).6
random_fieldGenerate ONE UNconditioned 2D random field (mean + correlated variation). It does NOT honour any data; for realizations that pass through observations use conditional_simulation.12
conditional_simulationRealizations that honour the data (conditioned random field), each integrated over plan polygons: probabilities of a TOTAL over an area -- volume above/below a level (rock to excavate, fill), area, any encounter -- with percentiles, exceedance, CSV files and figures.30
Parameters of kriging
ParameterTypeDescription
xarrayrequiredX-coordinates of measurement points (m).
yarrayrequiredY-coordinates of measurement points (m).
valuesarrayrequiredMeasured values at each point.
model_typestroptionalGSTools covariance model. allowed: Gaussian, Exponential, Matern, Spherical, Linear, Stable, Rational, Cubic, HyperSpherical default: "Gaussian"
kriging_typestroptionalordinary = unknown constant mean; simple = known mean (the sample mean of these observations); universal = linear drift in x and y. allowed: ordinary, simple, universal default: "ordinary"
grid_x_minfloatoptionalGrid X minimum (m). Omitted: the data's x range less 10%.
grid_x_maxfloatoptionalGrid X maximum (m). Omitted: the data's x range plus 10%.
grid_y_minfloatoptionalGrid Y minimum (m). Omitted: from the data, as x.
grid_y_maxfloatoptionalGrid Y maximum (m). Omitted: from the data, as x.
n_grid_xintoptionalGrid points in X (1 with min = max for one coordinate). default: 50
n_grid_yintoptionalGrid points in Y. default: 50
variancefloatoptionalSill variance (value units squared). Omitted: the sample variance of THESE observations. With fit_variogram=true (the default) it is only the starting guess and is overridden by the fit.
len_scalefloatoptionalCorrelation length (m). Omitted: a third of the data extent. With fit_variogram=true it is only the starting guess and is overridden by the fit.
nuggetfloatoptionalNugget variance (measurement error + variation below the data spacing); with a nugget the surface does not pass exactly through the data. With fit_variogram=true the nugget is fitted too, unless fit_nugget=false. default: 0.0
fit_variogrambooloptionalFit variance, len_scale AND nugget to the empirical variogram, overriding values given for them (the fitted values are returned). Refused with too few lag classes: then set false and give variance and len_scale. default: true
fit_nuggetbooloptionalWith fit_variogram: false holds the nugget at the value given (e.g. from the measurement error or twinned borings) and fits only variance and len_scale. Without fit_variogram nothing is fitted and true is refused. default: true
regionsarrayoptionalPlan regions: [{name, polygon: [[x, y], ...], level}], level one number or a list of levels to sweep (same units as values, e.g. an elevation in m). Totals over the cells whose centre is inside the polygon (concave shapes fine): volume_above = sum(max(z - level, 0) x cell area), area_above = cell area where z > level (the 'below' versions mirror it). Here from the kriging only: the kriged surface's totals, and Gaussian POINTWISE expectations (expected volume, expected area, mean cell probability). These are expectations cell by cell; the probability that a TOTAL exceeds a value needs conditional_simulation.
cell_sizefloatoptionalCell size (m) for the region totals; default the smallest round size giving at most ~3,000 cells.
quantitystroptionalRegion totals above (e.g. rock above an excavation level) or below (e.g. fill to a grade) the level. allowed: above, below default: "above"
marginfloatoptionalMargin (m) of the region lattice around the regions.
output_prefixstroptionalFile name stem for the files this call writes (<stem>_grid.csv for a grid over 2,500 points, <stem>_regions.csv with regions, <stem>_kriging_map.png); default kriging_<time>.
figuresbooloptionalDraw the kriging map: a plan, to scale, of the kriged mean and the kriging standard deviation as labelled contours, the standard deviation with a colour scale too (PNG + interactive). Set false in a sweep of many calls. default: true
namesarrayoptionalObservation names (e.g. boring IDs), one per point; label the map.
value_namestroptionalWhat the values are, in the logs' words (e.g. 'top of hard rock elevation'); names the map. Give it.
value_unitstroptionalUnit of the values (e.g. 'm').
north_degfloatoptionalNorth on the map, degrees clockwise from up, as the source plan shows it; up when not given.
outlinesarrayoptionalWhat the source plan shows besides the borings, drawn on the map for orientation: the property line, buildings, walls, roads. A list of {name, polygon: [[x, y], ...]} (closed, 3 points or more) or {name, line: [[x, y], ...]} (open, 2 or more), in the same x, y as the observations, with kind 'property_line' (drawn dash-dot) or 'outline' (default). Drawing only: they change no number.
observations_namestroptionalWhat the observation points are, in the logs' words (e.g. 'Borings', 'CPT soundings'): the map legend's name for them. 'Observations' when not given.
Applicability limits & conventions
  • The spread is what the chosen model implies: a Gaussian, stationary field with the covariance model, variance and length scale given (or computed from the data and echoed). With few borings these cannot be checked against the data and usually move the answer more than the method does — run cases.
  • Plan view (2D) only; inequality data (a boring that ended above rock) by rejection sampling.

4.7 Reliability & sensitivity

The variability engine: propagate parameter uncertainty to a reliability index and a probability of failure, and find which input governs.

4.7.1 reliability — Reliability engine

Problems it solves

The variability engine: turn any deterministic method into a probabilistic one and report the reliability index β and probability of failure Pf — because with soil COVs of 10–40% the honest deliverable is a distribution, not a lone factor of safety.

Methods & theories implemented
  • FOSM (First-Order Second-Moment), PEM (Rosenblueth point-estimate), Monte Carlo (with Cholesky correlation and Latin Hypercube), and native FORM (Hasofer–Lind design point).
  • A published COV knowledge base (Duncan 2000; TC304; Phoon & Kulhawy) queried by cov_guidance; Vanmarcke spatial-averaging variance reduction; combined COV.
  • Ready-made library functions (not agent tools): bearing_capacity_reliability, axial_pile_reliability, slope_reliability.
  • References: Duncan (2000); Phoon & Kulhawy (1999); Baecher & Christian; Vanmarcke (1977); validated vs Duncan (2000) reliability example.
Agent-callable methods (from the shipped registry)
Property Variability
MethodWhat it doesParams
cov_guidancePublished COV ranges for soil/rock properties with full provenance: Duncan (2000) Table 1, ISSMGE-TC304 (2021) site-specific statistics (clay/sand/rock), Phoon & Kulhawy (1999) transformation uncertainty (via UFC 3-220-20). Use to pick a defensible cov for the engines.4
combined_covCombine inherent + measurement + transformation COVs (UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 7-5), optionally with Vanmarcke spatial-averaging variance reduction on the inherent part. All COVs as fractions (0.3 = 30%).4
variance_reductionVanmarcke variance reduction Gamma^2(L/delta) for spatial averaging over a failure surface/pile length. Give delta directly or a soil_type to use published scale-of-fluctuation guidance (Cami et al. 2020 / ISSMGE-TC304 2021).4
Reliability
MethodWhat it doesParams
fosmFOSM / Taylor-series reliability (Duncan 2000, UFC 3-220-20): central differences at +/-1 sigma -> moments of g, beta (normal+lognormal), pf, and the per-variable variance-contribution table (which variable matters). 2n+1 g-evaluations; supports correlation.4
pemRosenblueth point-estimate method (UFC 3-220-20 Eqs. 7-13/7-14): 2^n evaluations at mu+/-sigma (correlation-adjusted weights), or the 2n+1 'multiplicative' reduced scheme for many variables.5
monte_carloMonte Carlo simulation: seeded numpy sampling (optional Latin Hypercube), correlation via Cholesky in normal space, empirical pf with 95% CI + convergence trace, histogram, lognormal-fit beta. Its variables are scalars; for a property that varies across a site and must honour borings (e.g. a rock surface under a footprint), use gstools.conditional_simulation.8
formNative FORM (Hasofer-Lind / Rackwitz-Fiessler): HL-RF iteration with equivalent-normal transformation of non-normal variables; exact for the linear/lognormal cases. Returns beta, pf, design point x*, and alpha sensitivity vector (alpha^2 = uncertainty share).5
Parameters of monte_carlo
ParameterTypeDescription
variablesobjectrequiredRandom variables: {name: {mean, cov or std, dist, lower, upper}}. dist one of ['normal', 'lognormal', 'uniform', 'triangular'] (default normal). lower/upper truncate normal/lognormal or bound uniform/triangular. Example: {'su': {'mean': 50, 'cov': 0.3, 'dist': 'lognormal'}}.
g_expressionstrrequiredPerformance function of the variable names. With convention='fos' write a FACTOR OF SAFETY (failure at g<1), e.g. 'R/S'; with 'margin' a margin (failure at g<0), e.g. 'R - S'. Math functions allowed (sqrt, log, exp, tan, radians, ...).
conventionstroptional'fos': g is a factor of safety (failure g<1, lognormal beta reported). 'margin': g = R-S (failure g<0). allowed: fos, margin default: "fos"
correlationobjectoptionalPairwise correlations {'a,b': rho} or full matrix [[...]] in variable order. Omit for independent variables.
nintoptionalRealizations. Aim n >= 10/pf. default: 10000
seedintoptionalRNG seed for reproducibility.
samplingstroptional'lhs' = Latin Hypercube (variance reduction). allowed: random, lhs default: "random"
n_binsintoptionalHistogram bins. default: 30
Worked example

Ask → Resistance R (mean 500, COV 20%, lognormal) against load S (mean 300, COV 15%) — 50,000 Monte-Carlo trials: what is the reliability index and the probability of failure?

call_agent(
    agent_name='reliability',
    method='monte_carlo',
    parameters={
        "variables": {
                "R": {
                        "mean": 500.0,
                        "cov": 0.2,
                        "dist": "lognormal"
                },
                "S": {
                        "mean": 300.0,
                        "cov": 0.15,
                        "dist": "normal"
                }
        },
        "g_expression": "R - S",
        "convention": "margin",
        "n": 50000,
        "seed": 42
    },
)
Representative output (real, from the shipped code)
engine: monte_carlo
convention: margin
n: 50000
n_failed: 1008
pf: 0.0202
pf_ci95: [2 entries]
g_mean: 199.4937
g_std: 109.7902
g_cov: 0.5503
g_min: -175.3176
g_max: 803.6505
g_median: 191.5376
percentiles: {p1=-20.952, p5=34.8924, p10=66.1934, p50=191.5376, p90=343.9452, p95=394.0009}
beta_normal: 1.817
… (additional fields in the full result dict)

This is the payoff of the whole architecture: any deterministic method plugs into the same g() contract and returns β and Pf instead of a lone number.

Applicability limits & conventions
  • The performance function is a scalar g(values) of the named variables; a depth-varying undrained strength is varied as one correlated (a, b) pair through slope_stability’s probabilistic FOS (linear_su, V-030), not through this engine.

4.7.2 salib — Global sensitivity analysis (SALib)

Problems it solves

Which uncertain input actually governs the answer? Global sensitivity analysis apportions the variance of a model output to its inputs, so investigation and design effort go where they matter.

Methods & theories implemented
  • Sobol variance-based indices (first-order and total) and Morris elementary-effects screening, wrapping SALib; sample generation and index computation.
  • References: Sobol; Morris; the SALib library (installed with the app).
Agent-callable methods (from the shipped registry)
Sensitivity Analysis
MethodWhat it doesParams
sobol_analysisONE CALL Sobol variance-based sensitivity: samples, evaluates the model (an expression or a calculation-module spec) at every point, returns S1/ST indices only. Use this, not sobol_sample + sobol_analyze.9
morris_analysisONE CALL Morris elementary-effects screening: samples, evaluates the model (an expression or a calculation-module spec) at every point, returns mu*/sigma only. Cheaper than Sobol: evaluations = n_trajectories*(D+1).9
sobol_sampleGenerate Sobol quasi-random sample matrix for variance-based sensitivity analysis (two-step: YOU evaluate the model on every row, then sobol_analyze). Prefer sobol_analysis, which does it in one call.5
sobol_analyzeCompute Sobol first-order and total-order sensitivity indices from model output.6
morris_sampleGenerate Morris one-at-a-time (OAT) sample matrix for screening (two-step: YOU evaluate the model on every row, then morris_analyze). Prefer morris_analysis, which does it in one call.5
morris_analyzeCompute Morris elementary effects (mu*, sigma) for parameter screening.7
Parameters of sobol_sample
ParameterTypeDescription
var_namesarrayrequiredList of variable names (at least 2).
boundsarrayrequiredList of [min, max] bounds for each variable.
n_samplesintoptionalBase number of Sobol samples. Total rows = N*(2D+2) for second-order. default: 1024
calc_second_orderbooloptionalInclude second-order interaction indices. default: true
seedintoptionalRandom seed for reproducibility. default: 42

4.7.3 pystra — Structural reliability (pystra)

Problems it solves

Structural reliability for an explicit limit-state function: the reliability index and probability of failure by FORM, SORM, or Monte Carlo, with normal, lognormal, Gumbel, uniform, Weibull, gamma, beta and constant variables and a correlation matrix.

Methods & theories implemented
  • FORM / SORM / Monte Carlo on a user limit-state function, wrapping pystra (built on PyRe and FERUM).
  • References: the pystra library (installed with the app).
Agent-callable methods (from the shipped registry)
Reliability
MethodWhat it doesParams
form_analysisFirst Order Reliability Method (FORM) — find design point and reliability index.3
sorm_analysisSecond Order Reliability Method (SORM) — improved probability with curvature correction.3
monte_carlo_analysisCrude Monte Carlo reliability analysis — estimate failure probability by random sampling.4
Applicability limits & conventions
  • Complements the geotechnical reliability engine; use pystra for a general structural limit state and reliability for the geotechnical wrappers + COV database.

4.8 Structural analysis

Cross-section properties, reinforced-concrete section capacity, and elastic frame / continuous-beam analysis.

4.8.1 section_props — Cross-section properties

Problems it solves

Structural cross-section properties for rectangles, circles, CHS, RHS and I-sections given by their dimensions, and any polygon: area, moments of inertia, elastic and plastic moduli, radii of gyration, torsion and warping constants — the inputs every member check starts from. Dimensions in mm.

Methods & theories implemented
  • Exact closed-form integration over the section outline (Green’s theorem): parametric rectangle / circle / CHS / RHS / I-section, plus arbitrary polygon outlines.
  • Torsion and warping constants from the published closed forms — the exact St. Venant series for a rectangle, Bredt for closed boxes, El Darwish & Johnston / AISC for I-sections; arbitrary outlines fall back to a finite-difference Prandtl solve.
Agent-callable methods (from the shipped registry)
Cross-Section Analysis
MethodWhat it doesParams
section_propertiesProperties of parametric shapes (rectangle/circle/CHS/RHS/I): A, I, Z, S, r, J, warping. Dimensions in mm. One material; a multi-material PILE's composite EI (RC, concrete-filled pipe) is lateral_pile.composite_section_ei.10
polygon_sectionProperties of an arbitrary closed polygon section from vertex coordinates (mm).3
Applicability limits & conventions
  • Geometric properties only — no member design checks; nominal member capacity comes from the design reference layer as it grows.

4.8.2 concrete_props — RC section analysis

Problems it solves

Reinforced-concrete rectangular sections: gross and cracked stiffness, cracking moment, nominal moment capacity (sagging/hogging), and the N-M interaction diagram. mm and MPa in, kN·m out.

Methods & theories implemented
  • Strain-compatibility section analysis against the ACI 318-19 material model (Ec = 4700√f’c, rectangular stress block with ACI β1, fr = 0.62√f’c).
  • Capacities are NOMINAL — apply code φ factors separately.
Agent-callable methods (from the shipped registry)
RC Section Analysis
MethodWhat it doesParams
rc_rectangular_sectionRectangular RC section: gross/cracked Ixx, cracking moment, nominal Mn (sag/hog), optional N-M interaction. mm/MPa in, kN*m out. For a circular RC or concrete-filled pipe PILE's composite EI use lateral_pile.composite_section_ei.13
Applicability limits & conventions
  • Rectangular sections with edge bar layers, one layer per face.

4.8.3 pynite — Frame & beam analysis (PyNite)

Problems it solves

Elastic frame and continuous-beam analysis: reactions, member moment/shear/axial envelopes, and deflections for 2D/3D skeletal structures. SI units (m, kN, kPa).

Methods & theories implemented
  • Matrix displacement analysis (PyNiteFEA, MIT); plane frames are auto-stabilized out-of-plane; the continuous-beam method reports textbook sagging-positive conventions.
Agent-callable methods (from the shipped registry)
Frame Analysis
MethodWhat it doesParams
frame_analysisLinear-elastic 2D/3D frame: nodes/members/supports/loads -> reactions + member force/deflection envelopes. SI: m, kN, kPa.7
continuous_beamMulti-span continuous beam: reactions, support (hogging) and span (sagging) moments, deflections. Sagging positive.7
Applicability limits & conventions
  • Linear-static only; the toolkit has no nonlinear or dynamic frame analysis. Where numpy is held at 1.26 (Foundry) PyNiteFEA cannot install and the tool is left out.

4.10 Also available: native soil correlations

SPT field corrections (N → N60 → (N1)60 per Youd et al. 2001 / Liao & Whitman), Bolton stress-dilatancy, the small-strain Gmax family (Vs, CPT, Hardin-Black, Andersen), Ishibashi & Zhang modulus-reduction/damping curves, and Brinkgreve HS-parameter estimation are implemented natively (geotech_common.soil_properties, seismic_geotech.dynamic_properties, fem2d.hs_correlations) and exposed through the subsurface, seismic, and fem2d agents. The former third-party groundhog wrapper was removed in favor of these.

Chapter 5The reference library

The agent doesn’t just compute — it reads the standards back to you. geotech-references is a companion package of digitized design manuals: their tables and equations as callable lookups, their chapter text in a full-text search index, and their figures in a searchable catalog paired with a vision read-off. There are 35 reference modules.

5.2 Find with text, read with pixels

Retrieval is lexical: reference_search runs a full-text (SQLite FTS5) query over the chapter text and equation captions, expanded with a curated synonym map so a query for “passive resistance” also finds “Kp”. That roughly quadrupled recall@5 in the retrieval eval with no disturbance to the top hit. Figures are handled the same way for search, then differently for reading: figure_search finds a chart by meaning, and read_reference_figure renders the actual page and hands it to a vision model to read a value off the axes — because a design chart’s value lives in its pixels, not its caption.

Why not image embeddings?

CLIP-style image embeddings were evaluated and rejected — they are a poor fit for axis-labelled line charts. The architecture is deliberately “find lexically, read visually.” This keeps retrieval cheap and explainable while still getting an accurate value off the chart.

In agent workflows all of this is reached through the consult_references sub-agent described in Chapter 3, so the primary agent stays focused on the analysis while a scoped consultant handles citations and figure read-offs.

Chapter 6Geometry import & model setup

Real analyses start from a real cross-section — a CAD file or a PDF drawing, not a set of hand-typed coordinates. Three modules get geometry in and a fourth gets a calc package out; a fifth orchestrates a staged, human-gated model build.

6.1 DXF import

dxf_import reads a DXF, discovers its layers, and converts polylines into the SlopeGeometry and FEM inputs the analysis modules consume. The workflow is discover → parse → build: list the layers, map them to surface / soil boundaries / water table / soil nails, then build the model. ezdxf is installed with the app.

6.2 PDF cross-section import

pdf_import extracts geometry from a PDF drawing by vector extraction (PyMuPDF get_drawings() for exact line work, through the planlens package). It calibrates the scale from two points and a known distance or proposes it from the scale notes, proposes a colour–to–role mapping from the labels, cleans up the geometry, and cross-checks the vector result against a vision extraction made outside the tool, so the two methods can confirm each other.

6.3 DXF export

dxf_export writes a cross-section back out to DXF — surface, soil boundaries, water table, soil nails, and annotations — so a model built or checked in the toolkit can return to CAD.

6.4 Staged, human-gated model setup (geo_project)

geo_project is a canonical project document for building 2D LE/FEM models in stages with confirmation gates. The agent never trusts its own read of a drawing: it ingests geometry with provenance quarantine, then renders an echo-back cross-section so a human visually confirms the numbers before they enter the model. It is wired to the v2 deep agent as an opt-in model-setup sub-agent.

6.5 Calc-package reporting

calc_package turns a module result into a Mathcad-style calculation package — HTML or LaTeX, with figures and equation traces — for 17 of the analysis modules. It emits PDF by pdflatex where that is installed and otherwise by PyMuPDF’s HTML engine (Databricks, Foundry), a simpler layout.

Chapter 7Reliability & probabilistic analysis

This is the payoff of the whole architecture. Soil properties carry coefficients of variation of 10–40% — far larger than structural materials — so the honest deliverable is not a lone factor of safety but a reliability index β and a probability of failure Pf. The reliability module turns any deterministic method into a probabilistic one.

7.1 Declare the uncertainty, pick an engine

Declare the uncertain inputs as random variables, hand the engine a performance function g(values) that returns a factor of safety or a margin, and pick an engine. All four share the same g() contract:

EngineCostWhat it does
FOSMcheapFirst-Order Second-Moment — propagates means and variances for an instant β, no sampling
PEMrobustRosenblueth point-estimate — evaluates g() at ± points; handles non-linearity without a derivative
Monte Carloexact-ishSamples the joint distribution N times and counts failures; correlations via Cholesky, optional Latin Hypercube
FORMefficientNative first-order reliability — finds the design point; β at a fraction of Monte Carlo’s calls
Worked example

Ask → Resistance R (mean 500, COV 20%, lognormal) against load S (mean 300, COV 15%) — 50,000 Monte-Carlo trials: what is the reliability index and the probability of failure?

call_agent(
    agent_name='reliability',
    method='monte_carlo',
    parameters={
        "variables": {
                "R": {
                        "mean": 500.0,
                        "cov": 0.2,
                        "dist": "lognormal"
                },
                "S": {
                        "mean": 300.0,
                        "cov": 0.15,
                        "dist": "normal"
                }
        },
        "g_expression": "R - S",
        "convention": "margin",
        "n": 50000,
        "seed": 42
    },
)
Representative output (real, from the shipped code)
engine: monte_carlo
convention: margin
n: 50000
n_failed: 1008
pf: 0.0202
pf_ci95: [2 entries]
g_mean: 199.4937
g_std: 109.7902
g_cov: 0.5503
g_min: -175.3176
g_max: 803.6505
g_median: 191.5376
percentiles: {p1=-20.952, p5=34.8924, p10=66.1934, p50=191.5376, p90=343.9452, p95=394.0009}
beta_normal: 1.817
… (additional fields in the full result dict)

This is the payoff of the whole architecture: any deterministic method plugs into the same g() contract and returns β and Pf instead of a lone number.

7.2 Don’t assume a COV — look it up

cov_guidance is a queryable knowledge base of published coefficients of variation (Duncan 2000, TC304, Phoon & Kulhawy) keyed by soil property, so the input uncertainty is defensible rather than assumed. variance_reduction applies Vanmarcke spatial averaging — a footing averages over its footprint, a long slope samples many weak and strong zones, so the variance that actually matters is reduced over the volume the structure loads. combined_cov composes several sources of uncertainty.

7.3 Which input governs? — global sensitivity

salib wraps SALib for variance-based global sensitivity: Sobol indices and Morris screening answer which input drives the spread of the answer, so the site investigation and the design effort go where they matter. pystra adds a dedicated structural reliability engine (FORM / SORM / Monte Carlo) for limit-state functions.

7.4 Probabilistic paths that ship out of the box

The reliability wrappers — bearing_capacity_reliability, axial_pile_reliability, and slope_reliability — and the slope-stability module’s built-in FOSM and Monte-Carlo FOS mean the probabilistic path is available directly, without hand-wiring the performance function for the most common problems.

Chapter 8Validation basis

Beyond the per-module unit suites (which regress each method against textbook answers), the package carries a published-example validation layer: real worked examples from the design manuals and FE verification suites, with complete numeric inputs and published numeric answers, run through the analysis modules offline. The problems (V-001 onward) and their sources are in validation_examples/INVENTORY.md; the run-by-run verdicts are in validation_examples/RESULTS.md. Flagship modules additionally carry a VALIDATION.md (slope_stability vs Fredlund & Krahn 1977 / ACADS / Duncan; fem2d vs Griffiths & Lane and the Prandtl solution; lateral_pile vs a COM624P oracle). Verdicts are graded honestly: PASS (reproduces the published answer within tolerance), CONVENTION (a defensibly different but documented convention — the module is not tuned to the one example), and N/A (scope) (the module implements a different method than the example — a documented coverage gap, not a failure). Across 107 comparisons there were zero unexplained discrepancies.

8.2 How to read the verdicts

PASS

The module reproduces the published answer within the stated tolerance. Example: the Mononobe–Okabe seismic coefficient KAE reproduces the GEC-11 value to within 0.06%; the Fellenius/Bishop factors of safety match the Caltrans slice table to the printed digit.

CONVENTION

The module and the example use a defensibly different convention, and the delta is documented — the module is not tuned to the one example. Example: for the GEC-6 spread footing, the packaged high-level call applies Brinch Hansen’s depth factors while the example takes dq = 1.0 and GEC-6’s Cw groundwater factors; assembled the example’s way, the module recovers the published closed form exactly.

N/A (scope)

The module implements a different method than the example — a documented coverage gap, not a failure. Example: a slope problem whose pore pressure is supplied as an interpolated flow-net grid, which the module (piezometric surface or per-layer ru) does not accept.

The philosophy is visible in these notes: where the module and a source differ, the manual says why, in the source’s own terms, rather than quietly fitting the code to one benchmark. Several checks even surfaced errors in the published examples (for instance an under-iterated Bishop value that the module iterates to convergence).

Chapter 9Limitations & responsible use

Everything in the disclaimer at the front of this manual applies. This chapter makes the boundaries concrete, because knowing where a tool stops is part of using it well.

9.1 It is a multiplier for judgment, not a replacement

The toolkit runs the methods; it does not know your site and cannot exercise engineering judgment. A qualified, licensed professional engineer familiar with the site must independently review every input, assumption, method selection, and result before it is relied upon. Using this software creates no engineer-of-record relationship.

9.2 Validation covers only the documented cases

Agreement on a benchmark (Chapter 8) does not certify correctness for any other geometry, parameter range, or loading condition. The absence of a validation entry means a result has not been independently checked here. Read the module’s DESIGN.md and VALIDATION.md for its exact scope, sign conventions, and edge cases before trusting it on a new problem.

9.3 Known method boundaries

A few honest scope notes drawn straight from the validation record:

  • wave_equation models every hammer as a rigid ram at its rated energy; a diesel’s combustion and changing stroke are not modelled and the result warns that its blow counts are likely low (GEC-12 Vol. 2 p. 206); treat diesel bearing graphs as a trend, not a tie-out.
  • slope_stability’s tension crack keeps the cracked wedge as zero-strength driving soil by default (a conservative convention); tension_crack_model='truncation' removes it from the sliding mass as Slide2 does.
  • ground_improvement uses an equal-strain settlement-reduction model for aggregate piers, not the GEC-13 stiffness-modulus two-layer method; the Priebe curve is GEC-13's printed curve (φ = 37.5°) and depends on the area-ratio convention you feed it.
  • The high-level bearing_capacity call applies Brinch Hansen’s depth factors by default (depth_factor_method) and an effective-unit-weight groundwater model — different from GEC-6’s Cw groundwater factors, which are not offered; know which convention your check needs.
  • Soldier-pile effective widths and arching are not modelled in soe or sheet_pile (continuous walls per metre run); sheet_pile’s anchored embedment is classical free earth support, while the FHWA apparent-diagram embedment is in soe.

9.4 Treat agent output with particular care

The LLM agent can select the wrong method, mis-transcribe a value, or read a chart imperfectly. Its answers are a starting point for review, never a final basis for design. Inspect the tool calls (result.tool_calls, or verbose=True) — the methods and parameters actually used — not just the prose. Confirm the inputs and units: everything is SI, and mis-scaled units are the user’s responsibility to catch.

The bottom line

Responsibility for the safety, adequacy, and code-compliance of any design remains entirely with the licensed professional engineer who adopts it. This software is provided under the MIT License “AS IS”, without warranty of any kind.

Appendix AFull method & parameter reference

Every agent-callable method on every module, with its full parameter list, generated directly from the shipped dispatch registry. This is the authoritative, complete catalog — the narrative chapters show one headline method per module; here is all of them.

10.1 Analysis modules

10.1.1 bearing_capacity — Bearing capacity

bearing_capacity_analysis — Full bearing capacity analysis for a shallow foundation (Vesic/Meyerhof/Hansen, or Terzaghi 1943 via factor_method='terzaghi').

ParameterTypeDescription
widthfloatrequiredFooting width B (m).
lengthfloatoptionalFooting length L (m). Omit for strip.
depthfloatoptionalEmbedment depth Df (m). default: 0.0
shapestroptionalFooting shape. allowed: strip, square, rectangular, circular default: "strip"
cohesionfloatoptionalSoil cohesion c (kPa). default: 0.0
friction_anglefloatoptionalFriction angle phi (degrees). default: 0.0
unit_weightfloatrequiredSoil unit weight gamma (kN/m3).
gwt_depthfloatoptionalGroundwater depth below surface (m).
layer2_cohesionfloatoptionalSecond layer cohesion (kPa). default: 0.0
layer2_friction_anglefloatoptionalSecond layer phi (degrees). default: 0.0
layer2_unit_weightfloatoptionalSecond layer gamma (kN/m3). Triggers 2-layer analysis.
layer1_thicknessfloatoptionalFirst layer thickness (m) for 2-layer.
layer1_descriptionstroptionalFirst layer label for the result.
layer2_descriptionstroptionalSecond layer label for the result.
factor_of_safetyfloatoptionalFactor of safety. default: 3.0
factor_methodstroptionalShape/depth/inclination-factor method. Each takes its own N-gamma unless ngamma_method names another; 'meyerhof' = UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-6, with the shape factors 1 under an inclined load (its note A); it has no base-tilt or ground-slope factors (UFC p. 294, Table 5-3), so base_tilt and ground_slope are refused with it. Hansen applies to N-gamma only: use ngamma_method='hansen'. 'terzaghi' = Terzaghi (1943): his Nc, Nq, N-gamma and shape coefficients (1.3cNc; 0.4/0.3 gamma B Ngamma square/circular), no depth or inclination factors; not for inclined loads, slopes or tilted bases (UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-3). allowed: vesic, meyerhof, terzaghi default: "vesic"
ngamma_methodstroptionalNgamma factor method. Default depends on factor_method: the method's own, 'vesic' = 2(Nq+1)tan(phi) (GEC-6 Eq. 5-8), 'meyerhof' = (Nq-1)tan(1.4 phi) (UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-6), 'kumbhojkar' with factor_method='terzaghi'. 'hansen' = 1.5(Nq-1)tan(phi). Another than the method's own is a mixed method; the result's choices say so. With factor_method='terzaghi' (Terzaghi gave N-gamma only as a chart): 'kumbhojkar' (Kumbhojkar 1993 as tabulated in Das) or 'coduto' (Coduto et al. 2016 approximation, UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-2); the result reports the other beside it. allowed: vesic, meyerhof, hansen, kumbhojkar, coduto
failure_modestroptionalfactor_method='terzaghi' only: 'local' applies Terzaghi's local-shear reduction c* = 2/3 c, tan(phi*) = 2/3 tan(phi) (UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-4). allowed: general, local default: "general"
base_tiltfloatoptionalBase tilt angle (degrees). With factor_method 'vesic' only (GEC-6 Table 5-5 factors); 'meyerhof' and 'terzaghi' have none and refuse it (UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-3). default: 0.0
eccentricity_BfloatoptionalLoad eccentricity along B (m). default: 0.0
eccentricity_LfloatoptionalLoad eccentricity along L (m). default: 0.0
load_inclinationfloatoptionalLoad inclination from vertical (degrees), 0 to below 90; with factor_method 'meyerhof' below phi, as UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-6 takes theta = atan(H/V) < phi' (refused at phi or more). default: 0.0
ground_slopefloatoptionalGround slope angle down from horizontal (degrees), 0 to 45, this tool's own limit: Vesic's g_q = (1 - tan omega)^2 is 0 at 45 deg. With factor_method 'vesic' only; 'meyerhof' and 'terzaghi' have no ground-slope factors and refuse it (UFC 3-220-20 p. 294, Table 5-3). For a footing on or near a slope GEC-6 Sec. 5.2.3.4 uses N_cq and N_gamma-q (Fig. 5-7). default: 0.0
vertical_loadfloatoptionalRequired with factor_method 'vesic', a load_inclination and a soil with cohesion (or phi = 0): the vertical load V on the footing (kN; kN/m for a strip). Vesic's load inclination factors take H = V tan(load_inclination) over V + A' c cot(phi) (Vesic 1975, EN 1997-1:2004 Annex D.4); with c = 0 that is tan(load_inclination) and V cancels. Without it the call is refused (factor_method 'meyerhof' takes the angle alone, UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-6).
depth_factor_methodstroptionalDepth factors for an embedded footing. 'hansen': Brinch Hansen's (1970) k = Df/B below Df/B = 1, arctan(Df/B) from 1 (UFC 3-220-20 Tables 5-7, 5-8 note B) in the factor_method's d factors (Meyerhof's: k = Df/B up to 1 as UFC Table 5-6 prints it); at phi = 0 Vesic's cohesion term adds Table 5-7's d_c = 0.4 k, as UFC Eq. 5-21 does. 'gec6' (factor_method 'vesic' only): GEC-6 Eq. 5-14 and Table 5-4, d_q on the surcharge term alone, 1.0 below Df/B = 1. 'linear' (factor_method 'meyerhof' only): Meyerhof's depth factors with k = Df/B at every depth, as UFC Table 5-6 (p. 294) prints them, d_c = 1 + 0.2 k sqrt(Kp), d_q = d_gamma = 1 + 0.1 k sqrt(Kp) for phi > 10 deg (1 at phi = 0); larger than 'hansen' beyond Df/B = 1. 'none': no depth factors, as GEC-6 Sec. 5.2.3.3 advises unless the cover over the footing is competent and sure to stay. The result's choices give what each option gives. allowed: hansen, gec6, linear, none default: "hansen"

shapestroptionalFooting shape. allowed: square, rectangular, strip, circular default: "square"
time_yearsfloatoptionalTime for creep factor. default: 0.0
gamma_soilfloatrequiredEffective unit weight (kN/m3) below the base, for sigma'_vp = q_overburden + gamma_soil * z_peak, the vertical effective stress at the depth of the peak, in Izp = 0.5 + 0.1*sqrt(dq/sigma'_vp) (NHI-06-089 Fig. 8-21b).

consolidation_settlement — Cc/Cr e-log(p) consolidation settlement with layer summation.

ParameterTypeDescription
layersarrayrequiredArray of {thickness (m), depth_to_center (m), e0, Cc, Cr (recompression index; ~Cc/10 if unknown), sigma_v0 (initial effective stress at layer center, kPa, must be > 0), sigma_p (preconsolidation, kPa, optional)} dicts. All of thickness/depth_to_center/e0/Cc/Cr/sigma_v0 are required.
delta_sigmafloatoptionalUniform stress increase (kPa). Or use delta_sigmas array.
delta_sigmasarrayoptionalPer-layer stress increases (kPa), one per layer.
q_netfloatoptionalNet pressure for auto stress distribution; required without delta_sigma(s).
BfloatoptionalFooting width for stress distribution (m); required without delta_sigma(s).
LfloatoptionalFooting length for stress distribution (m). Defaults to B.
stress_methodstroptionalStress distribution method. allowed: 2:1, boussinesq, westergaard also read as: 2to1 = 2:1 default: "2:1"

hough_settlement — Hough (1959) granular C'-index settlement: dH = H/C'*log10[(sigma'_vo + delta_sigma)/sigma'_vo] per layer, with a 2:1 stress increase (GEC-6). Use for sands/gravels with SPT data (C' is the Hough bearing-capacity index from corrected N', NOT Cc/(1+e0)).

ParameterTypeDescription
q_netfloatrequiredNet bearing pressure at footing base (kPa).
BfloatrequiredFooting width (m).
layersarrayrequiredArray of granular {thickness (m), depth_to_center (m, mid-depth below footing base), sigma_v0 (effective overburden at layer center, kPa, > 0), C_prime (Hough bearing-capacity index, dimensionless, > 0)} dicts. All four keys are required per layer.
LfloatoptionalFooting length (m). Defaults to B (square footing); 2:1 increase is q*B*L/((B+z)(L+z)).

combined_settlement_analysis — Full analysis: immediate + consolidation + secondary + time curve.

ParameterTypeDescription
q_appliedfloatrequiredApplied pressure (kPa).
BfloatrequiredFooting width (m).
EsfloatoptionalElastic modulus for immediate settlement (kPa), for the elastic method. Not given: no immediate settlement is computed (0).
consolidation_layersarrayoptionalArray of consolidation layer dicts.
schmertmann_layersarrayoptionalArray of Schmertmann layer dicts.
cvfloatoptionalCoefficient of consolidation (m2/yr). With consolidation_layers, adds the time curve and t50/t90 to the result.
HdrfloatoptionalDrainage path length (m) for the time curve. Default: consolidating thickness / 2 (double drainage) or the whole thickness (single).
immediate_methodstroptionalImmediate settlement method. allowed: elastic, schmertmann default: "elastic"
drainagestroptionalDrainage condition for time rate. allowed: single, double default: "double"
stress_methodstroptionalStress distribution method. allowed: 2:1, boussinesq, westergaard also read as: 2to1 = 2:1 default: "2:1"
q_overburdenfloatoptionalOverburden pressure at footing base (kPa). default: 0.0
LfloatoptionalFooting length (m). Not given: L = B for a square or circular footing; a strip is taken as infinitely long (plane strain), which the elastic method refuses unless Iw is given (its Iw grows with L/B without limit); a rectangular footing needs L.
shapestroptionalFooting shape. allowed: square, rectangular, strip, circular also read as: circle = circular default: "square"
nufloatoptionalPoisson's ratio for immediate settlement. default: 0.3
IwfloatoptionalElastic influence factor for the elastic method. Not given: GEC-6 Table 5-12's shape factor at the centre of a flexible footing (1.12 for a square, by L/B for a rectangle, interpolated in log(L/B); 1.00 for a circle).
gamma_soilfloatoptionalEffective unit weight below the base (kN/m3), for Schmertmann's sigma'_vp at the depth of the peak strain influence factor (NHI-06-089 Fig. 8-21b). Required with immediate_method 'schmertmann'.
C_alphafloatoptionalSecondary compression index. Enables secondary settlement.
e0_secondaryfloatoptionalOne void ratio for the secondary settlement of every consolidation layer. Not given: each layer's own e0, layer by layer.
t_secondaryfloatoptionalTime for secondary settlement (years). default: 0.0
time_years_schmertmannfloatoptionalCreep time for Schmertmann immediate method (years). default: 0.0

10.1.3 axial_pile — Axial pile capacity

axial_pile_capacity — Full driven pile axial capacity analysis (Nordlund/Tomlinson/Beta).

ParameterTypeDescription
pile_typestrrequiredPile type. pipe_closed/pipe_open require diameter + wall_thickness; concrete_square/concrete_circular require width (side dimension OR diameter); h_pile requires designation; or a custom section (pile_area, pile_perimeter, pile_width, pile_tip_area) for any but pipe_open, timber always. allowed: pipe_closed, pipe_open, concrete_square, concrete_circular, h_pile, timber
diameterfloatoptionalPile diameter (m) for pipe piles.
wall_thicknessfloatoptionalPipe wall thickness (m).
widthfloatoptionalSide dimension (m) for concrete piles.
designationstroptionalH-pile designation (e.g., 'HP14x117').
pile_lengthfloatrequiredEmbedded pile length from the pile head to the tip (m).
layersarrayrequiredArray of soil-layer dicts (measured from the GROUND SURFACE): {thickness (m), soil_type, unit_weight (kN/m3), friction_angle (deg, for cohesionless), cohesion (kPa, for cohesive), toe_friction_angle (deg, OPTIONAL: separate end-bearing phi if the pile tip is in this layer; defaults to friction_angle), delta_phi_ratio (OPTIONAL Nordlund delta/phi; default from GEC-12 Fig. 7-9 by pile type and displaced volume), beta and Nt (OPTIONAL, beta method: the layer's beta and toe Nt from local experience, GEC-12 Steps 2a/5a), fig_7_18_case (OPTIONAL, a cohesive layer: 'sand_over_stiff_clay', 'soft_clay_over_stiff_clay', 'stiff_clay', 'none'; GEC-12 Fig. 7-18's case, which starts a clay stratum at the layer's top), soil_class (OPTIONAL: 'clay', 'silt', 'sand' or 'gravel', GEC-12 Table 7-9's soil type for beta_coefficients 'table_7_9'; default clay or sand), alpha or adhesion (OPTIONAL, a cohesive layer: a site-specific adhesion factor, or Ca in kPa, used in place of the chart's, e.g. adhesion = cohesion from site tests as in NHI-06-089 Example 9-3; give adhesion_basis, where it came from, with it), highly_overconsolidated (OPTIONAL, a cohesive layer: true or false, the engineer's call; where su is past the alpha method's chart, true takes API RP 2A's alpha and false holds Ca at the curve's end, winning over highly_overconsolidated_su_ratio for that layer)}. soil_type must be 'cohesionless' or 'cohesive' (NOT 'sand'/'clay').
gwt_depthfloatoptionalGroundwater depth below ground surface (m).
head_depthfloatoptionalDepth of the pile head below the ground surface (m), e.g. the bottom of a footing 1.5 m down. Layers above the head contribute no skin friction; overburden above the head still raises effective stress at the tip. Default 0 = head at the ground surface. default: 0.0
factor_of_safetyfloatoptionalFactor of safety for the allowable capacity. Default 2.5: FHWA NHI-06-089 Table 9-5 (indicator piles with wave equation analysis); 2.00 with a static load test, 2.25 with dynamic testing, 2.75 wave equation only, 3.50 Gates formula. GEC-12 itself designs by resistance factors: the result also gives the factored resistance (Table 7-1, Eq. 7-3). default: 2.5
methodstroptionalauto = by soil type: the Nordlund method in cohesionless soil (GEC-12 Sec. 7.2.1.3.1), the alpha method with Tomlinson's adhesion in cohesive soil (Sec. 7.2.1.3.2); beta = the beta (effective stress) method in every layer (Sec. 7.2.1.3.4). allowed: auto, beta default: "auto"
include_upliftbooloptionalAlso report uplift (tension) capacity. default: false
cohesive_phifloatoptionalFALLBACK drained phi' (deg) for cohesive layers under method='beta' (skin AND tip); a per-layer friction_angle on a cohesive layer wins over this global. default: 25.0
uplift_skin_fractionfloatoptionalFraction of the outside side resistance taken in uplift (with include_uplift). Default 1.0: GEC-12 Eq. 7-38 takes the whole shaft resistance and puts the uplift reduction in the resistance factor; 0.7 is the customary share in free-draining soils GEC-12 cites. default: 1.0
pile_weightfloatoptionalPile self-weight (kN) added to uplift capacity (with include_uplift).
toe_stress_limitfloatoptionalLimit on sigma'p at the toe for the Nordlund toe resistance (kPa). Default 143.6 kPa = 3 ksf, GEC-12 Step 8; null for no limit (GEC-12's worked example did not limit it). default: 143.640777
inside_friction_ratiofloatoptionalOpen-end pipe, unplugged case: interior over exterior unit side resistance. Default 1/3, the low end of GEC-12's 'typically on the order of 1/3 to 1/2' (Sec. 7.10.7). default: 0.3333333333333333
open_pipe_toe_limitfloatoptionalOpen-end pipe in cohesionless soil: limiting unit toe resistance (kPa). Default 5027 kPa = 105 ksf (Tomlinson, GEC-12 Sec. 7.10.7); null for none. default: 5027.427195
open_pipe_methodstroptionalOpen-end pipe: 'auto' takes Tomlinson's Eq. 7-90 for a pipe under 24 in with the toe in clay and over half its length in clay (GEC-12 Vol I p. 407), else the lesser of the plugged and unplugged cases (Eqs. 7-88/7-89, 'paikowsky_whitman'). allowed: auto, paikowsky_whitman, tomlinson default: "auto"
cohesive_Ntfloatoptionalmethod='beta': Nt of a cohesive toe layer. Default 3 (GEC-12: a relatively low Nt in clays unless local correlations suggest higher; Table 7-9 clay 3-30). A layer's own Nt wins. default: 3.0
h_pile_toe_areastroptionalH-pile toe area: 'box' (depth x flange width, GEC-12 Sec. 7.10.7) or 'steel'. GEC-12 Step 9 leaves it to past experience and local load tests. allowed: box, steel default: "box"
adhesion_curvestroptionalalpha-method: GEC-12 Fig. 7-17 curves. 'auto' = smooth steel for pipe piles, the concrete/timber/corrugated curve for H-piles (GEC-12 Vol I p. 247) and concrete or timber piles. allowed: auto, concrete_timber_corrugated, smooth_steel default: "auto"
adhesion_beyond_chartstroptionalalpha method where a clay layer's su is past the end of the chart's curves (Fig. 7-17, or 7-18 where read); GEC-12 Vol I p. 247 and alpha-method Step 1 recommend API RP 2A's alpha there for highly overconsolidated clays. 'api_if_highly_overconsolidated': API alpha in a layer whose su / sigma'vo is at or above highly_overconsolidated_su_ratio, Ca held at the curve's end below it; 'chart_end': Ca held at the curve's end in every such layer (GEC-12's worked example, Vol 3 Table D-100); 'api': API alpha in every such layer. Within the curves Ca is read off Fig. 7-17 as drawn (it can exceed su). allowed: api_if_highly_overconsolidated, chart_end, api default: "api_if_highly_overconsolidated"
highly_overconsolidated_su_ratiofloatoptionalalpha method: the su / sigma'vo at and above which a clay is highly overconsolidated, for adhesion_beyond_chart 'api_if_highly_overconsolidated'. GEC-12 gives no value; it is the engineer's judgment, so a run with a clay layer whose su is past the chart's curves is refused until this (or adhesion_beyond_chart 'chart_end' or 'api') is given. Ask the user, or state the value taken as a judgment call.
displaced_volumefloatoptionalNordlund displaced volume V per unit length (m3/m). Default: the steel area of an H-pile, the gross area of other piles (an open pipe as a closed pipe; its steel area, if it drives unplugged, is below GEC-12 Fig. 7-9).
pile_areafloatoptionalCustom section (m2): the cross-section area, the steel of an H-pile or a closed pipe, the gross area of a concrete or timber pile (it gives the Nordlund displaced volume of an H-pile and of a solid pile). With pile_perimeter and pile_width it replaces diameter, wall_thickness, width or designation; pile_type still picks the GEC-12 curves (not for pipe_open: its section comes from diameter and wall_thickness).
pile_perimeterfloatoptionalCustom section: the perimeter for the side resistance (m); the box perimeter of an H-pile (GEC-12 Steps 6 and Vol I p. 247).
pile_tip_areafloatoptionalCustom section: the toe area (m2). Required for h_pile (its box area; h_pile_toe_area 'steel' takes pile_area) and pipe_closed (the gross area); a concrete or timber pile's is its pile_area when not given.
pile_widthfloatoptionalCustom section: the width or diameter b (m), an H-pile's flange width; for D/b and the width notes.
pile_depthfloatoptionalCustom section: the section's depth (m), an H-pile's; reported only.
pile_namestroptionalCustom section: its name, e.g. 'HP16x101'.
adhesion_chartstroptionalalpha-method chart (GEC-12 Vol I p. 246): 'fig_7_17' (Tomlinson's Ca, recommended generally), 'fig_7_18' (Tomlinson's alpha for each clay layer's stratigraphy case: sand or sandy gravel over stiff clay, soft clay over stiff clay, stiff clay alone) or 'smaller' (the smaller Ca of the two in each layer, which p. 246 advises the inexperienced user to take). A layer's case is its fig_7_18_case, else from the profile: cohesive layers under a cohesionless layer the sand case, from the ground surface the stiff-clay case; the soft-clay case only where a layer gives it. Eq. 7-90 (open pipe) takes Ca from Fig. 7-17 whatever this is (p. 407). allowed: fig_7_17, fig_7_18, smaller default: "fig_7_17"
shrink_swell_depthfloatoptionalDepth (m below the ground surface) of a shrink-swell zone: no shaft resistance in cohesive soil above it (GEC-12 Vol I p. 247). Default none.
beta_coefficientsstroptionalmethod='beta': beta and Nt where a layer gives none: GEC-12 Table 7-9 by the layer's soil_class (clay 0.15-0.35, silt 0.25-0.50, sand 0.30-0.90, gravel 0.35-0.80; Steps 2b/5b), a straight line in phi' between Table 7-9's range ends (the module's reading; the table prints only the ends). A clay toe takes cohesive_Nt. GEC-12 prints no beta formula from phi' alone; give a layer's beta and Nt for other values (local experience, Steps 2a/5a). allowed: table_7_9 default: "table_7_9"
toe_phi_zonestroptionalNordlund toe: the phi near the toe. 'toe_layer' (the toe layer's toe_friction_angle or friction_angle) or 'average_3b' (averaged over the cohesionless soil from the toe to 3b below, GEC-12 Step 7c's zone). allowed: toe_layer, average_3b default: "toe_layer"

10.1.4 lateral_pile — Lateral pile analysis

lateral_pile_analysis — Full lateral pile analysis with p-y curves and FD solver.

ParameterTypeDescription
pile_typestroptionalPile type. h_pile requires designation; filled_pipe also requires pile_thickness. For a solid pile/drilled shaft, use 'pipe' with no pile_thickness and set pile_E. allowed: pipe, h_pile, filled_pipe default: "pipe"
pile_diameterfloatrequiredPile diameter (m).
pile_lengthfloatrequiredPile length (m).
pile_EfloatoptionalPile Young's modulus (kPa). DEFAULT IS STEEL (200e6) — for concrete drilled shafts set this explicitly, e.g. ~25e6 gross or a reduced value (e.g. 0.3x) for cracked sections. default: 200000000.0
pile_thicknessfloatoptionalWall thickness (m) for hollow pipe. Omit for a solid section.
moment_of_inertiafloatoptionalMoment of inertia (m4). Overrides the value computed from diameter/thickness.
designationstroptionalH-pile designation (e.g. 'HP360x132') — required for pile_type 'h_pile'.
axisstroptionalBending axis — pile_type 'h_pile' only. allowed: strong, weak default: "strong"
fcfloatoptionalConcrete f'c (kPa) — pile_type 'filled_pipe' only. default: 28000.0
layersarrayrequiredArray of {top, bottom, model, ...model params}. Required model params: SoftClayMatlock/StiffClayAboveWT {c, gamma, eps50}; StiffClayBelowWT {c, gamma, eps50} with ks for loading='static' or kc for 'cyclic' (kN/m3, the k of the initial line p = (k x) y; Reese, Cox & Koop, COM624P Table 3.2 / GEC 9 Table A-1: ks 135,700 / 271,400 / 542,900 and kc 54,300 / 108,600 / 217,200 for an average c to five diameters of 48-96 / 96-192 / 192-383 kPa); StiffClayBelowWT is Reese et al. (1975), stiff clay with free water: GEC 9 p. 219 keeps it for stiff clay exposed to free water at or near the ground surface, and with the groundwater at depth prefers StiffClayAboveWT (Welch & Reese) even below the water table, gamma then submerged; it does not say how near is near, so which of the two a stiff clay below the water table takes is the engineer's call: state it and why, or ask; SoftClayJeanjean {su, gamma, Gmax} (not checked against a print: neither Jeanjean 2009 nor API RP 2GEO is in the reference library; GEC 9's soft clay criterion is SoftClayMatlock); SandReese/SandAPI {phi, gamma, k} where k (kN/m3) is the k of the initial line p = (k z) y: for SandReese GEC 9 Table A-3 gives it by relative density only, loose / medium / dense 5,429 / 16,287 / 33,931 submerged and 6,786 / 24,430 / 61,076 above the water (20 / 60 / 125 and 25 / 90 / 225 lb/in3); for SandAPI API RP 2A Fig. 6.8.7-1 by phi', e.g. phi' 30 / 35 / 40: 9,260 / 22,260 / 42,510 below the water table and 12,650 / 36,970 / 75,270 above; WeakRock {qu, Er}. SandReese also takes optional construction='reese1974' (default: GEC 9 App. A.4's four-segment curve, linear -> parabola -> straight line -> p_u, A and B from Figs. A-10 and A-11) | 'simplified' (the module's own three-part curve, which no held page prints). StiffClayAboveWT with loading='cyclic' also needs n_cycles, N, the number of times the design lateral load is applied (>= 1; the references give no number to assume; Welch & Reese, COM624P Eq. 3.29, y_c = y_s + y50 C log N, so y50 times 1 + 0.6 log10 N). WeakRock (Reese 1997, FHWA GEC 9 App. A.5) also takes optional RQD (%, default 100: alpha_r = 1/3, the printed lower bound; alpha_r rises linearly to 1.0 at RQD 0), krm (default 0.0005, the softer end of 0.00005-0.0005) and rock_top (depth of the rock surface, m; default the top of the weak-rock layers that hold the layer); its gamma_r is accepted and not used (the criterion does not use the unit weight).
VtfloatoptionalLateral load at pile top (kN). default: 0.0
MtfloatoptionalMoment at pile top (kN-m). default: 0.0
head_conditionstroptionalPile head condition. allowed: free, fixed default: "free"
QfloatoptionalAxial load at pile top (kN), for P-delta. default: 0.0
stickupfloatoptionalAbove-ground free length (m): head loads/BCs act at the top of the stickup; no soil resistance over it. pile_length stays the EMBEDDED length. Alias: free_length. default: 0.0
n_elementsintoptionalFinite-difference elements along the pile. default: 100
tolerancefloatoptionalConvergence tolerance on deflection (m). default: 1e-05
max_iterationsintoptionalMost p-y iterations. If they run out, a push of the pile head decides: when the soil cannot resist the load the call fails with 'No solution: the soil cannot resist this load' and the most the pile and soil carry; otherwise the result says converged false with a message (raise max_iterations). default: 500

get_py_curve — Extract a single p-y curve at a given depth for any soil model.

ParameterTypeDescription
modelstrrequiredP-y model. Required params: clay models need {c, gamma, eps50} (StiffClayBelowWT also ks for static loading or kc for cyclic); sand models need {phi, gamma, k}; WeakRock needs {qu, Er}. allowed: SoftClayMatlock, StiffClayBelowWT, StiffClayAboveWT, SoftClayJeanjean, SandReese, SandAPI, WeakRock
zfloatoptionalDepth (m). default: 5.0
pile_diameterfloatoptionalPile diameter (m). default: 0.6
n_pointsintoptionalPoints on curve. default: 50
cfloatoptionalUndrained shear strength (kPa). For clay models.
gammafloatoptionalEffective unit weight (kN/m3).
eps50floatoptionalStrain at 50% deviator stress. For clay.
phifloatoptionalFriction angle (deg). For sand.
kfloatoptionalk of the initial line p = (k z) y (kN/m3). For sand: SandReese GEC 9 Table A-3 by relative density, SandAPI API RP 2A Fig. 6.8.7-1 by phi' (see lateral_pile_analysis layers).
constructionstroptionalSandReese curve construction. 'reese1974' (default): GEC 9 App. A.4's four-segment Reese (1974) curve, the initial line to y_k, a parabola to the m-point (p_m = B p_s at y_m = b/60), a straight line to the ultimate point (p_u = A p_s at y_u = 3b/80), then p_u; A and B from GEC 9 Figs. A-10 and A-11. 'simplified': the module's own curve, the initial line, a 1/3-power parabola through the ultimate point and API's A; no held page prints it. allowed: reese1974, simplified default: "reese1974"
qufloatoptionalUniaxial compressive strength of intact rock (kPa). For WeakRock.
ErfloatoptionalModulus of the rock mass E_m (kPa), e.g. from a pressuremeter or dilatometer test. For WeakRock.
loadingstroptionalLoading type. allowed: static, cyclic default: "static"
n_cyclesintoptionalN, the number of times the design lateral load is applied (>= 1). Required with loading='cyclic' for StiffClayAboveWT, and refused otherwise; the references give no number to assume. Welch & Reese, COM624P Eqs. 3.28-3.29 (GEC 9 A-20, A-21), y_c = y_s + y50 C log N with C = 9.6 (p/pu)^4, so the static curve with y50 times 1 + 0.6 log10 N.
ksfloatoptionalk for static loading (kN/m3), the initial line p = (k x) y of StiffClayBelowWT (Reese, Cox & Koop 1975): required with loading='static' and refused with 'cyclic'. COM624P Table 3.2 (GEC 9 Table A-1): 135,700 / 271,400 / 542,900 for an average c to five diameters of 48-96 / 96-192 / 192-383 kPa.
kcfloatoptionalk for cyclic loading (kN/m3), the initial line p = (k x) y of StiffClayBelowWT: required with loading='cyclic' and refused with 'static'. COM624P Table 3.2 (GEC 9 Table A-1): 54,300 / 108,600 / 217,200 for an average c to five diameters of 48-96 / 96-192 / 192-383 kPa.
sufloatoptionalUndrained shear strength (kPa). For SoftClayJeanjean (not checked against a print).
GmaxfloatoptionalSmall-strain shear modulus (kPa). For SoftClayJeanjean.
JfloatoptionalMatlock J factor. For SoftClayMatlock, StiffClayAboveWT, SoftClayJeanjean. default: 0.5
gamma_rfloatoptionalRock unit weight (kN/m3). Accepted for WeakRock but not used: the weak-rock criterion (Reese 1997, GEC 9 App. A.5) does not use the unit weight. default: 22.0
RQDfloatoptionalRock quality designation (%), 0-100. For WeakRock: strength reduction alpha_r = 1 - (2/3) RQD/100 (1/3 at RQD 100, 1.0 at RQD 0; GEC 9 p. 231). The default 100 gives the printed lower bound alpha_r = 1/3. default: 100.0
krmfloatoptionalk_rm, strain at 50% of the ultimate, 0.00005-0.0005 (GEC 9 p. 232); the lower value is stiffer. For WeakRock; default 0.0005, the softer end. default: 0.0005
rock_topfloatoptionalDepth of the rock surface below the ground (m). For WeakRock: z_r = z - rock_top is the depth below the rock surface its p_ur and K_ir use. default: 0.0

composite_section_ei — Uncracked transformed-section composite EI/EA for a multi-material pile section (concrete-filled steel pipe, cased grout + optional bar ring, or reinforced concrete). Feed the returned EI/inertia into lateral_pile_analysis via moment_of_inertia (at pile_E = E_ref).

ParameterTypeDescription
section_typestrrequiredfilled_pipe = concrete/grout-filled steel pipe (needs outer_diameter, wall_thickness). cased_concrete = steel casing + grout core + optional circular bar ring. reinforced_concrete = circular (diameter) or rectangular (width, height) RC, no outer steel. allowed: filled_pipe, cased_concrete, reinforced_concrete
fcfloatoptionalConcrete/grout compressive strength f'c (kPa). Ec = 4700*sqrt(f'c[MPa]) (ACI 318). Provide fc OR E_concrete.
E_concretefloatoptionalConcrete/grout Young's modulus (kPa), used directly instead of the fc correlation.
outer_diameterfloatoptionalSteel pipe/casing outer diameter (m) — filled_pipe / cased_concrete.
wall_thicknessfloatoptionalSteel pipe/casing wall thickness (m) — filled_pipe / cased_concrete.
E_steelfloatoptionalSteel casing modulus (kPa). default: 200000000.0
diameterfloatoptionalConcrete diameter (m) — circular reinforced_concrete.
widthfloatoptionalRectangular concrete breadth (m). Bending about the axis parallel to width (I = width*height^3/12).
heightfloatoptionalRectangular concrete depth (m).
n_barsintoptionalNumber of bars in the circular ring (cased_concrete / circular reinforced_concrete); refused on a filled_pipe (use cased_concrete) and on a rectangular section (use bar_layers). default: 0
bar_diameterfloatoptionalIndividual reinforcing-bar diameter (m); required with n_bars or bar_layers. Use a standard size, e.g. 0.0254 for a #8 bar. default: 0.0
bar_circle_diameterfloatoptionalPitch-circle diameter of the bar ring (m) — circular reinforcement.
bar_layersarrayoptionalRectangular reinforcement: array of [n_bars, y_from_centroid_m] layers (y signed; symmetric layers keep the neutral axis centred). Requires bar_diameter.
E_barfloatoptionalReinforcing-steel modulus (kPa). default: 200000000.0

10.1.5 pile_group — Pile groups

pile_group_simple — Simplified elastic vertical group analysis.

n_rowsintoptionalRows for rectangular layout.
n_colsintoptionalColumns for rectangular layout.
spacing_xfloatoptionalX spacing (m). Or give a single 'spacing' for both directions.
spacing_yfloatoptionalY spacing (m). Or give a single 'spacing' for both directions.
spacingfloatoptionalUniform center-to-center spacing (m), used for both x and y.

MxfloatoptionalMoment about x (kN-m). default: 0.0
MyfloatoptionalMoment about y (kN-m). default: 0.0
axial_capacity_compressionfloatoptionalPer-pile compression capacity (kN) for utilization checks (rectangular layout).
axial_capacity_tensionfloatoptionalPer-pile tension capacity (kN) (rectangular layout).

pile_group_6dof — General 6-DOF rigid cap analysis (axial + lateral + moments).

ParameterTypeDescription
n_rowsintoptionalRows for rectangular layout.
n_colsintoptionalColumns.
spacing_xfloatoptionalX spacing (m). Or give a single 'spacing' for both directions.
spacing_yfloatoptionalY spacing (m). Or give a single 'spacing' for both directions.
spacingfloatoptionalUniform center-to-center spacing (m), used for both x and y.
pilesarrayoptionalExplicit pile list [{x, y, batter_x, batter_y, axial_stiffness, lateral_stiffness, label}] instead of n_rows/n_cols.
axial_stiffnessfloatrequiredPile-head axial stiffness ka (kN/m), e.g. from a load test or E*A/L for an end-bearing pile. REQUIRED for every pile: give it here with n_rows/n_cols, or on each piles[] entry.
lateral_stiffnessfloatoptionalPile-head lateral stiffness kl (kN/m), here with n_rows/n_cols or on each piles[] entry. Needed for vertical piles to carry Vx/Vy (0 if omitted).

VyfloatoptionalLateral load y (kN). default: 0.0

MyfloatoptionalMoment about y (kN-m). default: 0.0
MzfloatoptionalTorsion about z (kN-m). default: 0.0
