axial_capacity_tensionfloatoptionalPer-pile tension capacity (kN) (rectangular layout).

group_efficiency — Pile group axial and lateral group effects as GEC-12 and UFC 3-220-20 print them: the group efficiency factor eta_g, block failure, the row p-multiplier.

ParameterTypeDescription
n_rowsintoptionalNumber of rows (for block failure).
n_colsintoptionalNumber of columns (for block failure).
pile_diameterfloatoptionalPile diameter or width b (m).
spacingfloatoptionalCentre-to-centre pile spacing (m), both directions.
spacing_xfloatoptionalX spacing (m), if it differs from spacing. eta_g takes the smaller of x and y.
spacing_yfloatoptionalY spacing (m), if it differs from spacing.
soil_typestroptionalGives the group efficiency factor eta_g: 'cohesionless' (UFC's coarse-grained) or 'cohesive' (fine-grained), the stratum giving most of the resistance (GEC-12 Vol I p. 281). Driven piles, GEC-12 Secs. 7.2.2.1-7.2.2.2 (Vol I pp. 282, 284): cohesionless not underlain by a weak deposit, 1.0; clay with su < 2 ksf and the cap not in firm contact with the ground, 0.65 at s = 2.5b to 1.0 at 6b, linear between; else 1.0. Other pile types: UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-26 (see pile_type). Below the table's minimum spacing (2.5b driven piles and drilled shafts, 3b the others) the call is refused. The group resistance is the lesser of n*eta_g*R_n and block failure. allowed: cohesionless, cohesive
cap_in_contactbooloptionalWhether the pile cap is in firm contact with the ground (sets eta_g's row). Left out where the row depends on it, the lower eta_g (not in contact) is taken and the result's choices give the other.
cufloatoptionalUndrained shear strength of the clay (kPa): sets eta_g's row against 2 ksf (95.76 kPa) for soil_type 'cohesive' (left out where it matters, su < 2 ksf is taken, said in the choices); and, for block failure, su1 and su2 where those are not given.
pile_typestroptionalThe column of UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-26 for eta_g: 'driven' (GEC-12), 'drilled_shaft', 'cfa', 'ddp' (drilled displacement) or 'micropile'; and the resistance factor for block failure: 0.60 driven (GEC-12 Table 7-1, Vol I p. 224), 0.55 drilled shafts, 0.60 micropiles (UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-27, p. 433); none printed for 'cfa' or 'ddp' (nominal only). allowed: driven, drilled_shaft, cfa, ddp, micropile default: "driven"
pile_lengthfloatoptionalPile embedded length D (m). With su1 and su2 (or cu), n_rows, n_cols, spacing and pile_diameter, gives the resistance to block failure: GEC-12 Eq. 7-36, R = 2D(B+Z)su1 + B*Z*su2*Nc, Nc = 5[1 + D/(5B)][1 + B/(5Z)] <= 9 (Eq. 7-37), B and Z the group's width and length to the outer pile faces (Fig. 7-31). Nominal, and factored by pile_type's printed resistance factor (block_failure_factored_kN).
su1floatoptionalBlock failure: weighted average undrained shear strength along the group's perimeter over the embedded length (kPa); for cohesionless soils along the sides, their weighted average unit shaft resistance (GEC-12 Vol I p. 287).
su2floatoptionalBlock failure: average undrained shear strength below the toes to a depth of 2B (kPa; UFC 3-220-20 p. 433: 2B to 3B, whichever lower), that of the weak layer for a group in sand over it.
row_positionintoptionalRow number, 1 = the lead row (UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 6-25): gives the row's lateral p-multiplier p_m.
spacing_diameter_ratiofloatoptionals/b for the p-multiplier, s the spacing of the rows in the direction of the load (from spacing/pile_diameter if omitted). Below 3 the call is refused (p_m is printed from 3b).
p_multiplier_methodstroptional'aashto' (default): AASHTO's p_m as GEC-12 prints it (Vol I pp. 367, 370): rows 1, 2, 3+ = 0.8, 0.4, 0.3 at 3b and 1.0, 0.85, 0.7 at 5b, interpolated (0.90, 0.625, 0.5 at 4b, as GEC-12 Vol. III takes them), to 1.0 at 6b and beyond (UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-38). 'mokwa': Mokwa (1999), UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-38: p_m = 0.06(s/b)+0.64, 0.11(s/b)+0.34, 0.14(s/b)+0.16, 0.16(s/b)+0.04 for rows 1, 2, 3, 4+, each <= 1. allowed: aashto, mokwa default: "aashto"

group_uplift — Uplift resistance of a pile group in net tension, or of the piles in tension of a group (GEC-12 Vol. III checks the back row in tension of an abutment group in compression), as GEC-12 Sec. 7.2.3.2 and UFC 3-220-20 Eqs. 6-40 to 6-43 print it: the lesser of the sum of the piles' factored tension resistances and the group's as a block (cohesionless soil: the effective weight of the soil within sides at 1H:4V from the toes; cohesive soil: the block's weight plus 2D(B+Z)su on its sides), factored by phi_ug.

ParameterTypeDescription
n_rowsintrequiredRows of the group, or of the piles in tension (1 for one row, as GEC-12 Vol. III checks a back row in tension).
n_colsintrequiredColumns.
spacingfloatoptionalCentre-to-centre pile spacing (m), both directions.
spacing_xfloatoptionalX spacing (m), if it differs from spacing.
spacing_yfloatoptionalY spacing (m), if it differs from spacing.
pile_diameterfloatrequiredPile diameter or width b (m): the block's width and length at the toes are to the outer faces of the outer piles, (n - 1)s + b.
pile_lengthfloatrequiredPile embedded length D (m), the block's height.
soil_typestrrequired'cohesionless': the block is the soil within sides at 1H:4V from the toes up (GEC-12 Fig. 7-33; UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 6-41), its effective weight. 'cohesive': the block is B x Z x D, its effective weight plus the undrained shear on its sides, 2D(B+Z)su (GEC-12 Eq. 7-41; UFC 3-220-20 Eqs. 6-42, 6-43). The piles are taken as soil. allowed: cohesionless, cohesive
unit_weightfloatoptionalThe soil's effective unit weight (kN/m3; below the water table the buoyant) over the embedded length. Or give layers.
layersarrayoptionalThe soil from the top of the block down, [{thickness (m), unit_weight (effective, kN/m3)}, ...], to the toes at least, in place of one unit_weight (e.g. the water table inside the block). In cohesionless soil each layer's volume is taken between its bottom and top plan dimensions (UFC 3-220-20 p. 436; GEC-12 Vol. III Eq. D-1).
cufloatoptionalsoil_type 'cohesive': the weighted average undrained shear strength over the embedded length along the group's perimeter (kPa), GEC-12 Eq. 7-41's su.
cap_weightfloatoptionalThe pile cap's effective weight over the block (kN), part of the block (GEC-12 Eq. 7-41's W_g 'including pile cap weight'; UFC 3-220-20 p. 435); for the piles in tension of a group, the cap over them (GEC-12 Vol. III p. 207 takes the tributary area over the back row in tension). Leave it out (0, the safe side) where the uplift load already carries it. default: 0.0
pile_typestroptionalThe block's resistance factor phi_ug: 0.50 driven (GEC-12 Table 7-1, Vol I p. 224), 0.45 drilled shafts, 0.50 micropiles (UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-28, p. 434); none printed for 'cfa' or 'ddp' (nominal only). Reduced by 20 % for a small group: fewer than 3 driven piles (GEC-12 Vol I p. 225), fewer than 5 of the others (UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-28 note A). allowed: driven, drilled_shaft, cfa, ddp, micropile default: "driven"
axial_capacity_tensionfloatoptionalOne pile's factored tension resistance phi_up R_s (kN; GEC-12 Eq. 7-38, phi_up from Table 7-1 by the static method, 0.60 with a static load test or 0.50 dynamic testing with signal matching, Table 7-2; for a small group reduced by 20 %, GEC-12 Vol I p. 225). With it, the piles' sum n phi_up R_s (Eq. 7-40) and the governing resistance, the lesser.
uplift_loadfloatoptionalThe factored uplift on the piles in the block (kN, positive): the net uplift on a group in tension, or the summed tension of the piles in tension; for the utilization, the load over the governing resistance.
piles_under_capintoptionalThe piles under the cap when the block is part of the group (the piles in tension), for the small-group rule, which counts the piles per substructure unit (GEC-12 Vol I p. 225). At least n_rows x n_cols.

meyerhof_group_settlement — Meyerhof (1976) SPT pile-group settlement in sand, GEC-12 Eqs. 7-50 to 7-52: S[in] = 4·pf[ksf]·If·√B[ft]/N1(60) (8 for silty sand). SI in, mm out.

ParameterTypeDescription
group_widthfloatrequiredGroup plan width B, the SMALLER plan dimension (m).
group_lengthfloatrequiredGroup plan length Z, the larger plan dimension (m). Used with group_width to form the plan area when load_kN is given.
N160floatrequiredAverage corrected SPT N1(60) within a depth B below the pile toe (dimensionless).
load_kNfloatoptionalTotal unfactored permanent load Q (kN); pf = Q/(B·Z), B and Z to the outer pile faces (GEC-12 Vol. III p. 62). Provide this OR pf_kPa.
pf_kPafloatoptionalDesign foundation pressure pf (kPa), supplied directly. Takes precedence over load_kN. Provide this OR load_kN.
embedment_DBfloatoptionalThe embedment D whose 2/3 is D' in If = 1 − D'/(8B) >= 0.5 (Eq. 7-52), m. GEC-12 Vol. I p. 319 and UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 6-47 take the pile embedded length; GEC-12 Vol. III Table D-23 the embedment into the bearing stratum. Default 0.0 (If = 1.0, the upper bound). default: 0.0
silty_sandbooloptionalTrue: Eq. 7-51 for silty sand (coefficient 8, twice Eq. 7-50's). default: false

10.1.6 drilled_shaft — Drilled shafts

drilled_shaft_capacity — Full drilled shaft capacity (GEC-10 alpha/beta/rock socket).

ParameterTypeDescription
diameterfloatrequiredShaft diameter (m).
shaft_lengthfloatrequiredShaft length (m). Alias: length.
layersarrayrequiredArray of {thickness, soil_type, unit_weight, cu, phi, N60, qu, RQD} dicts. soil_type: cohesive/cohesionless/rock. A cohesionless layer at the shaft tip needs its N60 (end bearing q_b = 57.5*N60 kPa, GEC-10 Eq. 10-14, N60 the mean of the cohesionless layers' N60 between the base and two base diameters below it, by thickness, limited to 50, p. 10-15; a layer there with no N60, or of cohesive soil or rock, is left out); without it the call is refused. Under beta_method 'rational' (the default, GEC-10 2018 Eq. 10-13) each cohesionless layer the shaft passes through needs its N60 (sigma'p by Eq. 10-11 or 10-12) or a direct OCR, else the call is refused; it also takes N1_60 (overburden-corrected SPT; phi' = 27.5+9.2*log10[(N1)60], GEC-10 Example 10-1 and Eq. A-2, where the layer gives no phi; a phi given is used and the result's choices give the correlation's value beside it), sigma_p_correlation ('clean_sand' default: Eq. 10-11 with m = 0.6, clean quartzitic sands; 'silty_sand': m = 0.8, silty sands to sandy silts; 'gravel': Eq. 10-12, sigma'p/pa = 0.15*N60, gravelly soils; GEC-10 p. 10-11) and sigma_v_ref (kPa, pre-scour effective stress for the OCR; default the layer's own sigma'v); under beta_method 'depth' the depth beta uses neither N1_60 nor OCR: they enter only the result's beta_method 'rational' alternative (choices). A rock layer's RQD (default 100) sets alpha_E of the side resistance under rock_side_method 'caving' (GEC-10 Table 10-3) and the base under rock_base_method 'rqd'; under the default 'gec10' an RQD below 100 within one base diameter below the base needs rock_base_conditions_met, or the tip rock layer's GSI and m_i. A rock layer also takes GSI (Geological Strength Index of the rock mass, 0 to 100, from the core descriptions; GEC-10 p. 10-23 names GSI, not RMR) and m_i (Hoek-Brown constant of the intact rock, by rock type, GEC 5 Table 9-10, as GEC-10 p. 10-24 points to): with the base in that layer they give GEC-10's base for a fractured rock mass, the Hoek-Brown base, Eqs. 10-24 to 10-29, taken where the rock is not taken to meet the conditions of Eq. 10-23 and shown beside 2.5*qu where it is (see rock_base_conditions_met); a rock layer within one base diameter below the base that gives them has its own Hoek-Brown base among the result's alternatives. GSI or m_i on any other layer (above the base, further below it, or with the base in soil) is refused: nothing would use them; capacity_vs_depth takes them on any layer a trial base is in.
gwt_depthfloatoptionalGroundwater depth (m).
factor_of_safetyfloatoptionalFactor of safety. default: 2.5
beta_methodstroptionalCohesionless side resistance. 'rational' (default) = GEC-10 (2018) Sec. 10.3.5.1, Eqs. 10-5 to 10-13 (pp. 10-10 to 10-12): f_SN = beta*sigma'v on each layer's average sigma'v, beta = (K/Ko)*Ko*tan(phi'), Ko = (1-sin phi')*OCR^(sin phi') <= Kp, OCR = sigma'p/sigma'v, sigma'p from the layer's N60 (Eq. 10-11 or 10-12), beta limited to its value at 7.5 ft, no limit on f_SN; needs each cohesionless layer's N60 or OCR. 'depth' = O'Neill & Reese (1999) beta = 1.5-0.135*sqrt(z, ft) = 1.5-0.245*sqrt(z, m), 0.25-1.2, x N60/15 where N60 < 15, f_s <= 4 ksf = 191.5 kPa (FHWA NHI-06-089 Eqs. 9-41 to 9-43, the limit p. 9-133), which GEC-10 (2018) does not print. allowed: rational, depth default: "rational"
K_over_KofloatoptionalK/Ko in the GEC-10 beta (beta_method 'rational'): 1 = 'a rational first-order approximation', no stress change from construction (GEC-10 p. 10-11); 2/3 or lower 'when these aspects of construction quality are not controlled properly' or soil caving is allowed (p. 10-12). 0 < K_over_Ko <= 1. default: 1.0
top_exclusionfloatoptionalSide resistance left out over the top of the shaft (m), in every layer, when given. Left out: none over the top 1.5 m in cohesive soil, GEC-10's 'top 5 ft' (p. 10-17, printed in Sec. 10.3.5.2 for cohesive soils, 'or to the depth of seasonal moisture change', 'subject to modification based on local experience and judgment of the designer'), and side resistance from the top in cohesionless soil and rock (Secs. 10.3.5.1 and 10.3.5.3 print no such zone; Examples 10-1 and 10-5 take the sand's from the surface, Example 10-4 the socket's over its whole length). Give 1.5 to leave the top 5 ft out of sand and rock too (frost, seasonal moisture, gapping from cyclic lateral load), or the depth of seasonal moisture change. casing_depth, where deeper, takes its place.
bottom_exclusionfloatoptionalSide resistance left out over the bottom of the shaft (m) in cohesive soil. Default 0: GEC-10 (2018) prints no such zone, and Example 10-2 (p. 10-18) takes the clay's side resistance to the base. FHWA NHI-06-089 p. 9-129 (O'Neill & Reese 1999) leaves out the bottom 5 ft (1.524 m), its Fig. 9-49 the bottom one diameter (give the diameter for that). default: 0.0
alpha_methodstroptionalCohesive side resistance. 'rational' (default) = GEC-10 (2018) Sec. 10.3.5.2, Eq. 10-18 (p. 10-16): alpha = 0.30+0.17/(su(CIUC)/pa), f_SN = alpha*su(CIUC), su(CIUC) from cu by su_test_type. 'aashto' = O'Neill & Reese (1999) as FHWA NHI-06-089 Eqs. 9-37a/b print it (p. 9-129): alpha = 0.55 for cu/pa <= 1.5, 0.55-0.1*(cu/pa-1.5) to 2.5, on cu; GEC-10 recommends Eq. 10-18 'as a revision' to it. allowed: rational, aashto default: "rational"
su_test_typestroptionalFor alpha_method 'rational': the lab test each layer's cu came from. 'ciuc' (default) = cu taken as su(CIUC), no transform; 'uc' / 'uu' = transformed to su(CIUC) on the layer's sigma'vo by GEC-10 Eq. 10-16 / 10-17 (Chen & Kulhawy 1993, p. 10-16; Example 10-2 takes a UU strength). The base in clay takes the same su(CIUC) (Example 10-3). allowed: ciuc, uc, uu default: "ciuc"
clay_base_methodstroptionalBase resistance with the tip in cohesive soil. 'gec10' (default) = GEC-10 (2018) p. 10-19: q_BN = N*c*su (Eq. 10-19), su the mean of the cohesive soil over 2B below the base, by thickness (p. 10-19; the tip layer at its su(CIUC) as its side resistance took it, each clay layer below on its own cu, transformed alike; cohesionless or rock layers within 2B left out; where the profile ends short of 2B, the mean of what it gives, said in the choices), N*c from Table 10-2 by su (6.5 at 500 psf, 8.0 at 1,000 psf, 9.0 at 2,000 psf or more; held at 6.5 below 500 psf), (2/3)[1 + D/(6B)]*N*c*su where the depth D < 3B (Eq. 10-20), no upper limit. 'oneill_reese' = FHWA NHI-06-089 Eqs. 9-39, 9-40 (p. 9-131): Nc = 6[1 + 0.2 z/D] <= 9, x 0.67 where su < 0.5 ksf, q_t <= 80 ksf, on the tip layer's cu. allowed: gec10, oneill_reese default: "gec10"
rock_base_methodstroptionalBase resistance with the tip in rock. 'gec10' (default) = GEC-10 (2018) Eq. 10-23 (p. 10-22): q_BN = 2.5*qu, for rock massive or tightly jointed to one diameter below the base, no cavities beneath, a clean base (Example 10-4 takes it with RQD 37 to 100); for a fractured rock mass the Hoek-Brown base, Eqs. 10-24 to 10-29 (pp. 10-23, 10-24; Turner and Ramey 2010): m_b = m_i*exp((GSI-100)/28), s = exp((GSI-100)/9), a = 1/2+(1/6)(exp(-GSI/15)-exp(-20/3)), A = sigma'vb + qu*(m_b*sigma'vb/qu + s)^a, q_BN = A + qu*(m_b*A/qu + s)^a, q_BN/qu limited to 2.5 (p. 10-24), on the tip rock layer's qu, GSI and m_i and the vertical effective stress at the base; resistance factor 0.50 (p. 10-24, Table 8-4); which of the two by rock_base_conditions_met. 'rqd' = q_b/q_u reduced by the tip rock's RQD below 70 (1.5 at 50, 0.8 at 25, 0.4 at 0), cited to GEC-10's 2010 edition, not in the reference library, and not a method GEC-10 Table 8-4 gives a resistance factor for. allowed: gec10, rqd default: "gec10"
rock_base_conditions_metbooloptionalFor rock_base_method 'gec10' with the tip in rock: whether the rock below the base meets the three conditions GEC-10 p. 10-22 sets on q_BN = 2.5*qu (massive or tightly jointed, no compressible seams or joints, to at least one diameter below the base; no solution cavities or voids beneath it; a clean base achieved and verified). The engineer's judgment: Example 10-4 takes 2.5 with RQD 37 to 100 because 'Rock coring and local experience indicate the rock mass below the socket tip is competent'. true = 2.5*qu (Eq. 10-23) as stated. false = GEC-10's base for a fractured rock mass, the Hoek-Brown base (Eqs. 10-24 to 10-29), on the tip rock layer's GSI and m_i; refused, naming them, where that layer does not give them. Left out = taken as met, said in the result's choices, where every layer within one base diameter below the base is rock with RQD 100 (the layer default), with the Hoek-Brown base on the tip rock layer's GSI and m_i beside it where they are given; where a layer there has an RQD below 100 or is soil, the Hoek-Brown base on the tip rock layer's GSI and m_i (2.5*qu bounds it above), and the call is refused, naming them, where that layer does not give them.
large_base_reductionbooloptionalO'Neill & Reese's (1999) reduction of base resistance for a large base: 1.27/B in cohesionless soil for a base wider than 1.27 m, F_r = 2.5/(a*B + 2.5*b) <= 1 in cohesive soil for a base wider than 1.90 m (B the bell's where there is one). Default false: GEC-10 (2018) prints neither (Eqs. 10-14, 10-19, 10-20); true applies it. default: false
pafloatoptionalAtmospheric pressure (kPa) for the rational chains. default: 101.325
rock_side_CfloatoptionalC in the rock side resistance f_s = C*pa*sqrt(qu/pa) (GEC-10 Eq. 10-21, p. 10-20). Default 1.0, 'recommended for design of "normal" rock sockets' (pp. 10-20, 10-21; Example 10-4): conventional equipment, nominally clean sidewalls, no caving, no smearing. 0.65 = the value of Eq. 10-22 with alpha_E = 1.0 (rock_side_method 'caving' takes alpha_E from Table 10-3 by RQD). 1.9 for roughened sockets, verified by load tests or local experience (p. 10-22). For rock_side_method 'normal'; refused with 'caving', which takes no C. Needs a rock layer. default: 1.0
rock_side_methodstroptionalRock side resistance. 'normal' (default) = GEC-10 Eq. 10-21, f_s = C*pa*sqrt(qu/pa) with rock_side_C, for a 'normal' socket: conventional equipment, nominally clean sidewalls (pp. 10-20, 10-21). 'caving' = Eq. 10-22 (O'Neill and Reese 1999), f_s = 0.65*alpha_E*pa*sqrt(qu/pa), alpha_E from Table 10-3 (p. 10-21) by each rock layer's RQD and rock_joints (closed joints 1.00, 0.85, 0.60, 0.50, 0.45; open or gouge-filled 0.85, 0.55, 0.55, 0.50, 0.45 at RQD 100, 70, 50, 30, 20 %; linear between the rows, held at 0.45 below RQD 20), for highly fractured or weathered rock that cannot be drilled without artificial support (casing, plug-ahead) or where caving is anticipated. Needs a rock layer. allowed: normal, caving default: "normal"
rock_jointsstroptionalFor rock_side_method 'caving': the joint condition of GEC-10 Table 10-3, 'closed' (default) or 'open' (open or gouge-filled joints), from the cores. allowed: closed, open default: "closed"
socket_diameterfloatoptionalRock socket diameter (m). Defaults to shaft diameter. One diameter for every rock layer: GEC-10 sizes a socket by one diameter B (Eq. 10-3, p. 10-9; Example 10-4) and gives none per rock layer. The rock side resistance and, with the tip in rock, the base (pi/4*B^2, GEC-10 Example 10-4, p. 10-28) take it.
bell_diameterfloatoptionalBelled base diameter (m).
casing_depthfloatoptionalPermanent casing depth (m, no side resistance). default: 0.0
fractured_rock_thicknessfloatoptionalDecomposed or fractured rock (m) below the top of the first rock layer that is 'not considered part of the socket for design purposes' (GEC-10 p. 8-15): no rock side resistance over it, while the soil above keeps its own (casing_depth takes both). 0 = all rock is socket. Needs a rock layer. default: 0.0
concrete_fcfloatoptionalCompressive strength f'c of the shaft concrete (kPa; 28 MPa = 28000, at least 1000). The rock side resistance takes qu no higher than it: 'For design, the value of qu used in Equation 10-21 should not exceed the compressive strength of the drilled shaft concrete' (GEC-10 p. 10-21; Example 10-4 gives qu 360 ksf and f'c 576 ksf), in Eq. 10-22 alike. With the base in rock it also checks the base against the concrete's own bearing (GEC-10 p. 10-25): Eq. 12-7 (p. 12-8), 0.70*[0.85*f'c*A1*m], the tip taken as plain concrete as Example 10-4 does (with the cage to the tip p. 12-8 prints Eq. 12-6 at phi 0.70, not computed: the tool takes no f_y), A1 the socket's cross-sectional area, m = 2.0 (printed for a socket on competent rock), against the geotechnical 0.50*Q_tip (Example 10-4 p. 10-28 makes this check), in base_steps.concrete_bearing and the choices; lrfd_capacity takes the factored base as the smaller of the two. Q_tip, Q_ultimate and Q_allowable stay the geotechnical ones. Left out, neither limit is checked and the result's choices say so. No other structural check of the shaft is made. Needs a rock layer.

capacity_vs_depth — Capacity vs depth curve for length optimization.

ParameterTypeDescription
diameterfloatrequiredShaft diameter (m).
shaft_lengthfloatrequiredMaximum shaft length (m); upper bound of the depth sweep. Alias: length.
layersarrayrequiredArray of {thickness, soil_type, unit_weight, cu, phi, N60, qu, RQD} dicts. soil_type: cohesive/cohesionless/rock. A cohesionless layer at the shaft tip needs its N60 (end bearing q_b = 57.5*N60 kPa, GEC-10 Eq. 10-14, N60 the mean of the cohesionless layers' N60 between the base and two base diameters below it, by thickness, limited to 50, p. 10-15; a layer there with no N60, or of cohesive soil or rock, is left out); without it the call is refused. Under beta_method 'rational' (the default, GEC-10 2018 Eq. 10-13) each cohesionless layer the shaft passes through needs its N60 (sigma'p by Eq. 10-11 or 10-12) or a direct OCR, else the call is refused; it also takes N1_60 (overburden-corrected SPT; phi' = 27.5+9.2*log10[(N1)60], GEC-10 Example 10-1 and Eq. A-2, where the layer gives no phi; a phi given is used and the result's choices give the correlation's value beside it), sigma_p_correlation ('clean_sand' default: Eq. 10-11 with m = 0.6, clean quartzitic sands; 'silty_sand': m = 0.8, silty sands to sandy silts; 'gravel': Eq. 10-12, sigma'p/pa = 0.15*N60, gravelly soils; GEC-10 p. 10-11) and sigma_v_ref (kPa, pre-scour effective stress for the OCR; default the layer's own sigma'v); under beta_method 'depth' the depth beta uses neither N1_60 nor OCR: they enter only the result's beta_method 'rational' alternative (choices). A rock layer's RQD (default 100) sets alpha_E of the side resistance under rock_side_method 'caving' (GEC-10 Table 10-3) and the base under rock_base_method 'rqd'; under the default 'gec10' an RQD below 100 within one base diameter below the base needs rock_base_conditions_met, or the tip rock layer's GSI and m_i. A rock layer also takes GSI (Geological Strength Index of the rock mass, 0 to 100, from the core descriptions; GEC-10 p. 10-23 names GSI, not RMR) and m_i (Hoek-Brown constant of the intact rock, by rock type, GEC 5 Table 9-10, as GEC-10 p. 10-24 points to): with the base in that layer they give GEC-10's base for a fractured rock mass, the Hoek-Brown base, Eqs. 10-24 to 10-29, taken where the rock is not taken to meet the conditions of Eq. 10-23 and shown beside 2.5*qu where it is (see rock_base_conditions_met); a rock layer within one base diameter below the base that gives them has its own Hoek-Brown base among the result's alternatives. GSI or m_i on any other layer (above the base, further below it, or with the base in soil) is refused: nothing would use them; capacity_vs_depth takes them on any layer a trial base is in.
gwt_depthfloatoptionalGroundwater depth (m).
factor_of_safetyfloatoptionalFactor of safety. default: 2.5
beta_methodstroptionalCohesionless side resistance. 'rational' (default) = GEC-10 (2018) Sec. 10.3.5.1, Eqs. 10-5 to 10-13 (pp. 10-10 to 10-12): f_SN = beta*sigma'v on each layer's average sigma'v, beta = (K/Ko)*Ko*tan(phi'), Ko = (1-sin phi')*OCR^(sin phi') <= Kp, OCR = sigma'p/sigma'v, sigma'p from the layer's N60 (Eq. 10-11 or 10-12), beta limited to its value at 7.5 ft, no limit on f_SN; needs each cohesionless layer's N60 or OCR. 'depth' = O'Neill & Reese (1999) beta = 1.5-0.135*sqrt(z, ft) = 1.5-0.245*sqrt(z, m), 0.25-1.2, x N60/15 where N60 < 15, f_s <= 4 ksf = 191.5 kPa (FHWA NHI-06-089 Eqs. 9-41 to 9-43, the limit p. 9-133), which GEC-10 (2018) does not print. allowed: rational, depth default: "rational"
K_over_KofloatoptionalK/Ko in the GEC-10 beta (beta_method 'rational'): 1 = 'a rational first-order approximation', no stress change from construction (GEC-10 p. 10-11); 2/3 or lower 'when these aspects of construction quality are not controlled properly' or soil caving is allowed (p. 10-12). 0 < K_over_Ko <= 1. default: 1.0

Give 1.5 to leave the top 5 ft out of sand and rock too (frost, seasonal moisture, gapping from cyclic lateral load), or the depth of seasonal moisture change. casing_depth, where deeper, takes its place.

gwt_depthfloatoptionalGroundwater depth (m).
tip_soil_typestroptionalSoil type at the shaft tip, for the base resistance factor (GEC-10 Table 8-4: 0.40 cohesive, 0.50 cohesionless and rock). Left out, the soil of the layer the base is in; given, it must be that soil, else the call is refused. allowed: cohesive, cohesionless, rock
beta_methodstroptionalCohesionless side resistance. 'rational' (default) = GEC-10 (2018) Sec. 10.3.5.1, Eqs. 10-5 to 10-13 (pp. 10-10 to 10-12): f_SN = beta*sigma'v on each layer's average sigma'v, beta = (K/Ko)*Ko*tan(phi'), Ko = (1-sin phi')*OCR^(sin phi') <= Kp, OCR = sigma'p/sigma'v, sigma'p from the layer's N60 (Eq. 10-11 or 10-12), beta limited to its value at 7.5 ft, no limit on f_SN; needs each cohesionless layer's N60 or OCR. 'depth' = O'Neill & Reese (1999) beta = 1.5-0.135*sqrt(z, ft) = 1.5-0.245*sqrt(z, m), 0.25-1.2, x N60/15 where N60 < 15, f_s <= 4 ksf = 191.5 kPa (FHWA NHI-06-089 Eqs. 9-41 to 9-43, the limit p. 9-133), which GEC-10 (2018) does not print. allowed: rational, depth default: "rational"
K_over_KofloatoptionalK/Ko in the GEC-10 beta (beta_method 'rational'): 1 = 'a rational first-order approximation', no stress change from construction (GEC-10 p. 10-11); 2/3 or lower 'when these aspects of construction quality are not controlled properly' or soil caving is allowed (p. 10-12). 0 < K_over_Ko <= 1. default: 1.0
top_exclusionfloatoptionalSide resistance left out over the top of the shaft (m), in every layer, when given. Left out: none over the top 1.5 m in cohesive soil, GEC-10's 'top 5 ft' (p. 10-17, printed in Sec. 10.3.5.2 for cohesive soils, 'or to the depth of seasonal moisture change', 'subject to modification based on local experience and judgment of the designer'), and side resistance from the top in cohesionless soil and rock (Secs. 10.3.5.1 and 10.3.5.3 print no such zone; Examples 10-1 and 10-5 take the sand's from the surface, Example 10-4 the socket's over its whole length). Give 1.5 to leave the top 5 ft out of sand and rock too (frost, seasonal moisture, gapping from cyclic lateral load), or the depth of seasonal moisture change. casing_depth, where deeper, takes its place.
bottom_exclusionfloatoptionalSide resistance left out over the bottom of the shaft (m) in cohesive soil. Default 0: GEC-10 (2018) prints no such zone, and Example 10-2 (p. 10-18) takes the clay's side resistance to the base. FHWA NHI-06-089 p. 9-129 (O'Neill & Reese 1999) leaves out the bottom 5 ft (1.524 m), its Fig. 9-49 the bottom one diameter (give the diameter for that). default: 0.0
alpha_methodstroptionalCohesive side resistance. 'rational' (default) = GEC-10 (2018) Sec. 10.3.5.2, Eq. 10-18 (p. 10-16): alpha = 0.30+0.17/(su(CIUC)/pa), f_SN = alpha*su(CIUC), su(CIUC) from cu by su_test_type. 'aashto' = O'Neill & Reese (1999) as FHWA NHI-06-089 Eqs. 9-37a/b print it (p. 9-129): alpha = 0.55 for cu/pa <= 1.5, 0.55-0.1*(cu/pa-1.5) to 2.5, on cu; GEC-10 recommends Eq. 10-18 'as a revision' to it. allowed: rational, aashto default: "rational"
su_test_typestroptionalFor alpha_method 'rational': the lab test each layer's cu came from. 'ciuc' (default) = cu taken as su(CIUC), no transform; 'uc' / 'uu' = transformed to su(CIUC) on the layer's sigma'vo by GEC-10 Eq. 10-16 / 10-17 (Chen & Kulhawy 1993, p. 10-16; Example 10-2 takes a UU strength). The base in clay takes the same su(CIUC) (Example 10-3). allowed: ciuc, uc, uu default: "ciuc"
clay_base_methodstroptionalBase resistance with the tip in cohesive soil. 'gec10' (default) = GEC-10 (2018) p. 10-19: q_BN = N*c*su (Eq. 10-19), su the mean of the cohesive soil over 2B below the base, by thickness (p. 10-19; the tip layer at its su(CIUC) as its side resistance took it, each clay layer below on its own cu, transformed alike; cohesionless or rock layers within 2B left out; where the profile ends short of 2B, the mean of what it gives, said in the choices), N*c from Table 10-2 by su (6.5 at 500 psf, 8.0 at 1,000 psf, 9.0 at 2,000 psf or more; held at 6.5 below 500 psf), (2/3)[1 + D/(6B)]*N*c*su where the depth D < 3B (Eq. 10-20), no upper limit. 'oneill_reese' = FHWA NHI-06-089 Eqs. 9-39, 9-40 (p. 9-131): Nc = 6[1 + 0.2 z/D] <= 9, x 0.67 where su < 0.5 ksf, q_t <= 80 ksf, on the tip layer's cu. allowed: gec10, oneill_reese default: "gec10"
rock_base_methodstroptionalBase resistance with the tip in rock. 'gec10' (default) = GEC-10 (2018) Eq. 10-23 (p. 10-22): q_BN = 2.5*qu, for rock massive or tightly jointed to one diameter below the base, no cavities beneath, a clean base (Example 10-4 takes it with RQD 37 to 100); for a fractured rock mass the Hoek-Brown base, Eqs. 10-24 to 10-29 (pp. 10-23, 10-24; Turner and Ramey 2010): m_b = m_i*exp((GSI-100)/28), s = exp((GSI-100)/9), a = 1/2+(1/6)(exp(-GSI/15)-exp(-20/3)), A = sigma'vb + qu*(m_b*sigma'vb/qu + s)^a, q_BN = A + qu*(m_b*A/qu + s)^a, q_BN/qu limited to 2.5 (p. 10-24), on the tip rock layer's qu, GSI and m_i and the vertical effective stress at the base; resistance factor 0.50 (p. 10-24, Table 8-4); which of the two by rock_base_conditions_met. 'rqd' = q_b/q_u reduced by the tip rock's RQD below 70 (1.5 at 50, 0.8 at 25, 0.4 at 0), cited to GEC-10's 2010 edition, not in the reference library, and not a method GEC-10 Table 8-4 gives a resistance factor for. allowed: gec10, rqd default: "gec10"
rock_base_conditions_metbooloptionalFor rock_base_method 'gec10' with the tip in rock: whether the rock below the base meets the three conditions GEC-10 p. 10-22 sets on q_BN = 2.5*qu (massive or tightly jointed, no compressible seams or joints, to at least one diameter below the base; no solution cavities or voids beneath it; a clean base achieved and verified). The engineer's judgment: Example 10-4 takes 2.5 with RQD 37 to 100 because 'Rock coring and local experience indicate the rock mass below the socket tip is competent'. true = 2.5*qu (Eq. 10-23) as stated. false = GEC-10's base for a fractured rock mass, the Hoek-Brown base (Eqs. 10-24 to 10-29), on the tip rock layer's GSI and m_i; refused, naming them, where that layer does not give them. Left out = taken as met, said in the result's choices, where every layer within one base diameter below the base is rock with RQD 100 (the layer default), with the Hoek-Brown base on the tip rock layer's GSI and m_i beside it where they are given; where a layer there has an RQD below 100 or is soil, the Hoek-Brown base on the tip rock layer's GSI and m_i (2.5*qu bounds it above), and the call is refused, naming them, where that layer does not give them.
large_base_reductionbooloptionalO'Neill & Reese's (1999) reduction of base resistance for a large base: 1.27/B in cohesionless soil for a base wider than 1.27 m, F_r = 2.5/(a*B + 2.5*b) <= 1 in cohesive soil for a base wider than 1.90 m (B the bell's where there is one). Default false: GEC-10 (2018) prints neither (Eqs. 10-14, 10-19, 10-20); true applies it. default: false
pafloatoptionalAtmospheric pressure (kPa) for the rational chains. default: 101.325
rock_side_CfloatoptionalC in the rock side resistance f_s = C*pa*sqrt(qu/pa) (GEC-10 Eq. 10-21, p. 10-20). Default 1.0, 'recommended for design of "normal" rock sockets' (pp. 10-20, 10-21; Example 10-4): conventional equipment, nominally clean sidewalls, no caving, no smearing. 0.65 = the value of Eq. 10-22 with alpha_E = 1.0 (rock_side_method 'caving' takes alpha_E from Table 10-3 by RQD). 1.9 for roughened sockets, verified by load tests or local experience (p. 10-22). For rock_side_method 'normal'; refused with 'caving', which takes no C. Needs a rock layer. default: 1.0
rock_side_methodstroptionalRock side resistance. 'normal' (default) = GEC-10 Eq. 10-21, f_s = C*pa*sqrt(qu/pa) with rock_side_C, for a 'normal' socket: conventional equipment, nominally clean sidewalls (pp. 10-20, 10-21). 'caving' = Eq. 10-22 (O'Neill and Reese 1999), f_s = 0.65*alpha_E*pa*sqrt(qu/pa), alpha_E from Table 10-3 (p. 10-21) by each rock layer's RQD and rock_joints (closed joints 1.00, 0.85, 0.60, 0.50, 0.45; open or gouge-filled 0.85, 0.55, 0.55, 0.50, 0.45 at RQD 100, 70, 50, 30, 20 %; linear between the rows, held at 0.45 below RQD 20), for highly fractured or weathered rock that cannot be drilled without artificial support (casing, plug-ahead) or where caving is anticipated. Needs a rock layer. allowed: normal, caving default: "normal"
rock_jointsstroptionalFor rock_side_method 'caving': the joint condition of GEC-10 Table 10-3, 'closed' (default) or 'open' (open or gouge-filled joints), from the cores. allowed: closed, open default: "closed"
socket_diameterfloatoptionalRock socket diameter (m). Defaults to shaft diameter. One diameter for every rock layer: GEC-10 sizes a socket by one diameter B (Eq. 10-3, p. 10-9; Example 10-4) and gives none per rock layer. The rock side resistance and, with the tip in rock, the base (pi/4*B^2, GEC-10 Example 10-4, p. 10-28) take it.
bell_diameterfloatoptionalBelled base diameter (m).
casing_depthfloatoptionalPermanent casing depth (m, no side resistance). default: 0.0
fractured_rock_thicknessfloatoptionalDecomposed or fractured rock (m) below the top of the first rock layer that is 'not considered part of the socket for design purposes' (GEC-10 p. 8-15): no rock side resistance over it, while the soil above keeps its own (casing_depth takes both). 0 = all rock is socket. Needs a rock layer. default: 0.0
concrete_fcfloatoptionalCompressive strength f'c of the shaft concrete (kPa; 28 MPa = 28000, at least 1000). The rock side resistance takes qu no higher than it: 'For design, the value of qu used in Equation 10-21 should not exceed the compressive strength of the drilled shaft concrete' (GEC-10 p. 10-21; Example 10-4 gives qu 360 ksf and f'c 576 ksf), in Eq. 10-22 alike. With the base in rock it also checks the base against the concrete's own bearing (GEC-10 p. 10-25): Eq. 12-7 (p. 12-8), 0.70*[0.85*f'c*A1*m], the tip taken as plain concrete as Example 10-4 does (with the cage to the tip p. 12-8 prints Eq. 12-6 at phi 0.70, not computed: the tool takes no f_y), A1 the socket's cross-sectional area, m = 2.0 (printed for a socket on competent rock), against the geotechnical 0.50*Q_tip (Example 10-4 p. 10-28 makes this check), in base_steps.concrete_bearing and the choices; lrfd_capacity takes the factored base as the smaller of the two. Q_tip, Q_ultimate and Q_allowable stay the geotechnical ones. Left out, neither limit is checked and the result's choices say so. No other structural check of the shaft is made. Needs a rock layer.

get_resistance_factors — GEC-10 Table 8-4 resistance factors for drilled shaft design. The table includes uplift factors (uplift_cohesive, uplift_cohesionless, uplift_rock); the module has NO uplift capacity analysis, so those are for hand calculation only and no tool here uses them.

No parameters.

10.1.7 wave_equation — Wave-equation drivability

single_blow — Simulate a single hammer blow — set, stress, blow count.

ParameterTypeDescription
hammer_namestroptionalHammer name (use list_available_hammers).
pile_lengthfloatrequiredPile length (m).
pile_areafloatrequiredPile area (m2).
R_totalfloatrequiredTotal soil resistance (kN). Alias: R_ultimate.
skin_fractionfloatoptionalSkin friction fraction. default: 0.5
damping_modelstroptionalSmith damping form (UFC 3-220-20 (2025) Sec. 6-9.2, pp. 487-488): 'smith' (default), damping proportional to the mobilized static resistance, J x R_static x v, set 'in most instances' (GEC-12 Vol 2 p. 242); 'smith_viscous', proportional to the fully mobilized static resistance, J x R_ult x v, which GEC-12 Vol 2 (p. 242) selects for a residual stress analysis or a vibratory hammer, and sometimes for a refined analysis's match. allowed: smith, smith_viscous default: "smith"
quake_sidefloatoptionalShaft quake (m): 0.10 in (0.0025 m), usually satisfactory (GEC-12 Vol 2 Sec. 12.6.7, p. 211). default: 0.0025
quake_toefloatoptionalToe quake (m). Default 0.10 in (0.0025 m), GEC-12 Vol 2's toe quake for a non-displacement pile, e.g. an H-pile (p. 171). A displacement pile (closed end pipe, concrete): pile diameter or width D over 120 to D over 60 (p. 211), D/60 in medium or dense sand and D/120 in very dense soil (Examples 1, 3, 6, pp. 162, 170, 182); GEC-12 Vol 3 (p. 40) also gives H-piles D/60 and D/120. Hard rock: 0.04 in (0.001 m) (p. 212). Saturated or sensitive soils can reach well over D/60 (p. 211). default: 0.0025
damping_sidefloatoptionalShaft Smith damping (s/m), GEC-12 Vol 2 Sec. 12.6.7 (p. 211): 0.05 s/ft (0.16 s/m, the default) non-cohesive soils, 0.10 s/ft (0.33) silty sands, clayey sands and sandy silts, 0.15 s/ft (0.49) cohesive silts and sandy clays, 0.20 s/ft (0.66) cohesive soils. For restrike, perhaps twice as high (p. 211). default: 0.16
damping_toefloatoptionalToe Smith damping (s/m): about 0.15 s/ft (0.49 s/m) for most soils (GEC-12 Vol 2 p. 211); lower on hard rock, e.g. 0.05 s/ft (0.16 s/m) (p. 212). default: 0.49
embedded_lengthfloatoptionalThe pile's embedded length, its penetration below grade (m), at most pile_length: the shaft resistance acts only below grade, the pile above it standing free (GEC-12 Vol 2 p. 224: 'Penetration refers to the analyzed pile toe penetration below grade'; Example 1, p. 162, a 65 ft pile driven 62 ft; Example 6, p. 182, 66 ft with 'an embedded length of 52.5 feet'). Left out: pile_length, the pile embedded over its full length.
shaft_distributionstroptionalHow the shaft resistance (skin_fraction of R_ult) is spread over the embedded length, as GEC-12 Vol 2's examples print it: 'uniform' (default), the same per metre (Example 5, p. 179: '92% uniform shaft resistance'); 'triangular', rising linearly from none at grade to its largest at the pile toe (Example 1, p. 162, Fig. 12-3; Example 6, p. 182: 'distributed triangularly along the embedded portion of the pile shaft'). A distribution from a static analysis layer by layer (Example 4, Fig. 12-9) is not offered. GEC-12 Vol 2 p. 212: the stresses, tension above all, are sensitive to the distribution. allowed: uniform, triangular default: "uniform"
ram_weightfloatoptionalCustom hammer ram weight (kN) — used with stroke when hammer_name is omitted.
strokefloatoptionalCustom hammer stroke (m).
efficiencyfloatoptionalCustom hammer efficiency: the share of the potential ram energy (ram weight x stroke) that reaches the ram as kinetic energy at impact (GEC-12 Vol 2 (FHWA-NHI-16-010) Sec. 12.6.2, p. 205). GEC-12 Vol 2 prints 0.67 for an air hammer and 0.80 for an open end diesel (Example 6, p. 185), and say 0.95 for a hydraulic hammer whose ram kinetic energy is measured (p. 205). Default 0.67. default: 0.67
hammer_custom_namestroptionalCustom hammer label. default: "Custom"
hammer_typestroptionalCustom hammer type: a label in the result and calc package only. Every type is modelled as a rigid ram striking at v = sqrt(2 g stroke efficiency); a diesel hammer's combustion pressure is not modelled, and its result carries a warning (GEC-12 Vol 2 p. 206: its stroke rises with the resistance, and too high a stroke gives non-conservative nominal resistances). Give the type's losses through efficiency (GEC-12 Vol 2 (FHWA-NHI-16-010) Sec. 12.6.2, p. 205: relatively high, say 0.95, for a hydraulic hammer whose ram kinetic energy is measured and displayed). allowed: single_acting, diesel, hydraulic default: "single_acting"
segment_lengthfloatoptionalPile segment length (m): about 1 m (GEC-12 Vol 2 Sec. 12.3, p. 155; GRLWEAP's 3.3 ft, p. 213). Shorter segments for stiff, uncushioned driving systems (p. 210). default: 1.0
cushion_stiffnessfloatoptionalHammer cushion stiffness (kN/m), with cushion_cor and helmet_weight. Or give cushion_area + cushion_thickness + cushion_E: stiffness = E A / t (GEC-12 Vol 2 p. 155); two materials in series 1/k = 1/k1 + 1/k2 (p. 209). The model has one cushion spring, between the ram and the helmet (whose weight is lumped with the pile head); GEC-12 Vol 2 Fig. 12-2 (p. 157) has a hammer cushion and a pile cushion with the helmet between. Left out with no cushion properties: the hammer's printed driving system where a held reference prints one (hammer_name 'Vulcan 014', GEC-12 Vol 2 Table 12-2, p. 183), or the one named by driving_system; for any other hammer the call is refused and the error lists the printed options (GEC-12 prints no cushion by hammer otherwise; ideally the contractor's submittal, Vol II p. 226).
cushion_areafloatoptionalCushion area (m2) — with cushion_thickness and cushion_E.
cushion_thicknessfloatoptionalCushion thickness (m).
cushion_EfloatoptionalCushion elastic modulus (kPa), with the nominal (uncompressed) thickness. Plywood pile cushions 30 ksi (207,000 kPa) new and 75 ksi (517,000 kPa) used; oak boards 60 and 90 ksi (GEC-12 Vol 2 p. 209).
cushion_corfloatoptionalHammer cushion coefficient of restitution, required with a cushion given by stiffness or properties (no held reference prints one COR for every cushion). GEC-12 Vol 2: the hammer cushions of its examples 0.90 to 0.92 (pp. 174, 183); wood 0.50, a badly worn softwood cushion 0.25 (p. 156); a refined analysis adjusts it between 0.10 and 1.0 (p. 216). With a printed driving system and no cushion given: that system's COR unless given (Vulcan 014 0.91, ICE 42S 0.92, p. 183).
pile_EfloatoptionalPile elastic modulus (kPa). Default steel, 29,000 ksi (GEC-12 Vol 1 p. 317). Concrete: on the order of 4,000 ksi, varying with its strength (Vol 1 p. 317); its dynamic modulus is usually higher than the static (Vol 2 p. 213). default: 200000000.0
pile_unit_weightfloatoptionalPile material unit weight (kN/m3). Default steel, 492 lb/ft3 (GEC-12 Vol 2 p. 462). default: 77.3
helmet_weightfloatoptionalHelmet weight (kN): helmet, hammer cushion, striker plate and inserts (GEC-12 Vol 2 p. 226), lumped with the pile head; 0 with no helmet mass. Required with a cushion given. With a printed driving system and no cushion given: that system's helmet unless given (Vulcan 014 1.67 kips, 7.43 kN; ICE 42S 2.05 kips, 9.12 kN; p. 183). GEC-12's examples give 1.0 to 4.07 kips (4.4 to 18.1 kN; Vol II pp. 163, 167, 174, 179, 183).
driving_systemstroptionalA driving system (hammer cushion and helmet) as a held reference prints it, by its hammer: GEC-12 Vol 2 Example 6, Table 12-2 (p. 183), on a steel pipe pile. 'Vulcan 014': Nycast, 208 ksi, 234 in2, 6.0 in (1.42 million kN/m), COR 0.91, helmet 1.67 kips; 'ICE 42S': Blue Nylon, 175 ksi, 398 in2, 2.0 in (6.10 million kN/m), COR 0.92, helmet 2.05 kips. cushion_cor and helmet_weight, if given, replace the system's. Not with cushion_stiffness or cushion properties. Left out: the named hammer's own printed system, which only hammer_name 'Vulcan 014' has; any other hammer needs a cushion given. A run with another hammer says so in its choices. allowed: ICE 42S, Vulcan 014

pile_EfloatoptionalPile elastic modulus (kPa). Default steel, 29,000 ksi (GEC-12 Vol 1 p. 317). Concrete: on the order of 4,000 ksi, varying with its strength (Vol 1 p. 317); its dynamic modulus is usually higher than the static (Vol 2 p. 213). default: 200000000.0
pile_unit_weightfloatoptionalPile material unit weight (kN/m3). Default steel, 492 lb/ft3 (GEC-12 Vol 2 p. 462). default: 77.3
helmet_weightfloatoptionalHelmet weight (kN): helmet, hammer cushion, striker plate and inserts (GEC-12 Vol 2 p. 226), lumped with the pile head; 0 with no helmet mass. Required with a cushion given. With a printed driving system and no cushion given: that system's helmet unless given (Vulcan 014 1.67 kips, 7.43 kN; ICE 42S 2.05 kips, 9.12 kN; p. 183). GEC-12's examples give 1.0 to 4.07 kips (4.4 to 18.1 kN; Vol II pp. 163, 167, 174, 179, 183).
driving_systemstroptionalA driving system (hammer cushion and helmet) as a held reference prints it, by its hammer: GEC-12 Vol 2 Example 6, Table 12-2 (p. 183), on a steel pipe pile. 'Vulcan 014': Nycast, 208 ksi, 234 in2, 6.0 in (1.42 million kN/m), COR 0.91, helmet 1.67 kips; 'ICE 42S': Blue Nylon, 175 ksi, 398 in2, 2.0 in (6.10 million kN/m), COR 0.92, helmet 2.05 kips. cushion_cor and helmet_weight, if given, replace the system's. Not with cushion_stiffness or cushion properties. Left out: the named hammer's own printed system, which only hammer_name 'Vulcan 014' has; any other hammer needs a cushion given. A run with another hammer says so in its choices. allowed: ICE 42S, Vulcan 014

drivability — Drivability study: can the hammer drive the pile to target depth?

ParameterTypeDescription
hammer_namestroptionalHammer name.
pile_areafloatrequiredPile area (m2).
depthsarrayrequiredDepth stations (m).
R_at_deptharrayrequiredSRD at each depth (kN).
skin_fractionsarrayoptionalSkin friction fraction per depth station.
refusal_blow_countfloatoptionalBlow count (blows/m) above which the pile has refused. Default 393.7 (120 blows/ft): GEC-12 Vol 2 Sec. 12.4 (p. 161) chooses hammer and cushion so the maximum expected penetration resistance is under 120 blows/ft, and the drivability study of Vol 3 (p. 43) calls it practical refusal. Piles through soft soils seated on hard rock: 787.4 (240 blows/ft, p. 161), the refusal of Vol 2's Examples 3, 4 and 7. default: 393.7
damping_modelstroptionalSmith damping form (UFC 3-220-20 (2025) Sec. 6-9.2, pp. 487-488): 'smith' (default), damping proportional to the mobilized static resistance, J x R_static x v, set 'in most instances' (GEC-12 Vol 2 p. 242); 'smith_viscous', proportional to the fully mobilized static resistance, J x R_ult x v, which GEC-12 Vol 2 (p. 242) selects for a residual stress analysis or a vibratory hammer, and sometimes for a refined analysis's match. allowed: smith, smith_viscous default: "smith"
pile_lengthfloatoptionalThe pile's total length in the leads (m), the same at every depth: at each depth the pile is this long, embedded to the depth, the shaft resistance only below grade (GEC-12 Vol 2 p. 224: 'Length is the total pile length in the leads'; 'Penetration refers to ... final penetration for Drivability Analyses'; p. 236, the depths to be analyzed). No depth may be deeper (p. 227). Left out: the deepest depth analysed, the shortest pile that reaches it (p. 227), the same pile at every depth; the result's choices say so.
shaft_distributionstroptionalHow the shaft resistance (skin_fraction of R_ult) is spread over the embedded length, as GEC-12 Vol 2's examples print it: 'uniform' (default), the same per metre (Example 5, p. 179: '92% uniform shaft resistance'); 'triangular', rising linearly from none at grade to its largest at the pile toe (Example 1, p. 162, Fig. 12-3; Example 6, p. 182: 'distributed triangularly along the embedded portion of the pile shaft'). A distribution from a static analysis layer by layer (Example 4, Fig. 12-9) is not offered. GEC-12 Vol 2 p. 212: the stresses, tension above all, are sensitive to the distribution. allowed: uniform, triangular default: "uniform"
quake_sidefloatoptionalShaft quake (m): 0.10 in (0.0025 m), usually satisfactory (GEC-12 Vol 2 Sec. 12.6.7, p. 211). default: 0.0025
quake_toefloatoptionalToe quake (m). Default 0.10 in (0.0025 m), GEC-12 Vol 2's toe quake for a non-displacement pile, e.g. an H-pile (p. 171). A displacement pile (closed end pipe, concrete): pile diameter or width D over 120 to D over 60 (p. 211), D/60 in medium or dense sand and D/120 in very dense soil (Examples 1, 3, 6, pp. 162, 170, 182); GEC-12 Vol 3 (p. 40) also gives H-piles D/60 and D/120. Hard rock: 0.04 in (0.001 m) (p. 212). Saturated or sensitive soils can reach well over D/60 (p. 211). default: 0.0025
damping_sidefloatoptionalShaft Smith damping (s/m), GEC-12 Vol 2 Sec. 12.6.7 (p. 211): 0.05 s/ft (0.16 s/m, the default) non-cohesive soils, 0.10 s/ft (0.33) silty sands, clayey sands and sandy silts, 0.15 s/ft (0.49) cohesive silts and sandy clays, 0.20 s/ft (0.66) cohesive soils. For restrike, perhaps twice as high (p. 211). default: 0.16
damping_toefloatoptionalToe Smith damping (s/m): about 0.15 s/ft (0.49 s/m) for most soils (GEC-12 Vol 2 p. 211); lower on hard rock, e.g. 0.05 s/ft (0.16 s/m) (p. 212). default: 0.49
ram_weightfloatoptionalCustom hammer ram weight (kN) — used with stroke when hammer_name is omitted.
strokefloatoptionalCustom hammer stroke (m).
efficiencyfloatoptionalCustom hammer efficiency: the share of the potential ram energy (ram weight x stroke) that reaches the ram as kinetic energy at impact (GEC-12 Vol 2 (FHWA-NHI-16-010) Sec. 12.6.2, p. 205). GEC-12 Vol 2 prints 0.67 for an air hammer and 0.80 for an open end diesel (Example 6, p. 185), and say 0.95 for a hydraulic hammer whose ram kinetic energy is measured (p. 205). Default 0.67. default: 0.67
hammer_custom_namestroptionalCustom hammer label. default: "Custom"
hammer_typestroptionalCustom hammer type: a label in the result and calc package only. Every type is modelled as a rigid ram striking at v = sqrt(2 g stroke efficiency); a diesel hammer's combustion pressure is not modelled, and its result carries a warning (GEC-12 Vol 2 p. 206: its stroke rises with the resistance, and too high a stroke gives non-conservative nominal resistances). Give the type's losses through efficiency (GEC-12 Vol 2 (FHWA-NHI-16-010) Sec. 12.6.2, p. 205: relatively high, say 0.95, for a hydraulic hammer whose ram kinetic energy is measured and displayed). allowed: single_acting, diesel, hydraulic default: "single_acting"
segment_lengthfloatoptionalPile segment length (m): about 1 m (GEC-12 Vol 2 Sec. 12.3, p. 155; GRLWEAP's 3.3 ft, p. 213). Shorter segments for stiff, uncushioned driving systems (p. 210). default: 1.0
cushion_stiffnessfloatoptionalHammer cushion stiffness (kN/m), with cushion_cor and helmet_weight. Or give cushion_area + cushion_thickness + cushion_E: stiffness = E A / t (GEC-12 Vol 2 p. 155); two materials in series 1/k = 1/k1 + 1/k2 (p. 209). The model has one cushion spring, between the ram and the helmet (whose weight is lumped with the pile head); GEC-12 Vol 2 Fig. 12-2 (p. 157) has a hammer cushion and a pile cushion with the helmet between. Left out with no cushion properties: the hammer's printed driving system where a held reference prints one (hammer_name 'Vulcan 014', GEC-12 Vol 2 Table 12-2, p. 183), or the one named by driving_system; for any other hammer the call is refused and the error lists the printed options (GEC-12 prints no cushion by hammer otherwise; ideally the contractor's submittal, Vol II p. 226).
cushion_areafloatoptionalCushion area (m2) — with cushion_thickness and cushion_E.
cushion_thicknessfloatoptionalCushion thickness (m).
cushion_EfloatoptionalCushion elastic modulus (kPa), with the nominal (uncompressed) thickness. Plywood pile cushions 30 ksi (207,000 kPa) new and 75 ksi (517,000 kPa) used; oak boards 60 and 90 ksi (GEC-12 Vol 2 p. 209).
cushion_corfloatoptionalHammer cushion coefficient of restitution, required with a cushion given by stiffness or properties (no held reference prints one COR for every cushion). GEC-12 Vol 2: the hammer cushions of its examples 0.90 to 0.92 (pp. 174, 183); wood 0.50, a badly worn softwood cushion 0.25 (p. 156); a refined analysis adjusts it between 0.10 and 1.0 (p. 216). With a printed driving system and no cushion given: that system's COR unless given (Vulcan 014 0.91, ICE 42S 0.92, p. 183).
pile_EfloatoptionalPile elastic modulus (kPa). Default steel, 29,000 ksi (GEC-12 Vol 1 p. 317). Concrete: on the order of 4,000 ksi, varying with its strength (Vol 1 p. 317); its dynamic modulus is usually higher than the static (Vol 2 p. 213). default: 200000000.0
pile_unit_weightfloatoptionalPile material unit weight (kN/m3). Default steel, 492 lb/ft3 (GEC-12 Vol 2 p. 462). default: 77.3
helmet_weightfloatoptionalHelmet weight (kN): helmet, hammer cushion, striker plate and inserts (GEC-12 Vol 2 p. 226), lumped with the pile head; 0 with no helmet mass. Required with a cushion given. With a printed driving system and no cushion given: that system's helmet unless given (Vulcan 014 1.67 kips, 7.43 kN; ICE 42S 2.05 kips, 9.12 kN; p. 183). GEC-12's examples give 1.0 to 4.07 kips (4.4 to 18.1 kN; Vol II pp. 163, 167, 174, 179, 183).
driving_systemstroptionalA driving system (hammer cushion and helmet) as a held reference prints it, by its hammer: GEC-12 Vol 2 Example 6, Table 12-2 (p. 183), on a steel pipe pile. 'Vulcan 014': Nycast, 208 ksi, 234 in2, 6.0 in (1.42 million kN/m), COR 0.91, helmet 1.67 kips; 'ICE 42S': Blue Nylon, 175 ksi, 398 in2, 2.0 in (6.10 million kN/m), COR 0.92, helmet 2.05 kips. cushion_cor and helmet_weight, if given, replace the system's. Not with cushion_stiffness or cushion properties. Left out: the named hammer's own printed system, which only hammer_name 'Vulcan 014' has; any other hammer needs a cushion given. A run with another hammer says so in its choices. allowed: ICE 42S, Vulcan 014

list_available_hammers — List all available pile driving hammers.

No parameters.

10.1.8 downdrag — Downdrag / neutral plane

downdrag_analysis — Downdrag (negative skin friction), neutral plane method: every method's neutral plane and drag force side by side.

ParameterTypeDescription
pile_lengthfloatrequiredPile length (m).
pile_diameterfloatrequiredPile diameter (m).
layersarrayrequiredArray of {thickness, soil_type, unit_weight, phi, cu, beta, alpha, skin_friction_method, soil_class, settling, description} dicts. soil_type must be 'cohesionless' or 'cohesive' (NOT 'sand'/'clay'/'settling_fill'). Skin friction: cohesionless = beta x sigma'v (Beta method, UFC 3-220-20 Eq 6-7), beta as given, else from phi' by GEC-12 Table 7-9 (UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-15, driven piles) for the layer's soil_class ('silt' 0.25-0.50 over 28-34 deg, 'sand' 0.30-0.90 over 32-40 deg, the default, 'gravel' 0.35-0.80 over 35-45 deg), a straight line in phi' between GEC-12 Table 7-9's range ends (the module's reading; the table prints only the ends), held at the ends outside the range; soil_class also picks the toe's Nt row (Nt_method); cohesive = alpha x cu (Alpha method, UFC 3-220-20 Eq 6-8, the default; alpha as given, else read off alpha_chart: UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-16 and Fig 6-14 by default), or with skin_friction_method 'beta' beta x sigma'v for long-term, drained conditions (UFC 3-220-20 6-5.4.1; GEC-12 7.2.1.3.4), beta required (GEC-12 Table 7-9: clay 0.15-0.35; cu then only for a toe in the layer). A cohesive layer takes no phi, and beta only with skin_friction_method 'beta'; a cohesionless layer takes no alpha. Mark settling layers with settling=True; a settling layer also needs its compressibility: cohesionless -> E_s (elastic modulus, kPa, > 0) and optional nu_s; cohesive -> Cc and e0 (optional Cr, sigma_p kPa) or C_ec/C_er.
Q_deadfloatoptionalDead load at pile top (kN). default: 0.0
fill_thicknessfloatoptionalFill thickness causing downdrag (m). default: 0.0
fill_unit_weightfloatoptionalFill unit weight (kN/m3). default: 19.0
gw_drawdownfloatoptionalGroundwater drawdown (m). default: 0.0
gwt_depthfloatoptionalGroundwater depth (m). default: 0.0
pile_EfloatoptionalPile elastic modulus (kPa). Default is steel. default: 200000000.0
pile_perimeterfloatoptionalPile perimeter (m). Computed from diameter if omitted.
pile_areafloatoptionalPile cross-section area (m2). Computed from diameter if omitted.
structural_capacityfloatoptionalPile structural capacity (kN) for the max-load check.
allowable_settlementfloatoptionalAllowable pile settlement (m) for the settlement check.
NtfloatoptionalToe bearing capacity factor: R_toe = Nt x sigma'v(toe) x A_toe in cohesionless soil, Nt x cu x A_toe in cohesive. Give the MOBILIZED value -- the toe resistance actually developed at the pile's settlement -- not the ultimate. Omitted, Nt is the ULTIMATE value: 9 in clay (UFC 3-220-20 6-5.4.3.3), and in cohesionless soil from the toe layer's phi' by Nt_method (60-120 in dense sand at 34-38 deg by the default); then the load and resistance curves often do not intersect and the neutral plane is where the pile and soil settle equally, the toe force compatible with the toe penetration (UFC 3-220-20 6-5.8.4.3; see neutral_plane_method). UFC 3-220-20 6-5.8.4.2: check 0 %, 50 % and 100 % toe mobilization.
Nt_methodstringoptionalWhere a cohesionless toe's ultimate Nt comes from when Nt is not given, both UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-17 (p. 421; qb = Nq sigma'zD, Eq 6-20): 'fellenius' (default) = its Fellenius (2021) column, the same values as GEC-12 Table 7-9, by the toe layer's soil_class (silt 20-40 over 28-34 deg, sand 30-150 over 32-40 deg, gravel 60-300 over 35-45 deg), a straight line in phi' between GEC-12 Table 7-9's range ends (the module's reading; the table prints only the ends), held at the ends outside the range; 'cheng' = its equation after Cheng (2004), Nq ~= 1.2 (Z/b)^-0.437 exp[6.34 (Z/b)^0.0486 tan phi'], Z the pile length and b pile_diameter, at most 200 unless project-specific information supports more (give Nt then). The result's choices give the other route's value. allowed: fellenius, cheng default: "fellenius"
pile_unit_weightfloatoptionalPile material unit weight (kN/m3), times pile_area for the pile's own weight; used only when include_pile_weight is true. Default 78.5 = steel, the same material as the pile_E default (concrete is about 24). For an H or pipe pile give pile_area as the steel area (pile_area defaults to the solid circle). default: 78.5
include_pile_weightbooloptionalWhether the load curve carries the pile's own weight. Default false: left out, as UFC 3-220-20 Fig 6-26 and FHWA GEC-12 7.3.6.1 (and their worked examples) do. True adds the weight of the pile above the neutral plane to Q_np and the drag force. default: false
n_sublayersintoptionalSublayers per soil layer for the depth discretization. default: 10
neutral_plane_methodstringoptionalWhich method gives the reported numbers; every method is evaluated and returned in neutral_plane_comparison whatever is chosen. 'auto' (default) = the UFC 3-220-20 6-7.4 procedure: the intersection of the load and resistance curves with the toe at toe_mobilization, or, when they do not intersect, where the pile and soil settle equally with the toe force compatible with the toe penetration (UFC 6-5.8.4.3, Fig 6-19). 'force_equilibrium' (the curves' intersection only; error if they do not intersect); 'settlement_compatibility' (pile and soil settle equally, toe force compatible with the toe penetration); 'bearing_layer_top' (top of the bearing layer, end-bearing pile, UFC 6-7.4 step 5); 'pile_toe' (whole shaft in negative skin friction, upper bound); 'endo' (Endo et al. 1969, CGPR #56 Table 3.1 fraction of the embedment; needs endo_bearing_condition). allowed: auto, force_equilibrium, settlement_compatibility, bearing_layer_top, pile_toe, endo default: "auto"
toe_mobilizationfloatoptionalFraction (0-1) of the nominal toe resistance mobilized where the load and resistance curves intersect. 1.0 = UFC 6-7.4 step 3 full mobilization ('a conservative approach for evaluating the drag force'); 0.5 and 0 = the other UFC 6-5.8.4.2 / GEC-12 7.3.6.1 cases for settlement (all three always reported in the comparison). default: 1.0
endo_bearing_conditionstringoptionalCGPR #56 Table 3.1 condition for Endo et al. (1969). allowed: floating, stiff_flexible, end_bearing
skin_friction_stressstringoptionalEffective stress for Beta-method skin friction (sand, and clay with skin_friction_method 'beta') and the sand toe: 'final' (default; sigma'v0 + fill/drawdown change, as UFC 3-220-20 6-7.4 step 2 requires) or 'initial' (sigma'v0). allowed: final, initial default: "final"
influence_depth_criterionstringoptionalHow deep below the toe the toe load is counted in the settlement (toe force spread 2V:1H from an equivalent footing as wide as the pile): to where its stress increase falls below 'bearing_stress' (default) = 10% of the bearing stress of the equivalent footing (UFC 3-220-20 6-5.8.4.3; 2.16 pile widths for a single pile) or 'effective_stress' = 10% of the existing vertical effective stress (FHWA GEC-12 Vol I step 1c: 7.3.5.3 for clay below the toe, 7.3.5.6 for sand, 7.3.5.5 for both; deeper for a loaded toe in soft soil). Either way the fill / drawdown, which does not decay with depth, compresses the settling layers below the toe down to the bottom of the soil profile; give the profile down to the base of the compressible soil. allowed: bearing_stress, effective_stress default: "bearing_stress"
influence_depth_warning_percentfloatoptionalThe result warns when the two influence_depth_criterion rules (UFC 3-220-20 6-5.8.4.3 and FHWA GEC-12 step 1c) give pile head settlements or drag forces that differ by more than this percentage of the larger of the two (of allowable_settlement / structural_capacity where given), and whenever a settlement or structural check passes with one rule and fails with the other. The rule used is not changed. Default 25 %: the engineer's call, not a reference's figure; neither reference says how far two settlement estimates may differ before it matters. default: 25.0
alpha_chartstringoptionalWhere a cohesive layer's alpha comes from when the layer leaves it out (a given alpha is kept). 'ufc_fig_6_14' (default; UFC 3-220-20 6-5.4.2, pp. 415-417, as its drag example App. B-5.4 reads it): soft clay (su below 800 psf) alpha 1 by Table 6-16; firm to very stiff clay off Fig 6-14 by su/Pa, curve A at Z of 40b or more, curve B at Z = 10b, linear between, Z from the ground surface to the clay's base or the pile toe and b = pile_diameter. 'gec12_fig_7_17': FHWA GEC-12 7.2.1.3.2 Step 1, Ca off Fig. 7-17 by su, D/b and fig_7_17_curve, as drawn (Ca may exceed su). choices states each clay's alpha and where it came from. Refused (with fig_7_17_curve and alpha_transition_zone) where no cohesive layer along the pile leaves alpha out. allowed: ufc_fig_6_14, gec12_fig_7_17 default: "ufc_fig_6_14"
fig_7_17_curvestringoptionalWith alpha_chart 'gec12_fig_7_17' only, and then required where a clay leaves alpha out: the Fig. 7-17 curves for the pile, 'concrete_timber_corrugated' (concrete, timber or corrugated steel; an H-pile takes the corrugated curve, GEC-12 Vol I p. 247) or 'smooth_steel'. allowed: concrete_timber_corrugated, smooth_steel
alpha_transition_zonebooloptionalWhether the top 10 pile widths of a stiff or very stiff clay (su 1500 psf or more) directly under soft clay take UFC 3-220-20 Eq 6-9, alpha = 0.28 (su/Pa)^-0.44 with the unit side resistance at least the soft clay's, and under sand alpha 1.0 (pp. 416-417, as App. B-5.4 does). Left out: true with alpha_chart 'ufc_fig_6_14', false with 'gec12_fig_7_17'. Applies only where the stiff clay's alpha is left out; refused where no such clay lies under soft clay or sand. The zone runs 10 pile widths from the top of the stiff clay however it is split into layers.
ground_elevationfloatoptionalElevation of the ground surface the depths are measured from (m): the top of the layers, where the pile head is taken (the original ground under a fill). Figures only: the calc package's profiles are drawn against elevation; every result stays in depth and no number changes.
