cu_averagefloatrequiredAverage undrained strength, surface to NP (kPa).
delta_qfloatrequiredIncreased vertical effective stress from fill/water table change (kPa).

group_drag_reduction — Group drag load via Jeong & Briaud reduction factor A on a single-pile result (CGPR #56 4.3.2, Table 4.1).

ParameterTypeDescription
F_max_singlefloatrequiredMax pile force from a single-pile method (kN).
Q_static_groupfloatrequiredTotal static load on the group (kN).
n_pilesintrequiredNumber of piles (reduction valid ~9-25 piles).
locationstringrequiredPile position in the group. allowed: interior, side, corner
s_over_dfloatoptionalSpacing/diameter ratio. Or give spacing + pile_diameter.
spacingfloatoptionalCenter-to-center spacing (m).
pile_diameterfloatoptionalPile diameter/width (m).

post_liquefaction_downdrag — Post-liquefaction downdrag (FHWA GEC-10 10.7): neutral plane, drag force and settlement before the earthquake and after the liquefied layers reconsolidate, every neutral-plane method and every cited side resistance for the liquefied layers side by side.

ParameterTypeDescription
pile_lengthfloatrequiredPile length (m).
pile_diameterfloatrequiredPile diameter (m).
layersarrayrequiredArray of {thickness, soil_type, unit_weight, phi, cu, beta, alpha, skin_friction_method, soil_class, settling, description} dicts. soil_type must be 'cohesionless' or 'cohesive' (NOT 'sand'/'clay'/'settling_fill'). Skin friction: cohesionless = beta x sigma'v (Beta method, UFC 3-220-20 Eq 6-7), beta as given, else from phi' by GEC-12 Table 7-9 (UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-15, driven piles) for the layer's soil_class ('silt' 0.25-0.50 over 28-34 deg, 'sand' 0.30-0.90 over 32-40 deg, the default, 'gravel' 0.35-0.80 over 35-45 deg), a straight line in phi' between GEC-12 Table 7-9's range ends (the module's reading; the table prints only the ends), held at the ends outside the range; soil_class also picks the toe's Nt row (Nt_method); cohesive = alpha x cu (Alpha method, UFC 3-220-20 Eq 6-8, the default; alpha as given, else read off alpha_chart: UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-16 and Fig 6-14 by default), or with skin_friction_method 'beta' beta x sigma'v for long-term, drained conditions (UFC 3-220-20 6-5.4.1; GEC-12 7.2.1.3.4), beta required (GEC-12 Table 7-9: clay 0.15-0.35; cu then only for a toe in the layer). A cohesive layer takes no phi, and beta only with skin_friction_method 'beta'; a cohesionless layer takes no alpha. Mark settling layers with settling=True; a settling layer also needs its compressibility: cohesionless -> E_s (elastic modulus, kPa, > 0) and optional nu_s; cohesive -> Cc and e0 (optional Cr, sigma_p kPa) or C_ec/C_er.
Q_deadfloatoptionalDead load at pile top (kN). default: 0.0
fill_thicknessfloatoptionalFill thickness causing downdrag (m). default: 0.0
fill_unit_weightfloatoptionalFill unit weight (kN/m3). default: 19.0
gw_drawdownfloatoptionalGroundwater drawdown (m). default: 0.0
gwt_depthfloatoptionalGroundwater depth (m). default: 0.0
pile_EfloatoptionalPile elastic modulus (kPa). Default is steel. default: 200000000.0
pile_perimeterfloatoptionalPile perimeter (m). Computed from diameter if omitted.
pile_areafloatoptionalPile cross-section area (m2). Computed from diameter if omitted.
structural_capacityfloatoptionalPile structural capacity (kN) for the max-load check.
allowable_settlementfloatoptionalAllowable pile settlement (m) for the settlement check.
NtfloatoptionalToe bearing capacity factor: R_toe = Nt x sigma'v(toe) x A_toe in cohesionless soil, Nt x cu x A_toe in cohesive. Give the MOBILIZED value -- the toe resistance actually developed at the pile's settlement -- not the ultimate. Omitted, Nt is the ULTIMATE value: 9 in clay (UFC 3-220-20 6-5.4.3.3), and in cohesionless soil from the toe layer's phi' by Nt_method (60-120 in dense sand at 34-38 deg by the default); then the load and resistance curves often do not intersect and the neutral plane is where the pile and soil settle equally, the toe force compatible with the toe penetration (UFC 3-220-20 6-5.8.4.3; see neutral_plane_method). UFC 3-220-20 6-5.8.4.2: check 0 %, 50 % and 100 % toe mobilization.
Nt_methodstringoptionalWhere a cohesionless toe's ultimate Nt comes from when Nt is not given, both UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-17 (p. 421; qb = Nq sigma'zD, Eq 6-20): 'fellenius' (default) = its Fellenius (2021) column, the same values as GEC-12 Table 7-9, by the toe layer's soil_class (silt 20-40 over 28-34 deg, sand 30-150 over 32-40 deg, gravel 60-300 over 35-45 deg), a straight line in phi' between GEC-12 Table 7-9's range ends (the module's reading; the table prints only the ends), held at the ends outside the range; 'cheng' = its equation after Cheng (2004), Nq ~= 1.2 (Z/b)^-0.437 exp[6.34 (Z/b)^0.0486 tan phi'], Z the pile length and b pile_diameter, at most 200 unless project-specific information supports more (give Nt then). The result's choices give the other route's value. allowed: fellenius, cheng default: "fellenius"
pile_unit_weightfloatoptionalPile material unit weight (kN/m3), times pile_area for the pile's own weight; used only when include_pile_weight is true. Default 78.5 = steel, the same material as the pile_E default (concrete is about 24). For an H or pipe pile give pile_area as the steel area (pile_area defaults to the solid circle). default: 78.5
include_pile_weightbooloptionalWhether the load curve carries the pile's own weight. Default false: left out, as UFC 3-220-20 Fig 6-26 and FHWA GEC-12 7.3.6.1 (and their worked examples) do. True adds the weight of the pile above the neutral plane to Q_np and the drag force. default: false
n_sublayersintoptionalSublayers per soil layer for the depth discretization. default: 10
neutral_plane_methodstringoptionalWhich method gives the reported numbers; every method is evaluated before and after and returned in by_method whatever is chosen. 'auto' (default) = the UFC 3-220-20 6-7.4 procedure: the intersection of the load and resistance curves with the toe at toe_mobilization, or, when they do not intersect, where the pile and soil settle equally with the toe force compatible with the toe penetration (UFC 6-5.8.4.3, Fig 6-19). 'force_equilibrium' (the curves' intersection only; error if they do not intersect); 'settlement_compatibility' (pile and soil settle equally, toe force compatible with the toe penetration); 'bearing_layer_top' (top of the bearing layer, end-bearing pile, UFC 6-7.4 step 5); 'pile_toe' (whole shaft in negative skin friction, upper bound); 'endo' (Endo et al. 1969, CGPR #56 Table 3.1 fraction of the embedment; needs endo_bearing_condition). allowed: auto, force_equilibrium, settlement_compatibility, bearing_layer_top, pile_toe, endo default: "auto"
toe_mobilizationfloatoptionalFraction (0-1) of the nominal toe resistance mobilized where the load and resistance curves intersect. 1.0 = UFC 6-7.4 step 3 full mobilization ('a conservative approach for evaluating the drag force'); 0.5 and 0 = the other UFC 6-5.8.4.2 / GEC-12 7.3.6.1 cases for settlement (all three always reported in the comparison). default: 1.0
endo_bearing_conditionstringoptionalCGPR #56 Table 3.1 condition for Endo et al. (1969). allowed: floating, stiff_flexible, end_bearing
skin_friction_stressstringoptionalEffective stress for Beta-method skin friction (sand, and clay with skin_friction_method 'beta') and the sand toe: 'final' (default; sigma'v0 + fill/drawdown change, as UFC 3-220-20 6-7.4 step 2 requires) or 'initial' (sigma'v0). allowed: final, initial default: "final"
influence_depth_criterionstringoptionalHow deep below the toe the toe load is counted in the settlement (toe force spread 2V:1H from an equivalent footing as wide as the pile): to where its stress increase falls below 'bearing_stress' (default) = 10% of the bearing stress of the equivalent footing (UFC 3-220-20 6-5.8.4.3; 2.16 pile widths for a single pile) or 'effective_stress' = 10% of the existing vertical effective stress (FHWA GEC-12 Vol I step 1c: 7.3.5.3 for clay below the toe, 7.3.5.6 for sand, 7.3.5.5 for both; deeper for a loaded toe in soft soil). Either way the fill / drawdown, which does not decay with depth, compresses the settling layers below the toe down to the bottom of the soil profile; give the profile down to the base of the compressible soil. allowed: bearing_stress, effective_stress default: "bearing_stress"
influence_depth_warning_percentfloatoptionalThe result warns when the two influence_depth_criterion rules (UFC 3-220-20 6-5.8.4.3 and FHWA GEC-12 step 1c) give pile head settlements or drag forces that differ by more than this percentage of the larger of the two (of allowable_settlement / structural_capacity where given), and whenever a settlement or structural check passes with one rule and fails with the other. The rule used is not changed. Default 25 %: the engineer's call, not a reference's figure; neither reference says how far two settlement estimates may differ before it matters. default: 25.0
alpha_chartstringoptionalWhere a cohesive layer's alpha comes from when the layer leaves it out (a given alpha is kept). 'ufc_fig_6_14' (default; UFC 3-220-20 6-5.4.2, pp. 415-417, as its drag example App. B-5.4 reads it): soft clay (su below 800 psf) alpha 1 by Table 6-16; firm to very stiff clay off Fig 6-14 by su/Pa, curve A at Z of 40b or more, curve B at Z = 10b, linear between, Z from the ground surface to the clay's base or the pile toe and b = pile_diameter. 'gec12_fig_7_17': FHWA GEC-12 7.2.1.3.2 Step 1, Ca off Fig. 7-17 by su, D/b and fig_7_17_curve, as drawn (Ca may exceed su). choices states each clay's alpha and where it came from. Refused (with fig_7_17_curve and alpha_transition_zone) where no cohesive layer along the pile leaves alpha out. allowed: ufc_fig_6_14, gec12_fig_7_17 default: "ufc_fig_6_14"
fig_7_17_curvestringoptionalWith alpha_chart 'gec12_fig_7_17' only, and then required where a clay leaves alpha out: the Fig. 7-17 curves for the pile, 'concrete_timber_corrugated' (concrete, timber or corrugated steel; an H-pile takes the corrugated curve, GEC-12 Vol I p. 247) or 'smooth_steel'. allowed: concrete_timber_corrugated, smooth_steel
alpha_transition_zonebooloptionalWhether the top 10 pile widths of a stiff or very stiff clay (su 1500 psf or more) directly under soft clay take UFC 3-220-20 Eq 6-9, alpha = 0.28 (su/Pa)^-0.44 with the unit side resistance at least the soft clay's, and under sand alpha 1.0 (pp. 416-417, as App. B-5.4 does). Left out: true with alpha_chart 'ufc_fig_6_14', false with 'gec12_fig_7_17'. Applies only where the stiff clay's alpha is left out; refused where no such clay lies under soft clay or sand. The zone runs 10 pile widths from the top of the stiff clay however it is split into layers.
liquefied_layersarrayoptionalThe layers that liquefy, instead of liquefaction_result: array of {top, bottom (m below the pile head), volumetric_strain (post-liquefaction reconsolidation strain, decimal: 0.03 = 3 %) or settlement (m, the layer's reconsolidation settlement), su_r (kPa, residual undrained strength; optional), N1_60 (optional; su_r by GEC-10 Eq 9-13 when su_r is not given), fs_liq (optional, reported)}. The other inputs (layers, pile, Q_dead, fill, neutral_plane_method, ...) describe the state before the earthquake, as for downdrag_analysis.
liquefaction_resultobjectoptionalThe liquefaction tool's whole result, instead of liquefied_layers: from a CPT its depth_profile rows (top_m, bottom_m, FOS_liq, volumetric_strain: the strains come with it); from SPT its layer_results rows (depth_m, FOS_liq, N1_60; give volumetric_strain); or a profile with depth, factor_of_safety and volumetric_strain arrays. A reading liquefies where FOS_liq <= fs_liq_threshold and stands for its row's top_m to bottom_m, or the depth halfway to its neighbours, below gwt_depth.
volumetric_strainfloatoptionalReconsolidation volumetric strain (decimal) for liquefaction_result's readings: one value for every liquefied reading, or a list with one value per reading in the result's order. Required with liquefaction_result when the result carries no strains: the liquefaction tool's SPT routes compute none, and no reference in the library prints an SPT method (GEC-10 10.7 names Ishihara and Yoshimine (1992) as described in Idriss and Boulanger (2008), without printing it), so say where the value comes from. A CPT result carries its own (Zhang et al. 2002); a value given here replaces them.
fs_liq_thresholdfloatoptionalA reading of liquefaction_result liquefies where FOS_liq <= this. 1.0 = GEC-10 9.4.2.2 ('layers predicted to undergo liquefaction (FSliq <= 1.0)'); 1.0 < FSliq <= about 1.5 generates excess pore pressure. default: 1.0
liquefied_side_resistancestringoptionalUnit side resistance of the liquefied layers after reconsolidation, as drag above the neutral plane and resistance below it, for the reported numbers; every option that can be evaluated is reported in side_resistance_comparison whatever is chosen. 'half_pre_earthquake' (default) = 50 percent of the pre-earthquake (static) side resistance, GEC-10 10.7 p. 10-52 (Rollins et al. 2018); 'zero' = none, GEC-10 p. 10-51 and UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-49 (the state while liquefied); 'residual_strength' = su_r, the lower bound of GEC-10 p. 10-51 and GEC-12 7.4.2.2 (needs su_r or N1_60 for each layer; never more than the static value); 'ratio' = liquefied_side_resistance_ratio x the static value. The other layers keep their static side resistance. allowed: half_pre_earthquake, zero, residual_strength, ratio default: "half_pre_earthquake"
liquefied_side_resistance_ratiofloatoptionalFraction (0-1) of the pre-earthquake unit side resistance the liquefied layers carry. Required when liquefied_side_resistance='ratio'; given with another option, it adds a 'ratio' row to side_resistance_comparison.
detailstringoptional'full' = the whole result: each method's and option's source and assumptions, neutral_plane_basis, Q_np, toe forces and settlement parts, every liquefied zone with the methods it lies below, and after liquefaction the resistance below the plane, the settlement below the toe and the depth profiles (about 20,000 characters for one zone). Left out: the result keeps every neutral plane, drag force and pile settlement (each method before and after, each side-resistance option), the tables as {columns, rows}, more than 6 liquefied zones summarised, and result_note says what only 'full' has. allowed: full

10.1.9 sheet_pile — Sheet-pile walls

cantilever_wall — Cantilever sheet pile wall: embedment depth and maximum moment.

ParameterTypeDescription
excavation_depthfloatrequiredExcavation depth (m).
layersarrayrequiredArray of soil-layer dicts, top down: {thickness (m, required), unit_weight (kN/m3, required; alias gamma), friction_angle (deg, default 30; alias phi), cohesion (kPa, default 0), wall_friction_deg (deg, 0 to friction_angle; alias delta), interface_soil (the soil against the steel, a row of the steel sheet pile wall friction table printed in UFC 3-220-20 Table 4-1, p. 184, EM 1110-2-2504 Table 3-3, p. 3-4, and the USS Steel Sheet Piling Design Manual Table 4, p. 13: 'clean_gravel' 22 deg (clean gravel, gravel-sand mixtures, well-graded rock fill with spalls), 'clean_sand' 17 (clean sand, silty sand-gravel mixture, single size hard rock fill), 'silty_sand' 14 (silty sand, gravel or sand mixed with silt or clay), 'fine_sandy_silt' 11 (fine sandy silt, nonplastic silt); at most friction_angle; not with wall_friction_deg)}. wall_friction_deg or interface_soil is used on both sides by pressure_method 'coulomb' and 'log_spiral'. A layer giving neither takes, with 'log_spiral', the clean_sand row (17 deg, at most its phi') on the passive side when it has no cohesion and no wall friction on the active side or in a layer with cohesion (UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-37 step 1, p. 237: 'Passive pressures for clean coarse grained soils include wall friction (see Table 4-1)'; it ignores wall friction in other soils, so give wall_friction_deg 0 in a silty sand or silt); with 'coulomb' none (UFC 3-220-20 p. 190: passive pressure 'should be calculated using the log spiral method and not the Coulomb method'). The result's choices give each layer's wall friction and its Kp at the other rows and at delta = 0, and where a layer took the clean sand row by default the embedment with none.
surchargefloatoptionalSurface surcharge (kPa). default: 0.0
FOS_passivefloatoptionalFOS applied to passive resistance. default: 1.5
gwt_depth_activefloatoptionalGroundwater depth on the active (retained) side, m below the top of the wall.
gwt_depth_passivefloatoptionalGroundwater depth on the passive (excavated) side, m below the top of the wall, the same datum as gwt_depth_active. A depth less than excavation_depth is water standing in front of the wall above the dredge line: its pressure, gamma_w times the depth below that level, acts on the wall from there down (UFC 3-220-20 Sec. 4-4.1, p. 199: 'Water applies a triangular pressure distribution equivalent to a soil with a unit weight of 62.4 pcf and an earth pressure coefficient of unity') and the soil below the dredge line is submerged (Fig. 4-41, p. 242: water levels can differ on the two sides; its example Fig. 4-43, p. 245, has water 5 ft below the top on both sides). The net water pressure is the retained side's less this side's (Figs. 4-5 and 4-6, p. 183: 'Net water pressure = u = gamma_w z2'), so the same depth on both sides (balanced water) gives none. Left out: the excavation level, or gwt_depth_active where that is deeper (no water on either side when gwt_depth_active is left out too), so no water stands in front of the wall.
pressure_methodstroptionalEarth pressure theory. 'log_spiral' uses Coulomb active + the log-spiral PASSIVE coefficient from log_spiral_source (avoids Coulomb's over-prediction of Kp at high delta/phi). 'coulomb' and 'log_spiral' take each layer's wall friction (layers: wall_friction_deg or interface_soil; what a layer giving neither takes is in the layers description). allowed: rankine, coulomb, log_spiral also read as: caquot_kerisel = log_spiral, logspiral = log_spiral default: "rankine"
log_spiral_sourcestroptionalWith pressure_method 'log_spiral', the printed source of the passive Kp. 'ufc_3_220_20' (default): UFC 3-220-20 (DM 7.2), the source the wall's geometry calls for (pp. 191-193); a sheet pile has a vertical face and the tool takes level ground in front of it, so that is Eq. 4-12 (p. 191), at each layer's wall_friction_deg. 'caquot_kerisel_1948': the Caquot and Kerisel (1948) chart, Kp at delta = phi times the printed reduction factor R(delta/phi), Caltrans Trenching and Shoring Manual Fig. 4-20 (p. 4-30), the method its Sec. 4-6 uses for passive pressure. 'dm7_2_fig_4_12', 'dm7_2_fig_4_13': UFC 3-220-20 Figs. 4-12 (p. 192, theta = 0 curve) and 4-13 (p. 193, beta = 0 row), Kerisel and Absi (1990), drawn for delta/phi' = 0.66 only, so every layer's wall_friction_deg must be 0.66 x its friction_angle; UFC 3-220-20 p. 260 says Kp for a tied-back wall 'should be obtained from Figure 4-12'. 'dm7_2_eq_4_12': Eq. 4-12 by name. They differ: at phi 30, delta/phi 0.66 the 1948 chart gives 5.4, the UFC charts 5.3 and Eq. 4-12 5.1. UFC 3-220-20 footnote 21 (p. 191): the 1982 DM 7.2 charts 'used delta/phi' = 1 along with reduction ratios', which 'were averages that introduced substantial inaccuracy for some cases'; the 1948 chart takes that form (Kp at delta = phi times R). UFC 3-220-20 Table 4-2 (p. 194) is not used: the log-spiral Kp in its row headed delta/phi' = 0.5, 5.3, 8.0, 12 and 20 at phi' = 30, 35, 40 and 45, are Fig. 4-13's values, drawn for delta/phi' = 0.66 (5.30, 8.00, 12.0, 20), and the Coulomb Kp printed beside them, 6.1, 9.8, 18 and 44, are Coulomb's at delta = 0.66 phi' (at 0.5 it gives 5.0, 7.4, 11.8 and 21.4). Eq. 4-12 at delta/phi' = 0.5 gives 4.46, 6.33, 9.33 and 14.3. The tool reads Fig. 4-13 at the 0.66 it is drawn for and Eq. 4-12 at the wall friction given. The result's choices give each layer's Kp from the source used and from the others. allowed: ufc_3_220_20, caquot_kerisel_1948, dm7_2_eq_4_12, dm7_2_fig_4_12, dm7_2_fig_4_13 default: "ufc_3_220_20"
embedment_increasefloatoptionalD / D0, the multiplier on the embedment from moment equilibrium: 1.2 (default), as the Caltrans Trenching and Shoring Manual (7-5.02 step 3, p. 7-11: 'The 20 percent increase is not a factor of safety'; its Example 7-3 takes it after FS 1.3 on the moments) and UFC 3-220-20 (Fig. 4-41 step 6, p. 242: 'Increase D by 20% to allow for dredging, scour, etc.'; its example Fig. 4-43 takes it after phi'allow = atan(tan 35 deg / 1.5) = 25 deg, Kp 3.6) both print it beside a factor of safety on the passive side. FOS_passive divides the passive pressure, UFC Fig. 4-41 step 2's alternative to phi'allow. Must be >= 1.0. default: 1.2

10.1.10 soe — Support of excavation

braced_excavation — Multi-level braced excavation analysis (Terzaghi-Peck).

ParameterTypeDescription
excavation_depthfloatrequiredExcavation depth (m).
layersarrayrequiredArray of soil-layer dicts, top down: {thickness (m, required), unit_weight (kN/m3, required), friction_angle (deg, default 30), cohesion (kPa, default 0), soil_type ('sand' or 'clay', also 'soft_clay' or 'stiff_clay'; REQUIRED on each layer above the excavation base, refused if missing)}. soil_type picks the Terzaghi-Peck apparent-pressure envelope: the one for sands where sand is the thicker over the excavation depth, else the one for clays, soft to medium or stiff fissured by the average N = gamma*H/cu over the excavation depth (> 4 soft). The embedment below the excavation uses each layer's own phi and c. The last layer continues below its thickness.
supportsarrayoptionalSupport levels [{depth (m), support_type ('strut' or 'anchor'), spacing (m), angle_deg}].
surchargefloatoptionalSurface surcharge (kPa); added to the envelope as Ka*q (sand) or q (clay). default: 10.0
gwt_depthfloatoptionalGroundwater depth behind the wall (m); water pressure is added for sand envelopes.
gwt_depth_excavationfloatoptionalGroundwater depth on the excavation side (m from top of wall), never above the excavation base. Default: same as gwt_depth.
FOS_passivefloatoptionalEmbedment FS, MR = FS*MD about the lowest support (Caltrans uses 1.3). default: 1.5
embedment_increasefloatoptionalMultiplier on the free-earth-support embedment. default: 1.0
support_load_methodstroptionalHow the support loads and span moments are taken: 'hinge' (default) = the Caltrans Trenching and Shoring Manual's hinge method (Sec. 8-4.02, Fig. 8-7, p. 8-10; Example 8-2): the load above the first support to it, its moment M1 there carried by the span below (T1L = P/2 + M1/L, T2U = P/2 - M1/L), simple spans between supports, and the lowest support's load from below by free earth support about it (FS = 1; one support: the whole wall about it); 'hinge_subgrade' = GEC-4's hinge method (Fig. 38, p. 79): the same above, simple spans down to the excavation base, which takes a subgrade reaction R; 'simple_spans' = UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-54 (p. 257): simple spans between supports, the span below the lowest support a cantilever on it (UFC's 80 % moment reduction not applied). Choices give the other methods' loads. allowed: hinge, hinge_subgrade, simple_spans default: "hinge"
stiff_clay_coefficientfloatoptionalThe stiff clay envelope's ordinate as a multiple of gamma H, 0.2 to 0.4: 0.4 (default) per UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-53 (p. 256, internally supported walls, N0 <= 4); 0.2 'when movements are minimal and the construction period is short' (UFC); the Caltrans Trenching and Shoring Manual (Eq. 8-3-2, p. 8-5) leaves it between 0.2 and 0.4 to judgment. Read for stiff fissured clay (N <= 4) and, for 4 < N < 6, as the ordinate soft clay must reach (Caltrans Sec. 8-3.02: the larger of the two). default: 0.4
passive_theorystroptionalThe passive coefficient below the excavation: 'rankine' (default) = Rankine's Kp, no wall friction, as the Caltrans Trenching and Shoring Manual's examples take it where the wall friction is zero (pp. 7-18, 7-27), with its note that Rankine 'tends to underestimate the passive earth pressure' and Sec. 4-6 (p. 4-28): Rankine 'should not be used ... because it does not account for wall friction'; 'log_spiral' (or 'caquot_kerisel', the same) = the log-spiral Kp of log_spiral_source at passive_wall_friction_deg in each layer below the excavation. Choices give the other theory's Kp and embedment. allowed: rankine, log_spiral, caquot_kerisel also read as: logspiral = log_spiral, log-spiral = log_spiral default: "rankine"
log_spiral_sourcestroptionalWith passive_theory 'log_spiral', the printed source of Kp, as earth_pressure_coefficient takes it: 'ufc_3_220_20' (default) = UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 4-12 (p. 191), its log-spiral Kp for a vertical face and level ground at any wall friction; 'caquot_kerisel_1948' = the Caltrans Trenching and Shoring Manual Fig. 4-20 chart (its Example 8-1), and 'dm7_2_eq_4_12' = UFC Eq. 4-12 by name, both needing passive_wall_friction_deg given; 'dm7_2_fig_4_12' / 'dm7_2_fig_4_13' = UFC's charts, drawn for delta/phi' 0.66 only. allowed: ufc_3_220_20, caquot_kerisel_1948, dm7_2_eq_4_12, dm7_2_fig_4_12, dm7_2_fig_4_13 default: "ufc_3_220_20"
passive_wall_friction_degfloatoptionalWith passive_theory 'log_spiral', the wall friction delta (deg) in every layer below the excavation, at most its phi': the engineer's call (UFC 3-220-20 Table 4-1, p. 184; Caltrans Example 8-1 takes 15 deg on phi 30). Left out: delta/phi' = 0.66 (UFC p. 191, 'a common assumption') in a layer without cohesion, none in a layer with cohesion (UFC Fig. 4-37 step 1, p. 237: 'Passive pressures for clean coarse grained soils include wall friction'; in other soils it ignores wall friction); refused with 'caquot_kerisel_1948' or 'dm7_2_eq_4_12', which need it given (Caltrans p. 4-29: 'Given delta'). For soldier piles in coarse-grained soil UFC p. 249 takes KP 'without wall friction': give 0.
FyfloatoptionalSteel yield strength (MPa) for section sizing. default: 345.0
Fb_ratiofloatoptionalAllowable bending stress / Fy for the required section: 0.60 (default) as the Caltrans Trenching and Shoring Manual's examples take it (Example 7-3, p. 7-43; Example 8-1); GEC-4 (p. 81) recommends 0.55 for permanent walls and temporary walls that are critical; 0.66 the Caltrans railroad example (p. 9-20). Choices give the section at each. default: 0.6

cantilever_excavation — Cantilever (unbraced) excavation wall analysis.

ParameterTypeDescription
excavation_depthfloatrequiredExcavation depth (m).
layersarrayrequiredArray of soil-layer dicts, top down: {thickness (m, required), unit_weight (kN/m3, required), friction_angle (deg, default 30), cohesion (kPa, default 0), soil_type (optional and not read here: the cantilever analysis uses each layer's own phi and c; accepted so the same layers serve braced_excavation)}. The last layer continues below its thickness.
surchargefloatoptionalSurface surcharge (kPa). default: 10.0
gwt_depthfloatoptionalGroundwater depth behind the wall (m).
gwt_depth_excavationfloatoptionalGroundwater depth on the excavation side (m from top of wall), never above the excavation base. Default: same as gwt_depth.
FOS_passivefloatoptionalFOS on passive resistance. default: 1.5
embedment_increasefloatoptionalD / D0 (Caltrans/AASHTO 1.2; use 1.0 to carry all safety on FOS_passive). default: 1.2
passive_theorystroptionalThe passive coefficient below the excavation: 'rankine' (default) = Rankine's Kp, no wall friction, as the Caltrans Trenching and Shoring Manual's examples take it where the wall friction is zero (pp. 7-18, 7-27), with its note that Rankine 'tends to underestimate the passive earth pressure' and Sec. 4-6 (p. 4-28): Rankine 'should not be used ... because it does not account for wall friction'; 'log_spiral' (or 'caquot_kerisel', the same) = the log-spiral Kp of log_spiral_source at passive_wall_friction_deg in each layer below the excavation. Choices give the other theory's Kp and embedment. allowed: rankine, log_spiral, caquot_kerisel also read as: logspiral = log_spiral, log-spiral = log_spiral default: "rankine"
log_spiral_sourcestroptionalWith passive_theory 'log_spiral', the printed source of Kp, as earth_pressure_coefficient takes it: 'ufc_3_220_20' (default) = UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 4-12 (p. 191), its log-spiral Kp for a vertical face and level ground at any wall friction; 'caquot_kerisel_1948' = the Caltrans Trenching and Shoring Manual Fig. 4-20 chart (its Example 8-1), and 'dm7_2_eq_4_12' = UFC Eq. 4-12 by name, both needing passive_wall_friction_deg given; 'dm7_2_fig_4_12' / 'dm7_2_fig_4_13' = UFC's charts, drawn for delta/phi' 0.66 only. allowed: ufc_3_220_20, caquot_kerisel_1948, dm7_2_eq_4_12, dm7_2_fig_4_12, dm7_2_fig_4_13 default: "ufc_3_220_20"
passive_wall_friction_degfloatoptionalWith passive_theory 'log_spiral', the wall friction delta (deg) in every layer below the excavation, at most its phi': the engineer's call (UFC 3-220-20 Table 4-1, p. 184; Caltrans Example 8-1 takes 15 deg on phi 30). Left out: delta/phi' = 0.66 (UFC p. 191, 'a common assumption') in a layer without cohesion, none in a layer with cohesion (UFC Fig. 4-37 step 1, p. 237: 'Passive pressures for clean coarse grained soils include wall friction'; in other soils it ignores wall friction); refused with 'caquot_kerisel_1948' or 'dm7_2_eq_4_12', which need it given (Caltrans p. 4-29: 'Given delta'). For soldier piles in coarse-grained soil UFC p. 249 takes KP 'without wall friction': give 0.
FyfloatoptionalSteel yield strength (MPa) for section sizing. default: 345.0
Fb_ratiofloatoptionalAllowable bending stress / Fy for the required section: 0.60 (default) as the Caltrans Trenching and Shoring Manual's examples take it (Example 7-3, p. 7-43; Example 8-1); GEC-4 (p. 81) recommends 0.55 for permanent walls and temporary walls that are critical; 0.66 the Caltrans railroad example (p. 9-20). Choices give the section at each. default: 0.6

apparent_pressure — Terzaghi-Peck apparent earth pressure envelope.

ParameterTypeDescription
excavation_depthfloatrequiredExcavation depth (m).
layersarrayrequiredArray of soil-layer dicts, top down: {thickness (m, required), unit_weight (kN/m3, required), friction_angle (deg, default 30), cohesion (kPa, default 0), soil_type ('sand' or 'clay', also 'soft_clay' or 'stiff_clay'; REQUIRED on each layer above the excavation base, refused if missing)}. soil_type picks the Terzaghi-Peck apparent-pressure envelope: the one for sands where sand is the thicker over the excavation depth, else the one for clays, soft to medium or stiff fissured by the average N = gamma*H/cu over the excavation depth (> 4 soft). The embedment below the excavation uses each layer's own phi and c. The last layer continues below its thickness.
surchargefloatoptionalSurface surcharge (kPa); not part of the envelope (braced_excavation adds it). default: 0.0
gwt_depthfloatoptionalGroundwater depth (m); the sand envelope uses the effective unit weight below it.
stiff_clay_coefficientfloatoptionalThe stiff clay envelope's ordinate as a multiple of gamma H, 0.2 to 0.4: 0.4 (default) per UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-53 (p. 256, internally supported walls, N0 <= 4); 0.2 'when movements are minimal and the construction period is short' (UFC); the Caltrans Trenching and Shoring Manual (Eq. 8-3-2, p. 8-5) leaves it between 0.2 and 0.4 to judgment. Read for stiff fissured clay (N <= 4) and, for 4 < N < 6, as the ordinate soft clay must reach (Caltrans Sec. 8-3.02: the larger of the two). default: 0.4

select_wall_section — Select lightest HP/sheet/W section for demand.

ParameterTypeDescription
required_Sx_cm3floatrequiredRequired section modulus (cm3).
section_typestroptionalSection family. allowed: hp, sheet_pile, w default: "hp"

check_basal_heave — Basal heave stability check (Terzaghi, Bjerrum-Eide, or Caltrans force-balance).

ParameterTypeDescription
HfloatrequiredExcavation depth (m).
cufloatrequiredUndrained shear strength (kPa).
gammafloatrequiredSoil unit weight (kN/m3).
methodstroptionalCheck method. terzaghi = GEC-4 Eq. 35 (p. 106), FS = Nc Su / (gamma H + q - sqrt(2) Su H / B), a cut of infinite length with Nc from GEC-4 Fig. 51(c) (B/L = 0); with B left out (0), Eq. 37, FS = Nc Su / (gamma H + q), Nc 5.14; with B, parameters.FOS_ufc_fig_2_7b and a note give UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 2-7(b)'s FBH = (5.7 Su B1 + Su H) / ((gamma H + q) B1), B1 = 0.7B, which adds the side strength to the resistance and stays finite in a narrow cut where Eq. 35 runs high (UFC p. 73 note 10). bjerrum_eide requires Be+Le (inverted-footing bearing ratio, NO side shear; Nc from the Caltrans Fig. 10-15 and Eq. 10-3-4). caltrans requires B (Caltrans Sec. 10-3 force balance with sidewall shear S=cu*H and the 0.7B block; optional L for Eq. 10-3-4's rectangular Nc). allowed: terzaghi, bjerrum_eide, caltrans default: "terzaghi"
BfloatoptionalExcavation width (m); terzaghi (0 = a very wide cut, GEC-4 Eq. 37) and caltrans methods. default: 0.0
LfloatoptionalExcavation length (m) for the caltrans rectangular Nc (Eq. 10-3-4; default square).
NcfloatoptionalExplicit chart-read bearing factor Nc (caltrans); default Bjerrum and Eide's, the Caltrans Fig. 10-15 square curve at H/B times 0.84 + 0.16 B/L (Eq. 10-3-4).
BefloatoptionalExcavation width (m). REQUIRED for bjerrum_eide.
LefloatoptionalExcavation length (m). REQUIRED for bjerrum_eide.
width_factorfloatoptionalFailure-block width as a fraction of B (caltrans). Default 0.7 (Terzaghi). A hard layer D below the base within 0.7B: give D / B (Caltrans Sec. 10-3.01, p. 10-19). default: 0.7
q_surchargefloatoptionalSurface surcharge (kPa). default: 0.0
FOS_requiredfloatoptionalRequired FOS. default: 1.5

fhwa_apparent_pressure_anchored_wall — FHWA/GEC-4 apparent-pressure anchored-wall design (tributary method): apparent envelope pe + tributary anchor loads + subgrade reaction + hinge moments + anchor design loads.

ParameterTypeDescription
HfloatrequiredTotal wall height (m).
anchor_depthsarrayrequiredDepths of the anchor levels below the top of wall (m), e.g. [2.5, 6.25].
gammafloatrequiredRetained-soil unit weight (kN/m3).
phifloatrequiredRetained-soil friction angle (deg).
surchargefloatoptionalUniform surface surcharge q (kPa); adds ps = Ka*q. default: 0.0
spacingfloatoptionalHorizontal anchor spacing (m) for the design loads. default: 1.0
inclination_degfloatoptionalAnchor inclination from horizontal (deg). default: 0.0
KafloatoptionalActive coefficient override (default Rankine Ka).
KpfloatoptionalPassive coefficient below the excavation, for the embedment (default Rankine; pass a log-spiral value).
FOS_embedmentfloatoptionalEmbedment FS, MR = FS*MD about the anchor, the lowest with two or more (Caltrans T&S Manual Secs. 8-4.01 and 8-4.02). default: 1.3

check_bottom_blowout — Bottom blowout (hydraulic uplift) check.

hw_excessfloatrequiredExcess water head (m).
gamma_soilfloatrequiredSubmerged (buoyant) unit weight of the soil plug (kN/m3); the formula is FOS = gamma_soil * D_embed / (gamma_w * hw_excess), so do not give the total unit weight.
gamma_wfloatoptionalWater unit weight (kN/m3). default: 9.81
FOS_requiredfloatoptionalRequired FOS. default: 1.5
