design_ground_anchor — Ground anchor design per GEC-4 (FHWA-IF-99-015) Sec. 5.3: unbonded and bond lengths, tendon, test load.

ParameterTypeDescription
design_load_kNfloatrequiredDesign anchor load (kN).
anchor_depthfloatrequiredAnchor depth (m).
excavation_depthfloatrequiredExcavation depth H (m); the unbonded length extends the greater of 1.5 m and H/5 behind the critical potential failure surface (GEC-4 App. E, p. E-15).
phi_degfloatrequiredSoil friction angle (degrees): the critical potential failure surface rises from the corner of the excavation at 45 + phi/2 (GEC-4 Sec. 5.3.2, p. 65, walls in cohesionless soils).
soil_typestroptionalGround of the bond zone, a printed row: soil from GEC-4 Table 6 (p. 71; small diameter straight shaft gravity-grouted anchors; SPT corrected for overburden): sand_gravel_loose 145, sand_gravel_medium 220, sand_gravel_dense 290, sand_loose 100, sand_medium 145, sand_dense 190, sand_silt_loose 70, sand_silt_medium 100, sand_silt_dense 130, silt_clay_stiff 30, silt_clay_hard 60 kN/m (silt-clay mixtures with low plasticity); rock from Table 8 (p. 74): granite_basalt 730, dolomitic_limestone 580, soft_limestone 440, sandstone 440, slates_hard_shales 360, soft_shales 150 kN/m. The ultimate load transfer is per metre of bond length (the hole diameter does not enter it). Also sets FOS_bond's default and the minimum bond length (soil or rock). With bond_stress_kPa or load_transfer_kN_per_m it is required, and may be the ground alone, 'soil' or 'rock': the value does not say the ground (GEC-4 Table 7, p. 73: 0.15 to 3.1 MPa in rock, 0.03 to 1.38 MPa in soil). allowed: sand_gravel_loose, sand_gravel_medium, sand_gravel_dense, sand_loose, sand_medium, sand_dense, sand_silt_loose, sand_silt_medium, sand_silt_dense, silt_clay_stiff, silt_clay_hard, granite_basalt, dolomitic_limestone, soft_limestone, sandstone, slates_hard_shales, soft_shales, soil, rock default: "sand_medium"
tendon_typestroptionalTendon type. Bar or strand sets the minimum unbonded length (GEC-4 p. 67: 3 m bar, 4.5 m strand) and, in rock, the minimum bond length (p. E-15: 3 m bar, 4.5 m strand; 4.5 m for both in soil). allowed: strand_13mm, strand_15mm, bar_26mm, bar_32mm, bar_36mm, bar_44mm default: "strand_15mm"
anchor_angle_degfloatoptionalAnchor inclination below horizontal (deg). default: 15.0
load_transfer_kN_per_mfloatoptionalUltimate load transfer per metre of bond length (kN/m), in place of soil_type's, e.g. as verified by preproduction performance tests (GEC-4 p. 75). Not with bond_stress_kPa. Give soil_type with it (a row, or 'soil' or 'rock').
bond_stress_kPafloatoptionalAverage ultimate bond stress at the grout/ground interface (kPa), e.g. from GEC-4 Table 7 (p. 73, after PTI 1996), in place of soil_type's load transfer: multiplied by the perimeter of drill_diameter_mm. Not with load_transfer_kN_per_m. Give soil_type with it (a row, or 'soil' or 'rock').
drill_diameter_mmfloatoptionalDrill hole diameter (mm): the perimeter a given bond_stress_kPa acts on (GEC-4 p. 72: capacity estimates on the as-drilled hole diameter; p. 70: generally less than 150 mm, hollow stem augered anchors about 300 mm). Not used with a load transfer per metre. default: 150.0
FOS_bondfloatoptionalFOS on the ultimate load transfer. Default depends on soil_type: 3.0 for the Table 8 rock rows and 'rock' (competent rock, GEC-4 p. 74), else 2.0 (soil, p. 71). GEC-4 also gives 2.0 for weak rocks such as clay shales, intermediate geomaterials of unconfined compressive strength 0.5 to 5.0 MPa (p. 74).
lock_off_pctfloatoptionalLock-off load fraction of design load. Reported as tendon.lock_off_kN only; it does not size the tendon. default: 0.8
max_load_pctfloatoptionalDesign-load limit as a fraction of the tendon's SMTS (GEC-4 Sec. 5.3.8, p. 77: 0.60). The tendon is also sized so the test load (test_load_factor x design load) is at most 0.80 SMTS, which allows 0.80 / test_load_factor SMTS (0.60 at 1.33, 0.53 at 1.50); tendon.governed_by names the limit that sized it. default: 0.6
test_load_factorfloatoptionalTest load as a multiple of the design load: the maximum load of the proof and performance tests, carried by the tendon at no more than 0.80 SMTS. GEC-4 Sec. 7.4.2.2 (p. 143): 1.20 to 1.50, 1.33 commonly used for permanent and 1.20 for temporary applications, 1.50 for potentially creeping soils; Tables 21 and 22 (pp. 144, 147) test to 1.33, which may be set at 1.20 for a temporary support of excavation. Default 1.33, the stricter; at max_load_pct 0.60, 1.20 gives the same tendon. default: 1.33

10.1.11 retaining_walls — Retaining walls (cantilever & MSE)

cantilever_wall — Full cantilever retaining wall stability analysis (sliding, overturning, eccentricity, bearing); the backfill is taken as drained unless water_table_depth puts a water table behind the wall.

ParameterTypeDescription
wall_heightfloatrequiredTOTAL wall height H (m), measured from the UNDERSIDE of the base slab (footing) to the top of the stem: H = base_thickness + stem height. The active thrust acts over H on the vertical plane through the back of the heel. If you know the height retained above the top of the footing, add base_thickness (4.0 m retained on a 0.5 m footing is wall_height 4.5).
gamma_backfillfloatrequiredBackfill unit weight (kN/m3).
phi_backfillfloatrequiredBackfill friction angle (degrees).
base_widthfloatoptionalBase width (m). Auto-sized if omitted.
toe_lengthfloatoptionalToe length (m). Auto-sized if omitted.
stem_thickness_topfloatoptionalStem thickness at top (m). default: 0.3
stem_thickness_basefloatoptionalStem thickness at base (m).
base_thicknessfloatoptionalBase slab thickness (m). Auto-sized if omitted: H/10 (FHWA NHI-06-089 Fig. 10-16(a), p. 10-38: H/12 to H/10).
stem_batterstroptionalWhich face of a tapered stem (thicker at its base than at its top) is battered. 'back' (default): the front face vertical, the backfill over the battered back counted as resisting weight. 'front': the back face vertical, as UFC 3-220-20 App. B-1 Fig. B-2 (p. 598) and FHWA NHI-06-089 Fig. 10-16(a) and Example 10-3 (p. 10-52) draw it. allowed: back, front default: "back"
embedment_depthfloatoptionalDepth of the underside of the base below the ground in front of the wall, Df (m), 0 to wall_height. Left out: the base thickness, the ground in front at the top of the base. Deeper, the soil over the toe counts as resisting weight (UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-27, p. 220: 'Weight includes ... weight of soil above footing'; App. B-1.3, p. 599), at gamma_foundation, and include_passive's passive resistance acts over Df.
has_shear_keybooloptionalInclude a shear key below the base (with key_depth). It acts only with include_passive: the sliding check then takes the passive resistance over the depth of the key only, from the underside of the base (depth embedment_depth below the ground in front) to the bottom of the key (embedment_depth + key_depth), the trapezoid UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-29 draws below the toe (p. 224: 'the passive pressure is applied only along the depth of the key and not along the entire burial depth of the wall'; GEC-6 Fig. 5-22 likewise), in place of the passive over the embedment; with the undrained rule it counts cu, as GEC-6 Eq. 5-41 (p. 101) counts Pp in front of the key. GEC-6 Sec. 5.4 (pp. 100-101): keys in granular soils 'are not very efficient in developing passive pressures'; its key method is for stiff, overconsolidated clays and soft rock. UFC: 'it is also prudent to consider some amount of future excavation in front of the wall'. default: false
key_depthfloatoptionalShear key depth below the underside of the base slab (m). default: 0.0
surchargefloatoptionalUniform LIVE-load surcharge on the backfill (kPa), e.g. traffic. Its thrust K*q*H drives every check. Over the heel it is NOT a resisting force in sliding, overturning or the eccentricity check by default (live_load_resists), and it does load the base in the bearing pressures (surcharge_in_bearing). A pavement or slab is not a surcharge here: model it as retained soil up to the ground surface (it then rests on the heel and resists like the backfill). Any other surcharge is transient live load: its thrust counts in every check, but its weight over the heel does not resist sliding or overturning. A permanent load you want carried as a surcharge goes in dead_load_surcharge. default: 0.0
dead_load_surchargefloatoptionalUniform DEAD-load (permanent) surcharge on the backfill (kPa), a permanent load that is not part of the retained soil (FHWA NHI-06-089 Sec. 10.4.2). Pavements and slabs are normally modelled as retained soil up to the ground surface instead. Its thrust drives every check, added to the live load's. Over the heel it is not a resisting force by default (dead_load_resists=true counts it as resisting weight in sliding and overturning); it loads the base in the bearing pressures (surcharge_in_bearing). default: 0.0
live_load_resistsbooloptionalCount the live-load surcharge over the heel (and its share of a sloped or Coulomb thrust's vertical component) as a resisting force in sliding, overturning and the eccentricity check. Default false: FHWA NHI-06-089 Sec. 10.5.5 (p. 10-43), 'the live load surcharge is not considered as a stabilizing force over the heel of the wall when sliding resistance is being checked'; UFC 3-220-20 App. B-1.2 (p. 597), 'For overturning and sliding checks, it is assumed that the traffic pressure does not act over the wall heel'. true = the free body with the load over the heel, which none of these references uses for a live load. The result's choices say which was used. default: false
dead_load_resistsbooloptionalCount the dead-load surcharge over the heel as a resisting force in sliding, overturning and the eccentricity check. Default false: FHWA NHI-06-089 Sec. 10.5.3 (p. 10-41), for CIP semi-gravity walls the surcharge loads are 'conservatively neglected within the width of the base slab since they contribute to overturning and sliding resistance'. true = counted as a permanent load: GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-22 (AASHTO), loads that increase sliding resistance are included 'only if those loads are permanent'. default: false
surcharge_in_bearingbooloptionalCount the surcharges over the heel in the bearing pressures (q_toe, q_heel, FOS_bearing). Default true: UFC 3-220-20 App. B-1.6 (p. 602), 'it is conservative to include the surcharge over the heel of the wall, if this is possible to occur, in the bearing capacity check'; GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-26. false = the surcharge taken as located behind the heel (NHI-06-089 p. 10-41). default: true
backfill_slopefloatoptionalBackfill slope angle (degrees), rising away from the wall. A backfill descending away from the wall (below 0) is refused. default: 0.0
c_backfillfloatoptionalBackfill cohesion (kPa). The active pressure Ka sigma_v - 2 c sqrt(Ka) is taken as zero where it is negative, the tension zone (UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-5 Note A; FHWA NHI-06-089 p. 10-15); the result's choices give the thrust with c neglected and with NHI's minimum active pressure of 5z kN/m2 beside it. default: 0.0
phi_foundationfloatoptionalFoundation soil friction angle (deg), FULL value — the sliding check applies delta_b = (2/3)*phi_foundation INTERNALLY. Do NOT pre-reduce (passing 2/3*phi here double-counts the reduction). To set the base friction angle directly, use delta_base instead. Defaults to phi_backfill. phi_foundation = 0 gives an undrained strength (c_foundation = cu): sliding_cohesion then defaults to 'undrained'.
c_foundationfloatoptionalFoundation soil cohesion (kPa), FULL value, no 2/3 factor. The sliding check counts it by sliding_cohesion: NOT at all with 'drained' (the default unless phi_foundation is 0), as the undrained shear strength cu with 'undrained' (ca = cu) or 'friction_plus_adhesion' (Ca from UFC 3-220-20 Table 4-1). To set the adhesion directly, use base_adhesion. default: 0.0
sliding_cohesionstroptionalHow the sliding check counts the foundation soil's cohesion, by the rule a reference prints. Default depends on phi_foundation: 'undrained' when phi_foundation is 0 (c_foundation is then cu), else 'drained'. 'drained': R = V tan delta_b, c_foundation NOT counted (GEC-6 Sec. 5.4 Eq. 5-38, p. 100: 'Equations 5-38 and 5-39 should not be combined for use at the same time'; EN 1997-1 6.5.3(10): 'Any effective cohesion c' should be neglected'). 'undrained': R = ca B alone, no friction, ca = c_foundation taken as the undrained shear strength cu, or base_adhesion (GEC-6 Eq. 5-39: 'ca is typically taken as equal to the undrained shear strength'). 'friction_plus_adhesion': R = V tan delta_b + Ca Be, Ca from UFC 3-220-20 Table 4-1 (p. 184) at c_foundation taken as the undrained shear strength (up to 191.5 kPa), or base_adhesion; Be = B - 2e, the effective base width (UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-27 and Sec. 4-5.1.3, p. 223, which adds that the minimum FS 'may also need to be increased when base adhesion is included'). The result's choices give the rule used, its basis and each other rule's FOS_sliding on the same wall. allowed: drained, undrained, friction_plus_adhesion
delta_basefloatoptionalBase interface friction angle delta_b (deg), used DIRECTLY in the sliding check with NO 2/3 factor. Overrides the (2/3)*phi_foundation default. delta_b = phi_foundation for concrete cast against the ground (GEC-6 Sec. 5.4, p. 99: tan delta 'will be equal to the tangent of the friction angle (tan phi) for the soil supporting the footing'). The result's choices state the delta_b used, its basis and the other reading. Refused with sliding_cohesion 'undrained', which counts no friction.
base_adhesionfloatoptionalBase adhesion ca (kPa), used DIRECTLY with sliding_cohesion 'undrained' (in place of cu) or 'friction_plus_adhesion' (in place of the UFC 3-220-20 Table 4-1 value). Refused with 'drained', which counts no adhesion: give sliding_cohesion with it.
include_passivebooloptionalInclude passive resistance in front of the wall in the sliding check (Rankine's Kp unless passive_theory says otherwise; UFC 3-220-20 p. 219: 'typically ignored', and with it considered FSL >= 2.0, Fig. 4-27, so FOS_sliding_required then defaults to 2.0), acting over the embedment, from the ground in front to the underside of the base (embedment_depth, default the base thickness), or with has_shear_key over the depth of the key only (from embedment_depth to embedment_depth + key_depth below the ground in front, UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-29). With the undrained rule it counts the foundation's cu, Kp sigma_v + 2 cu sqrt(Kp) (UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 4-7, p. 178, and p. 181); with the other rules c_foundation is not counted in it (p. 179). default: false
gamma_foundationfloatoptionalFoundation soil unit weight (kN/m3): the passive resistance in front of the wall and the soil over the toe (embedment_depth below the top of the base). Defaults to gamma_backfill.
passive_theorystroptionalWith include_passive, the passive coefficient in front of the wall: 'rankine' (default) = Rankine's Kp, no wall friction; 'log_spiral' (or 'caquot_kerisel', the same) = the log-spiral Kp of log_spiral_source at passive_wall_friction_deg. UFC 3-220-20 (Sec. 4-5.1, Figs. 4-27 and 4-29, pp. 219-224) names no theory for it; choices give the other theory's Kp and FOS_sliding and the FOS with no passive. allowed: rankine, log_spiral, caquot_kerisel also read as: logspiral = log_spiral, log-spiral = log_spiral default: "rankine"
log_spiral_sourcestroptionalWith passive_theory 'log_spiral', the printed source of Kp, as earth_pressure_coefficient takes it: 'ufc_3_220_20' (default) = UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 4-12 (p. 191), its log-spiral Kp for a vertical face and level ground at any wall friction; 'caquot_kerisel_1948' = the Caltrans Trenching and Shoring Manual Fig. 4-20 chart, and 'dm7_2_eq_4_12' = UFC Eq. 4-12 by name, both needing passive_wall_friction_deg given; 'dm7_2_fig_4_12' / 'dm7_2_fig_4_13' = UFC's charts, drawn for delta/phi' 0.66 only. allowed: ufc_3_220_20, caquot_kerisel_1948, dm7_2_eq_4_12, dm7_2_fig_4_12, dm7_2_fig_4_13 default: "ufc_3_220_20"
passive_wall_friction_degfloatoptionalWith passive_theory 'log_spiral', the wall friction delta in front of the wall (deg), 0 to phi_foundation: the engineer's call (UFC 3-220-20 Table 4-1, p. 184). Left out: delta/phi' = 0.66 (UFC p. 191, 'a common assumption'); refused with 'caquot_kerisel_1948' or 'dm7_2_eq_4_12', which need it given (Caltrans p. 4-29: 'Given delta').
q_allowablefloatoptionalAllowable bearing pressure (kPa) for the bearing check. On soil (bearing_pressure 'uniform', the default) it is compared with q_eq = V/(B - 2e), the uniform pressure over the effective width B' = B - 2e, so give the allowable bearing pressure for B' (GEC-6 Sec. 6.4.2, p. 119: 'Bf in Equation 5-14 may be replaced by B'f'); with 'linear' (the default with founded_on_rock), with the larger edge pressure. Without it the bearing check is NOT RUN: FOS_bearing and passes_bearing are null and checks_not_run lists 'bearing' (q_toe / q_heel are still reported).
gamma_concretefloatoptionalConcrete unit weight (kN/m3). Default 23.6, 150 pcf, as UFC 3-220-20 App. B-1.3 (p. 599) and FHWA NHI-06-089 Example 10-3 (p. 10-53) take it. default: 23.6
FOS_sliding_requiredfloatoptionalRequired sliding FOS; the check passes at or above it. Default depends on include_passive: 1.5 (GEC-6 Eq. 5-40, p. 100; UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-27; FHWA NHI-06-089 Fig. 10-17), 2.0 with the passive resistance counted (UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-27, p. 220, and Sec. 4-5.1.3, p. 223: 'If passive resistance is included, the minimum FSL should be increased to 2.0'). The result's choices say which was taken.
FOS_overturning_requiredfloatoptionalRequired overturning FOS; the check passes at or above it. Default depends on founded_on_rock: 2.0 on soil, 1.5 on rock (FHWA NHI-06-089 Sec. 10.5.5, p. 10-44: 'approximately of 2.0 for soils and 1.5 for rocks'; GEC-6 Sec. 7.3, p. 124: 'greater than about 2.0 for permanent dead loads'). UFC 3-220-20 Sec. 4-5.1.2 (p. 223) asks FOT >= 1.5 for any wall.
pressure_methodstroptionalEarth pressure theory. The active thrust acts on the vertical plane through the back of the heel. 'rankine' (default): the thrust parallel to the backfill slope. 'coulomb': Coulomb's Ka (UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 4-10) at the wall friction on that plane, wall_friction_deg, by default the backfill slope (FHWA NHI-06-089 p. 10-20 and Example 10-3; delta = 0 behind level backfill). At that default Coulomb's Ka on a vertical plane is Rankine's (sloped) Ka, the same thrust (NHI Example 10-3's 0.35 at phi 30, beta 10 is both), so 'coulomb' changes the result only with wall_friction_deg given. allowed: rankine, coulomb default: "rankine"
wall_friction_degfloatoptionalWall friction delta on the vertical plane through the back of the heel (deg), with pressure_method 'coulomb', 0 to phi_backfill. Left out: the backfill slope (FHWA NHI-06-089 p. 10-20: on that plane 'there is soil-to-soil contact ... it is generally conservative to assume that the earth pressure is parallel to the slope of the backfill'). Refused with 'rankine'. The result's choices give the delta used and the other reading's Ka.
interface_gap_possiblebooloptionalWhether water or air can reach the base-clay interface. With sliding_cohesion 'undrained' (an undrained clay under the base) the base resistance is then held to 0.4 V (EN 1997-1 Sec. 6.5.3(12)P, Eq. 6.5, p. 65). GEC-6 and UFC 3-220-20 print no such limit. Refused with the other rules. The result's choices give FOS_sliding under the other reading. default: false
founded_on_rockbooloptionalWhether the wall is founded on rock. On rock the eccentricity limit is B/4, the middle half, in place of B/6 (GEC-6 Sec. 6.4.1, p. 119; UFC 3-220-20 Sec. 4-5.1.2, p. 223; FHWA NHI-06-089 Fig. 10-17), FOS_overturning_required defaults to 1.5 and bearing_pressure to 'linear'. default: false
water_table_depthfloatoptionalDepth of a level water table behind the wall below the top of the backfill at the stem (m), 0 or more (0 = water at the top of the backfill). Left out: no water table, the backfill drained (FHWA NHI-06-089 Sec. 10.5.3, p. 10-41: 'If adequate drainage measures are provided, the hydrostatic pressure due to groundwater behind the wall generally need not be considered. However, hydrostatic pressure must be considered for portions of the wall below the level of the weep holes unless a deeper drainage system is provided behind the base of the wall'). Given: below it the earth pressure is on the buoyant unit weight gamma_sat - gamma_w and the water pressure gamma_w z is added, horizontal (UFC 3-220-20 Sec. 4-4.1 and Fig. 4-16(a), pp. 199-202; FHWA NHI-06-089 Fig. 10-12, p. 10-27: 'should consider the greatest unbalanced water head anticipated'); the water pressure under the base (base_uplift) comes off V in sliding and adds to the overturning moment. In front of the wall no water is taken above the underside of the base. At or below the underside of the base (wall_height or deeper) it changes nothing. The result's choices give the drained backfill's FOS beside it.
gamma_sat_backfillfloatoptionalWith water_table_depth, the backfill's saturated unit weight below the water table (kN/m3), more than gamma_w (9.81). Left out: gamma_backfill, as UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-16(a) (p. 202) takes gamma 125 pcf above the water table and gamma_b 62.5 pcf below it; against a larger gamma_sat that errs on the safe side for sliding and overturning where the heel carries soil below the water table, on the unsafe side for the bearing pressures and a wall with little or no heel. Refused without water_table_depth.
base_upliftstroptionalWith water_table_depth, the water pressure under the base (uplift), h_w being the water's height above the underside of the base: 'linear' (default) = gamma_w h_w at the heel to 0 at the toe, no water in front of the wall, a straight line between the heads at the heel and the toe as EM 1110-2-2104 para. E-12 (p. 115) prints a wall's uplift; 'uniform' = gamma_w h_w under the whole base, the same head at both (EM 1110-2-2104 para. E-12, p. 116; UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 5-40, p. 346, a structure below the water table). The uplift comes off V in sliding and its moment about the toe adds to the overturning moment (the choices give the FOS with it taken off the stabilizing moment instead, and the other distribution's). Refused without water_table_depth. allowed: linear, uniform default: "linear"
uplift_in_bearingbooloptionalWith water_table_depth, count the uplift in the bearing pressures (q_toe, q_heel, q_eq, FOS_bearing). Default false: UFC 3-220-20 Sec. 5-3.2 (p. 292), 'Uplift is present on the base of the foundation when the groundwater table is above the bearing elevation. Its effect on the bearing pressure can be conservatively ignored unless sliding or uplift is a concern', on the safe side while the resultant is in the middle third (e <= B/6). true = the effective pressure under the base, the weights less the uplift (EN 1997-1 Sec. 6.5.2.1(3)P, p. 63: 'Water pressures not caused by the foundation load shall be included as actions'). Give q_allowable for the water table at that level (GEC-6 Sec. 5.2.3.2, p. 56). Refused without water_table_depth. default: false
bearing_pressurestroptionalThe bearing pressure compared with q_allowable. Default depends on founded_on_rock: 'uniform' on soil, 'linear' on rock. 'uniform' (the default on soil): q_eq = V / B', B' = B - 2e (GEC-6 Eq. 6-6 and Sec. 6.4.2, p. 119; FHWA NHI-06-089 Fig. 10-17: 'Use uniform stress, qeq, for soils'; UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 4-27 and Sec. 4-5.1.4, p. 224, for soil that is 'relatively ductile'). 'linear' (the default with founded_on_rock): the larger edge pressure of the trapezoid or triangle, q_toe or q_heel (UFC Sec. 4-5.1.4: 'For more brittle materials, such as rock and sensitive clays'; FHWA NHI-06-089 Fig. 10-17). The result's choices give the other pressure's FOS_bearing. allowed: uniform, linear

earth_pressure_coefficient — Lateral earth pressure coefficient Ka/Kp/K0 (Rankine, Coulomb, or the log-spiral passive Kp: by default UFC 3-220-20's Eq. 4-12, Fig. 4-12 or Fig. 4-13 by wall geometry, or the Caquot-Kerisel 1948 chart; K0 also behind sloping ground).

ParameterTypeDescription
phi_degfloatrequiredSoil friction angle (degrees). Alias: phi.
theorystroptionalEarth pressure theory. 'caquot_kerisel' or 'log_spiral' (the same) = the log-spiral PASSIVE coefficient Kp (state must be 'passive'; UFC 3-220-20 p. 190: passive pressure 'should be calculated using the log spiral method and not the Coulomb method', which over-predicts Kp at high wall friction), from the printed source log_spiral_source names: by default UFC 3-220-20's for the wall's geometry, 'caquot_kerisel_1948' for the Caquot-Kerisel (1948) chart. Theory is ignored for at_rest, which uses K0 = (1 - sin(phi)) sqrt(OCR) (EN 1997-1 Eq. 9.1; OCR 1 is Jaky's 1 - sin(phi)), and behind ground rising from the wall (beta_deg > 0) EN 1997-1 Eq. 9.2, K0 (1 + sin beta). allowed: rankine, coulomb, caquot_kerisel, log_spiral also read as: logspiral = log_spiral, log-spiral = log_spiral default: "rankine"
statestroptionalPressure state: Ka (active), Kp (passive), or K0 (at rest). 'caquot_kerisel' requires 'passive'. allowed: active, passive, at_rest default: "active"
delta_degfloatoptionalWall friction angle (degrees): Coulomb and caquot_kerisel only; Rankine and K0 take none and refuse a non-zero value. Alias: delta. Not given, it depends on the theory: Coulomb takes delta = 0, no wall friction; caquot_kerisel takes delta = 0.66 phi' with the UFC 3-220-20 sources (p. 191: 'a common assumption', and the one value its Figs. 4-12 and 4-13 are drawn for), and 'caquot_kerisel_1948' and 'dm7_2_eq_4_12' need it given and refuse a call without it (Caltrans T&S p. 4-29: 'Given delta, beta, and phi'); defaults_used gives the value taken. With the default source, a battered face (theta_deg) or sloping ground (beta_deg) at another wall friction is refused: UFC prints none. The wall friction is the engineer's call (UFC 3-220-20 Table 4-1, p. 184, by wall material and soil; FHWA NHI-06-089 p. 10-17 suggests at most 1/2 phi' for passive); the result's choices give the delta used and the Kp at delta = 0.
beta_degfloatoptionalSlope of the ground behind the wall (degrees, + rising away from the wall; for a passive Kp, the ground in front of the wall). Rankine active, Coulomb, caquot_kerisel (by default UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-13: a vertical face, beta/phi' -0.6 to +1 at delta/phi' 0.66; the Caquot-Kerisel 1948 chart, Caltrans T&S Fig. 4-20: beta/phi -0.9 to +1, phi 10 to 45 deg, any wall friction; Eq. 4-12 and Fig. 4-12 are for level ground) and at_rest (EN 1997-1:2004 Eq. 9.2, p. 104: K0;beta = K0 (1 + sin beta), the horizontal component of the at-rest pressure, for ground sloping upwards from the wall at 0 < beta <= phi'; ground falling away is refused). Rankine passive is for level ground and refuses a non-zero value. Aliases: beta, backfill_slope. default: 0.0
alpha_degfloatoptionalWall back face angle from horizontal (degrees, 90 = vertical; below 90 when the soil overhangs the face, as UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-7 draws a gravity wall's back, where its theta = 90 - alpha_deg is positive). Coulomb only; the others take a vertical back and refuse another value (the log-spiral Kp takes a battered face as theta_deg = 90 - alpha_deg). Alias: alpha. default: 90.0
theta_degfloatoptionalWith theory 'caquot_kerisel' (passive): the wall face's angle from vertical (degrees), UFC 3-220-20's theta (Figs. 4-7, 4-12): positive when the face slopes down into the soil it bears on, so the soil overhangs it (Kp falls; Fig. 4-12 draws the toe of the face farther into the soil than its top), negative the other way (Kp rises); theta_deg = 90 - Coulomb's alpha_deg. A non-zero value reads UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-12 (p. 192): level ground only, theta -30 to +40 deg, delta/phi' 0.66 only, Kp up to 15. Alias: theta. default: 0.0
OCRfloatoptionalOverconsolidation ratio for the at-rest K0 only (state 'at_rest'): EN 1997-1:2004 Sec. 9.5.2(3), Eq. 9.1 (p. 104), K0 = (1 - sin phi') x sqrt(OCR), then Eq. 9.2 behind sloping ground. 1 = normally consolidated (the default; the result's choices say whether it was given or taken as 1). At least 1. The standard says 'The formula should not be used for very high values of OCR' and prints no limit, so the choices quote that for OCR above 1 and leave the call to you. Aliases: ocr, overconsolidation_ratio. Refused with active or passive, which take none. default: 1.0
log_spiral_sourcestroptionalWith theory 'caquot_kerisel', the printed source of the log-spiral passive Kp. 'ufc_3_220_20' (default): UFC 3-220-20 (DM 7.2), the source the wall's geometry calls for (pp. 191-193): Eq. 4-12 (p. 191) for a vertical face and level ground, at any wall friction; Fig. 4-12 (p. 192) for a battered face (theta_deg) with level ground and Fig. 4-13 (p. 193) for a vertical face with sloping ground (beta_deg), both drawn for delta/phi' = 0.66 only. UFC prints nothing for a battered face with sloping ground, nor for those two charts at another wall friction: the default refuses those and names what covers them. 'caquot_kerisel_1948': the Caquot and Kerisel (1948) chart, Kp at delta = phi times the printed reduction factor R(delta/phi), Caltrans Trenching and Shoring Manual Fig. 4-20 (p. 4-30), the method its Sec. 4-6 uses for passive pressure; a vertical wall, level or sloping ground, any wall friction, given as delta_deg. 'dm7_2_eq_4_12', 'dm7_2_fig_4_12', 'dm7_2_fig_4_13': each UFC source on its own. They differ: at phi 30, delta/phi 0.66 on level ground the 1948 chart gives 5.4, Figs. 4-12 and 4-13 5.3, Eq. 4-12 5.1. UFC 3-220-20 footnote 21 (p. 191): the 1982 DM 7.2 charts 'used delta/phi' = 1 along with reduction ratios', which 'were averages that introduced substantial inaccuracy for some cases'; the 1948 chart takes that form. UFC 3-220-20 Table 4-2 (p. 194) is not used: its row headed delta/phi' = 0.5 prints Fig. 4-13's values for 0.66 (5.3, 8.0, 12, 20 at phi' 30, 35, 40, 45) and Coulomb's Kp at 0.66 (6.1, 9.8, 18, 44); Eq. 4-12 at 0.5 gives 4.46, 6.33, 9.33, 14.3. The result's choices give the route taken and each other source's Kp. allowed: ufc_3_220_20, caquot_kerisel_1948, dm7_2_eq_4_12, dm7_2_fig_4_12, dm7_2_fig_4_13 default: "ufc_3_220_20"

mse_wall — MSE wall external + internal stability analysis (GEC-11), level or sloping backfill (incl. a broken backslope), vertical or battered face.

ParameterTypeDescription
wall_heightfloatrequiredDesign wall height H (m): the height of the reinforced soil mass, incl. embedment (GEC-11).
gamma_backfillfloatrequiredBackfill unit weight (kN/m3).
phi_backfillfloatrequiredBackfill friction angle (degrees). GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-10: above 34 deg only from triaxial or direct shear tests on the project's fill, and never above 40 deg; the result warns past either.
reinforcement_namestroptionalBuilt-in reinforcement name for every level, or omit and define a custom reinforcement via reinforcement_type + reinforcement_Tallowable; for a different reinforcement at different levels give reinforcement_per_level instead. The built-ins are reinforcements GEC-11 Vol II's worked examples print, with their Tal as printed: 'ribbed_steel_strip_50x4' (Example E3's 50 x 4 mm ribbed strip), 'welded_wire_grid_w11' (Example E4's 4W11 bar mat, W11 transverse wires at 0.5 ft), 'bar_mat_e4_3w11_w11x0_5', 'bar_mat_e4_4w15_w11x1' and 'bar_mat_e4_4w15_w11x1_5' (E4's other mats, Table E4-7.4, p. E4-18), 'geogrid_gec11_e1_gg1', 'geogrid_gec11_e1_gg2' and 'geogrid_gec11_e1_gg3' (Example E1's geogrids GG-I to GG-III); list_reinforcement gives each one's Tal and its basis. They are the worked examples' reinforcements, not products: where the wall's reinforcement is specified, give it as a custom reinforcement with its own Tal (for a geosynthetic, Tult / RF for the wall's backfill and design life). A steel strip or grid also needs its horizontal spacing (reinforcement_horizontal_spacing) or coverage_ratio. A built-in carries its own Tal, type and bar geometry, and refuses reinforcement_Tallowable, reinforcement_type, reinforcement_thickness and reinforcement_transverse_spacing.
reinforcement_per_levellistoptionalA reinforcement for each level, from the top down, instead of reinforcement_name and the custom reinforcement_* inputs, as GEC-11 Vol II Example E4 takes 4W11 mats at Levels 1, 3 and 4, a 3W11 mat at Level 2 and 4W15 mats from Level 5 down (Table E4-7.4, p. E4-18). One entry a level, as many as the wall has levels (one a depth of level_depths; without it wall_height / reinforcement_spacing rounded down, at reinforcement_spacing x (i + 1/2) from the top); a list of another length is refused, naming the levels' depths. Each entry is a built-in name (see reinforcement_name and list_reinforcement) or a custom reinforcement {Tallowable, type, width, thickness, transverse_spacing, name}, the keys as the reinforcement_* inputs without the prefix. reinforcement_horizontal_spacing and coverage_ratio apply level by level, one number for the wall or a list with one per level. Pullout and rupture take each level's own Tal, width, Rc, F* and alpha, and each level of the result names its reinforcement. Example, a 3 m wall at reinforcement_spacing 0.75 (four levels) with reinforcement_horizontal_spacing 1.524: ["welded_wire_grid_w11", "bar_mat_e4_3w11_w11x0_5", "bar_mat_e4_4w15_w11x1", {"name": "Mat X", "type": "metallic_grid", "Tallowable": 150, "width": 0.457, "thickness": 0.0095, "transverse_spacing": 0.457}]. Left out, one reinforcement holds at every level (reinforcement_name, or the custom reinforcement_* inputs). This tool refuses a wall that mixes steel and geosynthetic levels, its choice: GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-33 and Fig. 4-9 give one failure surface for inextensible and another for extensible reinforcement, and none for a wall with both.
reinforcement_horizontal_spacingfloat or listoptionalCentre-to-centre horizontal spacing Sh (m) of the strips, grids or sheets at one level (GEC-11 Vol I p. 3-12): one number for the wall, or a list with one per reinforcement level from the top down, as GEC-11 Vol II Example E3 changes it with depth (Table E3-7.3, p. E3-19: 2 strips a 5 ft panel at Levels 1 to 8, 3 at Levels 9 to 12); a list must have as many values as the wall has levels. With the reinforcement's width b it gives the coverage ratio Rc = b/Sh (Eq. 3-1), which scales the pullout resistance (Eq. 4-35, p. 4-49) and the tensile resistance (Tal x Rc, p. 4-47) to a metre of wall. Required for a steel strip or grid unless coverage_ratio is given instead; a call with neither is refused, since GEC-11 prints no spacing to assume (Vol II Example E3 uses 50 mm strips at 0.76 and 0.51 m, 2 or 3 per 1.5 m panel). A geosynthetic with neither is a continuous layer, Rc = 1 (p. 3-13). Aliases: Sh, horizontal_spacing.
coverage_ratiofloat or listoptionalCoverage ratio Rc = b/Sh (GEC-11 Vol I Eq. 3-1, p. 3-12), more than 0 and at most 1, given directly instead of reinforcement_horizontal_spacing with reinforcement_width (not both): one number for the wall, or a list with one per reinforcement level from the top down. Alias: Rc.
F_star_testedfloat or listoptionalPullout resistance factor F* from pullout tests on the product in the wall's backfill (GEC-11 Vol I Table 3-6 note (i), p. 3-17; Appendix B): one number at every level, or [[depth_m, F*], ...] with depths below the top of the wall, linear between and the end value beyond. Replaces the empirical F* (Eqs. 3-4 to 3-8); note (i) accepts the empirical values only for Table 3-1 granular fill with Cu >= 4 ('For fill outside these limits, tests must be run'). The result's choices give FOS_pullout at the empirical F* beside it.
alpha_testedfloatoptionalScale effect correction factor alpha from pullout tests on reinforcements of different lengths (GEC-11 Vol I p. 3-16, Appendix B), more than 0 and at most 1. Left out, Table 3-6's alpha for the reinforcement type (p. 3-17): 1.0 for steel strips and grids, 0.8 for geogrids, 0.6 for geotextiles; a reinforcement_type 'geosynthetic' needs it. Table 3-6 note (ii): 'Pullout testing to determine alpha is recommended if alpha shown in table is less than 1.0'. The result's choices give FOS_pullout at the table's alpha beside a tested one.
Cu_backfillfloatoptionalUniformity coefficient Cu = D60/D10 of the reinforced backfill, for the pullout resistance factor of ribbed steel strips: F* = 1.2 + log Cu at the top of the wall, 2.0 maximum, falling linearly to tan phi_backfill at 20 ft (6 m) and below (GEC-11 Vol I Eqs. 3-4 and 3-5, p. 3-20). Left out, Cu = 4 (F* 1.8 at the top): p. 3-20, 'If the specific Cu for the wall backfill is unknown at design time, a Cu = 4 should be assumed' for fills meeting its Sec. 3.1. Table 3-6 note (i) (p. 3-17) accepts these empirical values only for Table 3-1 granular fill with Cu >= 4 ('For fill outside these limits, tests must be run'); a Cu below 4 is computed and the choices say so. A steel grid given t/St and a geosynthetic keep their own F*, which takes no Cu; given with them, Cu is checked against Table 3-6 note (i) only. The result's choices give the F* used and FOS_pullout at the top level and the lowest at the other reading, or for a grid or geosynthetic whether the given Cu is within note (i). With F_star_tested it is in no check: the tested F* replaces the empirical one, and the F* choice says what the Cu bears on (a strip's empirical F* given beside the tested one, and note (i)'s check on the empirical F*). Aliases: Cu, uniformity_coefficient. default: 4.0
reinforcement_typestroptionalCustom reinforcement type, required with reinforcement_Tallowable. Drives the internal-stability lateral-stress-ratio Kr/Ka and pullout F* curves: ribbed STRIP (metallic_strip: Kr/Ka 1.7->1.2, F* 1.2 + log Cu (2.0 at most; Cu_backfill) -> tan-phi), steel bar mat / welded grid (metallic_grid / bar_mat / welded_grid: Kr/Ka 2.5->1.2, F* 20(t/St)->10(t/St), GEC-11 Vol I Eqs. 3-6, 3-7 — reinforcement_thickness=t and reinforcement_transverse_spacing=St are required, or F_star_tested; a grid with neither is refused), or geogrid / geotextile (Kr/Ka 1.0, F* (2/3) tan phi, Eq. 3-8; GEC-11 Fig. 4-10's geosynthetic line 'Does not apply to polymer strip reinforcement'). It also sets the scale effect correction factor alpha, GEC-11 Vol I Table 3-6 (p. 3-17): 1.0 steel, 0.8 geogrid, 0.6 geotextile; 'geosynthetic' (either kind) needs alpha_tested. allowed: metallic_strip, metallic_grid, bar_mat, welded_grid, geogrid, geotextile, geosynthetic also read as: barmat = metallic_grid, welded_wire_grid = metallic_grid, steel_grid = metallic_grid, ribbed_strip = metallic_strip
reinforcement_TallowablefloatoptionalLong-term allowable tensile strength Tal (kN/m) of a custom reinforcement, per metre of the reinforcement's own width: a strength per strip or per mat is that divided by its width b. The rupture check compares Tal x Rc, per metre of wall (p. 4-47), with the unfactored Tmax. For steel it requires a factor of safety of 1.0, so Tal is an allowable, a fraction of GEC-11 Vol I Eq. 3-11a (p. 3-22), Fy Ac / b with Ac the area after corrosion: 0.55 Fy for strips and 0.48 Fy for bar mats (p. 4-77); a bar mat's Ac is the number of longitudinal bars times one bar's corroded area (Fig. 3-5, p. 3-24). For a geosynthetic it requires 1.5 (1.35 / phi 0.90, Table 4-7), so Tal is the long-term strength Tult / RF (Eq. 3-12, p. 3-28), not divided by a factor of safety. Required when reinforcement_name is not a built-in.
reinforcement_lengthfloatoptionalReinforcement length (m). Left out, max(0.7H, 2.5 m): GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-11, preliminary length 'the greater of 0.7H or 8 ft (2.5 m)'.
reinforcement_spacingfloatoptionalVertical reinforcement spacing Sv (m): the levels sit at Sv (i + 1/2) below the top of the wall, wall_height / Sv of them rounded down, each taking Sv in Tmax and sigma_H at its depth; when wall_height is not a whole number of spacings the bottom level's contributory height runs from the midpoint above it to the base of the wall, more than Sv, with sigma_H at its middle (GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-47, Fig. 4-14). A spacing of twice wall_height or more is refused. Not taken with level_depths, which places the levels itself. default: 0.6
level_depthslistoptionalThe depths z (m) of the reinforcement levels below the top of the wall, from the top down, instead of reinforcement_spacing, as GEC-11 Vol II's examples print Z (Example E4, Table E4-7.1, p. E4-11: 1.87 ft, then 2.5 ft apart to 24.37 ft). Each must lie inside the wall (0 < z < wall_height) and below the one above; a list that does not is refused. Each level then takes its contributory height Svt (GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-46): from the midpoints between it and its neighbours, the top level's from the top of the wall and the bottom level's to its base (p. 4-47, Fig. 4-14), and Tmax = sigma_H x Svt with sigma_H averaged over Svt (sigma_H_average). Each level of internal_results then also gives Svt_m and sigma_H_kPa. reinforcement_per_level then needs one entry a depth. Example, a 6 m wall: [0.4, 1.15, 1.9, 2.65, 3.4, 4.15, 4.9, 5.65]. Alias: reinforcement_depths.
sigma_H_averagestroptionalWith level_depths: how sigma_H is averaged over each level's contributory height Svt, the two GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-47 gives: 'trapezoidal' (default), the average of sigma_H at the top and the bottom of Svt, as Vol II Examples E3 and E4 take it at every level (pp. E3-15, E4-13); 'midpoint', sigma_H at the middle of Svt. They differ only where Kr/Ka changes with depth (steel reinforcement, within 6.1 m (20 ft) of the top). Refused without level_depths. allowed: trapezoidal, midpoint default: "trapezoidal"
reinforcement_widthfloatoptionalGross width b (m) of the strip, grid or sheet; for a grid, centre to centre of the outside longitudinal bars (GEC-11 Vol I p. 3-12, Fig. 3-3). Required with reinforcement_horizontal_spacing for Rc = b/Sh, except for a built-in that carries its own (ribbed_steel_strip_50x4: 0.05 m; welded_wire_grid_w11 and E4's 4W15 mats: 0.457 m, 4 wires at 0.152 m; bar_mat_e4_3w11_w11x0_5: 0.305 m, 3 wires).
reinforcement_thicknessfloatoptionalStrip thickness (m) for a strip; transverse-bar diameter t (m) for a steel bar mat / welded grid (the t in F* = 20 t/St, GEC-11 Vol I Eq. 3-6), required for a custom grid unless F_star_tested is given. default: 0.0
reinforcement_transverse_spacingfloatoptionalTransverse-bar (grid) spacing St (m) for a steel bar mat / welded grid (the St in F* = 20 t/St, GEC-11 Vol I Eq. 3-6), required for a custom grid unless F_star_tested is given. Used only for bar_mat/welded_grid/metallic_grid. Checked against GEC-11 Vol I p. 3-21's 'maximum St distance is 24 in. (610 mm)' with the empirical F* (grid_spacing; a larger St fails), and under 6 in. (152 mm) it carries a warning (p. 3-20: 'St > 6 inches'); with F* from pullout tests (F_star_tested) an St over 24 in. is a warning, not a check. default: 0.0
surchargefloatoptionalLive-load (traffic) surcharge (kPa), e.g. heq*gamma. Externally its thrust drives every check; over the reinforced zone it is not a resisting force in sliding or overturning and it loads the base for bearing (GEC-11 Fig. 4-2; live_load_resists, surcharge_in_bearing). Internally it is in Tmax and not in the pullout resistance, which GEC-11 takes 'neglecting traffic loads' (p. 4-49). With a sloping backfill it is taken only with broken_backslope_height, as traffic on the level ground behind the crest; refused on a slope that continues. default: 0.0
backfill_slopefloatoptionalSlope of the backfill surface above the wall, beta (degrees from horizontal), rising away from the face; 0 = level. GEC-11 Section 4.4.4: Coulomb Kab with the interface angle delta = beta (Eqs. 4-2/4-3); thrust F_T = 1/2*Kab*gamma_retained*h^2 on h = H + L*tan(beta), inclined at beta (Eq. 4-7); the slope fill over the reinforced zone is added to the weight; internally the slope adds S_eq = 1/2*(0.7H)*tan(beta) of fill (Fig. 4-11). Must not be steeper than phi_retained. default: 0.0
face_batterfloatoptionalBatter of the front face and reinforced zone, omega (degrees from vertical, the top set back toward the fill); 0 = vertical. Below 10 deg the wall is taken as vertical (GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-15, 'near vertical walls'; the choices say so). From 10 deg (GM-307): externally Kab by Eqs. 4-2, 4-3 with theta = 90 + omega and delta = beta, F_T at h/3 on the back of the zone at delta - omega to the horizontal (p. 4-15, Fig. 4-5); internally Ka by Eq. 4-26 (p. 4-36; taken as Eqs. 4-2, 4-3 with delta = beta = 0, the printed bracket lacking its square, choices give both), and for geosynthetics the Coulomb failure plane of Fig. 4-9(b) (p. 4-34) through the toe; steel keeps 0.3 H1 from the face (Fig. 4-9(a) note). Refused under a broken backslope (no printed rule) and with an outward lean (below 0). The result's face_batter gives the basis. Aliases: wall_batter, batter, batter_angle, face_batter_deg. default: 0.0
phi_retainedfloatoptionalFriction angle (deg) of the retained fill behind the reinforced zone, for the external thrust. Left out: 30 deg, the assumed value GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-10 prints for the retained backfill ('recommended only for preliminary sizing'), stated in choices.
gamma_retainedfloatoptionalUnit weight (kN/m3) of the retained fill behind the reinforced zone. Defaults to gamma_backfill.
broken_backslope_heightfloatoptionalFor a broken backslope (GEC-11 Fig. 4-4): the height S (m) of the slope crest above the top of the wall, with level ground behind it. Omit for a slope that continues. Kab and the thrust inclination then use I, the angle from the top of the wall to the ground 2H behind the face, and h = H + min(L*tan(beta), S).
traffic_vertical_resistsbooloptionalBroken backslope with traffic (surcharge) behind the crest only: count the traffic thrust's vertical component F2*sin(I) as sliding and eccentricity resistance, as GEC-11 Example E1 does (Vol II pp. E1-7 to E1-9). Default false: the GEC-11 text counts loads that increase sliding resistance 'only if those loads are permanent' (Vol I p. 4-22). Bearing counts it either way (p. 4-26). The result's backslope.traffic_basis says which was used. default: false
live_load_resistsbooloptionalCount the live-load surcharge over the reinforced zone (q*L; behind the crest of a broken backslope, q over the level ground on the zone) as resisting weight in sliding and overturning. Default false: GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-19, 'The live load surcharge is not considered as a stabilizing force when checking sliding'; p. 4-21 (Eq. 4-12), 'the live load is excluded since it increases sliding stability'; p. 4-22, loads that increase sliding resistance only 'if those loads are permanent', and the eccentricity (overturning) check 'only applies the live load above the retained backfill' (Fig. 4-2). true = the free body with the load over the zone, W = gamma*H*L + q*L. The result's choices say which was used. default: false
surcharge_in_bearingbooloptionalCount the live-load surcharge over the reinforced zone in the bearing pressure sigma_v and its eccentricity. Default true: GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-26, 'The bearing check applies live load above both the reinforced zone and the retained backfill' (Fig. 4-2; Eqs. 4-19, 4-20). false = the live load taken as not over the zone. default: true
phi_foundationfloatoptionalFoundation soil friction angle (deg). Sliding takes mu = min(tan phi_foundation, tan phi_backfill) (GEC-11 Vol I Eq. 4-12, p. 4-22). Left out: 30 deg, as GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-10 prints for the foundation soil 'in absence of specific data' ('recommended only for preliminary sizing'), stated in choices. phi_foundation = 0 gives an undrained strength (c_foundation = cu): sliding_cohesion then defaults to 'undrained'.
c_foundationfloatoptionalFoundation soil cohesion (kPa). The sliding check counts it only by sliding_cohesion 'undrained', as the undrained shear strength cu; with 'drained' (the default unless phi_foundation is 0) it is not counted, as GEC-11 Eq. 4-12 prints no cohesion term. default: 0.0
sliding_cohesionstroptionalHow the sliding check counts the foundation soil's cohesion. Default depends on phi_foundation: 'undrained' when phi_foundation is 0 (c_foundation is then cu), else 'drained'. 'drained': R = V min(tan phi_foundation, tan phi_backfill), c_foundation NOT counted (GEC-11 Vol I Eqs. 4-12, 4-13, p. 4-21: Rr = V mu, no cohesion term; GEC-6 Eq. 5-38). 'undrained': R = min(cu L, V tan phi_backfill), cu = c_foundation, no base friction: GEC-11 p. 4-21 Step 3 takes the weaker of sliding along the foundation soil ('based on c'f + tan phi'f and/or cu for cohesive soils') and along the reinforced fill; the foundation's resistance cu over the base as GEC-6 Eq. 5-39 gives it ('ca is typically taken as equal to the undrained shear strength'). GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-19 evaluates sliding on the base 'using the same procedures as for spread footings on soil as per Article 10.6.3.4 (AASHTO, 2007)', which is not held; UFC 3-220-20 Sec. 4-5.1.3 (p. 223) takes the lowest of the resistance at the interface between the base and a bearing layer and 'the resistance within the clay using the full undrained shear strength'. Before GM-297 the tool added 2/3 c_foundation x L to the friction, which no reference held prints. The result's choices give the rule used, its basis and the other rule's FOS_sliding on the same wall. allowed: drained, undrained
interface_gap_possiblebooloptionalWhether water or air can reach the interface between the base and an undrained clay foundation. With sliding_cohesion 'undrained' the foundation's resistance is then held to 0.4 V (EN 1997-1 Sec. 6.5.3(12)P, Eq. 6.5, p. 65: 'If it is possible for water or air to reach the interface between a foundation and an undrained clay subgrade, the following check shall be made: Rd <= 0,4 Vd'). GEC-11, GEC-6 and UFC 3-220-20 print no such limit. Refused with the drained rule. The result's choices give FOS_sliding under the other reading. default: false
rho_testedfloatoptionalFor a geosynthetic at the lowest level, sliding is also checked along it. Sheet reinforcement (GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-21 Step 3(iii): 'For sheet type reinforcement, sliding along the weaker of the upper and lower soil-reinforcement interfaces'; Vol II Example E1 p. E1-7: 'sliding should also be checked at the elevation of the first layer of soil reinforcement'): the block above the lowest layer, its own weight and thrust, slides on tan rho, and the lesser of that and the base governs. The soil-reinforcement interface friction angle rho (deg) from interface direct shear tests, which p. 4-21 prefers ('should preferably be measured by means of interface direct shear tests'). Default 2/3 tan phi_backfill for tan rho ('In absence of testing, it may be taken as 2/3 tan phi'r'; Eq. 3-9, p. 3-21, 'for geotextiles, geogrids and geonet type drainage composites'). Refused when the lowest level's reinforcement is steel.
q_allowablefloatoptionalAllowable bearing pressure (kPa). Without it the external bearing check is NOT RUN (FOS_bearing null, checks_not_run lists 'bearing'); sigma_v is still reported.

mse_lrfd_external_stability — MSE wall external stability by AASHTO/GEC-11 LRFD: sliding / eccentricity / bearing capacity:demand ratios (CDRs) under Strength I (max+min) and Service I (with the Service I resultant within L/6, and GEC-11 Eq. 4-24 on a cohesive foundation), level or sloping backfill. Distinct from mse_wall, which reports ASD factors of safety.

ParameterTypeDescription
wall_heightfloatrequiredDesign wall height H (m), incl. embedment. Alias: height.
gamma_backfillfloatrequiredReinforced fill unit weight (kN/m3). Alias: gamma.
phi_backfillfloatrequiredReinforced fill friction angle (deg). GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-10: above 34 deg only from triaxial or direct shear tests on the project's fill, and never above 40 deg; the result warns past either. Alias: phi.
reinforcement_lengthfloatoptionalReinforcement length L (m). Left out, max(0.7H, 2.5 m): GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-11, preliminary length 'the greater of 0.7H or 8 ft (2.5 m)'.
surchargefloatoptionalLive-load surcharge q (kPa) over the mass (e.g. heq*gamma). Used as the LL unless live_load overrides. With a broken backslope it is traffic on the level ground behind the crest (thrust Kab*q*h, inclined at I; GEC-11 Example E1); refused on a slope that continues. default: 0.0
backfill_slopefloatoptionalSlope of the backfill surface above the wall, beta (degrees from horizontal), rising away from the face; 0 = level. GEC-11 Section 4.4.6 (Examples E3, E1): Coulomb Kab with delta = beta; F_T = 1/2*Kab*gamma_retained*h^2 on h = H + L*tan(beta) (Eq. 4-7), inclined at beta; F_T*cos(beta) drives and F_T*sin(beta) resists, both EH-factored (Eqs. 4-11, 4-13, 4-16, 4-21); the slope fill over the zone (V2) is an EV load. Must not be steeper than phi_retained. default: 0.0
broken_backslope_heightfloatoptionalFor a broken backslope (GEC-11 Fig. 4-4): the height S (m) of the slope crest above the top of the wall, with level ground behind it. Omit for a slope that continues. Kab and the thrust inclination then use I, the angle from the top of the wall to the ground 2H behind the face, and h = H + min(L*tan(beta), S).
traffic_vertical_resistsbooloptionalBroken backslope with traffic (surcharge) behind the crest only: count the traffic thrust's vertical component F2*sin(I) as sliding and eccentricity resistance, as GEC-11 Example E1 does (Vol II pp. E1-7 to E1-9). Default false: the GEC-11 text counts loads that increase sliding resistance 'only if those loads are permanent' (Vol I p. 4-22). Bearing counts it either way (p. 4-26). The result's backslope.traffic_basis says which was used. default: false
phi_foundationfloatoptionalFoundation friction angle (deg); the sliding interface uses mu = min(tan phi_backfill, tan phi_foundation) (GEC-11 Vol I Eq. 4-12, p. 4-22). Left out: 30 deg, as GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-10 prints for the foundation soil 'in absence of specific data' ('recommended only for preliminary sizing'), stated in choices. phi_foundation = 0 gives an undrained strength (c_foundation = cu): sliding_cohesion then defaults to 'undrained'.
phi_retainedfloatoptionalRetained (behind-mass) fill friction angle (deg) for the external active thrust. Left out: 30 deg, the assumed value GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-10 prints for the retained backfill ('recommended only for preliminary sizing'), stated in choices.
gamma_retainedfloatoptionalRetained fill unit weight (kN/m3). Defaults to gamma_backfill.
live_loadfloatoptionalLive-load surcharge q (kPa) if different from surcharge.
bearing_resistance_strengthfloatoptionalFactored bearing resistance qR at the strength limit (kPa) = phi_b*qn; enables the strength/critical bearing CDR = qR/sigma_v. Give it or gamma_foundation, not both.
gamma_foundationfloatoptionalFoundation soil unit weight (kN/m3). Given in place of bearing_resistance_strength, it works the strength bearing resistance out for each Strength I combination, as GEC-11 Vol II Example E2 does: qn = c_foundation*Nc + 0.5*L'*gamma_foundation*Ngamma (GEC-11 Vol I Eq. 4-22; Nc, Ngamma from Table 4-6 for phi_foundation, which must then be given: the reinforced fill's phi_backfill is not taken for it) over that combination's L' = L - 2eB (L' = L when eB < 0), for a level grade in front of the wall and no groundwater influence, the wall's embedment neglected (p. 4-28); qR = phi_bearing*qn (Eq. 4-23). For a slope in front of the wall or a high water table work qn out by AASHTO 10.6.3.1.2 and give bearing_resistance_strength.
phi_bearingfloatoptionalBearing resistance factor phi_b for the qn worked out from gamma_foundation (GEC-11 Table 4-5: 0.65). default: 0.65
local_shear_possiblebooloptionalWith gamma_foundation: local or punching shear failure is possible under the wall, so qn takes the reduced strengths c* = 0.67 c_foundation and phi* = tan^-1(0.67 tan phi_foundation). GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-30: 'If local shear or punching shear failure is possible, Section 10.6.3.1.2b of AASHTO (2007) requires the use of reduced shear strength parameters for calculating the nominal bearing resistance'; local shear 'can occur in loose or compressible soils, in weak soils under slow (drained) loading'. Sliding keeps the strengths given. Default false (general shear). Refused without gamma_foundation: work a given bearing_resistance_strength out with c* and phi* instead. default: false
bearing_resistance_servicefloatoptionalService bearing resistance (kPa); enables the Service I bearing CDR.
c_foundationfloatoptionalFoundation cohesion (kPa): c_f in qn when gamma_foundation is given, and in sliding only by sliding_cohesion 'undrained', as the undrained shear strength cu; with 'drained' (the default unless phi_foundation is 0) sliding does not count it, as GEC-11 Eq. 4-12 prints no cohesion term. default: 0.0
sliding_cohesionstroptionalHow the sliding check counts the foundation soil's cohesion. Default depends on phi_foundation: 'undrained' when phi_foundation is 0 (c_foundation is then cu), else 'drained'. 'drained': Rr = phi_sliding x gamma_EV x V x min(tan phi_foundation, tan phi_backfill), c_foundation NOT counted (GEC-11 Vol I Eqs. 4-12, 4-13, p. 4-21; GEC-6 Eq. 5-38). 'undrained': Rr = phi_sliding x min(cu L, gamma_EV x V x tan phi_backfill), cu = c_foundation, no base friction (GEC-11 p. 4-21 Step 3: the weaker of sliding along the foundation soil, 'based on c'f + tan phi'f and/or cu for cohesive soils', and along the reinforced fill; cu over the base as GEC-6 Eq. 5-39 gives it). GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-19 evaluates sliding on the base 'using the same procedures as for spread footings on soil as per Article 10.6.3.4 (AASHTO, 2007)', which is not held; UFC 3-220-20 Sec. 4-5.1.3 (p. 223) takes the lowest of the resistance at the interface between the base and a bearing layer and 'the resistance within the clay using the full undrained shear strength'. Before GM-297 the tool added 2/3 c_foundation x L, which no reference held prints. The result's choices give the rule used, its basis and the other rule's governing sliding CDR. allowed: drained, undrained
interface_gap_possiblebooloptionalWhether water or air can reach the interface between the base and an undrained clay foundation. With sliding_cohesion 'undrained' the foundation's resistance is then held to 0.4 V gamma_EV (EN 1997-1 Sec. 6.5.3(12)P, Eq. 6.5, p. 65: 'If it is possible for water or air to reach the interface between a foundation and an undrained clay subgrade, the following check shall be made: Rd <= 0,4 Vd'). GEC-11, GEC-6 and UFC 3-220-20 print no such limit. Refused with the drained rule. The result's choices give the governing sliding CDR under the other reading. default: false
lowest_sheet_depthfloatoptionalFor sheet (geosynthetic) reinforcement, the depth (m) below the top of the wall of its lowest layer: sliding is then also checked along it with the same load combinations. Sheet reinforcement (GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-21 Step 3(iii): 'For sheet type reinforcement, sliding along the weaker of the upper and lower soil-reinforcement interfaces'; Vol II Example E1 p. E1-7: 'sliding should also be checked at the elevation of the first layer of soil reinforcement'): the block above the lowest layer, its own weight and thrust, slides on tan rho, and the lesser of that and the base governs. Give it for geogrid or geotextile reinforcement; leave it out for steel strips or grids. Not given: sliding is checked at the base only.
rho_testedfloatoptionalWith lowest_sheet_depth, sliding along the lowest sheet: The soil-reinforcement interface friction angle rho (deg) from interface direct shear tests, which p. 4-21 prefers ('should preferably be measured by means of interface direct shear tests'). Default 2/3 tan phi_backfill for tan rho ('In absence of testing, it may be taken as 2/3 tan phi'r'; Eq. 3-9, p. 3-21, 'for geotextiles, geogrids and geonet type drainage composites'). Needs lowest_sheet_depth.
gamma_EV_maxfloatoptionalMax vertical-earth (EV) load factor (AASHTO Strength I). default: 1.35
gamma_EV_minfloatoptionalMin vertical-earth (EV) load factor. default: 1.0
gamma_EH_maxfloatoptionalMax horizontal-earth (EH) load factor. default: 1.5
gamma_EH_minfloatoptionalMin horizontal-earth (EH) load factor. default: 0.9
gamma_LLfloatoptionalLive-load (LL) factor. default: 1.75
phi_slidingfloatoptionalSliding resistance factor (AASHTO 11.10.5.3). default: 1.0
ecc_limit_ratiofloatoptionalLimiting-eccentricity ratio e_max/L: 0.25 (L/4) on soil, 0.375 (3L/8) on rock. GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-23: the resultant 'within the middle one-half of the base width for soil foundations (i.e., emax = L / 4) and middle three-fourths of the base width for rock foundations (i.e., emax = 3/8 L)'. default: 0.25
ecc_limit_ratio_servicefloatoptionalLimiting-eccentricity ratio for the Service I resultant: 1/6 (L/6), as GEC-11 Vol II Examples E3, E4 and E5 check it (Tables E3-6.3, E4-6.3, E5-7.1: 'Limiting eccentricity, e = L/4 for strength limit states and e = L/6 for service limit state'). Each example is on soil and no page held prints the service limit on rock, so with ecc_limit_ratio above 0.25 and this left at L/6 the result warns. Must be in (0, 0.5]. default: 0.16666666666666666

list_reinforcement — List the built-in reinforcements (GEC-11 Vol II worked examples' strip, bar mats and geogrids) with their Tal and its basis.

No parameters.

10.1.12 ground_improvement — Ground improvement

aggregate_piers — Aggregate pier (stone column) design: settlement reduction, capacity increase.

ParameterTypeDescription
column_diameterfloatrequiredPier column diameter (m).
spacingfloatrequiredCenter-to-center spacing (m). Alternatively give area_replacement_ratio (As/A, 0.1-0.35 typical) and spacing is back-calculated.
area_replacement_ratiofloatoptionalArea replacement ratio As/A (0.1-0.35 typical). Used to compute spacing when spacing is not given.
patternstroptionalInstallation pattern. allowed: triangular, square default: "triangular"
E_soilfloatoptionalSurrounding soil modulus (kPa). With settlement_method 'stress_ratio', used only for the composite modulus E_comp = E_soil*[1 + as*(n-1)]; the GEC-13 Fig. 5-21 methods need it given, for E_c/E_s. default: 5000.0
nfloatoptionalStress concentration ratio sigma_c/sigma_s; sets the improved bearing and, with settlement_method 'stress_ratio', the settlement reduction factor. GEC-13 for stone columns: measured 'between 2.0 and 5.0' (p. 5-31), and 'For preliminary design, a ratio of 2.5 is often conservatively used for stability and bearing resistance calculations' (p. 5-32); for rammed aggregate piers 5 to 10 under flexible embankment loading and 10 under rigid footings (p. 5-43); 'stress concentration ratios range from 4 to 45 for rigid footings' (p. 5-45). default: 5.0
settlement_methodstroptionalHow the settlement over the columns is worked out. 'stress_ratio' (default): SRF = 1/[1 + as*(n-1)] from n. The others give the settlement ratio (settlement without columns / with them; GEC-13 p. 5-36 prints it as 'n', which is not the stress ratio n) by E_c/E_s off GEC-13 Fig. 5-21, and need E_column and E_soil: 'weighted_modulus' (curve 2, settlement ratio = 1 + as*(E_c/E_s - 1), any E_c/E_s); 'balaam_rigid' (curves 5b, 5c: E_c/E_s 5 to 10, A/A_c 1.75 to 9); 'balaam_flexible' (curve 5a: E_c/E_s = 10, A/A_c 1.5 to 8.5). GEC-13 p. 5-37: the FHWA (1983) Equilibrium Method, 'roughly equivalent to the Balaam relationships', 'represents an average or lower bound estimate suitable for preliminary analyses'; the Priebe curve (priebe_improvement_factor) 'the upper bound effectiveness'. allowed: stress_ratio, weighted_modulus, balaam_rigid, balaam_flexible default: "stress_ratio"
E_columnfloatoptionalAggregate column modulus E_c (kPa), with E_soil, for the settlement_method 'weighted_modulus', 'balaam_rigid' or 'balaam_flexible' (E_c/E_s, GEC-13 Fig. 5-21). Refused with 'stress_ratio', which takes n instead. Alias: column_modulus.
q_unreinforcedfloatoptionalUnreinforced bearing capacity (kPa). 0 = not computed. default: 0.0
S_unreinforcedfloatoptionalUnreinforced settlement (mm). 0 = not computed. default: 0.0

priebe_improvement_factor — Stone columns: the settlement ratio off the Priebe curve GEC-13 prints, Fig. 5-21 curve (4), phi = 37.5 deg (p. 5-36), which GEC-13 calls the upper bound, for preliminary estimates (p. 5-37).

ParameterTypeDescription
as_ratiofloatrequiredArea replacement ratio as = Ac/A, 0 < as < 1. The tool reads the curve at A/A_c = 1/as from 1.6 to 8.0 (as 0.125 to 0.625); outside that it is refused, not extended (the printed curve runs on to about A/A_c 8.5 to 8.7; past 8.0, read the figure). GEC-13 Example 2 takes A/A_sc = (s/d)^2 (p. 5-48). Alias: area_replacement_ratio.

wick_drains — Prefabricated vertical drain (PVD) consolidation: radial by GEC-13 Eq. 2-1 with F(n) = ln(n) - 0.75 (Eq. 2-2), well resistance not modelled (GEC-13 p. 2-36: 'rarely significant'), combined with vertical drainage by Carrillo (UFC 3-220-10 Eq. 5-27).

ParameterTypeDescription
spacingfloatrequiredCenter-to-center drain spacing (m).
chfloatrequiredHorizontal coefficient of consolidation (m2/yr).
cvfloatrequiredVertical coefficient of consolidation (m2/yr).
HdrfloatrequiredVertical drainage path (m).
timefloatrequiredAnalysis time (years).
dwfloatoptionalEquivalent drain diameter (m). Default 2.5 in (0.0635 m), GEC-13 p. 2-35: 'Various diameters ranging from 1.5 inch to 5.5 inch have been used, but the most common is to use 2.5 inch.' A band drain's is 2(a + b)/pi (Eq. 2-3). default: 0.0635
patternstroptionalInstallation pattern. allowed: triangular, square default: "triangular"
smear_ratiofloatoptionalSmear zone ratio s = ds/dw. Not given: smear ignored (F_s = 0), GEC-13 p. 2-35, 'The effects of both soil disturbance and well resistance are often ignored for typical projects.' Above 1, F_s = (kh/ks) ln(s) is added to F(n), as UFC 3-220-10 (2026) Eq. 5-25 prints it; GEC-13 prints no F_s formula, only 'a sample disturbance factor Fs ≈ 2 may be considered' in highly plastic, sensitive soils whose ch is accurately determined.
kh_ks_ratiofloatoptionalPermeability ratio kh/ks, used only with smear_ratio above 1 (UFC 3-220-10 Eq. 5-25). default: 1.0
n_time_pointsintoptionalPoints in the time-settlement curve. default: 50

design_drain_spacing — Find required drain spacing for a target combined (vertical and radial) consolidation in a target time, by GEC-13 Eq. 2-1 and Carrillo (UFC 3-220-10 Eq. 5-27). GEC-13 p. 2-33 gives typical spacings of 3 to 5 ft in homogeneous clays, 4 to 6 ft in silty clays, 5 to 6.5 ft in coarser soils for about 90 percent consolidation in 3 to 4 months.

cvfloatrequiredVertical coefficient of consolidation (m2/yr).
HdrfloatrequiredVertical drainage path (m).
dwfloatoptionalEquivalent drain diameter (m). Default 2.5 in (0.0635 m), GEC-13 p. 2-35: 'Various diameters ranging from 1.5 inch to 5.5 inch have been used, but the most common is to use 2.5 inch.' A band drain's is 2(a + b)/pi (Eq. 2-3). default: 0.0635
patternstroptionalInstallation pattern. allowed: triangular, square default: "triangular"
smear_ratiofloatoptionalSmear zone ratio s = ds/dw. Not given: smear ignored (F_s = 0), GEC-13 p. 2-35, 'The effects of both soil disturbance and well resistance are often ignored for typical projects.' kh_ks_ratiofloatoptionalPermeability ratio kh/ks, used only with smear_ratio above 1 (UFC 3-220-10 Eq. 5-25). default: 1.0
spacing_rangearrayoptionalSpacing search range [min, max] (m). default: [1.0, 3.5]

surcharge_preloading — Surcharge preloading settlement and time analysis (optionally with wick drains).

ParameterTypeDescription
S_ultimatefloatrequiredUltimate consolidation settlement under the surcharge (m). Compute first via the settlement module if unknown.
surcharge_kPafloatrequiredApplied surcharge pressure (kPa).
cvfloatrequiredVertical coefficient of consolidation (m2/yr).
HdrfloatrequiredVertical drainage path (m).

vibro_compaction — Vibro compaction (vibroflotation) feasibility by GEC-13 Ch. 4 (fines content, SPT N by Table 4-8), and the probe spacing for a target relative density off GEC-13 Fig. 4-34.

ParameterTypeDescription
fines_contentfloatrequiredPercent passing #200 sieve (0-100). GEC-13 p. 4-65: 'proper densification generally cannot be achieved when the granular soil contains more than 12 to 15 percent silt OR more than 2 percent clay'; p. 4-67: fines below 10 percent ideally suited. Above 15 not feasible, 12 to 15 marginal.
initial_N_sptfloatrequiredCurrent SPT blow count (blows/ft), read as a density by GEC-13 Table 4-8 (normally consolidated sand). Very dense (N above 50, relative density 85 to 100 percent) is not feasible: p. 4-75, 'It is unlikely, even for heavy loading, that it will be necessary to achieve a relative density above 85 percent.'
target_relative_densityfloatoptionalTarget relative density (%), 55 to 90: the probe spacing is read off GEC-13 Fig. 4-34 (p. 4-77), relative density versus probe spacing for silty sands, the lower bound gradation (p. 4-76); refused outside 55 to 90, where the curve is not printed. GEC-13 p. 4-77: 60 percent for floor slabs, flat bottom tanks, embankments; 70 to 75 percent for column and bridge footings; 80 percent for machinery and mat foundations. Not given: no spacing. Alias: target_Dr.
patternstroptionalProbe pattern. GEC-13 p. 4-77: a square pattern 'requires 5 to 8 percent more points to achieve the same minimum densities in large areas'. allowed: triangular, square default: "triangular"

feasibility — Ground improvement method feasibility screening.

ParameterTypeDescription
soil_typestrrequiredSoil type to improve. allowed: soft_clay, loose_sand, mixed, organic
fines_contentfloatoptionalPercent passing #200 sieve. Required for vibro assessment.
N_sptfloatoptionalAverage SPT N in the treatment zone.
cu_kPafloatoptionalAverage undrained shear strength (kPa).
thickness_mfloatoptionalThickness of the compressible/treatable layer (m). The treatment reaches depth_to_top_m + thickness_m (see depth_to_top_m). default: 0.0
depth_to_top_mfloatoptionalDepth to the top of the treatable layer (m). The treatment reaches depth_to_top_m + thickness_m, held against GEC-13's printed depths: aggregate piers not applicable beyond 100 ft (30.5 m), the typical maximum practical depth of stone columns, and stone columns only beyond 35 ft (10.7 m), that of rammed aggregate piers (p. 5-9: 'Typically, the maximum practical depth of stone columns and rammed aggregate piers is 100 feet and 35 feet respectively'); vibro-compaction not applicable beyond about 165 ft (50 m) and noted beyond the generally recommended about 100 ft (30.5 m) (p. 4-65). default: 0.0
required_bearing_kPafloatoptionalRequired bearing capacity (kPa). 0 = not a bearing problem. default: 0.0
current_bearing_kPafloatoptionalCurrent (unimproved) bearing capacity (kPa). default: 0.0
predicted_settlement_mmfloatoptionalPredicted settlement without improvement (mm). default: 0.0
allowable_settlement_mmfloatoptionalAllowable settlement limit (mm). default: 50.0
time_constraint_monthsfloatoptionalTime available (months). 0 = no constraint. default: 0.0
cv_m2_per_yearfloatoptionalVertical coefficient of consolidation (m2/yr).
Hdr_mfloatoptionalVertical drainage path length (m).

10.1.13 slope_stability — Slope stability

analyze_slope — Analyze ONE specified slip surface (Fellenius/Bishop/Janbu+f0/Spencer/Morgenstern-Price/GLE). Requires a trial circle (xc/yc/radius) or slip_points. If you do NOT already have a specific trial surface, use search_critical_surface instead — it auto-finds the critical surface and avoids 'circle does not intersect the ground surface' errors. Supports reinforcement (nails/anchors/geosynthetics), ponded water (auto), SHANSEP and Hoek-Brown layer strengths, pseudo-static kh, tension cracks.

ParameterTypeDescription
surface_pointsarrayrequiredGround surface as [[x,y], ...] array (x increasing).
soil_layersarrayrequiredArray of soil-layer dicts: {top_elevation, bottom_elevation, gamma (all required); name, gamma_sat, phi, c_prime, cu, analysis_mode ('drained'|'undrained'), ru optional; bottom_boundary_points and top_boundary_points ([[x,z],...], sorted by x) optional, a sloping bottom or top in place of the flat elevation}. Per-layer strength_model: 'mohr_coulomb' (default), 'shansep' (su = shansep_S ocr^shansep_m sigma'_v; fields shansep_S, shansep_m, ocr, su_min) 'hoek_brown' (Generalized Hoek-Brown; fields hb_sigci kPa, hb_gsi, hb_mi, hb_D) or 'anisotropic' (undrained su varies with the slice-base inclination alpha; fields su_active [kPa, ACTIVE/crest zone, alpha>=+45deg], su_dss [direct simple shear, alpha=0], su_passive [PASSIVE/toe zone, alpha<=-45deg] — su_active>=su_dss>=su_passive for K>1 clays; Casagrande-Carrillo sin(2alpha) interpolation; standard toe-at-low-x slope). For rapid_drawdown_fos, low-permeability layers also take the total-stress R-envelope R_c (kPa) and R_phi (deg); R_phi omitted/null => free-draining. One material per point: where two layers cover the same ground the one listed FIRST holds it, for weight and strength (reported in layer_overlaps); ground above the deepest layer's bottom that no layer covers is refused.
gwt_pointsarrayoptionalGroundwater table [[x,y],...]. If above the ground surface, ponded water is auto-detected (water weight + horizontal hydrostatic thrust applied as external loads).
khfloatoptionalHorizontal pseudo-static seismic coefficient (acts on soil weight only). default: 0.0
surchargefloatoptionalVertical surcharge (kPa). A single loaded zone; use 'surcharges' for several distinct loaded areas. default: 0.0
surcharge_x_rangearrayoptional[x_start, x_end] extent of the single 'surcharge'.
surchargesarrayoptionalSeveral distinct surcharge zones (bench + crest loads, etc.): [{pressure kPa, x_start, x_end}, ...]. Each zone's pressure is summed at any x it covers, ON TOP OF the single 'surcharge'/'surcharge_x_range'. Represent a linearly-varying (trapezoidal) load as its mean uniform pressure or as several thin zones.
tension_crack_depthfloatoptionalTension crack depth at the crest (m). default: 0.0
tension_crack_water_depthfloatoptionalWater depth in the tension crack (m). default: 0.0
tension_crack_sidestroptionalWhich crest end the tension crack is on: 'entry' (default, low-x / slip-surface entry) or 'exit' (high-x). Put it on whichever side the crest is on; no need to mirror the slope. allowed: entry, exit default: "entry"
tension_crack_modelstroptionalTension-crack mechanism: 'strength' (default) keeps the cracked wedge as zero-shear-strength driving soil; 'truncation' removes it from the sliding mass (mass ends at the vertical crack face, as Slide2/UTEXAS do). Truncation is less conservative. allowed: strength, truncation default: "strength"
reverse_curvaturestroptionalA circle whose centre is below the ground where it comes out would turn back above its centre (Slide2: reverse curvature). 'tension_crack' (default, as Slide2) closes it with a dry vertical crack; 'discard' drops such circles from searches. allowed: tension_crack, discard default: "tension_crack"
pore_pressure_pointsarrayoptionalDiscrete pore-pressure field as [[x, z, u], ...] triples (u in kPa) -- a flow-net / TIN sampling. When given, the base pore pressure at each slice is interpolated from this field (linear on the Delaunay triangulation, nearest-node fallback outside the hull, suction clamped to 0), OVERRIDING the gwt_points piezometric line and per-layer ru. The ponded-water buttress still comes from gwt_points, so set BOTH for a reservoir over a flow-net field.
nailsarrayoptionalSoil nails (per metre of slope run): [{x_head, z_head, length required; inclination deg below horizontal=15, bar_diameter mm=25, drill_hole_diameter mm=150, fy MPa=420, bond_stress kPa=100, spacing_h m=1.5, support_convention}]. Capacity = min(pullout behind slip surface, bar tensile)/spacing_h (FHWA GEC-7).
anchorsarrayoptionalTieback anchors: [{x_head, z_head, length, T_allow kN/m required; inclination=15, support_convention}]. Full T_allow applied when the bond zone crosses the slip surface.
geosyntheticsarrayoptionalHorizontal geosynthetic layers: [{elevation, T_allow kN/m required; x_start, x_end, support_convention optional}]. Every support (nails, anchors, geosynthetics, piles) acts at the base of the slice it crosses (Wright & Duncan 1991). support_convention: 'active' (default; Duncan & Wright Method A / Slide2 Active: the force is not divided by F and reduces the driving side -- give the ALLOWABLE force) or 'passive' (Method B / Slide2 Passive: divided by F with the soil strength -- give the ULTIMATE force; lower FOS for the same force). All methods.
stabilizing_pilesarrayoptionalSingle-row stabilizing/micro piles crossing the slope (Ito & Matsui 1975 or a specified shear): [{x required; spacing m=1.0 (D1); z_head, z_toe optional}]. Set the resistance EITHER by shear_capacity (kN per pile; per-metre force = shear_capacity/spacing) OR ito_matsui=true with diameter (m; D2=spacing-diameter) and optional c/phi/gamma (default: soil layer) giving the Ito-Matsui plastic lateral force integrated from head to slip surface. force_direction 'horizontal' (default) or 'normal'. support_convention 'active' (default) or 'passive' as for geosynthetics. Stabilizing force at the slip crossing.
reinforcement_forcefloatoptionalSingle equivalent horizontal reinforcement force (kN/m). Simpler alternative to nails/anchors. default: 0.0
reinforcement_elevationfloatoptionalElevation of the equivalent reinforcement force (m).
xcfloatoptionalCircle center x (m). Required for circular.
ycfloatoptionalCircle center y (m). Required for circular.
radiusfloatoptionalCircle radius (m). Required for circular.
slip_pointsarrayoptionalPolyline slip surface [[x,y],...] for noncircular. Use instead of xc/yc/radius.
methodstroptionalLimit-equilibrium method. 'janbu' reports the f0-corrected FOS; 'spencer'/'morgenstern_price'/'gle' use the rigorous Fredlund-Krahn GLE engine (interslice E/X integration). allowed: fellenius, bishop, janbu, spencer, morgenstern_price, gle default: "bishop"
f_interslicestroptionalInterslice force function f(x) for morgenstern_price/gle ('constant' reproduces Spencer). allowed: constant, half_sine, clipped_sine, trapezoidal default: "half_sine"
n_slicesintoptionalNumber of slices. default: 30
include_slice_databooloptionalInclude the per-slice force table (W, N', S_mob, u*l, alpha; interslice E/X and line of thrust for rigorous methods). default: false
compare_methodsbooloptionalAlso report FOS for every method on this surface. default: false
tolfloatoptionalConvergence tolerance for the iterative methods. default: 0.0001

compare_methods_table — Run ALL limit-equilibrium methods (OMS, Bishop, Janbu uncorr/corr, Spencer, Morgenstern-Price) on ONE slip surface and return a side-by-side FOS table (Fredlund & Krahn 1977 style method comparison).
