write_diggs — WRITE a DIGGS 2.6 file from boring/pit/sounding logs and lab results you have read (e.g. off a report's logs), given inline or as JSON files a helper saved. Checks the file against the DIGGS schema and reads it back; never hand-write DIGGS XML.

ParameterTypeDescription
investigationsarrayoptionalOne object per boring, pit or sounding, with the values read off its log. A number printed on the log goes in as printed. A depth read off the log's own drawn depth scale (log_grid's samples, layers and rows, or measure) is read from the log just as much as a printed one: write it, and note the reading in a prov {page, method: 'grid', note: e.g. 'sample depths off the depth scale +/-0.01 m'} on the value or once in the investigation's prov list. Never infer a value the log does not give, and never hold back a record whose values you have: leave out only what could not be read, and name each thing left out, and why, in your answer. Keys: investigation_id; kind (boring|test_pit|cpt|dcp|hand_auger|well|other); depth_unit ('m'|'ft'); x, y, coordinate_system; elevation {value, unit} (leave out any the source does not give: it is written as unknown, never 0); total_depth {value, unit}; date_started, date_finished; drilling {method, equipment, hammer_type, hammer_energy_ratio, sampler, contractor, logged_by}; layers [{top {value, unit}, bottom {value, unit}, description, uscs}]; samples [{sample_id (may be empty), top, bottom, kind (spt|ring|shelby|bulk|grab|core|cuttings|other), recovery {value, unit} (a printed length), recovery_percent, rqd_percent, water_content, fines_percent, liquid_limit, plastic_limit, uscs}]; spt [{depth_top, depth_bottom, blows [per increment; a string for refusal, e.g. '50/10cm'], increment {value, unit} (the length each drive is counted over, as the form prints it, e.g. 15 cm; 6 in when left out), n (ONLY if printed; a printed refusal such as '>50', 'R' or '50/5"' may be given as n and is recorded as refusal: true with its text kept), refusal, sample_id}]; water [{depth {value, unit}, when (while_drilling|at_completion|after_hours|not_encountered|not_measured|unknown), hours}] (not_encountered: leave depth out -- it is never written as a water level; not_measured: no reading taken; leave depth out); remarks; pages (0-based PDF pages the values were read from; none for a record no page gave, such as a placeholder). Every depth or elevation is {value, unit}. Unknown keys are refused by name.
lab_testsarrayoptionalLab results, one object per test on one specimen: kind (atterberg|gradation|compaction|cbr|moisture_content|density|chemical|specific_gravity|unconfined|unconfined_rock|direct_shear|triaxial|swell_consolidation|permeability|organic_content|summary_table|other), investigation_id, sample_id, depth_top {value, unit}, depth_bottom, standard, pages, and result {kind: the same kind, then: atterberg: ll, pl, pi, non_plastic; gradation: gravel_percent, sand_percent, silt_percent, clay_percent, fines_percent, percent_passing [{percent_passing, size {value, unit}, sieve}]; compaction: max_dry_density {value, unit}, optimum_wc; cbr: cbr_percent, swell_percent, soaked; moisture_content: wc; chemical: pH, sulfate, chloride, resistivity (numbers, {value, unit}, or the printed text e.g. '<10')}. A report's lab SUMMARY TABLE goes in too, as one object of kind summary_table with result {kind: summary_table, rows [{investigation_id, sample_id, depth_top, wc, ll, pl, pi, gravel_percent, sand_percent, fines_percent, max_dry_density, optimum_wc, pH, sulfate, chloride}]}: it is cross-checked against the individual sheets.
investigations_filestr|arrayoptionalThe same objects as investigations, from a JSON file in this conversation's folder (a list of them, or {investigations: [...]}), or a list of such files read in order. Records a helper extracts: brief it to save them with save_file as such a file and to name the file in its reply, then pass the name here -- never retype them. Checked as inline records are, each problem naming its file. Combines with inline investigations; one investigation_id in two inputs is refused, naming both.
lab_tests_filestr|arrayoptionalThe same for lab_tests: a JSON file (or files) of lab_tests objects, or {lab_tests: [...]}.
projectdictoptional{name, number, client, location, coordinate_system, elevation_datum} as printed.
output_pathstroptionalA file name for the .xml, e.g. 'site.diggs.xml'; omitted, it is named after the investigations (e.g. 'B-1_to_B-12.diggs.xml'). In the app it is written into this conversation's folder, whatever directory is given, and attached to the conversation.
document_idstroptionalAn identifier for the source document.

validate_diggs_dictionary — Validate DIGGS propertyClass values against DIGGS dictionary (via pydiggs).

ParameterTypeDescription
file_pathstroptionalPath to DIGGS XML file. Provide file_path or content, not both.
contentstroptionalDIGGS XML as string.

10.1.22 gstools — Geostatistics (kriging, random fields & conditional simulation)

kriging — Kriging (ordinary/simple/universal): ONE smoothed best estimate of a property between points -- the mean surface and its kriging variance. It understates the spread and cannot give the probability of a total over an area (use conditional_simulation).

ParameterTypeDescription
xarrayrequiredX-coordinates of measurement points (m).
yarrayrequiredY-coordinates of measurement points (m).
valuesarrayrequiredMeasured values at each point.
model_typestroptionalGSTools covariance model. allowed: Gaussian, Exponential, Matern, Spherical, Linear, Stable, Rational, Cubic, HyperSpherical default: "Gaussian"
kriging_typestroptionalordinary = unknown constant mean; simple = known mean (the sample mean of these observations); universal = linear drift in x and y. allowed: ordinary, simple, universal default: "ordinary"
grid_x_minfloatoptionalGrid X minimum (m). Omitted: the data's x range less 10%.
grid_x_maxfloatoptionalGrid X maximum (m). Omitted: the data's x range plus 10%.
grid_y_minfloatoptionalGrid Y minimum (m). Omitted: from the data, as x.
grid_y_maxfloatoptionalGrid Y maximum (m). Omitted: from the data, as x.
n_grid_xintoptionalGrid points in X (1 with min = max for one coordinate). default: 50
n_grid_yintoptionalGrid points in Y. default: 50
variancefloatoptionalSill variance (value units squared). Omitted: the sample variance of THESE observations. With fit_variogram=true (the default) it is only the starting guess and is overridden by the fit.
len_scalefloatoptionalCorrelation length (m). Omitted: a third of the data extent. With fit_variogram=true it is only the starting guess and is overridden by the fit.
nuggetfloatoptionalNugget variance (measurement error + variation below the data spacing); with a nugget the surface does not pass exactly through the data. With fit_variogram=true the nugget is fitted too, unless fit_nugget=false. default: 0.0
fit_variogrambooloptionalFit variance, len_scale AND nugget to the empirical variogram, overriding values given for them (the fitted values are returned). Refused with too few lag classes: then set false and give variance and len_scale. default: true
fit_nuggetbooloptionalWith fit_variogram: false holds the nugget at the value given (e.g. from the measurement error or twinned borings) and fits only variance and len_scale. Without fit_variogram nothing is fitted and true is refused. default: true
regionsarrayoptionalPlan regions: [{name, polygon: [[x, y], ...], level}], level one number or a list of levels to sweep (same units as values, e.g. an elevation in m). Totals over the cells whose centre is inside the polygon (concave shapes fine): volume_above = sum(max(z - level, 0) x cell area), area_above = cell area where z > level (the 'below' versions mirror it). Here from the kriging only: the kriged surface's totals, and Gaussian POINTWISE expectations (expected volume, expected area, mean cell probability). These are expectations cell by cell; the probability that a TOTAL exceeds a value needs conditional_simulation.
cell_sizefloatoptionalCell size (m) for the region totals; default the smallest round size giving at most ~3,000 cells.
quantitystroptionalRegion totals above (e.g. rock above an excavation level) or below (e.g. fill to a grade) the level. allowed: above, below default: "above"
marginfloatoptionalMargin (m) of the region lattice around the regions.
output_prefixstroptionalFile name stem for the files this call writes (<stem>_grid.csv for a grid over 2,500 points, <stem>_regions.csv with regions, <stem>_kriging_map.png); default kriging_<time>.
figuresbooloptionalDraw the kriging map: a plan, to scale, of the kriged mean and the kriging standard deviation as labelled contours, the standard deviation with a colour scale too (PNG + interactive). Set false in a sweep of many calls. default: true
namesarrayoptionalObservation names (e.g. boring IDs), one per point; label the map.
value_namestroptionalWhat the values are, in the logs' words (e.g. 'top of hard rock elevation'); names the map. Give it.
value_unitstroptionalUnit of the values (e.g. 'm').
north_degfloatoptionalNorth on the map, degrees clockwise from up, as the source plan shows it; up when not given.
outlinesarrayoptionalWhat the source plan shows besides the borings, drawn on the map for orientation: the property line, buildings, walls, roads. A list of {name, polygon: [[x, y], ...]} (closed, 3 points or more) or {name, line: [[x, y], ...]} (open, 2 or more), in the same x, y as the observations, with kind 'property_line' (drawn dash-dot) or 'outline' (default). Drawing only: they change no number.
observations_namestroptionalWhat the observation points are, in the logs' words (e.g. 'Borings', 'CPT soundings'): the map legend's name for them. 'Observations' when not given.

variogram — Estimate and fit an empirical variogram from spatial data (sill, range, nugget).

ParameterTypeDescription
xarrayrequiredX-coordinates of measurement points (m).
yarrayrequiredY-coordinates of measurement points (m).
valuesarrayrequiredMeasured values at each point.
model_typestroptionalCovariance model to fit. allowed: Gaussian, Exponential, Matern, Spherical, Linear, Stable, Rational, Cubic, HyperSpherical default: "Gaussian"
n_binsintoptionalNumber of lag classes between 0 and the largest pair separation. default: 10
nuggetfloatoptionalNugget variance. Left out: fitted with the sill and range. A number (0 or more): the nugget is fixed at it and only the sill and range are fitted (0 = no nugget). The nugget used is returned, with nugget_fitted.

random_field — Generate ONE UNconditioned 2D random field (mean + correlated variation). It does NOT honour any data; for realizations that pass through observations use conditional_simulation.

ParameterTypeDescription
model_typestroptionalCovariance model. allowed: Gaussian, Exponential, Matern, Spherical, Linear, Stable, Rational, Cubic, HyperSpherical default: "Gaussian"
variancefloatoptionalField variance. default: 1.0
len_scalefloatoptionalCorrelation length (m). default: 10.0
nuggetfloatoptionalNugget variance. default: 0.0
meanfloatoptionalMean value. default: 0.0
x_minfloatoptionalX-axis minimum (m). default: 0.0
x_maxfloatoptionalX-axis maximum (m). default: 100.0
y_minfloatoptionalY-axis minimum (m). default: 0.0
y_maxfloatoptionalY-axis maximum (m). default: 100.0
n_xintoptionalGrid points in X. default: 50
n_yintoptionalGrid points in Y. default: 50
seedintoptionalRandom seed for reproducibility. default: 42

conditional_simulation — Realizations that honour the data (conditioned random field), each integrated over plan polygons: probabilities of a TOTAL over an area -- volume above/below a level (rock to excavate, fill), area, any encounter -- with percentiles, exceedance, CSV files and figures.

ParameterTypeDescription
xarrayrequiredX-coordinates of the observations (m), at least 3.
yarrayrequiredY-coordinates of the observations (m).
valuesarrayrequiredObserved values, e.g. top-of-rock elevation (m) at each boring.
regionsarrayrequiredPlan regions: [{name, polygon: [[x, y], ...], level}], level one number or a list of levels to sweep (same units as values, e.g. an elevation in m). Totals over the cells whose centre is inside the polygon (concave shapes fine): volume_above = sum(max(z - level, 0) x cell area), area_above = cell area where z > level (the 'below' versions mirror it). Every region and level uses the SAME realizations, so differences between footprints or levels are meaningful.
namesarrayoptionalObservation names (e.g. boring IDs), one per point; label the map and files.
model_typestroptionalGSTools covariance model (Exponential is rougher than Gaussian). allowed: Gaussian, Exponential, Matern, Spherical, Linear, Stable, Rational, Cubic, HyperSpherical default: "Gaussian"
variancefloatoptionalSill variance (value units squared, m2 for elevations). Omitted: the sample variance of these observations, flagged. The percentiles follow it -- state its basis.
len_scalefloatoptionalCorrelation length (m). Omitted: a third of the data extent, flagged. State its basis.
nuggetfloatoptionalNugget variance (error + variation below the data spacing); default 0, or the largest measurement_error. With a nugget the field does not pass exactly through the data.
fit_variogrambooloptionalFit variance, len_scale (and the nugget if not given) to the empirical variogram. Off by default: with a handful of borings a fitted variogram is unstable. default: false
kriging_typestroptionalordinary = unknown constant mean; simple = known mean (the sample mean); universal = linear drift in x and y (variance is then the residual's). allowed: ordinary, simple, universal default: "ordinary"
measurement_errorfloatoptionalError variance at the observations (GSTools cond_err), one number or one per point; not above the nugget (GSTools counts it in the nugget). The field then need not pass through the data.
anisfloatoptionalAnisotropy ratio (minor / main correlation length). default: 1.0
angle_degfloatoptionalDirection of the main correlation length, degrees counter-clockwise from +x (GSTools angles, in degrees here). default: 0.0
cell_sizefloatoptionalCell size (m); default the smallest round size giving <= ~3,000 cells; over 5,000 cells refused (the message names a size).
marginfloatoptionalMargin (m) of the lattice around the regions (kriged-mean file, map).
quantitystroptionalabove = volume/area of the field above the level (e.g. rock to excavate); below = below it (e.g. fill). allowed: above, below default: "above"
n_realizationsintoptionalRealizations (max 20,000). The convergence table shows if more are needed. default: 1000
seedintoptionalRealization i uses seed + i (reproducible). default: 42
simulation_methodstroptionalkriging_residual = conditioning by kriging (Journel & Huijbregts 1978): draws what the chosen model implies, including the correlation between cells; seconds. condsrf = GSTools CondSRF (kriged field + unconditional field scaled by the kriging std): right pointwise variance, unconditioned correlation, so totals can spread too much; slower. condsrf reproduces a CondSRF notebook. allowed: kriging_residual, condsrf default: "kriging_residual"
boundsarrayoptionalInequality data [{x, y, max} or {x, y, min}, optional name], e.g. a boring that ended above rock: rock surface below its bottom elevation -> max.
bounds_modestroptionalreport = how often each bound is violated; reject = keep only realizations satisfying every bound (rejection sampling, not inequality kriging; at most 10 x n_realizations draws; acceptance rate reported). allowed: report, reject default: "report"
report_valuesarrayoptionalTotals for the exceedance table P(V > v); default round values per region and level.
figuresbooloptionalDraw the exceedance curve and the probability map (PNG + interactive). default: true
output_prefixstroptionalFile name stem for the CSVs and figures (default conditional_sim_<time>).
value_namestroptionalWhat the values are, in the logs' words (e.g. 'top of hard rock elevation'); names the figures. Give it.
value_unitstroptionalUnit of the values and the levels (e.g. 'm').
north_degfloatoptionalNorth on the map, degrees clockwise from up, as the source plan shows it; up when not given.
outlinesarrayoptionalWhat the source plan shows besides the borings, drawn on the probability map for orientation: the property line, buildings, walls, roads. A list of {name, polygon: [[x, y], ...]} (closed, 3 points or more) or {name, line: [[x, y], ...]} (open, 2 or more), in the same x, y as the observations, with kind 'property_line' (drawn dash-dot) or 'outline' (default). Drawing only: they change no number, and the regions are drawn anyway.
observations_namestroptionalWhat the observation points are, in the logs' words (e.g. 'Borings', 'CPT soundings'): the map legend's name for them. 'Observations' when not given.

10.1.23 reliability — Reliability engine

fosm — FOSM / Taylor-series reliability (Duncan 2000, UFC 3-220-20): central differences at +/-1 sigma -> moments of g, beta (normal+lognormal), pf, and the per-variable variance-contribution table (which variable matters). 2n+1 g-evaluations; supports correlation.

ParameterTypeDescription
variablesobjectrequiredRandom variables: {name: {mean, cov or std, dist, lower, upper}}. dist one of ['normal', 'lognormal', 'uniform', 'triangular'] (default normal). lower/upper truncate normal/lognormal or bound uniform/triangular. Example: {'su': {'mean': 50, 'cov': 0.3, 'dist': 'lognormal'}}.
g_expressionstrrequiredPerformance function of the variable names. With convention='fos' write a FACTOR OF SAFETY (failure at g<1), e.g. 'R/S'; with 'margin' a margin (failure at g<0), e.g. 'R - S'. Math functions allowed (sqrt, log, exp, tan, radians, ...).
conventionstroptional'fos': g is a factor of safety (failure g<1, lognormal beta reported). 'margin': g = R-S (failure g<0). allowed: fos, margin default: "fos"
correlationobjectoptionalPairwise correlations {'a,b': rho} or full matrix [[...]] in variable order. Omit for independent variables.

pem — Rosenblueth point-estimate method (UFC 3-220-20 Eqs. 7-13/7-14): 2^n evaluations at mu+/-sigma (correlation-adjusted weights), or the 2n+1 'multiplicative' reduced scheme for many variables.

ParameterTypeDescription
variablesobjectrequiredRandom variables: {name: {mean, cov or std, dist, lower, upper}}. dist one of ['normal', 'lognormal', 'uniform', 'triangular'] (default normal). lower/upper truncate normal/lognormal or bound uniform/triangular. Example: {'su': {'mean': 50, 'cov': 0.3, 'dist': 'lognormal'}}.
g_expressionstrrequiredPerformance function of the variable names. With convention='fos' write a FACTOR OF SAFETY (failure at g<1), e.g. 'R/S'; with 'margin' a margin (failure at g<0), e.g. 'R - S'. Math functions allowed (sqrt, log, exp, tan, radians, ...).
conventionstroptional'fos': g is a factor of safety (failure g<1, lognormal beta reported). 'margin': g = R-S (failure g<0). allowed: fos, margin default: "fos"
correlationobjectoptionalPairwise correlations {'a,b': rho} or full matrix [[...]] in variable order. Omit for independent variables.
schemestroptional'full' = 2^n points; 'multiplicative' = Rosenblueth 2n+1 (uncorrelated only). allowed: full, multiplicative default: "full"

monte_carlo — Monte Carlo simulation: seeded numpy sampling (optional Latin Hypercube), correlation via Cholesky in normal space, empirical pf with 95% CI + convergence trace, histogram, lognormal-fit beta. Its variables are scalars; for a property that varies across a site and must honour borings (e.g. a rock surface under a footprint), use gstools.conditional_simulation.

ParameterTypeDescription
variablesobjectrequiredRandom variables: {name: {mean, cov or std, dist, lower, upper}}. dist one of ['normal', 'lognormal', 'uniform', 'triangular'] (default normal). lower/upper truncate normal/lognormal or bound uniform/triangular. Example: {'su': {'mean': 50, 'cov': 0.3, 'dist': 'lognormal'}}.
g_expressionstrrequiredPerformance function of the variable names. With convention='fos' write a FACTOR OF SAFETY (failure at g<1), e.g. 'R/S'; with 'margin' a margin (failure at g<0), e.g. 'R - S'. Math functions allowed (sqrt, log, exp, tan, radians, ...).
conventionstroptional'fos': g is a factor of safety (failure g<1, lognormal beta reported). 'margin': g = R-S (failure g<0). allowed: fos, margin default: "fos"
correlationobjectoptionalPairwise correlations {'a,b': rho} or full matrix [[...]] in variable order. Omit for independent variables.
nintoptionalRealizations. Aim n >= 10/pf. default: 10000
seedintoptionalRNG seed for reproducibility.
samplingstroptional'lhs' = Latin Hypercube (variance reduction). allowed: random, lhs default: "random"
n_binsintoptionalHistogram bins. default: 30

form — Native FORM (Hasofer-Lind / Rackwitz-Fiessler): HL-RF iteration with equivalent-normal transformation of non-normal variables; exact for the linear/lognormal cases. Returns beta, pf, design point x*, and alpha sensitivity vector (alpha^2 = uncertainty share).

ParameterTypeDescription
variablesobjectrequiredRandom variables: {name: {mean, cov or std, dist, lower, upper}}. dist one of ['normal', 'lognormal', 'uniform', 'triangular'] (default normal). lower/upper truncate normal/lognormal or bound uniform/triangular. Example: {'su': {'mean': 50, 'cov': 0.3, 'dist': 'lognormal'}}.
g_expressionstrrequiredPerformance function of the variable names. With convention='fos' write a FACTOR OF SAFETY (failure at g<1), e.g. 'R/S'; with 'margin' a margin (failure at g<0), e.g. 'R - S'. Math functions allowed (sqrt, log, exp, tan, radians, ...).
conventionstroptional'fos': g is a factor of safety (failure g<1, lognormal beta reported). 'margin': g = R-S (failure g<0). allowed: fos, margin default: "fos"
correlationobjectoptionalPairwise correlations {'a,b': rho} or full matrix [[...]] in variable order. Omit for independent variables.
max_iterationsintoptionalHL-RF iteration cap. default: 100

cov_guidance — Published COV ranges for soil/rock properties with full provenance: Duncan (2000) Table 1, ISSMGE-TC304 (2021) site-specific statistics (clay/sand/rock), Phoon & Kulhawy (1999) transformation uncertainty (via UFC 3-220-20). Use to pick a defensible cov for the engines.

ParameterTypeDescription
propertystrrequiredProperty key or alias: phi/friction_angle, su, gamma/unit_weight, N/spt, qc/cpt, Cc, w, LL, PL, PI, OCR, K0, sigma_ci/ucs, RQD, GSI, ...
soil_typestroptionalFilter: 'clay', 'sand', 'rock'.
teststroptionalFilter by test, e.g. 'SPT', 'CPT', 'VST'.
categorystroptionalUncertainty component. allowed: inherent, site_specific, total_test, transformation

combined_cov — Combine inherent + measurement + transformation COVs (UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 7-5), optionally with Vanmarcke spatial-averaging variance reduction on the inherent part. All COVs as fractions (0.3 = 30%).

ParameterTypeDescription
cov_inherentfloatrequiredInherent (spatial) COV, fraction.
cov_measurementfloatoptionalMeasurement-error COV. default: 0.0
cov_transformationfloatoptionalTransformation-model COV. default: 0.0
variance_reductionfloatoptionalGamma^2 from the variance_reduction method (1 = point property). default: 1.0

variance_reduction — Vanmarcke variance reduction Gamma^2(L/delta) for spatial averaging over a failure surface/pile length. Give delta directly or a soil_type to use published scale-of-fluctuation guidance (Cami et al. 2020 / ISSMGE-TC304 2021).

ParameterTypeDescription
LfloatrequiredAveraging length (m).
deltafloatoptionalScale of fluctuation (m). Omit to look up by soil_type.
soil_typestroptionale.g. 'clay', 'sand', 'silt', 'soft clay' — used when delta is omitted (vertical average).
modelstroptional'exponential' (exact Markov ACF) or 'simple' (delta/L). allowed: exponential, simple default: "exponential"

10.1.24 salib — Global sensitivity analysis (SALib)

sobol_analysis — ONE CALL Sobol variance-based sensitivity: samples, evaluates the model (an expression or a calculation-module spec) at every point, returns S1/ST indices only. Use this, not sobol_sample + sobol_analyze.

ParameterTypeDescription
var_namesarrayrequiredVariable names (at least 2); the names the expression or variable_map uses.
boundsarrayrequired[min, max] for each variable, in var_names order (uniform over the range).
expressionstroptionalThe model as a safe arithmetic expression of the variables (the reliability engines' g_expression rules): +, -, *, /, **, %, comparisons, 'a if cond else b', and sqrt/log/exp/sin/cos/tan/asin/acos/atan/atan2/sinh/cosh/tanh/log10/ceil/floor/radians/degrees/abs/min/max/pi; scientific notation (1e-3) is fine. E.g. '(c + 18*z*tan(radians(phi)))/40'. Give this OR model (exactly one).
modeldictoptionalThe model as a calculation-module run per sample point, instead of expression: {agent_name, method, parameters (the fixed inputs), output (the result key to analyse; a dotted path such as 'results.fos' reaches into a nested result), variable_map (optional {variable: parameter}; default: each variable sets the parameter of the same name; a dotted path such as 'layers.0.phi' sets a nested value that already exists in parameters)}. E.g. {'agent_name': 'bearing_capacity', 'method': 'bearing_capacity_analysis', 'parameters': {'width': 2, 'depth': 1, 'unit_weight': 18}, 'output': 'q_ultimate_kPa', 'variable_map': {'phi': 'friction_angle', 'c': 'cohesion'}}. Calculation modules only (axial_pile, bearing_capacity, concrete_props, dm7, downdrag, drilled_shaft, fem2d, ground_improvement, lateral_pile, liquefaction, pavement_design, pile_group, pynite, retaining_walls, section_props, seismic_geotech, settlement, sheet_pile, slope_stability, soe, wave_equation); no file parameters. One trial run at the centre of the bounds checks the spec and prices the design against time_budget_s. Give this OR expression (exactly one).
n_samplesintoptionalBase sample size N (a power of 2). Evaluations = N*(D+2), or N*(2D+2) with calc_second_order. default: 256
calc_second_orderbooloptionalAlso compute second-order interaction indices S2 (doubles the evaluations). default: false
seedintoptionalRandom seed. default: 42
max_evaluationsintoptionalRefuse a design needing more model evaluations than this. default: 20000
time_budget_sfloatoptionalmodel only: refuse a design whose projected run time (trial run x evaluations) exceeds this, in seconds (max 600). default: 120.0

morris_analysis — ONE CALL Morris elementary-effects screening: samples, evaluates the model (an expression or a calculation-module spec) at every point, returns mu*/sigma only. Cheaper than Sobol: evaluations = n_trajectories*(D+1).

ParameterTypeDescription
var_namesarrayrequiredVariable names (at least 2); the names the expression or variable_map uses.
boundsarrayrequired[min, max] for each variable, in var_names order.
expressionstroptionalThe model as a safe arithmetic expression of the variables (the reliability engines' g_expression rules): +, -, *, /, **, %, comparisons, 'a if cond else b', and sqrt/log/exp/sin/cos/tan/asin/acos/atan/atan2/sinh/cosh/tanh/log10/ceil/floor/radians/degrees/abs/min/max/pi; scientific notation (1e-3) is fine. E.g. '(c + 18*z*tan(radians(phi)))/40'. Give this OR model (exactly one).
modeldictoptionalThe model as a calculation-module run per sample point, instead of expression: {agent_name, method, parameters (the fixed inputs), output (the result key to analyse; a dotted path such as 'results.fos' reaches into a nested result), variable_map (optional {variable: parameter}; default: each variable sets the parameter of the same name; a dotted path such as 'layers.0.phi' sets a nested value that already exists in parameters)}. E.g. {'agent_name': 'bearing_capacity', 'method': 'bearing_capacity_analysis', 'parameters': {'width': 2, 'depth': 1, 'unit_weight': 18}, 'output': 'q_ultimate_kPa', 'variable_map': {'phi': 'friction_angle', 'c': 'cohesion'}}. Calculation modules only (axial_pile, bearing_capacity, concrete_props, dm7, downdrag, drilled_shaft, fem2d, ground_improvement, lateral_pile, liquefaction, pavement_design, pile_group, pynite, retaining_walls, section_props, seismic_geotech, settlement, sheet_pile, slope_stability, soe, wave_equation); no file parameters. One trial run at the centre of the bounds checks the spec and prices the design against time_budget_s. Give this OR expression (exactly one).
n_trajectoriesintoptionalNumber of Morris trajectories. default: 20
num_levelsintoptionalNumber of grid levels. default: 4
seedintoptionalRandom seed. default: 42
max_evaluationsintoptionalRefuse a design needing more model evaluations than this. default: 20000
time_budget_sfloatoptionalmodel only: refuse a design whose projected run time (trial run x evaluations) exceeds this, in seconds (max 600). default: 120.0

sobol_sample — Generate Sobol quasi-random sample matrix for variance-based sensitivity analysis (two-step: YOU evaluate the model on every row, then sobol_analyze). Prefer sobol_analysis, which does it in one call.

ParameterTypeDescription
var_namesarrayrequiredList of variable names (at least 2).
boundsarrayrequiredList of [min, max] bounds for each variable.
n_samplesintoptionalBase number of Sobol samples. Total rows = N*(2D+2) for second-order. default: 1024
calc_second_orderbooloptionalInclude second-order interaction indices. default: true
seedintoptionalRandom seed for reproducibility. default: 42

sobol_analyze — Compute Sobol first-order and total-order sensitivity indices from model output.

ParameterTypeDescription
var_namesarrayrequiredList of variable names.
boundsarrayrequiredList of [min, max] bounds for each variable.
YarrayrequiredModel output array, one value per sample point from sobol_sample().
n_samplesintoptionalIgnored: not used by the analysis and not echoed; the result's n_samples is the length of Y, which must match the sobol_sample design's row count. default: 1024
calc_second_orderbooloptionalWhether second-order indices were computed. default: true
seedintoptionalRandom seed for resampling. default: 42

morris_sample — Generate Morris one-at-a-time (OAT) sample matrix for screening (two-step: YOU evaluate the model on every row, then morris_analyze). Prefer morris_analysis, which does it in one call.

ParameterTypeDescription
var_namesarrayrequiredList of variable names (at least 2).
boundsarrayrequiredList of [min, max] bounds for each variable.
n_trajectoriesintoptionalNumber of Morris trajectories. default: 20
num_levelsintoptionalNumber of grid levels. default: 4
seedintoptionalRandom seed for reproducibility. default: 42

morris_analyze — Compute Morris elementary effects (mu*, sigma) for parameter screening.

ParameterTypeDescription
var_namesarrayrequiredList of variable names.
boundsarrayrequiredList of [min, max] bounds for each variable.
XarrayrequiredSample matrix from morris_sample().
YarrayrequiredModel output array, one value per sample row.
n_trajectoriesintoptionalRecorded only (echoed in the result): not used by the analysis. The trajectories analysed are implied by the length of X and Y. default: 20
num_levelsintoptionalNumber of grid levels used in morris_sample(). default: 4
seedintoptionalRandom seed. default: 42

10.1.25 pystra — Structural reliability (pystra)

form_analysis — First Order Reliability Method (FORM) — find design point and reliability index.

ParameterTypeDescription
variablesarrayrequiredList of dicts with keys: name (str), dist (normal/lognormal/gumbel/uniform/constant/weibull/gamma_dist/beta), mean (float), stdv (float), value (float, for constant). uniform takes a (lower) and b (upper) instead of mean/stdv.
limit_statestrrequiredLimit state expression string. Positive = safe, negative = failure. Example: 'R - S'.
correlationarrayoptionalOptional correlation matrix as list of lists (symmetric, positive definite, 1.0 on diagonal).

sorm_analysis — Second Order Reliability Method (SORM) — improved probability with curvature correction.

ParameterTypeDescription
variablesarrayrequiredList of dicts with keys: name, dist, mean, stdv (same as FORM); uniform takes a and b, constant takes value.
limit_statestrrequiredLimit state expression string. Positive = safe, negative = failure.
correlationarrayoptionalOptional correlation matrix as list of lists.

monte_carlo_analysis — Crude Monte Carlo reliability analysis — estimate failure probability by random sampling.

ParameterTypeDescription
variablesarrayrequiredList of dicts with keys: name, dist, mean, stdv (same as FORM); uniform takes a and b, constant takes value.
limit_statestrrequiredLimit state expression string. Positive = safe, negative = failure.
n_samplesintoptionalNumber of Monte Carlo samples. default: 100000
correlationarrayoptionalOptional correlation matrix as list of lists.

10.1.32 calc_package — Calc-package reporting

pavement_design_package — Pavement design calc package: AASHTO 1993 flexible (required SN + layer split) or rigid (slab D) with reliability, drainage, and forward checks, UFC 3-250-01 flexible or rigid, or the two methods compared. US customary units. The parameters of the pavement_design tool design_type names.

ParameterTypeDescription
design_typestroptionalWhich procedure to run and report: AASHTO 1993 flexible or rigid (flexible_pavement_design, rigid_pavement_design), UFC 3-250-01 flexible_ufc or rigid_ufc, or compare (compare_pavement_methods). allowed: flexible, rigid, flexible_ufc, rigid_ufc, compare also read as: ufc = flexible_ufc, ufc_flexible = flexible_ufc, ufc_rigid = rigid_ufc, comparison = compare default: "flexible"
w18numberoptionalRequired when design_type is flexible or rigid. design_type=flexible: Design-lane 18-kip ESALs over the performance period (use design_traffic_esals to build it). | design_type=rigid: Design-lane 18-kip ESALs.
layersarrayoptionalRequired when design_type is flexible. List of layer dicts, TOP-DOWN; first must be layer_type 'asphalt'. Each: {layer_type: asphalt|granular_base|granular_subbase|cement_treated_base|bituminous_treated_base; modulus_psi (EAC/EBS/ESB -- required on granular layers below the surface in design mode); ucs_7day_psi (cement-treated, Fig 2.8 scale 200-1000 psi); marshall_stability_lb (bituminous-treated, Fig 2.9 scale 200-1800 lb); a (direct coefficient override); m (drainage, unbound layers) or drainage_quality + pct_saturation_time ('<1%'|'1-5%'|'5-25%'|'>25%'); thickness_in (set on EVERY layer for a check instead of a design); min_thickness_in (over a layer stiffer than 40,000 psi, e.g. a treated base, no SN is solved (II-37) and the layer above takes this or the Sec 3.1.4 minimum)}.
reliability_pctnumberoptionalDefault: compare 95 (design_type). design_type=flexible: Reliability R % (50-99.99), Table 4.1 -> ZR. Or give zr. | design_type=rigid: Reliability R % -> ZR (or give zr). | design_type=compare: AASHTO-side reliability.
zrnumberoptionaldesign_type=flexible: Standard normal deviate directly (overrides reliability_pct). | design_type=rigid: Standard normal deviate directly.
sonumberoptionalDefault: flexible 0.45; rigid 0.35; compare 0.45 (design_type). design_type=flexible: Overall standard deviation (flexible range 0.40-0.50). | design_type=rigid: Overall standard deviation (rigid 0.30-0.40). | design_type=compare: AASHTO overall standard deviation.
mr_psinumberoptionaldesign_type=flexible: Effective roadbed resilient modulus, psi (or monthly_mr_psi). | design_type=rigid: Roadbed MR, psi -> simplified k = MR/19.4 (no subbase). | design_type=compare: Subgrade Mr (CBR derived by inversion).
monthly_mr_psiarrayoptionalSeasonal roadbed MR list (psi) -> Fig 2.3/2.4 effective MR.
ptnumberoptionaldesign_type=flexible: Terminal serviceability. | design_type=rigid: Terminal serviceability (also in the strength-term exponent). | design_type=compare: AASHTO terminal serviceability. default: 2.5
ponumberoptionalDefault: flexible 4.2; rigid 4.5 (design_type). Initial serviceability.
delta_psinumberoptionaldesign_type=flexible: Serviceability loss directly (else po - pt). | design_type=rigid: Serviceability loss directly.
thickness_increment_innumberoptionaldesign_type=flexible: Round-UP increment. | design_type=flexible_ufc: Round layer thicknesses up to this increment (in). | design_type=rigid_ufc: Round the slab up to this increment (in). default: 0.5
enforce_minimumsbooleanoptionalApply Sec 3.1.4 minimum AC/base thicknesses. default: true
swellingobjectoptionalRoadbed swelling spec (Appendix G / Fig G.4): {vr_in: potential vertical rise (in), ps_pct: percent of area subject to swell, theta: swell rate constant (~0.04-0.20)}. Requires design_period_yr.
frostobjectoptionaldesign_type=flexible: Frost heave spec (Appendix G / Fig G.8): {phi_mm_day: heave rate, pf_pct: percent of area subject to heave, delta_psi_max: max loss (Fig G.7, from drainage quality x frost depth)}. Requires design_period_yr. | design_type=flexible_ufc: {uscs_class, finer_than_0_02mm_pct, frost_group} -> Ch 19 reduced-subgrade-strength frost check; governing section reported. frost_group (optional): the group a laboratory frost test set (Table 19-2 footnote ***); a soil Table 19-2 does not list is refused without it.
design_period_yrnumberoptionalAnalysis period (yr); required with swelling/frost -- their dPSI loss is subtracted from the design budget before the solve.
sc_psinumberoptionalRequired when design_type is rigid. PCC modulus of rupture (28-day, third-point), psi.
ec_psinumberoptionalRequired when design_type is rigid. PCC elastic modulus, psi.
jnumberoptionalLoad transfer coefficient J directly (else Table 2.6 midpoint from pavement_type/shoulder_type/load_transfer_devices).
pavement_typestringoptionalFor the Table 2.6 J lookup. allowed: plain_jointed_jrcp, crcp default: "plain_jointed_jrcp"
shoulder_typestringoptionalFor the Table 2.6 J lookup. allowed: asphalt, tied_pcc default: "asphalt"
load_transfer_devicesbooleanoptionalDowels present. default: true
cdnumberoptionalDrainage coefficient directly (else Table 2.5 midpoint from drainage_quality). default: 1.0
drainage_qualitystringoptionalFor the Table 2.5 Cd lookup. allowed: excellent, good, fair, poor, very_poor
pct_saturation_timestringoptionalMoisture exposure for the Cd lookup. allowed: <1%, 1-5%, 5-25%, >25%
k_pcinumberoptionaldesign_type=rigid: Effective modulus of subgrade reaction directly, pci. Give exactly one of k_pci / mr_psi / composite_k. | design_type=rigid_ufc: Modulus of subgrade reaction, 25 pci or more; above 500 taken as 500 (Table 10-1 note 2). Or give subgrade for Table 10-1.
composite_kobjectoptionalSec 3.2 worksheet spec: {seasonal: [{mr_psi, ...}], dsb_in, esb_psi, dsg_ft, ls}; slab_d_in is iterated automatically. Fig 3.3 is read off the printed chart: dsb_in 6-18, esb_psi 15,000-1,000,000, mr_psi 1,000-20,000.
slab_thickness_innumberoptionalGive to CHECK a slab instead of designing.
passes_18kipnumberoptionalRequired when design_type is flexible_ufc or rigid_ufc or compare. design_type=flexible_ufc: Design-life passes of the 18-kip single axle (design lane), 10 to 10,000,000 (the range Figure E-1 prints). NOT interchangeable with AASHTO W18 conceptually — same count, different damage model. | design_type=rigid_ufc: 18-kip single-axle passes, 1,000 to 50,000,000 (Figure F-1's pass-level lines). | design_type=compare: 18-kip single-axle passes (= AASHTO W18; LEF 1.0 by definition).
cbr_subgradenumberoptionalRequired when design_type is flexible_ufc. design_type=flexible_ufc: Subgrade design CBR (%), 1 or more. | design_type=compare: Subgrade CBR (Mr derived via FHWA 2555*CBR^0.64). Give this OR mr_psi.
cbr_basenumberoptionaldesign_type=flexible_ufc: Base course design CBR. | design_type=compare: Base CBR (both sides; AASHTO EBS read across the guide's Figure 2.6, CBR 20-100, unless ebs_psi given). default: 80
cbr_subbasenumberoptionalDefault: compare 30 (design_type). design_type=flexible_ufc: Subbase CBR (omit for a 2-layer section). A subbase is at least 4 in (UFC p. 20). | design_type=compare: Subbase CBR (both sides; AASHTO ESB read across Figure 2.7, CBR about 9-100, unless esb_psi given).
flexural_strength_psinumberoptionalRequired when design_type is rigid_ufc. Concrete 28-day flexural strength R (psi), 100-1,000. For a parking area para 13-3 enters R / 0.75.
subgradeobjectoptional{uscs_group, moisture_pct} -> Table 10-1 k.
stabilized_foundationobjectoptional{ef_psi, hs_in} -> Eq 13-1 reduction.
eac_psinumberoptionalAASHTO asphalt modulus. default: 400000
ebs_psinumberoptionalAASHTO base modulus override.
esb_psinumberoptionalAASHTO subbase modulus override.
project_namestroptionalProject name for header. default: "Project"
project_numberstroptionalProject number for header.
engineerstroptionalEngineer name for header.
checkerstroptionalChecker name for header.
companystroptionalCompany name for header.
datestroptionalDate string (auto-filled if empty).
assumptionsdictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user did not give, as {input name: its basis}, e.g. {"unit_weight": "not given; typical of the soil described"}. An assumption that is not an input is its own row: {"drained": "long-term condition"}. The package lists them under Assumed Inputs with the analysis's own defaults, so no assumption reads as given. A misspelt input name is refused with a did-you-mean.
givenlist|dictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user gave, by the names you pass them under, e.g. ["width", "depth", "friction_angle"], or with the user's own words, {"friction_angle": "phi 32 deg from the boring logs"}. Only these print under Given Inputs. Every other input you pass prints under Assumed Inputs as passed, not stated as given (with its basis when it is in assumptions); left out, no input is the user's. A value you read off, worked out or chose is assumed, not given.
output_pathstroptionalFile path to save output. Auto-generated if omitted.
formatstroptionalOutput format: 'html' (recommended, self-contained with embedded CSS), 'latex' (raw .tex source), or 'pdf' (requires pdflatex installed). HTML is always available; PDF requires a LaTeX compiler on the system. allowed: html, latex, pdf default: "html"

render_figures — The FIGURES of any canned *_package — slope section + trial-surface map, p-y curves, settlement/consolidation plots, wall pressure diagrams, pavement charts, FEM mesh/contours — saved as standalone PNGs WITHOUT building the package. For a bespoke html_to_pdf report (SOE, a multi-analysis narrative, anything with no canned template): run the analysis here, paste each figure's html_img_tag into your HTML. Same inputs as the package.

ParameterTypeDescription
packagestrrequiredWhich package's figures: e.g. 'slope_stability_package', 'axial_pile_package', 'settlement_package'. Any *_package method of this module except html_to_pdf. PLUS every input the named package takes, beside it — describe_method('calc_package', '<package>') lists them. The analysis runs exactly as the package would.
output_dirstroptionalFolder for the PNGs (one per figure). Defaults to the working folder.
name_prefixstroptionalFile-name prefix (default: module).

render_tables — The CALCULATION of any canned *_package as an HTML file, WITHOUT building the package, for a report you compose with html_to_pdf: the given and assumed inputs, the values used, the method choices, each step with its equation, the values put in, its result and its reference, the checks, the calculation tables and the reference list, printed as the package prints them. Same inputs as the package. Paste the returned html_include_tag into your report HTML where the calculation goes. The figures come from render_figures.

ParameterTypeDescription
packagestrrequiredWhich package's calculation: e.g. 'bearing_capacity_package', 'retaining_wall_package', 'soe_package'. Any *_package method of this module. PLUS every input the named package takes, beside it, given and assumptions included: describe_method('calc_package', '<package>') lists them. The analysis runs exactly as the package would.
output_pathstroptionalThe HTML file to write. Defaults to <module>_calculation_<time>.html in the working folder.

html_to_pdf — Render self-contained HTML (e.g. a custom report YOU composed) to a paginated PDF on the REAL filesystem. Use when no canned *_package method matches the analysis — compose the report HTML yourself (inline CSS; figures as a real local PNG path or a base64 PNG/JPEG data URI) and pass it here. Figures it cannot embed are a hard ERROR, never a silent blank. A figure that does not fit what is left of a page starts the next page at its full size; one taller than a page is scaled to fit a page. Backgrounds are not drawn: set things off with borders, bold or coloured text. A canned package's calculation (inputs, steps, tables) goes in from render_tables, its figures from render_figures. Pure-Python (PyMuPDF Story engine).

ParameterTypeDescription
htmlstroptionalSelf-contained HTML content to render: the finished page as ONE string value, written out in full with each figure's <img> tag in place (nothing in the call is run, so no code builds or edits it). Inline all CSS. FIGURES: use <img src="fig.png"> (a PNG/JPEG in the working folder, named as the figure tool returned it, or a real local path, is read and embedded for you — this is the easy path, e.g. the html_img_tag returned by profile_figure) or a base64 PNG/JPEG data URI. Inline <svg>, remote image URLs and literal '[image]' placeholders are REJECTED with a list of what to fix. CALCULATIONS: paste render_tables' html_include_tag, <div data-include="file.html"></div>, empty; that file's calculation is put there, with its styles. Provide this or 'html_path'.
html_pathstroptionalPath to an existing HTML file on the REAL filesystem (a save_file or calc-package output path — NOT a sandboxed scratch-filesystem path). Relative <img> paths inside it resolve against the working folder.
output_pathstroptionalPDF output path. Auto-generated if omitted.
allow_unembeddablebooloptionalEscape hatch: render anyway when the HTML references figures that cannot be embedded, instead of erroring. Those figures WILL BE MISSING from the PDF — the response then carries 'unembeddable' and 'renderer_warnings', and you must tell the user which figures are absent. Prefer fixing the figures. default: false

bearing_capacity_package — Run bearing capacity analysis and generate Mathcad-style calc package, with a table (CSV + printed) of the factors N, s, d, i, b, g and the value of each term.

ParameterTypeDescription
widthfloatrequiredFooting width B (m).
lengthfloatoptionalFooting length L (m). Omit for strip.
depthfloatoptionalEmbedment depth Df (m). default: 0.0
shapestroptionalFooting shape. allowed: strip, square, rectangular, circular default: "strip"
cohesionfloatoptionalSoil cohesion c (kPa). default: 0.0
friction_anglefloatoptionalFriction angle phi (degrees). default: 0.0
unit_weightfloatrequiredSoil unit weight gamma (kN/m3).
gwt_depthfloatoptionalGroundwater depth below surface (m).
layer2_cohesionfloatoptionalSecond layer cohesion (kPa). default: 0.0
layer2_friction_anglefloatoptionalSecond layer phi (degrees). default: 0.0
layer2_unit_weightfloatoptionalSecond layer gamma (kN/m3). Triggers 2-layer analysis.
layer1_thicknessfloatoptionalFirst layer thickness (m) for 2-layer.
layer1_descriptionstroptionalFirst layer label for the result.
layer2_descriptionstroptionalSecond layer label for the result.
factor_of_safetyfloatoptionalFactor of safety. default: 3.0
factor_methodstroptionalShape/depth/inclination-factor method. Each takes its own N-gamma unless ngamma_method names another; 'meyerhof' = UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-6, with the shape factors 1 under an inclined load (its note A); it has no base-tilt or ground-slope factors (UFC p. 294, Table 5-3), so base_tilt and ground_slope are refused with it. Hansen applies to N-gamma only: use ngamma_method='hansen'. 'terzaghi' = Terzaghi (1943): his Nc, Nq, N-gamma and shape coefficients (1.3cNc; 0.4/0.3 gamma B Ngamma square/circular), no depth or inclination factors; not for inclined loads, slopes or tilted bases (UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-3). allowed: vesic, meyerhof, terzaghi default: "vesic"
ngamma_methodstroptionalNgamma factor method. Default depends on factor_method: the method's own, 'vesic' = 2(Nq+1)tan(phi) (GEC-6 Eq. 5-8), 'meyerhof' = (Nq-1)tan(1.4 phi) (UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-6), 'kumbhojkar' with factor_method='terzaghi'. 'hansen' = 1.5(Nq-1)tan(phi). Another than the method's own is a mixed method; the result's choices say so. With factor_method='terzaghi' (Terzaghi gave N-gamma only as a chart): 'kumbhojkar' (Kumbhojkar 1993 as tabulated in Das) or 'coduto' (Coduto et al. 2016 approximation, UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-2); the result reports the other beside it. allowed: vesic, meyerhof, hansen, kumbhojkar, coduto
failure_modestroptionalfactor_method='terzaghi' only: 'local' applies Terzaghi's local-shear reduction c* = 2/3 c, tan(phi*) = 2/3 tan(phi) (UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-4). allowed: general, local default: "general"
base_tiltfloatoptionalBase tilt angle (degrees). With factor_method 'vesic' only (GEC-6 Table 5-5 factors); 'meyerhof' and 'terzaghi' have none and refuse it (UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-3). default: 0.0
eccentricity_BfloatoptionalLoad eccentricity along B (m). default: 0.0
eccentricity_LfloatoptionalLoad eccentricity along L (m). default: 0.0
load_inclinationfloatoptionalLoad inclination from vertical (degrees), 0 to below 90; with factor_method 'meyerhof' below phi, as UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-6 takes theta = atan(H/V) < phi' (refused at phi or more). default: 0.0
ground_slopefloatoptionalGround slope angle down from horizontal (degrees), 0 to 45, this tool's own limit: Vesic's g_q = (1 - tan omega)^2 is 0 at 45 deg. With factor_method 'vesic' only; 'meyerhof' and 'terzaghi' have no ground-slope factors and refuse it (UFC 3-220-20 p. 294, Table 5-3). For a footing on or near a slope GEC-6 Sec. 5.2.3.4 uses N_cq and N_gamma-q (Fig. 5-7). default: 0.0
vertical_loadfloatoptionalRequired with factor_method 'vesic', a load_inclination and a soil with cohesion (or phi = 0): the vertical load V on the footing (kN; kN/m for a strip). Vesic's load inclination factors take H = V tan(load_inclination) over V + A' c cot(phi) (Vesic 1975, EN 1997-1:2004 Annex D.4); with c = 0 that is tan(load_inclination) and V cancels. Without it the call is refused (factor_method 'meyerhof' takes the angle alone, UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-6).
depth_factor_methodstroptionalDepth factors for an embedded footing. 'hansen': Brinch Hansen's (1970) k = Df/B below Df/B = 1, arctan(Df/B) from 1 (UFC 3-220-20 Tables 5-7, 5-8 note B) in the factor_method's d factors (Meyerhof's: k = Df/B up to 1 as UFC Table 5-6 prints it); at phi = 0 Vesic's cohesion term adds Table 5-7's d_c = 0.4 k, as UFC Eq. 5-21 does. 'gec6' (factor_method 'vesic' only): GEC-6 Eq. 5-14 and Table 5-4, d_q on the surcharge term alone, 1.0 below Df/B = 1. 'linear' (factor_method 'meyerhof' only): Meyerhof's depth factors with k = Df/B at every depth, as UFC Table 5-6 (p. 294) prints them, d_c = 1 + 0.2 k sqrt(Kp), d_q = d_gamma = 1 + 0.1 k sqrt(Kp) for phi > 10 deg (1 at phi = 0); larger than 'hansen' beyond Df/B = 1. 'none': no depth factors, as GEC-6 Sec. 5.2.3.3 advises unless the cover over the footing is competent and sure to stay. The result's choices give what each option gives. allowed: hansen, gec6, linear, none default: "hansen"
project_namestroptionalProject name for header. default: "Project"
project_numberstroptionalProject number for header.
engineerstroptionalEngineer name for header.
checkerstroptionalChecker name for header.
companystroptionalCompany name for header.
datestroptionalDate string (auto-filled if empty).
assumptionsdictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user did not give, as {input name: its basis}, e.g. {"unit_weight": "not given; typical of the soil described"}. An assumption that is not an input is its own row: {"drained": "long-term condition"}. The package lists them under Assumed Inputs with the analysis's own defaults, so no assumption reads as given. A misspelt input name is refused with a did-you-mean.
givenlist|dictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user gave, by the names you pass them under, e.g. ["width", "depth", "friction_angle"], or with the user's own words, {"friction_angle": "phi 32 deg from the boring logs"}. Only these print under Given Inputs. Every other input you pass prints under Assumed Inputs as passed, not stated as given (with its basis when it is in assumptions); left out, no input is the user's. A value you read off, worked out or chose is assumed, not given.
output_pathstroptionalFile path to save output. Auto-generated if omitted.
formatstroptionalOutput format: 'html' (recommended, self-contained with embedded CSS), 'latex' (raw .tex source), or 'pdf' (requires pdflatex installed). HTML is always available; PDF requires a LaTeX compiler on the system. allowed: html, latex, pdf default: "html"

lateral_pile_package — Run lateral pile analysis and generate LPILE-style calc package, with tables (CSV + printed) of y, slope, M, V, p and Es at every node and each layer's p-y curve.

ParameterTypeDescription
pile_typestroptionalPile type. h_pile requires designation; filled_pipe also requires pile_thickness. For a solid pile/drilled shaft, use 'pipe' with no pile_thickness and set pile_E. allowed: pipe, h_pile, filled_pipe default: "pipe"
pile_diameterfloatrequiredPile diameter (m).
pile_lengthfloatrequiredPile length (m).
pile_EfloatoptionalPile Young's modulus (kPa). DEFAULT IS STEEL (200e6) — for concrete drilled shafts set this explicitly, e.g. ~25e6 gross or a reduced value (e.g. 0.3x) for cracked sections. default: 200000000.0
pile_thicknessfloatoptionalWall thickness (m) for hollow pipe. Omit for a solid section.
moment_of_inertiafloatoptionalMoment of inertia (m4). Overrides the value computed from diameter/thickness.
designationstroptionalH-pile designation (e.g. 'HP360x132') — required for pile_type 'h_pile'.
axisstroptionalBending axis — pile_type 'h_pile' only. allowed: strong, weak default: "strong"
fcfloatoptionalConcrete f'c (kPa) — pile_type 'filled_pipe' only. default: 28000.0
layersarrayrequiredArray of {top, bottom, model, ...model params}. Required model params: SoftClayMatlock/StiffClayAboveWT {c, gamma, eps50}; StiffClayBelowWT {c, gamma, eps50} with ks for loading='static' or kc for 'cyclic' (kN/m3, the k of the initial line p = (k x) y; Reese, Cox & Koop, COM624P Table 3.2 / GEC 9 Table A-1: ks 135,700 / 271,400 / 542,900 and kc 54,300 / 108,600 / 217,200 for an average c to five diameters of 48-96 / 96-192 / 192-383 kPa); StiffClayBelowWT is Reese et al. (1975), stiff clay with free water: GEC 9 p. 219 keeps it for stiff clay exposed to free water at or near the ground surface, and with the groundwater at depth prefers StiffClayAboveWT (Welch & Reese) even below the water table, gamma then submerged; it does not say how near is near, so which of the two a stiff clay below the water table takes is the engineer's call: state it and why, or ask; SoftClayJeanjean {su, gamma, Gmax} (not checked against a print: neither Jeanjean 2009 nor API RP 2GEO is in the reference library; GEC 9's soft clay criterion is SoftClayMatlock); SandReese/SandAPI {phi, gamma, k} where k (kN/m3) is the k of the initial line p = (k z) y: for SandReese GEC 9 Table A-3 gives it by relative density only, loose / medium / dense 5,429 / 16,287 / 33,931 submerged and 6,786 / 24,430 / 61,076 above the water (20 / 60 / 125 and 25 / 90 / 225 lb/in3); for SandAPI API RP 2A Fig. 6.8.7-1 by phi', e.g. phi' 30 / 35 / 40: 9,260 / 22,260 / 42,510 below the water table and 12,650 / 36,970 / 75,270 above; WeakRock {qu, Er}. SandReese also takes optional construction='reese1974' (default: GEC 9 App. A.4's four-segment curve, linear -> parabola -> straight line -> p_u, A and B from Figs. A-10 and A-11) | 'simplified' (the module's own three-part curve, which no held page prints). StiffClayAboveWT with loading='cyclic' also needs n_cycles, N, the number of times the design lateral load is applied (>= 1; the references give no number to assume; Welch & Reese, COM624P Eq. 3.29, y_c = y_s + y50 C log N, so y50 times 1 + 0.6 log10 N). WeakRock (Reese 1997, FHWA GEC 9 App. A.5) also takes optional RQD (%, default 100: alpha_r = 1/3, the printed lower bound; alpha_r rises linearly to 1.0 at RQD 0), krm (default 0.0005, the softer end of 0.00005-0.0005) and rock_top (depth of the rock surface, m; default the top of the weak-rock layers that hold the layer); its gamma_r is accepted and not used (the criterion does not use the unit weight).
VtfloatoptionalLateral load at pile top (kN). default: 0.0
MtfloatoptionalMoment at pile top (kN-m). default: 0.0
head_conditionstroptionalPile head condition. allowed: free, fixed default: "free"
QfloatoptionalAxial load at pile top (kN), for P-delta. default: 0.0
stickupfloatoptionalAbove-ground free length (m): head loads/BCs act at the top of the stickup; no soil resistance over it. pile_length stays the EMBEDDED length. Alias: free_length. default: 0.0
n_elementsintoptionalFinite-difference elements along the pile. default: 100
tolerancefloatoptionalConvergence tolerance on deflection (m). default: 1e-05
max_iterationsintoptionalMost p-y iterations. If they run out, a push of the pile head decides: when the soil cannot resist the load the call fails with 'No solution: the soil cannot resist this load' and the most the pile and soil carry; otherwise the result says converged false with a message (raise max_iterations). default: 500

project_numberstroptionalProject number for header.
engineerstroptionalEngineer name for header.
checkerstroptionalChecker name for header.
companystroptionalCompany name for header.
datestroptionalDate string (auto-filled if empty).
assumptionsdictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user did not give, as {input name: its basis}, e.g. {"unit_weight": "not given; typical of the soil described"}. An assumption that is not an input is its own row: {"drained": "long-term condition"}. The package lists them under Assumed Inputs with the analysis's own defaults, so no assumption reads as given. A misspelt input name is refused with a did-you-mean.
givenlist|dictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user gave, by the names you pass them under, e.g. ["width", "depth", "friction_angle"], or with the user's own words, {"friction_angle": "phi 32 deg from the boring logs"}. Only these print under Given Inputs. Every other input you pass prints under Assumed Inputs as passed, not stated as given (with its basis when it is in assumptions); left out, no input is the user's. A value you read off, worked out or chose is assumed, not given.
output_pathstroptionalFile path to save output. Auto-generated if omitted.
formatstroptionalOutput format: 'html' (recommended, self-contained with embedded CSS), 'latex' (raw .tex source), or 'pdf' (requires pdflatex installed). HTML is always available; PDF requires a LaTeX compiler on the system. allowed: html, latex, pdf default: "html"

soil_layersarrayrequiredList of dicts: name, top_elevation, bottom_elevation, gamma, phi, c_prime (or cu + analysis_mode). slope_report_package — One-call slope stability REPORT for a critical-surface SEARCH: input echo, search story (surfaces tried + rejection diagnostics + critical surface/FOS), FOS-by-method table, slice-force + interslice/thrust-line figures, reinforcement summary, a probabilistic annex (FOSM/Monte Carlo) when 'variables' is supplied, and CSV tables (every slice, every trial surface). No fixed circle needed — the search finds the critical surface.

ParameterTypeDescription
surface_pointsarrayrequiredList of [x, z] ground surface coordinates.
soil_layersarrayrequiredList of dicts: name, top_elevation, bottom_elevation, gamma, phi, c_prime (or cu + analysis_mode). Optional 'bottom_boundary_points' and 'top_boundary_points' ([[x,z],...]) define a non-horizontal layer base or top (e.g. a weak seam). One material per point: where two layers cover the same ground the one listed FIRST holds it, for weight and strength (reported in layer_overlaps); ground above the deepest layer's bottom that no layer covers is refused.
methodstroptionalLimit-equilibrium method the search minimizes and the report highlights. Default 'spencer' (rigorous — populates the interslice-force / line-of-thrust figure). allowed: spencer, morgenstern_price, gle, bishop, janbu, fellenius default: "spencer"
surface_typestroptionalTrial-surface family for the search. 'circular' grids circle centres over x_range/y_range and keeps only circles whose ends fall in x_entry_range/x_exit_range; the others draw their surfaces between x_entry_range and x_exit_range. Ranges not given are set from the slope (toe, crest, height, depth to the base). 'weak_layer' biases trials toward a defined weak seam. allowed: circular, entry_exit, noncircular, noncircular_de, pso, weak_layer default: "circular"
x_rangearrayoptional[min, max] circle-center x for the search grid (circular).
y_rangearrayoptional[min, max] circle-center y for the search grid (circular).
nxintoptionalGrid divisions in x (circular search). default: 10
nyintoptionalGrid divisions in y (circular search). default: 10
x_entry_rangearrayoptional[min, max] x where a trial surface's low-x end may lie (every search, circular included).
x_exit_rangearrayoptional[min, max] x where a trial surface's high-x end may lie (every search, circular included).
n_trialsintoptionalNumber of random trials (noncircular searches). default: 500
n_pointsintoptionalVertices per noncircular trial surface. default: 5
n_slicesintoptionalNumber of slices. default: 30
gwt_pointsarrayoptionalList of [x, z] GWT coordinates.
khfloatoptionalSeismic coefficient (pseudo-static). default: 0.0
seedintoptionalRandom seed for the search / Monte Carlo (reproducibility).
variablesdictoptionalProbabilistic variable spec {param[:layer]: {mean?, cov|std, dist?, source?}}. When given, adds a reliability annex (FOSM by default) on the critical surface.
monte_carlobooloptionalIf True (and 'variables' given), also run a Monte Carlo simulation on the critical surface for the annex. default: false
nintoptionalMonte Carlo realizations (when monte_carlo=True). default: 1000
research_surfacebooloptionalMonte Carlo: re-search the critical surface each realization (slower) instead of holding it fixed. default: false
time_budget_sfloatoptionalTime budget of EACH critical-surface search in seconds (at most 600), as slope_stability search_critical_surface: the report's search, and with research_surface each Monte Carlo realization's (per search, not for the run). A search cut short reports the lowest surface in what it covered and says so in its warnings. default: 180.0
fosmbooloptionalWith 'variables': run the FOSM annex. default: true
FOS_requiredfloatoptionalRequired factor of safety for the stability check. default: 1.5
surchargefloatoptionalSurface surcharge (kPa). default: 0.0
tolfloatoptionalConvergence tolerance for the iterative methods. default: 0.0001
f_interslicestroptionalInterslice force function for the rigorous re-analysis of the critical surface. default: "half_sine"
project_namestroptionalProject name for header. default: "Project"
project_numberstroptionalProject number for header.
engineerstroptionalEngineer name for header.
checkerstroptionalChecker name for header.
companystroptionalCompany name for header.
datestroptionalDate string (auto-filled if empty).
assumptionsdictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user did not give, as {input name: its basis}, e.g. {"unit_weight": "not given; typical of the soil described"}. An assumption that is not an input is its own row: {"drained": "long-term condition"}. The package lists them under Assumed Inputs with the analysis's own defaults, so no assumption reads as given. givenlist|dictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user gave, by the names you pass them under, e.g. ["width", "depth", "friction_angle"], or with the user's own words, {"friction_angle": "phi 32 deg from the boring logs"}. settlement_package — Run settlement analysis and generate calc package, with tables (CSV + printed) of consolidation settlement per layer (e0, Cc, Cr, stresses) and settlement against time.

ParameterTypeDescription
q_appliedfloatrequiredApplied pressure (kPa).
BfloatrequiredFooting width (m).
EsfloatoptionalElastic modulus for immediate settlement (kPa), for the elastic method. Not given: no immediate settlement is computed (0).
consolidation_layersarrayoptionalArray of consolidation layer dicts.
schmertmann_layersarrayoptionalArray of Schmertmann layer dicts.
cvfloatoptionalCoefficient of consolidation (m2/yr). With consolidation_layers, adds the time curve and t50/t90 to the result.
HdrfloatoptionalDrainage path length (m) for the time curve. Default: consolidating thickness / 2 (double drainage) or the whole thickness (single).
immediate_methodstroptionalImmediate settlement method. allowed: elastic, schmertmann default: "elastic"
drainagestroptionalDrainage condition for time rate. allowed: single, double default: "double"
stress_methodstroptionalStress distribution method. allowed: 2:1, boussinesq, westergaard also read as: 2to1 = 2:1 default: "2:1"
q_overburdenfloatoptionalOverburden pressure at footing base (kPa). default: 0.0
LfloatoptionalFooting length (m). Not given: L = B for a square or circular footing; a strip is taken as infinitely long (plane strain), which the elastic method refuses unless Iw is given (its Iw grows with L/B without limit); a rectangular footing needs L.
shapestroptionalFooting shape. allowed: square, rectangular, strip, circular also read as: circle = circular default: "square"
nufloatoptionalPoisson's ratio for immediate settlement. default: 0.3
IwfloatoptionalElastic influence factor for the elastic method. Not given: GEC-6 Table 5-12's shape factor at the centre of a flexible footing (1.12 for a square, by L/B for a rectangle, interpolated in log(L/B); 1.00 for a circle).
gamma_soilfloatoptionalEffective unit weight below the base (kN/m3), for Schmertmann's sigma'_vp at the depth of the peak strain influence factor (NHI-06-089 Fig. 8-21b). Required with immediate_method 'schmertmann'.
C_alphafloatoptionalSecondary compression index. Enables secondary settlement.
e0_secondaryfloatoptionalOne void ratio for the secondary settlement of every consolidation layer. Not given: each layer's own e0, layer by layer.
t_secondaryfloatoptionalTime for secondary settlement (years). default: 0.0
time_years_schmertmannfloatoptionalCreep time for Schmertmann immediate method (years). default: 0.0

axial_pile_package — Run axial pile capacity analysis and generate APILE-style calc package, with tables (CSV + printed) of side resistance per layer, load transfer at the ultimate load and capacity against pile length.

ParameterTypeDescription
pile_typestrrequiredPile type. pipe_closed/pipe_open require diameter + wall_thickness; concrete_square/concrete_circular require width (side dimension OR diameter); h_pile requires designation; or a custom section (pile_area, pile_perimeter, pile_width, pile_tip_area) for any but pipe_open, timber always. allowed: pipe_closed, pipe_open, concrete_square, concrete_circular, h_pile, timber
diameterfloatoptionalPile diameter (m) for pipe piles.
wall_thicknessfloatoptionalPipe wall thickness (m).
widthfloatoptionalSide dimension (m) for concrete piles.
designationstroptionalH-pile designation (e.g., 'HP14x117').
pile_lengthfloatrequiredEmbedded pile length from the pile head to the tip (m).
layersarrayrequiredArray of soil-layer dicts (measured from the GROUND SURFACE): {thickness (m), soil_type, unit_weight (kN/m3), friction_angle (deg, for cohesionless), cohesion (kPa, for cohesive), toe_friction_angle (deg, OPTIONAL: separate end-bearing phi if the pile tip is in this layer; defaults to friction_angle), delta_phi_ratio (OPTIONAL Nordlund delta/phi; default from GEC-12 Fig. 7-9 by pile type and displaced volume), beta and Nt (OPTIONAL, beta method: the layer's beta and toe Nt from local experience, GEC-12 Steps 2a/5a), fig_7_18_case (OPTIONAL, a cohesive layer: 'sand_over_stiff_clay', 'soft_clay_over_stiff_clay', 'stiff_clay', 'none'; GEC-12 Fig. 7-18's case, which starts a clay stratum at the layer's top), soil_class (OPTIONAL: 'clay', 'silt', 'sand' or 'gravel', GEC-12 Table 7-9's soil type for beta_coefficients 'table_7_9'; default clay or sand), alpha or adhesion (OPTIONAL, a cohesive layer: a site-specific adhesion factor, or Ca in kPa, used in place of the chart's, e.g. adhesion = cohesion from site tests as in NHI-06-089 Example 9-3; give adhesion_basis, where it came from, with it), highly_overconsolidated (OPTIONAL, a cohesive layer: true or false, the engineer's call; where su is past the alpha method's chart, true takes API RP 2A's alpha and false holds Ca at the curve's end, winning over highly_overconsolidated_su_ratio for that layer)}. soil_type must be 'cohesionless' or 'cohesive' (NOT 'sand'/'clay').
gwt_depthfloatoptionalGroundwater depth below ground surface (m).
head_depthfloatoptionalDepth of the pile head below the ground surface (m), e.g. the bottom of a footing 1.5 m down. Layers above the head contribute no skin friction; overburden above the head still raises effective stress at the tip. Default 0 = head at the ground surface. default: 0.0
factor_of_safetyfloatoptionalFactor of safety for the allowable capacity. Default 2.5: FHWA NHI-06-089 Table 9-5 (indicator piles with wave equation analysis); 2.00 with a static load test, 2.25 with dynamic testing, 2.75 wave equation only, 3.50 Gates formula. GEC-12 itself designs by resistance factors: the result also gives the factored resistance (Table 7-1, Eq. 7-3). default: 2.5
methodstroptionalauto = by soil type: the Nordlund method in cohesionless soil (GEC-12 Sec. 7.2.1.3.1), the alpha method with Tomlinson's adhesion in cohesive soil (Sec. 7.2.1.3.2); beta = the beta (effective stress) method in every layer (Sec. 7.2.1.3.4). allowed: auto, beta default: "auto"
include_upliftbooloptionalAlso report uplift (tension) capacity. default: false
cohesive_phifloatoptionalFALLBACK drained phi' (deg) for cohesive layers under method='beta' (skin AND tip); a per-layer friction_angle on a cohesive layer wins over this global. default: 25.0
uplift_skin_fractionfloatoptionalFraction of the outside side resistance taken in uplift (with include_uplift). Default 1.0: GEC-12 Eq. 7-38 takes the whole shaft resistance and puts the uplift reduction in the resistance factor; 0.7 is the customary share in free-draining soils GEC-12 cites. default: 1.0
pile_weightfloatoptionalPile self-weight (kN) added to uplift capacity (with include_uplift).
toe_stress_limitfloatoptionalLimit on sigma'p at the toe for the Nordlund toe resistance (kPa). Default 143.6 kPa = 3 ksf, GEC-12 Step 8; null for no limit (GEC-12's worked example did not limit it). default: 143.640777
inside_friction_ratiofloatoptionalOpen-end pipe, unplugged case: interior over exterior unit side resistance. Default 1/3, the low end of GEC-12's 'typically on the order of 1/3 to 1/2' (Sec. 7.10.7). default: 0.3333333333333333
open_pipe_toe_limitfloatoptionalOpen-end pipe in cohesionless soil: limiting unit toe resistance (kPa). Default 5027 kPa = 105 ksf (Tomlinson, GEC-12 Sec. 7.10.7); null for none. default: 5027.427195
open_pipe_methodstroptionalOpen-end pipe: 'auto' takes Tomlinson's Eq. 7-90 for a pipe under 24 in with the toe in clay and over half its length in clay (GEC-12 Vol I p. 407), else the lesser of the plugged and unplugged cases (Eqs. 7-88/7-89, 'paikowsky_whitman'). allowed: auto, paikowsky_whitman, tomlinson default: "auto"
cohesive_Ntfloatoptionalmethod='beta': Nt of a cohesive toe layer. Default 3 (GEC-12: a relatively low Nt in clays unless local correlations suggest higher; Table 7-9 clay 3-30). A layer's own Nt wins. default: 3.0
h_pile_toe_areastroptionalH-pile toe area: 'box' (depth x flange width, GEC-12 Sec. 7.10.7) or 'steel'. GEC-12 Step 9 leaves it to past experience and local load tests. allowed: box, steel default: "box"
adhesion_curvestroptionalalpha-method: GEC-12 Fig. 7-17 curves. 'auto' = smooth steel for pipe piles, the concrete/timber/corrugated curve for H-piles (GEC-12 Vol I p. 247) and concrete or timber piles. allowed: auto, concrete_timber_corrugated, smooth_steel default: "auto"
adhesion_beyond_chartstroptionalalpha method where a clay layer's su is past the end of the chart's curves (Fig. 7-17, or 7-18 where read); GEC-12 Vol I p. 247 and alpha-method Step 1 recommend API RP 2A's alpha there for highly overconsolidated clays. 'api_if_highly_overconsolidated': API alpha in a layer whose su / sigma'vo is at or above highly_overconsolidated_su_ratio, Ca held at the curve's end below it; 'chart_end': Ca held at the curve's end in every such layer (GEC-12's worked example, Vol 3 Table D-100); 'api': API alpha in every such layer. Within the curves Ca is read off Fig. 7-17 as drawn (it can exceed su). allowed: api_if_highly_overconsolidated, chart_end, api default: "api_if_highly_overconsolidated"
highly_overconsolidated_su_ratiofloatoptionalalpha method: the su / sigma'vo at and above which a clay is highly overconsolidated, for adhesion_beyond_chart 'api_if_highly_overconsolidated'. GEC-12 gives no value; it is the engineer's judgment, so a run with a clay layer whose su is past the chart's curves is refused until this (or adhesion_beyond_chart 'chart_end' or 'api') is given. Ask the user, or state the value taken as a judgment call.
displaced_volumefloatoptionalNordlund displaced volume V per unit length (m3/m). Default: the steel area of an H-pile, the gross area of other piles (an open pipe as a closed pipe; its steel area, if it drives unplugged, is below GEC-12 Fig. 7-9).
pile_areafloatoptionalCustom section (m2): the cross-section area, the steel of an H-pile or a closed pipe, the gross area of a concrete or timber pile (it gives the Nordlund displaced volume of an H-pile and of a solid pile). With pile_perimeter and pile_width it replaces diameter, wall_thickness, width or designation; pile_type still picks the GEC-12 curves (not for pipe_open: its section comes from diameter and wall_thickness).
pile_perimeterfloatoptionalCustom section: the perimeter for the side resistance (m); the box perimeter of an H-pile (GEC-12 Steps 6 and Vol I p. 247).
pile_tip_areafloatoptionalCustom section: the toe area (m2). Required for h_pile (its box area; h_pile_toe_area 'steel' takes pile_area) and pipe_closed (the gross area); a concrete or timber pile's is its pile_area when not given.
pile_widthfloatoptionalCustom section: the width or diameter b (m), an H-pile's flange width; for D/b and the width notes.
pile_depthfloatoptionalCustom section: the section's depth (m), an H-pile's; reported only.
pile_namestroptionalCustom section: its name, e.g. 'HP16x101'.
adhesion_chartstroptionalalpha-method chart (GEC-12 Vol I p. 246): 'fig_7_17' (Tomlinson's Ca, recommended generally), 'fig_7_18' (Tomlinson's alpha for each clay layer's stratigraphy case: sand or sandy gravel over stiff clay, soft clay over stiff clay, stiff clay alone) or 'smaller' (the smaller Ca of the two in each layer, which p. 246 advises the inexperienced user to take). A layer's case is its fig_7_18_case, else from the profile: cohesive layers under a cohesionless layer the sand case, from the ground surface the stiff-clay case; the soft-clay case only where a layer gives it. Eq. 7-90 (open pipe) takes Ca from Fig. 7-17 whatever this is (p. 407). allowed: fig_7_17, fig_7_18, smaller default: "fig_7_17"
shrink_swell_depthfloatoptionalDepth (m below the ground surface) of a shrink-swell zone: no shaft resistance in cohesive soil above it (GEC-12 Vol I p. 247). Default none.
beta_coefficientsstroptionalmethod='beta': beta and Nt where a layer gives none: GEC-12 Table 7-9 by the layer's soil_class (clay 0.15-0.35, silt 0.25-0.50, sand 0.30-0.90, gravel 0.35-0.80; Steps 2b/5b), a straight line in phi' between Table 7-9's range ends (the module's reading; the table prints only the ends). A clay toe takes cohesive_Nt. GEC-12 prints no beta formula from phi' alone; give a layer's beta and Nt for other values (local experience, Steps 2a/5a). allowed: table_7_9 default: "table_7_9"
toe_phi_zonestroptionalNordlund toe: the phi near the toe. 'toe_layer' (the toe layer's toe_friction_angle or friction_angle) or 'average_3b' (averaged over the cohesionless soil from the toe to 3b below, GEC-12 Step 7c's zone). allowed: toe_layer, average_3b default: "toe_layer"
project_namestroptionalProject name for header. default: "Project"
project_numberstroptionalProject number for header.
engineerstroptionalEngineer name for header.
checkerstroptionalChecker name for header.
companystroptionalCompany name for header.
datestroptionalDate string (auto-filled if empty).
assumptionsdictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user did not give, as {input name: its basis}, e.g. {"unit_weight": "not given; typical of the soil described"}. An assumption that is not an input is its own row: {"drained": "long-term condition"}. The package lists them under Assumed Inputs with the analysis's own defaults, so no assumption reads as given. A misspelt input name is refused with a did-you-mean.
givenlist|dictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user gave, by the names you pass them under, e.g. ["width", "depth", "friction_angle"], or with the user's own words, {"friction_angle": "phi 32 deg from the boring logs"}. Only these print under Given Inputs. Every other input you pass prints under Assumed Inputs as passed, not stated as given (with its basis when it is in assumptions); left out, no input is the user's. A value you read off, worked out or chose is assumed, not given.
output_pathstroptionalFile path to save output. Auto-generated if omitted.
formatstroptionalOutput format: 'html' (recommended, self-contained with embedded CSS), 'latex' (raw .tex source), or 'pdf' (requires pdflatex installed). HTML is always available; PDF requires a LaTeX compiler on the system. allowed: html, latex, pdf default: "html"

drilled_shaft_package — Run drilled shaft capacity analysis and generate SHAFT-style calc package, with tables (CSV + printed) of side resistance per layer, load transfer at the ultimate load and capacity against shaft length.

ParameterTypeDescription
diameterfloatrequiredShaft diameter (m).
shaft_lengthfloatrequiredShaft length (m). Alias: length.
layersarrayrequiredArray of {thickness, soil_type, unit_weight, cu, phi, N60, qu, RQD} dicts. soil_type: cohesive/cohesionless/rock. A cohesionless layer at the shaft tip needs its N60 (end bearing q_b = 57.5*N60 kPa, GEC-10 Eq. 10-14, N60 the mean of the cohesionless layers' N60 between the base and two base diameters below it, by thickness, limited to 50, p. 10-15; a layer there with no N60, or of cohesive soil or rock, is left out); without it the call is refused. Under beta_method 'rational' (the default, GEC-10 2018 Eq. 10-13) each cohesionless layer the shaft passes through needs its N60 (sigma'p by Eq. 10-11 or 10-12) or a direct OCR, else the call is refused; it also takes N1_60 (overburden-corrected SPT; phi' = 27.5+9.2*log10[(N1)60], GEC-10 Example 10-1 and Eq. A-2, where the layer gives no phi; a phi given is used and the result's choices give the correlation's value beside it), sigma_p_correlation ('clean_sand' default: Eq. 10-11 with m = 0.6, clean quartzitic sands; 'silty_sand': m = 0.8, silty sands to sandy silts; 'gravel': Eq. 10-12, sigma'p/pa = 0.15*N60, gravelly soils; GEC-10 p. 10-11) and sigma_v_ref (kPa, pre-scour effective stress for the OCR; default the layer's own sigma'v); under beta_method 'depth' the depth beta uses neither N1_60 nor OCR: they enter only the result's beta_method 'rational' alternative (choices).
