A rock layer's RQD (default 100) sets alpha_E of the side resistance under rock_side_method 'caving' (GEC-10 Table 10-3) and the base under rock_base_method 'rqd'; under the default 'gec10' an RQD below 100 within one base diameter below the base needs rock_base_conditions_met, or the tip rock layer's GSI and m_i. A rock layer also takes GSI (Geological Strength Index of the rock mass, 0 to 100, from the core descriptions; GEC-10 p. 10-23 names GSI, not RMR) and m_i (Hoek-Brown constant of the intact rock, by rock type, GEC 5 Table 9-10, as GEC-10 p. 10-24 points to): with the base in that layer they give GEC-10's base for a fractured rock mass, the Hoek-Brown base, Eqs. 10-24 to 10-29, taken where the rock is not taken to meet the conditions of Eq. 10-23 and shown beside 2.5*qu where it is (see rock_base_conditions_met); a rock layer within one base diameter below the base that gives them has its own Hoek-Brown base among the result's alternatives. GSI or m_i on any other layer (above the base, further below it, or with the base in soil) is refused: nothing would use them; capacity_vs_depth takes them on any layer a trial base is in.
gwt_depthfloatoptionalGroundwater depth (m).
factor_of_safetyfloatoptionalFactor of safety. default: 2.5
beta_methodstroptionalCohesionless side resistance. 'rational' (default) = GEC-10 (2018) Sec. 10.3.5.1, Eqs. 10-5 to 10-13 (pp. 10-10 to 10-12): f_SN = beta*sigma'v on each layer's average sigma'v, beta = (K/Ko)*Ko*tan(phi'), Ko = (1-sin phi')*OCR^(sin phi') <= Kp, OCR = sigma'p/sigma'v, sigma'p from the layer's N60 (Eq. 10-11 or 10-12), beta limited to its value at 7.5 ft, no limit on f_SN; needs each cohesionless layer's N60 or OCR. 'depth' = O'Neill & Reese (1999) beta = 1.5-0.135*sqrt(z, ft) = 1.5-0.245*sqrt(z, m), 0.25-1.2, x N60/15 where N60 < 15, f_s <= 4 ksf = 191.5 kPa (FHWA NHI-06-089 Eqs. 9-41 to 9-43, the limit p. 9-133), which GEC-10 (2018) does not print. allowed: rational, depth default: "rational"
K_over_KofloatoptionalK/Ko in the GEC-10 beta (beta_method 'rational'): 1 = 'a rational first-order approximation', no stress change from construction (GEC-10 p. 10-11); 2/3 or lower 'when these aspects of construction quality are not controlled properly' or soil caving is allowed (p. 10-12). 0 < K_over_Ko <= 1. default: 1.0
top_exclusionfloatoptionalSide resistance left out over the top of the shaft (m), in every layer, when given. Left out: none over the top 1.5 m in cohesive soil, GEC-10's 'top 5 ft' (p. 10-17, printed in Sec. 10.3.5.2 for cohesive soils, 'or to the depth of seasonal moisture change', 'subject to modification based on local experience and judgment of the designer'), and side resistance from the top in cohesionless soil and rock (Secs. 10.3.5.1 and 10.3.5.3 print no such zone; Examples 10-1 and 10-5 take the sand's from the surface, Example 10-4 the socket's over its whole length). Give 1.5 to leave the top 5 ft out of sand and rock too (frost, seasonal moisture, gapping from cyclic lateral load), or the depth of seasonal moisture change. casing_depth, where deeper, takes its place.
bottom_exclusionfloatoptionalSide resistance left out over the bottom of the shaft (m) in cohesive soil. Default 0: GEC-10 (2018) prints no such zone, and Example 10-2 (p. 10-18) takes the clay's side resistance to the base. FHWA NHI-06-089 p. 9-129 (O'Neill & Reese 1999) leaves out the bottom 5 ft (1.524 m), its Fig. 9-49 the bottom one diameter (give the diameter for that). default: 0.0
alpha_methodstroptionalCohesive side resistance. 'rational' (default) = GEC-10 (2018) Sec. 10.3.5.2, Eq. 10-18 (p. 10-16): alpha = 0.30+0.17/(su(CIUC)/pa), f_SN = alpha*su(CIUC), su(CIUC) from cu by su_test_type. 'aashto' = O'Neill & Reese (1999) as FHWA NHI-06-089 Eqs. 9-37a/b print it (p. 9-129): alpha = 0.55 for cu/pa <= 1.5, 0.55-0.1*(cu/pa-1.5) to 2.5, on cu; GEC-10 recommends Eq. 10-18 'as a revision' to it. allowed: rational, aashto default: "rational"
su_test_typestroptionalFor alpha_method 'rational': the lab test each layer's cu came from. 'ciuc' (default) = cu taken as su(CIUC), no transform; 'uc' / 'uu' = transformed to su(CIUC) on the layer's sigma'vo by GEC-10 Eq. 10-16 / 10-17 (Chen & Kulhawy 1993, p. 10-16; Example 10-2 takes a UU strength). The base in clay takes the same su(CIUC) (Example 10-3). allowed: ciuc, uc, uu default: "ciuc"
clay_base_methodstroptionalBase resistance with the tip in cohesive soil. 'gec10' (default) = GEC-10 (2018) p. 10-19: q_BN = N*c*su (Eq. 10-19), su the mean of the cohesive soil over 2B below the base, by thickness (p. 10-19; the tip layer at its su(CIUC) as its side resistance took it, each clay layer below on its own cu, transformed alike; cohesionless or rock layers within 2B left out; where the profile ends short of 2B, the mean of what it gives, said in the choices), N*c from Table 10-2 by su (6.5 at 500 psf, 8.0 at 1,000 psf, 9.0 at 2,000 psf or more; held at 6.5 below 500 psf), (2/3)[1 + D/(6B)]*N*c*su where the depth D < 3B (Eq. 10-20), no upper limit. 'oneill_reese' = FHWA NHI-06-089 Eqs. 9-39, 9-40 (p. 9-131): Nc = 6[1 + 0.2 z/D] <= 9, x 0.67 where su < 0.5 ksf, q_t <= 80 ksf, on the tip layer's cu. allowed: gec10, oneill_reese default: "gec10"
rock_base_methodstroptionalBase resistance with the tip in rock. 'gec10' (default) = GEC-10 (2018) Eq. 10-23 (p. 10-22): q_BN = 2.5*qu, for rock massive or tightly jointed to one diameter below the base, no cavities beneath, a clean base (Example 10-4 takes it with RQD 37 to 100); for a fractured rock mass the Hoek-Brown base, Eqs. 10-24 to 10-29 (pp. 10-23, 10-24; Turner and Ramey 2010): m_b = m_i*exp((GSI-100)/28), s = exp((GSI-100)/9), a = 1/2+(1/6)(exp(-GSI/15)-exp(-20/3)), A = sigma'vb + qu*(m_b*sigma'vb/qu + s)^a, q_BN = A + qu*(m_b*A/qu + s)^a, q_BN/qu limited to 2.5 (p. 10-24), on the tip rock layer's qu, GSI and m_i and the vertical effective stress at the base; resistance factor 0.50 (p. 10-24, Table 8-4); which of the two by rock_base_conditions_met. 'rqd' = q_b/q_u reduced by the tip rock's RQD below 70 (1.5 at 50, 0.8 at 25, 0.4 at 0), cited to GEC-10's 2010 edition, not in the reference library, and not a method GEC-10 Table 8-4 gives a resistance factor for. allowed: gec10, rqd default: "gec10"
rock_base_conditions_metbooloptionalFor rock_base_method 'gec10' with the tip in rock: whether the rock below the base meets the three conditions GEC-10 p. 10-22 sets on q_BN = 2.5*qu (massive or tightly jointed, no compressible seams or joints, to at least one diameter below the base; no solution cavities or voids beneath it; a clean base achieved and verified). The engineer's judgment: Example 10-4 takes 2.5 with RQD 37 to 100 because 'Rock coring and local experience indicate the rock mass below the socket tip is competent'. true = 2.5*qu (Eq. 10-23) as stated. false = GEC-10's base for a fractured rock mass, the Hoek-Brown base (Eqs. 10-24 to 10-29), on the tip rock layer's GSI and m_i; refused, naming them, where that layer does not give them. Left out = taken as met, said in the result's choices, where every layer within one base diameter below the base is rock with RQD 100 (the layer default), with the Hoek-Brown base on the tip rock layer's GSI and m_i beside it where they are given; where a layer there has an RQD below 100 or is soil, the Hoek-Brown base on the tip rock layer's GSI and m_i (2.5*qu bounds it above), and the call is refused, naming them, where that layer does not give them.
large_base_reductionbooloptionalO'Neill & Reese's (1999) reduction of base resistance for a large base: 1.27/B in cohesionless soil for a base wider than 1.27 m, F_r = 2.5/(a*B + 2.5*b) <= 1 in cohesive soil for a base wider than 1.90 m (B the bell's where there is one). Default false: GEC-10 (2018) prints neither (Eqs. 10-14, 10-19, 10-20); true applies it. default: false
pafloatoptionalAtmospheric pressure (kPa) for the rational chains. default: 101.325
rock_side_CfloatoptionalC in the rock side resistance f_s = C*pa*sqrt(qu/pa) (GEC-10 Eq. 10-21, p. 10-20). Default 1.0, 'recommended for design of "normal" rock sockets' (pp. 10-20, 10-21; Example 10-4): conventional equipment, nominally clean sidewalls, no caving, no smearing. 0.65 = the value of Eq. 10-22 with alpha_E = 1.0 (rock_side_method 'caving' takes alpha_E from Table 10-3 by RQD). 1.9 for roughened sockets, verified by load tests or local experience (p. 10-22). For rock_side_method 'normal'; refused with 'caving', which takes no C. Needs a rock layer. default: 1.0
rock_side_methodstroptionalRock side resistance. 'normal' (default) = GEC-10 Eq. 10-21, f_s = C*pa*sqrt(qu/pa) with rock_side_C, for a 'normal' socket: conventional equipment, nominally clean sidewalls (pp. 10-20, 10-21). 'caving' = Eq. 10-22 (O'Neill and Reese 1999), f_s = 0.65*alpha_E*pa*sqrt(qu/pa), alpha_E from Table 10-3 (p. 10-21) by each rock layer's RQD and rock_joints (closed joints 1.00, 0.85, 0.60, 0.50, 0.45; open or gouge-filled 0.85, 0.55, 0.55, 0.50, 0.45 at RQD 100, 70, 50, 30, 20 %; linear between the rows, held at 0.45 below RQD 20), for highly fractured or weathered rock that cannot be drilled without artificial support (casing, plug-ahead) or where caving is anticipated. Needs a rock layer. allowed: normal, caving default: "normal"
rock_jointsstroptionalFor rock_side_method 'caving': the joint condition of GEC-10 Table 10-3, 'closed' (default) or 'open' (open or gouge-filled joints), from the cores. allowed: closed, open default: "closed"
socket_diameterfloatoptionalRock socket diameter (m). Defaults to shaft diameter. One diameter for every rock layer: GEC-10 sizes a socket by one diameter B (Eq. 10-3, p. 10-9; Example 10-4) and gives none per rock layer. The rock side resistance and, with the tip in rock, the base (pi/4*B^2, GEC-10 Example 10-4, p. 10-28) take it.
bell_diameterfloatoptionalBelled base diameter (m).
casing_depthfloatoptionalPermanent casing depth (m, no side resistance). default: 0.0
fractured_rock_thicknessfloatoptionalDecomposed or fractured rock (m) below the top of the first rock layer that is 'not considered part of the socket for design purposes' (GEC-10 p. 8-15): no rock side resistance over it, while the soil above keeps its own (casing_depth takes both). 0 = all rock is socket. Needs a rock layer. default: 0.0
concrete_fcfloatoptionalCompressive strength f'c of the shaft concrete (kPa; 28 MPa = 28000, at least 1000). The rock side resistance takes qu no higher than it: 'For design, the value of qu used in Equation 10-21 should not exceed the compressive strength of the drilled shaft concrete' (GEC-10 p. 10-21; Example 10-4 gives qu 360 ksf and f'c 576 ksf), in Eq. 10-22 alike. With the base in rock it also checks the base against the concrete's own bearing (GEC-10 p. 10-25): Eq. 12-7 (p. 12-8), 0.70*[0.85*f'c*A1*m], the tip taken as plain concrete as Example 10-4 does (with the cage to the tip p. 12-8 prints Eq. 12-6 at phi 0.70, not computed: the tool takes no f_y), A1 the socket's cross-sectional area, m = 2.0 (printed for a socket on competent rock), against the geotechnical 0.50*Q_tip (Example 10-4 p. 10-28 makes this check), in base_steps.concrete_bearing and the choices; lrfd_capacity takes the factored base as the smaller of the two. Q_tip, Q_ultimate and Q_allowable stay the geotechnical ones. Left out, neither limit is checked and the result's choices say so. No other structural check of the shaft is made. Needs a rock layer.
project_namestroptionalProject name for header. default: "Project"
project_numberstroptionalProject number for header.
engineerstroptionalEngineer name for header.
checkerstroptionalChecker name for header.
companystroptionalCompany name for header.
datestroptionalDate string (auto-filled if empty).
assumptionsdictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user did not give, as {input name: its basis}, e.g. {"unit_weight": "not given; typical of the soil described"}. An assumption that is not an input is its own row: {"drained": "long-term condition"}. The package lists them under Assumed Inputs with the analysis's own defaults, so no assumption reads as given. A misspelt input name is refused with a did-you-mean.
givenlist|dictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user gave, by the names you pass them under, e.g. ["width", "depth", "friction_angle"], or with the user's own words, {"friction_angle": "phi 32 deg from the boring logs"}. Only these print under Given Inputs. Every other input you pass prints under Assumed Inputs as passed, not stated as given (with its basis when it is in assumptions); left out, no input is the user's. A value you read off, worked out or chose is assumed, not given.
output_pathstroptionalFile path to save output. Auto-generated if omitted.
formatstroptionalOutput format: 'html' (recommended, self-contained with embedded CSS), 'latex' (raw .tex source), or 'pdf' (requires pdflatex installed). HTML is always available; PDF requires a LaTeX compiler on the system. allowed: html, latex, pdf default: "html"

downdrag_package — Run downdrag analysis and generate calc package, with tables (CSV + printed) of axial load, unit skin friction and soil settlement along the pile, and every neutral-plane method side by side (CSV).

ParameterTypeDescription
pile_lengthfloatrequiredPile length (m).
pile_diameterfloatrequiredPile diameter (m).
layersarrayrequiredArray of {thickness, soil_type, unit_weight, phi, cu, beta, alpha, skin_friction_method, soil_class, settling, description} dicts. soil_type must be 'cohesionless' or 'cohesive' (NOT 'sand'/'clay'/'settling_fill'). Skin friction: cohesionless = beta x sigma'v (Beta method, UFC 3-220-20 Eq 6-7), beta as given, else from phi' by GEC-12 Table 7-9 (UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-15, driven piles) for the layer's soil_class ('silt' 0.25-0.50 over 28-34 deg, 'sand' 0.30-0.90 over 32-40 deg, the default, 'gravel' 0.35-0.80 over 35-45 deg), a straight line in phi' between GEC-12 Table 7-9's range ends (the module's reading; the table prints only the ends), held at the ends outside the range; soil_class also picks the toe's Nt row (Nt_method); cohesive = alpha x cu (Alpha method, UFC 3-220-20 Eq 6-8, the default; alpha as given, else read off alpha_chart: UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-16 and Fig 6-14 by default), or with skin_friction_method 'beta' beta x sigma'v for long-term, drained conditions (UFC 3-220-20 6-5.4.1; GEC-12 7.2.1.3.4), beta required (GEC-12 Table 7-9: clay 0.15-0.35; cu then only for a toe in the layer). A cohesive layer takes no phi, and beta only with skin_friction_method 'beta'; a cohesionless layer takes no alpha. Mark settling layers with settling=True; a settling layer also needs its compressibility: cohesionless -> E_s (elastic modulus, kPa, > 0) and optional nu_s; cohesive -> Cc and e0 (optional Cr, sigma_p kPa) or C_ec/C_er.
Q_deadfloatoptionalDead load at pile top (kN). default: 0.0
fill_thicknessfloatoptionalFill thickness causing downdrag (m). default: 0.0
fill_unit_weightfloatoptionalFill unit weight (kN/m3). default: 19.0
gw_drawdownfloatoptionalGroundwater drawdown (m). default: 0.0
gwt_depthfloatoptionalGroundwater depth (m). default: 0.0
pile_EfloatoptionalPile elastic modulus (kPa). Default is steel. default: 200000000.0
pile_perimeterfloatoptionalPile perimeter (m). Computed from diameter if omitted.
pile_areafloatoptionalPile cross-section area (m2). Computed from diameter if omitted.
structural_capacityfloatoptionalPile structural capacity (kN) for the max-load check.
allowable_settlementfloatoptionalAllowable pile settlement (m) for the settlement check.
NtfloatoptionalToe bearing capacity factor: R_toe = Nt x sigma'v(toe) x A_toe in cohesionless soil, Nt x cu x A_toe in cohesive. Give the MOBILIZED value -- the toe resistance actually developed at the pile's settlement -- not the ultimate. Omitted, Nt is the ULTIMATE value: 9 in clay (UFC 3-220-20 6-5.4.3.3), and in cohesionless soil from the toe layer's phi' by Nt_method (60-120 in dense sand at 34-38 deg by the default); then the load and resistance curves often do not intersect and the neutral plane is where the pile and soil settle equally, the toe force compatible with the toe penetration (UFC 3-220-20 6-5.8.4.3; see neutral_plane_method). UFC 3-220-20 6-5.8.4.2: check 0 %, 50 % and 100 % toe mobilization.
Nt_methodstringoptionalWhere a cohesionless toe's ultimate Nt comes from when Nt is not given, both UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-17 (p. 421; qb = Nq sigma'zD, Eq 6-20): 'fellenius' (default) = its Fellenius (2021) column, the same values as GEC-12 Table 7-9, by the toe layer's soil_class (silt 20-40 over 28-34 deg, sand 30-150 over 32-40 deg, gravel 60-300 over 35-45 deg), a straight line in phi' between GEC-12 Table 7-9's range ends (the module's reading; the table prints only the ends), held at the ends outside the range; 'cheng' = its equation after Cheng (2004), Nq ~= 1.2 (Z/b)^-0.437 exp[6.34 (Z/b)^0.0486 tan phi'], Z the pile length and b pile_diameter, at most 200 unless project-specific information supports more (give Nt then). The result's choices give the other route's value. allowed: fellenius, cheng default: "fellenius"
pile_unit_weightfloatoptionalPile material unit weight (kN/m3), times pile_area for the pile's own weight; used only when include_pile_weight is true. Default 78.5 = steel, the same material as the pile_E default (concrete is about 24). For an H or pipe pile give pile_area as the steel area (pile_area defaults to the solid circle). default: 78.5
include_pile_weightbooloptionalWhether the load curve carries the pile's own weight. Default false: left out, as UFC 3-220-20 Fig 6-26 and FHWA GEC-12 7.3.6.1 (and their worked examples) do. True adds the weight of the pile above the neutral plane to Q_np and the drag force. default: false
n_sublayersintoptionalSublayers per soil layer for the depth discretization. default: 10
neutral_plane_methodstringoptionalWhich method gives the reported numbers; every method is evaluated and returned in neutral_plane_comparison whatever is chosen. 'auto' (default) = the UFC 3-220-20 6-7.4 procedure: the intersection of the load and resistance curves with the toe at toe_mobilization, or, when they do not intersect, where the pile and soil settle equally with the toe force compatible with the toe penetration (UFC 6-5.8.4.3, Fig 6-19). 'force_equilibrium' (the curves' intersection only; error if they do not intersect); 'settlement_compatibility' (pile and soil settle equally, toe force compatible with the toe penetration); 'bearing_layer_top' (top of the bearing layer, end-bearing pile, UFC 6-7.4 step 5); 'pile_toe' (whole shaft in negative skin friction, upper bound); 'endo' (Endo et al. 1969, CGPR #56 Table 3.1 fraction of the embedment; needs endo_bearing_condition). allowed: auto, force_equilibrium, settlement_compatibility, bearing_layer_top, pile_toe, endo default: "auto"
toe_mobilizationfloatoptionalFraction (0-1) of the nominal toe resistance mobilized where the load and resistance curves intersect. 1.0 = UFC 6-7.4 step 3 full mobilization ('a conservative approach for evaluating the drag force'); 0.5 and 0 = the other UFC 6-5.8.4.2 / GEC-12 7.3.6.1 cases for settlement (all three always reported in the comparison). default: 1.0
endo_bearing_conditionstringoptionalCGPR #56 Table 3.1 condition for Endo et al. (1969). allowed: floating, stiff_flexible, end_bearing
skin_friction_stressstringoptionalEffective stress for Beta-method skin friction (sand, and clay with skin_friction_method 'beta') and the sand toe: 'final' (default; sigma'v0 + fill/drawdown change, as UFC 3-220-20 6-7.4 step 2 requires) or 'initial' (sigma'v0). allowed: final, initial default: "final"
influence_depth_criterionstringoptionalHow deep below the toe the toe load is counted in the settlement (toe force spread 2V:1H from an equivalent footing as wide as the pile): to where its stress increase falls below 'bearing_stress' (default) = 10% of the bearing stress of the equivalent footing (UFC 3-220-20 6-5.8.4.3; 2.16 pile widths for a single pile) or 'effective_stress' = 10% of the existing vertical effective stress (FHWA GEC-12 Vol I step 1c: 7.3.5.3 for clay below the toe, 7.3.5.6 for sand, 7.3.5.5 for both; deeper for a loaded toe in soft soil). Either way the fill / drawdown, which does not decay with depth, compresses the settling layers below the toe down to the bottom of the soil profile; give the profile down to the base of the compressible soil. allowed: bearing_stress, effective_stress default: "bearing_stress"
influence_depth_warning_percentfloatoptionalThe result warns when the two influence_depth_criterion rules (UFC 3-220-20 6-5.8.4.3 and FHWA GEC-12 step 1c) give pile head settlements or drag forces that differ by more than this percentage of the larger of the two (of allowable_settlement / structural_capacity where given), and whenever a settlement or structural check passes with one rule and fails with the other. The rule used is not changed. Default 25 %: the engineer's call, not a reference's figure; neither reference says how far two settlement estimates may differ before it matters. default: 25.0
alpha_chartstringoptionalWhere a cohesive layer's alpha comes from when the layer leaves it out (a given alpha is kept). 'ufc_fig_6_14' (default; UFC 3-220-20 6-5.4.2, pp. 415-417, as its drag example App. B-5.4 reads it): soft clay (su below 800 psf) alpha 1 by Table 6-16; firm to very stiff clay off Fig 6-14 by su/Pa, curve A at Z of 40b or more, curve B at Z = 10b, linear between, Z from the ground surface to the clay's base or the pile toe and b = pile_diameter. 'gec12_fig_7_17': FHWA GEC-12 7.2.1.3.2 Step 1, Ca off Fig. 7-17 by su, D/b and fig_7_17_curve, as drawn (Ca may exceed su). choices states each clay's alpha and where it came from. Refused (with fig_7_17_curve and alpha_transition_zone) where no cohesive layer along the pile leaves alpha out. allowed: ufc_fig_6_14, gec12_fig_7_17 default: "ufc_fig_6_14"
fig_7_17_curvestringoptionalWith alpha_chart 'gec12_fig_7_17' only, and then required where a clay leaves alpha out: the Fig. 7-17 curves for the pile, 'concrete_timber_corrugated' (concrete, timber or corrugated steel; an H-pile takes the corrugated curve, GEC-12 Vol I p. 247) or 'smooth_steel'. allowed: concrete_timber_corrugated, smooth_steel
alpha_transition_zonebooloptionalWhether the top 10 pile widths of a stiff or very stiff clay (su 1500 psf or more) directly under soft clay take UFC 3-220-20 Eq 6-9, alpha = 0.28 (su/Pa)^-0.44 with the unit side resistance at least the soft clay's, and under sand alpha 1.0 (pp. 416-417, as App. B-5.4 does). Left out: true with alpha_chart 'ufc_fig_6_14', false with 'gec12_fig_7_17'. Applies only where the stiff clay's alpha is left out; refused where no such clay lies under soft clay or sand. The zone runs 10 pile widths from the top of the stiff clay however it is split into layers.
ground_elevationfloatoptionalElevation of the ground surface the depths are measured from (m): the top of the layers, where the pile head is taken (the original ground under a fill). Figures only: the calc package's profiles are drawn against elevation; every result stays in depth and no number changes.
project_namestroptionalProject name for header. default: "Project"
project_numberstroptionalProject number for header.
engineerstroptionalEngineer name for header.
checkerstroptionalChecker name for header.
companystroptionalCompany name for header.
datestroptionalDate string (auto-filled if empty).
assumptionsdictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user did not give, as {input name: its basis}, e.g. {"unit_weight": "not given; typical of the soil described"}. An assumption that is not an input is its own row: {"drained": "long-term condition"}. The package lists them under Assumed Inputs with the analysis's own defaults, so no assumption reads as given. A misspelt input name is refused with a did-you-mean.
givenlist|dictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user gave, by the names you pass them under, e.g. ["width", "depth", "friction_angle"], or with the user's own words, {"friction_angle": "phi 32 deg from the boring logs"}. Only these print under Given Inputs. Every other input you pass prints under Assumed Inputs as passed, not stated as given (with its basis when it is in assumptions); left out, no input is the user's. A value you read off, worked out or chose is assumed, not given.
output_pathstroptionalFile path to save output. Auto-generated if omitted.
formatstroptionalOutput format: 'html' (recommended, self-contained with embedded CSS), 'latex' (raw .tex source), or 'pdf' (requires pdflatex installed). HTML is always available; PDF requires a LaTeX compiler on the system. allowed: html, latex, pdf default: "html"

seismic_package — Run seismic geotechnical analysis and generate calc package.

ParameterTypeDescription
analysis_typestroptionalWhich analysis to run and report: the site_classification, seismic_earth_pressure or liquefaction_evaluation tool. allowed: site_classification, seismic_earth_pressure, liquefaction also read as: liquefaction_evaluation = liquefaction default: "site_classification"
vs30floatoptionalTime-averaged shear wave velocity (m/s).
layer_thicknessesarrayoptionalLayer thicknesses for Vs30/N-bar calc (m).
layer_vsarrayoptionalLayer shear wave velocities (m/s).
layer_NarrayoptionalLayer field SPT N values, uncorrected, for N-bar calc (with layer_thicknesses); above 100 blows/ft is taken as 100 (GEC-7 p. 93).
n_barfloatoptionalAverage field SPT blow count (alternative to vs30).
su_layer_thicknessesarrayoptionalCohesive layer thicknesses for su-bar calc (m).
layer_suarrayoptionalLayer undrained strengths (kPa) for su-bar calc.
su_barfloatoptionalAverage undrained strength (kPa) (alternative to vs30).
SsfloatoptionalShort-period spectral acceleration. If provided with S1, computes Fa/Fv.
S1floatoptional1-second spectral acceleration.
pgafloatoptionalMapped peak ground acceleration (g). If provided with Ss/S1, also returns Fpga (read against PGA, GEC-12 Table 7-27) and As = Fpga PGA (GEC-12 Eq. 7-78).
phifloatoptionalRequired when analysis_type is seismic_earth_pressure. Friction angle (degrees).
khfloatoptionalRequired when analysis_type is seismic_earth_pressure. Horizontal seismic coefficient.
kvfloatoptionalVertical seismic coefficient (positive upward). Enters KAE through the seismic angle psi = atan(kh/(1-kv)) (UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 4-15) and, with gamma and H, the thrust PAE = (gamma H^2/2)(1-kv) KAE (Eq. 4-16). default: 0.0
deltafloatoptionalWall friction angle (deg). Defaults to 2/3 phi.
betafloatoptionalWall back face batter from vertical (degrees), positive when the back face leans toward the backfill (lowers KAE). UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 4-15 and Fig. 4-8 measure their theta the other way: theta = -beta. default: 0.0
ifloatoptionalBackfill slope angle (degrees); UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 4-15's beta. default: 0.0
include_passivebooloptionalAlso return KPE (passive seismic coefficient, GEC-4 Eq. 44). default: false
delta_passivefloatoptionalWall friction angle behind KPE (deg). Not given: 0.4 phi, the most UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-8 (p. 187) allows a planar (Coulomb) passive wedge ("unconservative for delta/phi' > 0.4"); FHWA NHI-06-089 p. 10-19 finds a planar passive wedge unreliable above phi'/3 and recommends log-spiral charts, with which its p. 10-17 maximum of phi/2 goes. Above 0.4 phi the result warns.
gammafloat|arrayoptionalRequired when analysis_type is liquefaction. analysis_type=seismic_earth_pressure: Soil unit weight (kN/m3) for force calculation. | analysis_type=liquefaction: Unit weights (kN/m3).
HfloatoptionalWall height (m) for force calculation.
KAfloatoptionalStatic active coefficient behind PA and delta-PAE. Not given: Rankine Ka from phi (vertical wall, level backfill, no wall friction).
depthsarrayoptionalRequired when analysis_type is liquefaction. Layer depths (m).
N160arrayoptionalRequired when analysis_type is liquefaction. Corrected SPT blow counts.
FCarrayoptionalRequired when analysis_type is liquefaction. Fines content (%).
amax_gfloatoptionalRequired when analysis_type is liquefaction. Peak ground acceleration (g).
gwt_depthfloatoptionalRequired when analysis_type is liquefaction. Groundwater depth (m).
magnitudefloatoptionalEarthquake magnitude. default: 7.5
project_namestroptionalProject name for header. default: "Project"
project_numberstroptionalProject number for header.
engineerstroptionalEngineer name for header.
checkerstroptionalChecker name for header.
companystroptionalCompany name for header.
datestroptionalDate string (auto-filled if empty).
assumptionsdictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user did not give, as {input name: its basis}, e.g. {"unit_weight": "not given; typical of the soil described"}. An assumption that is not an input is its own row: {"drained": "long-term condition"}. The package lists them under Assumed Inputs with the analysis's own defaults, so no assumption reads as given. A misspelt input name is refused with a did-you-mean.
givenlist|dictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user gave, by the names you pass them under, e.g. ["width", "depth", "friction_angle"], or with the user's own words, {"friction_angle": "phi 32 deg from the boring logs"}. Only these print under Given Inputs. Every other input you pass prints under Assumed Inputs as passed, not stated as given (with its basis when it is in assumptions); left out, no input is the user's. A value you read off, worked out or chose is assumed, not given.
output_pathstroptionalFile path to save output. Auto-generated if omitted.
formatstroptionalOutput format: 'html' (recommended, self-contained with embedded CSS), 'latex' (raw .tex source), or 'pdf' (requires pdflatex installed). HTML is always available; PDF requires a LaTeX compiler on the system. allowed: html, latex, pdf default: "html"

retaining_wall_package — Run a cantilever retaining wall (cantilever_wall), MSE wall (mse_wall, ASD) or MSE LRFD external stability (mse_lrfd_external_stability) analysis and generate its calc package.

ParameterTypeDescription
wall_typestroptionalThe wall to analyse and report: 'cantilever' (the cantilever_wall tool), 'mse' (the mse_wall tool, ASD factors of safety, external and internal) or 'mse_lrfd' (the mse_lrfd_external_stability tool, LRFD capacity:demand ratios under Strength I max and min, the critical combination and Service I, external stability only; GM-307). allowed: cantilever, mse, mse_lrfd also read as: cantilever_wall = cantilever, mse_wall = mse, mse_lrfd_external_stability = mse_lrfd default: "cantilever"
wall_heightfloatrequiredwall_type=cantilever: TOTAL wall height H (m), measured from the UNDERSIDE of the base slab (footing) to the top of the stem: H = base_thickness + stem height. The active thrust acts over H on the vertical plane through the back of the heel. If you know the height retained above the top of the footing, add base_thickness (4.0 m retained on a 0.5 m footing is wall_height 4.5). | wall_type=mse: Design wall height H (m): the height of the reinforced soil mass, incl. embedment (GEC-11). | wall_type=mse_lrfd: Design wall height H (m), incl. embedment. Alias: height.
gamma_backfillfloatrequiredwall_type=cantilever: Backfill unit weight (kN/m3). | wall_type=mse_lrfd: Reinforced fill unit weight (kN/m3). Alias: gamma.
phi_backfillfloatrequiredwall_type=cantilever: Backfill friction angle (degrees). | wall_type=mse: Backfill friction angle (degrees). GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-10: above 34 deg only from triaxial or direct shear tests on the project's fill, and never above 40 deg; the result warns past either. | wall_type=mse_lrfd: Reinforced fill friction angle (deg). GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-10: above 34 deg only from triaxial or direct shear tests on the project's fill, and never above 40 deg; the result warns past either. Alias: phi.
base_widthfloatoptionalBase width (m). Auto-sized if omitted.
toe_lengthfloatoptionalToe length (m). Auto-sized if omitted.
stem_thickness_topfloatoptionalStem thickness at top (m). default: 0.3
stem_thickness_basefloatoptionalStem thickness at base (m).
base_thicknessfloatoptionalBase slab thickness (m). Auto-sized if omitted: H/10 (FHWA NHI-06-089 Fig. 10-16(a), p. 10-38: H/12 to H/10).
stem_batterstroptionalWhich face of a tapered stem (thicker at its base than at its top) is battered. 'back' (default): the front face vertical, the backfill over the battered back counted as resisting weight. 'front': the back face vertical, as UFC 3-220-20 App. B-1 Fig. B-2 (p. 598) and FHWA NHI-06-089 Fig. 10-16(a) and Example 10-3 (p. 10-52) draw it. allowed: back, front default: "back"
embedment_depthfloatoptionalDepth of the underside of the base below the ground in front of the wall, Df (m), 0 to wall_height. Left out: the base thickness, the ground in front at the top of the base. Deeper, the soil over the toe counts as resisting weight (UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-27, p. 220: 'Weight includes ... weight of soil above footing'; App. B-1.3, p. 599), at gamma_foundation, and include_passive's passive resistance acts over Df.
has_shear_keybooloptionalInclude a shear key below the base (with key_depth). It acts only with include_passive: the sliding check then takes the passive resistance over the depth of the key only, from the underside of the base (depth embedment_depth below the ground in front) to the bottom of the key (embedment_depth + key_depth), the trapezoid UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-29 draws below the toe (p. 224: 'the passive pressure is applied only along the depth of the key and not along the entire burial depth of the wall'; GEC-6 Fig. 5-22 likewise), in place of the passive over the embedment; with the undrained rule it counts cu, as GEC-6 Eq. 5-41 (p. 101) counts Pp in front of the key. GEC-6 Sec. 5.4 (pp. 100-101): keys in granular soils 'are not very efficient in developing passive pressures'; its key method is for stiff, overconsolidated clays and soft rock. UFC: 'it is also prudent to consider some amount of future excavation in front of the wall'. default: false
key_depthfloatoptionalShear key depth below the underside of the base slab (m). default: 0.0
surchargefloatoptionalwall_type=cantilever: Uniform LIVE-load surcharge on the backfill (kPa), e.g. traffic. Its thrust K*q*H drives every check. Over the heel it is NOT a resisting force in sliding, overturning or the eccentricity check by default (live_load_resists), and it does load the base in the bearing pressures (surcharge_in_bearing). A pavement or slab is not a surcharge here: model it as retained soil up to the ground surface (it then rests on the heel and resists like the backfill). Any other surcharge is transient live load: its thrust counts in every check, but its weight over the heel does not resist sliding or overturning. A permanent load you want carried as a surcharge goes in dead_load_surcharge. | wall_type=mse: Live-load (traffic) surcharge (kPa), e.g. heq*gamma. Externally its thrust drives every check; over the reinforced zone it is not a resisting force in sliding or overturning and it loads the base for bearing (GEC-11 Fig. 4-2; live_load_resists, surcharge_in_bearing). Internally it is in Tmax and not in the pullout resistance, which GEC-11 takes 'neglecting traffic loads' (p. 4-49). With a sloping backfill it is taken only with broken_backslope_height, as traffic on the level ground behind the crest; refused on a slope that continues. | wall_type=mse_lrfd: Live-load surcharge q (kPa) over the mass (e.g. heq*gamma). Used as the LL unless live_load overrides. With a broken backslope it is traffic on the level ground behind the crest (thrust Kab*q*h, inclined at I; GEC-11 Example E1); refused on a slope that continues. default: 0.0
dead_load_surchargefloatoptionalUniform DEAD-load (permanent) surcharge on the backfill (kPa), a permanent load that is not part of the retained soil (FHWA NHI-06-089 Sec. 10.4.2). Pavements and slabs are normally modelled as retained soil up to the ground surface instead. Its thrust drives every check, added to the live load's. Over the heel it is not a resisting force by default (dead_load_resists=true counts it as resisting weight in sliding and overturning); it loads the base in the bearing pressures (surcharge_in_bearing). default: 0.0
live_load_resistsbooloptionalwall_type=cantilever: Count the live-load surcharge over the heel (and its share of a sloped or Coulomb thrust's vertical component) as a resisting force in sliding, overturning and the eccentricity check. Default false: FHWA NHI-06-089 Sec. 10.5.5 (p. 10-43), 'the live load surcharge is not considered as a stabilizing force over the heel of the wall when sliding resistance is being checked'; UFC 3-220-20 App. B-1.2 (p. 597), 'For overturning and sliding checks, it is assumed that the traffic pressure does not act over the wall heel'. true = the free body with the load over the heel, which none of these references uses for a live load. The result's choices say which was used. | wall_type=mse: Count the live-load surcharge over the reinforced zone (q*L; behind the crest of a broken backslope, q over the level ground on the zone) as resisting weight in sliding and overturning. Default false: GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-19, 'The live load surcharge is not considered as a stabilizing force when checking sliding'; p. 4-21 (Eq. 4-12), 'the live load is excluded since it increases sliding stability'; p. 4-22, loads that increase sliding resistance only 'if those loads are permanent', and the eccentricity (overturning) check 'only applies the live load above the retained backfill' (Fig. 4-2). true = the free body with the load over the zone, W = gamma*H*L + q*L. The result's choices say which was used. default: false
dead_load_resistsbooloptionalCount the dead-load surcharge over the heel as a resisting force in sliding, overturning and the eccentricity check. Default false: FHWA NHI-06-089 Sec. 10.5.3 (p. 10-41), for CIP semi-gravity walls the surcharge loads are 'conservatively neglected within the width of the base slab since they contribute to overturning and sliding resistance'. true = counted as a permanent load: GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-22 (AASHTO), loads that increase sliding resistance are included 'only if those loads are permanent'. default: false
surcharge_in_bearingbooloptionalwall_type=cantilever: Count the surcharges over the heel in the bearing pressures (q_toe, q_heel, FOS_bearing). Default true: UFC 3-220-20 App. B-1.6 (p. 602), 'it is conservative to include the surcharge over the heel of the wall, if this is possible to occur, in the bearing capacity check'; GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-26. false = the surcharge taken as located behind the heel (NHI-06-089 p. 10-41). | wall_type=mse: Count the live-load surcharge over the reinforced zone in the bearing pressure sigma_v and its eccentricity. Default true: GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-26, 'The bearing check applies live load above both the reinforced zone and the retained backfill' (Fig. 4-2; Eqs. 4-19, 4-20). false = the live load taken as not over the zone. default: true
backfill_slopefloatoptionalwall_type=cantilever: Backfill slope angle (degrees), rising away from the wall. A backfill descending away from the wall (below 0) is refused. | wall_type=mse: Slope of the backfill surface above the wall, beta (degrees from horizontal), rising away from the face; 0 = level. GEC-11 Section 4.4.4: Coulomb Kab with the interface angle delta = beta (Eqs. 4-2/4-3); thrust F_T = 1/2*Kab*gamma_retained*h^2 on h = H + L*tan(beta), inclined at beta (Eq. 4-7); the slope fill over the reinforced zone is added to the weight; internally the slope adds S_eq = 1/2*(0.7H)*tan(beta) of fill (Fig. 4-11). Must not be steeper than phi_retained. | wall_type=mse_lrfd: Slope of the backfill surface above the wall, beta (degrees from horizontal), rising away from the face; 0 = level. GEC-11 Section 4.4.6 (Examples E3, E1): Coulomb Kab with delta = beta; F_T = 1/2*Kab*gamma_retained*h^2 on h = H + L*tan(beta) (Eq. 4-7), inclined at beta; F_T*cos(beta) drives and F_T*sin(beta) resists, both EH-factored (Eqs. 4-11, 4-13, 4-16, 4-21); the slope fill over the zone (V2) is an EV load. Must not be steeper than phi_retained. default: 0.0
c_backfillfloatoptionalBackfill cohesion (kPa). The active pressure Ka sigma_v - 2 c sqrt(Ka) is taken as zero where it is negative, the tension zone (UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-5 Note A; FHWA NHI-06-089 p. 10-15); the result's choices give the thrust with c neglected and with NHI's minimum active pressure of 5z kN/m2 beside it. default: 0.0
phi_foundationfloatoptionalwall_type=cantilever: Foundation soil friction angle (deg), FULL value — the sliding check applies delta_b = (2/3)*phi_foundation INTERNALLY. Do NOT pre-reduce (passing 2/3*phi here double-counts the reduction). To set the base friction angle directly, use delta_base instead. Defaults to phi_backfill. phi_foundation = 0 gives an undrained strength (c_foundation = cu): sliding_cohesion then defaults to 'undrained'. | wall_type=mse: Foundation soil friction angle (deg). Sliding takes mu = min(tan phi_foundation, tan phi_backfill) (GEC-11 Vol I Eq. 4-12, p. 4-22). Left out: 30 deg, as GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-10 prints for the foundation soil 'in absence of specific data' ('recommended only for preliminary sizing'), stated in choices. phi_foundation = 0 gives an undrained strength (c_foundation = cu): sliding_cohesion then defaults to 'undrained'. | wall_type=mse_lrfd: Foundation friction angle (deg); the sliding interface uses mu = min(tan phi_backfill, tan phi_foundation) (GEC-11 Vol I Eq. 4-12, p. 4-22). Left out: 30 deg, as GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-10 prints for the foundation soil 'in absence of specific data' ('recommended only for preliminary sizing'), stated in choices. phi_foundation = 0 gives an undrained strength (c_foundation = cu): sliding_cohesion then defaults to 'undrained'.
c_foundationfloatoptionalwall_type=cantilever: Foundation soil cohesion (kPa), FULL value, no 2/3 factor. The sliding check counts it by sliding_cohesion: NOT at all with 'drained' (the default unless phi_foundation is 0), as the undrained shear strength cu with 'undrained' (ca = cu) or 'friction_plus_adhesion' (Ca from UFC 3-220-20 Table 4-1). To set the adhesion directly, use base_adhesion. | wall_type=mse: Foundation soil cohesion (kPa). The sliding check counts it only by sliding_cohesion 'undrained', as the undrained shear strength cu; with 'drained' (the default unless phi_foundation is 0) it is not counted, as GEC-11 Eq. 4-12 prints no cohesion term. | wall_type=mse_lrfd: Foundation cohesion (kPa): c_f in qn when gamma_foundation is given, and in sliding only by sliding_cohesion 'undrained', as the undrained shear strength cu; with 'drained' (the default unless phi_foundation is 0) sliding does not count it, as GEC-11 Eq. 4-12 prints no cohesion term. default: 0.0
sliding_cohesionstroptionalwall_type=cantilever: How the sliding check counts the foundation soil's cohesion, by the rule a reference prints. Default depends on phi_foundation: 'undrained' when phi_foundation is 0 (c_foundation is then cu), else 'drained'. 'drained': R = V tan delta_b, c_foundation NOT counted (GEC-6 Sec. 5.4 Eq. 5-38, p. 100: 'Equations 5-38 and 5-39 should not be combined for use at the same time'; EN 1997-1 6.5.3(10): 'Any effective cohesion c' should be neglected'). 'undrained': R = ca B alone, no friction, ca = c_foundation taken as the undrained shear strength cu, or base_adhesion (GEC-6 Eq. 5-39: 'ca is typically taken as equal to the undrained shear strength'). 'friction_plus_adhesion': R = V tan delta_b + Ca Be, Ca from UFC 3-220-20 Table 4-1 (p. 184) at c_foundation taken as the undrained shear strength (up to 191.5 kPa), or base_adhesion; Be = B - 2e, the effective base width (UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-27 and Sec. 4-5.1.3, p. 223, which adds that the minimum FS 'may also need to be increased when base adhesion is included'). The result's choices give the rule used, its basis and each other rule's FOS_sliding on the same wall. | wall_type=mse: How the sliding check counts the foundation soil's cohesion. Default depends on phi_foundation: 'undrained' when phi_foundation is 0 (c_foundation is then cu), else 'drained'. 'drained': R = V min(tan phi_foundation, tan phi_backfill), c_foundation NOT counted (GEC-11 Vol I Eqs. 4-12, 4-13, p. 4-21: Rr = V mu, no cohesion term; GEC-6 Eq. 5-38). 'undrained': R = min(cu L, V tan phi_backfill), cu = c_foundation, no base friction: GEC-11 p. 4-21 Step 3 takes the weaker of sliding along the foundation soil ('based on c'f + tan phi'f and/or cu for cohesive soils') and along the reinforced fill; the foundation's resistance cu over the base as GEC-6 Eq. 5-39 gives it ('ca is typically taken as equal to the undrained shear strength'). GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-19 evaluates sliding on the base 'using the same procedures as for spread footings on soil as per Article 10.6.3.4 (AASHTO, 2007)', which is not held; UFC 3-220-20 Sec. 4-5.1.3 (p. 223) takes the lowest of the resistance at the interface between the base and a bearing layer and 'the resistance within the clay using the full undrained shear strength'. Before GM-297 the tool added 2/3 c_foundation x L to the friction, which no reference held prints. The result's choices give the rule used, its basis and the other rule's FOS_sliding on the same wall. | wall_type=mse_lrfd: How the sliding check counts the foundation soil's cohesion. Default depends on phi_foundation: 'undrained' when phi_foundation is 0 (c_foundation is then cu), else 'drained'. 'drained': Rr = phi_sliding x gamma_EV x V x min(tan phi_foundation, tan phi_backfill), c_foundation NOT counted (GEC-11 Vol I Eqs. 4-12, 4-13, p. 4-21; GEC-6 Eq. 5-38). 'undrained': Rr = phi_sliding x min(cu L, gamma_EV x V x tan phi_backfill), cu = c_foundation, no base friction (GEC-11 p. 4-21 Step 3: the weaker of sliding along the foundation soil, 'based on c'f + tan phi'f and/or cu for cohesive soils', and along the reinforced fill; cu over the base as GEC-6 Eq. 5-39 gives it). GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-19 evaluates sliding on the base 'using the same procedures as for spread footings on soil as per Article 10.6.3.4 (AASHTO, 2007)', which is not held; UFC 3-220-20 Sec. 4-5.1.3 (p. 223) takes the lowest of the resistance at the interface between the base and a bearing layer and 'the resistance within the clay using the full undrained shear strength'. Before GM-297 the tool added 2/3 c_foundation x L, which no reference held prints. The result's choices give the rule used, its basis and the other rule's governing sliding CDR. allowed: drained, friction_plus_adhesion, undrained
delta_basefloatoptionalBase interface friction angle delta_b (deg), used DIRECTLY in the sliding check with NO 2/3 factor. Overrides the (2/3)*phi_foundation default. delta_b = phi_foundation for concrete cast against the ground (GEC-6 Sec. 5.4, p. 99: tan delta 'will be equal to the tangent of the friction angle (tan phi) for the soil supporting the footing'). The result's choices state the delta_b used, its basis and the other reading. Refused with sliding_cohesion 'undrained', which counts no friction.
base_adhesionfloatoptionalBase adhesion ca (kPa), used DIRECTLY with sliding_cohesion 'undrained' (in place of cu) or 'friction_plus_adhesion' (in place of the UFC 3-220-20 Table 4-1 value). Refused with 'drained', which counts no adhesion: give sliding_cohesion with it.
include_passivebooloptionalInclude passive resistance in front of the wall in the sliding check (Rankine's Kp unless passive_theory says otherwise; UFC 3-220-20 p. 219: 'typically ignored', and with it considered FSL >= 2.0, Fig. 4-27, so FOS_sliding_required then defaults to 2.0), acting over the embedment, from the ground in front to the underside of the base (embedment_depth, default the base thickness), or with has_shear_key over the depth of the key only (from embedment_depth to embedment_depth + key_depth below the ground in front, UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-29). With the undrained rule it counts the foundation's cu, Kp sigma_v + 2 cu sqrt(Kp) (UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 4-7, p. 178, and p. 181); with the other rules c_foundation is not counted in it (p. 179). default: false
gamma_foundationfloatoptionalwall_type=cantilever: Foundation soil unit weight (kN/m3): the passive resistance in front of the wall and the soil over the toe (embedment_depth below the top of the base). Defaults to gamma_backfill. | wall_type=mse_lrfd: Foundation soil unit weight (kN/m3). Given in place of bearing_resistance_strength, it works the strength bearing resistance out for each Strength I combination, as GEC-11 Vol II Example E2 does: qn = c_foundation*Nc + 0.5*L'*gamma_foundation*Ngamma (GEC-11 Vol I Eq. 4-22; Nc, Ngamma from Table 4-6 for phi_foundation, which must then be given: the reinforced fill's phi_backfill is not taken for it) over that combination's L' = L - 2eB (L' = L when eB < 0), for a level grade in front of the wall and no groundwater influence, the wall's embedment neglected (p. 4-28); qR = phi_bearing*qn (Eq. 4-23). For a slope in front of the wall or a high water table work qn out by AASHTO 10.6.3.1.2 and give bearing_resistance_strength.
passive_theorystroptionalWith include_passive, the passive coefficient in front of the wall: 'rankine' (default) = Rankine's Kp, no wall friction; 'log_spiral' (or 'caquot_kerisel', the same) = the log-spiral Kp of log_spiral_source at passive_wall_friction_deg. UFC 3-220-20 (Sec. 4-5.1, Figs. 4-27 and 4-29, pp. 219-224) names no theory for it; choices give the other theory's Kp and FOS_sliding and the FOS with no passive. allowed: rankine, log_spiral, caquot_kerisel also read as: logspiral = log_spiral, log-spiral = log_spiral default: "rankine"
log_spiral_sourcestroptionalWith passive_theory 'log_spiral', the printed source of Kp, as earth_pressure_coefficient takes it: 'ufc_3_220_20' (default) = UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 4-12 (p. 191), its log-spiral Kp for a vertical face and level ground at any wall friction; 'caquot_kerisel_1948' = the Caltrans Trenching and Shoring Manual Fig. 4-20 chart, and 'dm7_2_eq_4_12' = UFC Eq. 4-12 by name, both needing passive_wall_friction_deg given; 'dm7_2_fig_4_12' / 'dm7_2_fig_4_13' = UFC's charts, drawn for delta/phi' 0.66 only. allowed: ufc_3_220_20, caquot_kerisel_1948, dm7_2_eq_4_12, dm7_2_fig_4_12, dm7_2_fig_4_13 default: "ufc_3_220_20"
passive_wall_friction_degfloatoptionalWith passive_theory 'log_spiral', the wall friction delta in front of the wall (deg), 0 to phi_foundation: the engineer's call (UFC 3-220-20 Table 4-1, p. 184). Left out: delta/phi' = 0.66 (UFC p. 191, 'a common assumption'); refused with 'caquot_kerisel_1948' or 'dm7_2_eq_4_12', which need it given (Caltrans p. 4-29: 'Given delta').
q_allowablefloatoptionalwall_type=cantilever: Allowable bearing pressure (kPa) for the bearing check. On soil (bearing_pressure 'uniform', the default) it is compared with q_eq = V/(B - 2e), the uniform pressure over the effective width B' = B - 2e, so give the allowable bearing pressure for B' (GEC-6 Sec. 6.4.2, p. 119: 'Bf in Equation 5-14 may be replaced by B'f'); with 'linear' (the default with founded_on_rock), with the larger edge pressure. Without it the bearing check is NOT RUN: FOS_bearing and passes_bearing are null and checks_not_run lists 'bearing' (q_toe / q_heel are still reported). | wall_type=mse: Allowable bearing pressure (kPa). Without it the external bearing check is NOT RUN (FOS_bearing null, checks_not_run lists 'bearing'); sigma_v is still reported.
gamma_concretefloatoptionalConcrete unit weight (kN/m3). Default 23.6, 150 pcf, as UFC 3-220-20 App. B-1.3 (p. 599) and FHWA NHI-06-089 Example 10-3 (p. 10-53) take it. default: 23.6
FOS_sliding_requiredfloatoptionalRequired sliding FOS; the check passes at or above it. Default depends on include_passive: 1.5 (GEC-6 Eq. 5-40, p. 100; UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-27; FHWA NHI-06-089 Fig. 10-17), 2.0 with the passive resistance counted (UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-27, p. 220, and Sec. 4-5.1.3, p. 223: 'If passive resistance is included, the minimum FSL should be increased to 2.0'). The result's choices say which was taken.
FOS_overturning_requiredfloatoptionalRequired overturning FOS; the check passes at or above it. Default depends on founded_on_rock: 2.0 on soil, 1.5 on rock (FHWA NHI-06-089 Sec. 10.5.5, p. 10-44: 'approximately of 2.0 for soils and 1.5 for rocks'; GEC-6 Sec. 7.3, p. 124: 'greater than about 2.0 for permanent dead loads'). UFC 3-220-20 Sec. 4-5.1.2 (p. 223) asks FOT >= 1.5 for any wall.
pressure_methodstroptionalEarth pressure theory. The active thrust acts on the vertical plane through the back of the heel. 'rankine' (default): the thrust parallel to the backfill slope. 'coulomb': Coulomb's Ka (UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 4-10) at the wall friction on that plane, wall_friction_deg, by default the backfill slope (FHWA NHI-06-089 p. 10-20 and Example 10-3; delta = 0 behind level backfill). At that default Coulomb's Ka on a vertical plane is Rankine's (sloped) Ka, the same thrust (NHI Example 10-3's 0.35 at phi 30, beta 10 is both), so 'coulomb' changes the result only with wall_friction_deg given. allowed: rankine, coulomb default: "rankine"
wall_friction_degfloatoptionalWall friction delta on the vertical plane through the back of the heel (deg), with pressure_method 'coulomb', 0 to phi_backfill. Left out: the backfill slope (FHWA NHI-06-089 p. 10-20: on that plane 'there is soil-to-soil contact ... it is generally conservative to assume that the earth pressure is parallel to the slope of the backfill'). Refused with 'rankine'. The result's choices give the delta used and the other reading's Ka.
interface_gap_possiblebooloptionalwall_type=cantilever: Whether water or air can reach the base-clay interface. With sliding_cohesion 'undrained' (an undrained clay under the base) the base resistance is then held to 0.4 V (EN 1997-1 Sec. 6.5.3(12)P, Eq. 6.5, p. 65). GEC-6 and UFC 3-220-20 print no such limit. Refused with the other rules. The result's choices give FOS_sliding under the other reading. | wall_type=mse: Whether water or air can reach the interface between the base and an undrained clay foundation. With sliding_cohesion 'undrained' the foundation's resistance is then held to 0.4 V (EN 1997-1 Sec. 6.5.3(12)P, Eq. 6.5, p. 65: 'If it is possible for water or air to reach the interface between a foundation and an undrained clay subgrade, the following check shall be made: Rd <= 0,4 Vd'). GEC-11, GEC-6 and UFC 3-220-20 print no such limit. Refused with the drained rule. The result's choices give FOS_sliding under the other reading. | wall_type=mse_lrfd: Whether water or air can reach the interface between the base and an undrained clay foundation. With sliding_cohesion 'undrained' the foundation's resistance is then held to 0.4 V gamma_EV (EN 1997-1 Sec. 6.5.3(12)P, Eq. 6.5, p. 65: 'If it is possible for water or air to reach the interface between a foundation and an undrained clay subgrade, the following check shall be made: Rd <= 0,4 Vd'). GEC-11, GEC-6 and UFC 3-220-20 print no such limit. Refused with the drained rule. The result's choices give the governing sliding CDR under the other reading. default: false
founded_on_rockbooloptionalWhether the wall is founded on rock. On rock the eccentricity limit is B/4, the middle half, in place of B/6 (GEC-6 Sec. 6.4.1, p. 119; UFC 3-220-20 Sec. 4-5.1.2, p. 223; FHWA NHI-06-089 Fig. 10-17), FOS_overturning_required defaults to 1.5 and bearing_pressure to 'linear'. default: false
water_table_depthfloatoptionalDepth of a level water table behind the wall below the top of the backfill at the stem (m), 0 or more (0 = water at the top of the backfill). Left out: no water table, the backfill drained (FHWA NHI-06-089 Sec. 10.5.3, p. 10-41: 'If adequate drainage measures are provided, the hydrostatic pressure due to groundwater behind the wall generally need not be considered. However, hydrostatic pressure must be considered for portions of the wall below the level of the weep holes unless a deeper drainage system is provided behind the base of the wall'). Given: below it the earth pressure is on the buoyant unit weight gamma_sat - gamma_w and the water pressure gamma_w z is added, horizontal (UFC 3-220-20 Sec. 4-4.1 and Fig. 4-16(a), pp. 199-202; FHWA NHI-06-089 Fig. 10-12, p. 10-27: 'should consider the greatest unbalanced water head anticipated'); the water pressure under the base (base_uplift) comes off V in sliding and adds to the overturning moment. In front of the wall no water is taken above the underside of the base. At or below the underside of the base (wall_height or deeper) it changes nothing. The result's choices give the drained backfill's FOS beside it.
gamma_sat_backfillfloatoptionalWith water_table_depth, the backfill's saturated unit weight below the water table (kN/m3), more than gamma_w (9.81). Left out: gamma_backfill, as UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-16(a) (p. 202) takes gamma 125 pcf above the water table and gamma_b 62.5 pcf below it; against a larger gamma_sat that errs on the safe side for sliding and overturning where the heel carries soil below the water table, on the unsafe side for the bearing pressures and a wall with little or no heel. Refused without water_table_depth.
base_upliftstroptionalWith water_table_depth, the water pressure under the base (uplift), h_w being the water's height above the underside of the base: 'linear' (default) = gamma_w h_w at the heel to 0 at the toe, no water in front of the wall, a straight line between the heads at the heel and the toe as EM 1110-2-2104 para. E-12 (p. 115) prints a wall's uplift; 'uniform' = gamma_w h_w under the whole base, the same head at both (EM 1110-2-2104 para. E-12, p. 116; UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 5-40, p. 346, a structure below the water table). The uplift comes off V in sliding and its moment about the toe adds to the overturning moment (the choices give the FOS with it taken off the stabilizing moment instead, and the other distribution's). Refused without water_table_depth. allowed: linear, uniform default: "linear"
uplift_in_bearingbooloptionalWith water_table_depth, count the uplift in the bearing pressures (q_toe, q_heel, q_eq, FOS_bearing). Default false: UFC 3-220-20 Sec. 5-3.2 (p. 292), 'Uplift is present on the base of the foundation when the groundwater table is above the bearing elevation. Its effect on the bearing pressure can be conservatively ignored unless sliding or uplift is a concern', on the safe side while the resultant is in the middle third (e <= B/6). true = the effective pressure under the base, the weights less the uplift (EN 1997-1 Sec. 6.5.2.1(3)P, p. 63: 'Water pressures not caused by the foundation load shall be included as actions'). Give q_allowable for the water table at that level (GEC-6 Sec. 5.2.3.2, p. 56). Refused without water_table_depth. default: false
bearing_pressurestroptionalThe bearing pressure compared with q_allowable. Default depends on founded_on_rock: 'uniform' on soil, 'linear' on rock. 'uniform' (the default on soil): q_eq = V / B', B' = B - 2e (GEC-6 Eq. 6-6 and Sec. 6.4.2, p. 119; FHWA NHI-06-089 Fig. 10-17: 'Use uniform stress, qeq, for soils'; UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 4-27 and Sec. 4-5.1.4, p. 224, for soil that is 'relatively ductile'). 'linear' (the default with founded_on_rock): the larger edge pressure of the trapezoid or triangle, q_toe or q_heel (UFC Sec. 4-5.1.4: 'For more brittle materials, such as rock and sensitive clays'; FHWA NHI-06-089 Fig. 10-17). The result's choices give the other pressure's FOS_bearing. allowed: uniform, linear
reinforcement_namestroptionalBuilt-in reinforcement name for every level, or omit and define a custom reinforcement via reinforcement_type + reinforcement_Tallowable; for a different reinforcement at different levels give reinforcement_per_level instead. The built-ins are reinforcements GEC-11 Vol II's worked examples print, with their Tal as printed: 'ribbed_steel_strip_50x4' (Example E3's 50 x 4 mm ribbed strip), 'welded_wire_grid_w11' (Example E4's 4W11 bar mat, W11 transverse wires at 0.5 ft), 'bar_mat_e4_3w11_w11x0_5', 'bar_mat_e4_4w15_w11x1' and 'bar_mat_e4_4w15_w11x1_5' (E4's other mats, Table E4-7.4, p. E4-18), 'geogrid_gec11_e1_gg1', 'geogrid_gec11_e1_gg2' and 'geogrid_gec11_e1_gg3' (Example E1's geogrids GG-I to GG-III); list_reinforcement gives each one's Tal and its basis. They are the worked examples' reinforcements, not products: where the wall's reinforcement is specified, give it as a custom reinforcement with its own Tal (for a geosynthetic, Tult / RF for the wall's backfill and design life). A steel strip or grid also needs its horizontal spacing (reinforcement_horizontal_spacing) or coverage_ratio. A built-in carries its own Tal, type and bar geometry, and refuses reinforcement_Tallowable, reinforcement_type, reinforcement_thickness and reinforcement_transverse_spacing.
reinforcement_per_levellistoptionalA reinforcement for each level, from the top down, instead of reinforcement_name and the custom reinforcement_* inputs, as GEC-11 Vol II Example E4 takes 4W11 mats at Levels 1, 3 and 4, a 3W11 mat at Level 2 and 4W15 mats from Level 5 down (Table E4-7.4, p. E4-18). One entry a level, as many as the wall has levels (one a depth of level_depths; without it wall_height / reinforcement_spacing rounded down, at reinforcement_spacing x (i + 1/2) from the top); a list of another length is refused, naming the levels' depths. Each entry is a built-in name (see reinforcement_name and list_reinforcement) or a custom reinforcement {Tallowable, type, width, thickness, transverse_spacing, name}, the keys as the reinforcement_* inputs without the prefix. reinforcement_horizontal_spacing and coverage_ratio apply level by level, one number for the wall or a list with one per level. Pullout and rupture take each level's own Tal, width, Rc, F* and alpha, and each level of the result names its reinforcement. Example, a 3 m wall at reinforcement_spacing 0.75 (four levels) with reinforcement_horizontal_spacing 1.524: ["welded_wire_grid_w11", "bar_mat_e4_3w11_w11x0_5", "bar_mat_e4_4w15_w11x1", {"name": "Mat X", "type": "metallic_grid", "Tallowable": 150, "width": 0.457, "thickness": 0.0095, "transverse_spacing": 0.457}]. Left out, one reinforcement holds at every level (reinforcement_name, or the custom reinforcement_* inputs). This tool refuses a wall that mixes steel and geosynthetic levels, its choice: GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-33 and Fig. 4-9 give one failure surface for inextensible and another for extensible reinforcement, and none for a wall with both.
reinforcement_horizontal_spacingfloat or listoptionalCentre-to-centre horizontal spacing Sh (m) of the strips, grids or sheets at one level (GEC-11 Vol I p. 3-12): one number for the wall, or a list with one per reinforcement level from the top down, as GEC-11 Vol II Example E3 changes it with depth (Table E3-7.3, p. E3-19: 2 strips a 5 ft panel at Levels 1 to 8, 3 at Levels 9 to 12); a list must have as many values as the wall has levels. With the reinforcement's width b it gives the coverage ratio Rc = b/Sh (Eq. 3-1), which scales the pullout resistance (Eq. 4-35, p. 4-49) and the tensile resistance (Tal x Rc, p. 4-47) to a metre of wall. Required for a steel strip or grid unless coverage_ratio is given instead; a call with neither is refused, since GEC-11 prints no spacing to assume (Vol II Example E3 uses 50 mm strips at 0.76 and 0.51 m, 2 or 3 per 1.5 m panel). A geosynthetic with neither is a continuous layer, Rc = 1 (p. 3-13). Aliases: Sh, horizontal_spacing.
coverage_ratiofloat or listoptionalCoverage ratio Rc = b/Sh (GEC-11 Vol I Eq. 3-1, p. 3-12), more than 0 and at most 1, given directly instead of reinforcement_horizontal_spacing with reinforcement_width (not both): one number for the wall, or a list with one per reinforcement level from the top down. Alias: Rc.
F_star_testedfloat or listoptionalPullout resistance factor F* from pullout tests on the product in the wall's backfill (GEC-11 Vol I Table 3-6 note (i), p. 3-17; Appendix B): one number at every level, or [[depth_m, F*], ...] with depths below the top of the wall, linear between and the end value beyond. Replaces the empirical F* (Eqs. 3-4 to 3-8); note (i) accepts the empirical values only for Table 3-1 granular fill with Cu >= 4 ('For fill outside these limits, tests must be run'). The result's choices give FOS_pullout at the empirical F* beside it.
alpha_testedfloatoptionalScale effect correction factor alpha from pullout tests on reinforcements of different lengths (GEC-11 Vol I p. 3-16, Appendix B), more than 0 and at most 1. Left out, Table 3-6's alpha for the reinforcement type (p. 3-17): 1.0 for steel strips and grids, 0.8 for geogrids, 0.6 for geotextiles; a reinforcement_type 'geosynthetic' needs it. Table 3-6 note (ii): 'Pullout testing to determine alpha is recommended if alpha shown in table is less than 1.0'. The result's choices give FOS_pullout at the table's alpha beside a tested one.
Cu_backfillfloatoptionalUniformity coefficient Cu = D60/D10 of the reinforced backfill, for the pullout resistance factor of ribbed steel strips: F* = 1.2 + log Cu at the top of the wall, 2.0 maximum, falling linearly to tan phi_backfill at 20 ft (6 m) and below (GEC-11 Vol I Eqs. 3-4 and 3-5, p. 3-20). Left out, Cu = 4 (F* 1.8 at the top): p. 3-20, 'If the specific Cu for the wall backfill is unknown at design time, a Cu = 4 should be assumed' for fills meeting its Sec. 3.1. Table 3-6 note (i) (p. 3-17) accepts these empirical values only for Table 3-1 granular fill with Cu >= 4 ('For fill outside these limits, tests must be run'); a Cu below 4 is computed and the choices say so. A steel grid given t/St and a geosynthetic keep their own F*, which takes no Cu; given with them, Cu is checked against Table 3-6 note (i) only. The result's choices give the F* used and FOS_pullout at the top level and the lowest at the other reading, or for a grid or geosynthetic whether the given Cu is within note (i). With F_star_tested it is in no check: the tested F* replaces the empirical one, and the F* choice says what the Cu bears on (a strip's empirical F* given beside the tested one, and note (i)'s check on the empirical F*). Aliases: Cu, uniformity_coefficient. default: 4.0
reinforcement_typestroptionalCustom reinforcement type, required with reinforcement_Tallowable. Drives the internal-stability lateral-stress-ratio Kr/Ka and pullout F* curves: ribbed STRIP (metallic_strip: Kr/Ka 1.7->1.2, F* 1.2 + log Cu (2.0 at most; Cu_backfill) -> tan-phi), steel bar mat / welded grid (metallic_grid / bar_mat / welded_grid: Kr/Ka 2.5->1.2, F* 20(t/St)->10(t/St), GEC-11 Vol I Eqs. 3-6, 3-7 — reinforcement_thickness=t and reinforcement_transverse_spacing=St are required, or F_star_tested; a grid with neither is refused), or geogrid / geotextile (Kr/Ka 1.0, F* (2/3) tan phi, Eq. 3-8; GEC-11 Fig. 4-10's geosynthetic line 'Does not apply to polymer strip reinforcement'). It also sets the scale effect correction factor alpha, GEC-11 Vol I Table 3-6 (p. 3-17): 1.0 steel, 0.8 geogrid, 0.6 geotextile; 'geosynthetic' (either kind) needs alpha_tested. allowed: metallic_strip, metallic_grid, bar_mat, welded_grid, geogrid, geotextile, geosynthetic also read as: barmat = metallic_grid, welded_wire_grid = metallic_grid, steel_grid = metallic_grid, ribbed_strip = metallic_strip
reinforcement_TallowablefloatoptionalLong-term allowable tensile strength Tal (kN/m) of a custom reinforcement, per metre of the reinforcement's own width: a strength per strip or per mat is that divided by its width b. The rupture check compares Tal x Rc, per metre of wall (p. 4-47), with the unfactored Tmax. For steel it requires a factor of safety of 1.0, so Tal is an allowable, a fraction of GEC-11 Vol I Eq. 3-11a (p. 3-22), Fy Ac / b with Ac the area after corrosion: 0.55 Fy for strips and 0.48 Fy for bar mats (p. 4-77); a bar mat's Ac is the number of longitudinal bars times one bar's corroded area (Fig. 3-5, p. 3-24). For a geosynthetic it requires 1.5 (1.35 / phi 0.90, Table 4-7), so Tal is the long-term strength Tult / RF (Eq. 3-12, p. 3-28), not divided by a factor of safety. Required when reinforcement_name is not a built-in.
reinforcement_lengthfloatoptionalwall_type=mse: Reinforcement length (m). Left out, max(0.7H, 2.5 m): GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-11, preliminary length 'the greater of 0.7H or 8 ft (2.5 m)'. | wall_type=mse_lrfd: Reinforcement length L (m). Left out, max(0.7H, 2.5 m): GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-11, preliminary length 'the greater of 0.7H or 8 ft (2.5 m)'.
reinforcement_spacingfloatoptionalVertical reinforcement spacing Sv (m): the levels sit at Sv (i + 1/2) below the top of the wall, wall_height / Sv of them rounded down, each taking Sv in Tmax and sigma_H at its depth; when wall_height is not a whole number of spacings the bottom level's contributory height runs from the midpoint above it to the base of the wall, more than Sv, with sigma_H at its middle (GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-47, Fig. 4-14). A spacing of twice wall_height or more is refused. Not taken with level_depths, which places the levels itself. default: 0.6
level_depthslistoptionalThe depths z (m) of the reinforcement levels below the top of the wall, from the top down, instead of reinforcement_spacing, as GEC-11 Vol II's examples print Z (Example E4, Table E4-7.1, p. E4-11: 1.87 ft, then 2.5 ft apart to 24.37 ft). Each must lie inside the wall (0 < z < wall_height) and below the one above; a list that does not is refused. Each level then takes its contributory height Svt (GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-46): from the midpoints between it and its neighbours, the top level's from the top of the wall and the bottom level's to its base (p. 4-47, Fig. 4-14), and Tmax = sigma_H x Svt with sigma_H averaged over Svt (sigma_H_average). Each level of internal_results then also gives Svt_m and sigma_H_kPa. reinforcement_per_level then needs one entry a depth. Example, a 6 m wall: [0.4, 1.15, 1.9, 2.65, 3.4, 4.15, 4.9, 5.65]. Alias: reinforcement_depths.
sigma_H_averagestroptionalWith level_depths: how sigma_H is averaged over each level's contributory height Svt, the two GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-47 gives: 'trapezoidal' (default), the average of sigma_H at the top and the bottom of Svt, as Vol II Examples E3 and E4 take it at every level (pp. E3-15, E4-13); 'midpoint', sigma_H at the middle of Svt. They differ only where Kr/Ka changes with depth (steel reinforcement, within 6.1 m (20 ft) of the top). Refused without level_depths. allowed: trapezoidal, midpoint default: "trapezoidal"
reinforcement_widthfloatoptionalGross width b (m) of the strip, grid or sheet; for a grid, centre to centre of the outside longitudinal bars (GEC-11 Vol I p. 3-12, Fig. 3-3). Required with reinforcement_horizontal_spacing for Rc = b/Sh, except for a built-in that carries its own (ribbed_steel_strip_50x4: 0.05 m; welded_wire_grid_w11 and E4's 4W15 mats: 0.457 m, 4 wires at 0.152 m; bar_mat_e4_3w11_w11x0_5: 0.305 m, 3 wires).
reinforcement_thicknessfloatoptionalStrip thickness (m) for a strip; transverse-bar diameter t (m) for a steel bar mat / welded grid (the t in F* = 20 t/St, GEC-11 Vol I Eq. 3-6), required for a custom grid unless F_star_tested is given. default: 0.0
reinforcement_transverse_spacingfloatoptionalTransverse-bar (grid) spacing St (m) for a steel bar mat / welded grid (the St in F* = 20 t/St, GEC-11 Vol I Eq. 3-6), required for a custom grid unless F_star_tested is given. Used only for bar_mat/welded_grid/metallic_grid. Checked against GEC-11 Vol I p. 3-21's 'maximum St distance is 24 in. (610 mm)' with the empirical F* (grid_spacing; a larger St fails), and under 6 in. (152 mm) it carries a warning (p. 3-20: 'St > 6 inches'); with F* from pullout tests (F_star_tested) an St over 24 in. is a warning, not a check. default: 0.0
face_batterfloatoptionalBatter of the front face and reinforced zone, omega (degrees from vertical, the top set back toward the fill); 0 = vertical. Below 10 deg the wall is taken as vertical (GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-15, 'near vertical walls'; the choices say so). From 10 deg (GM-307): externally Kab by Eqs. 4-2, 4-3 with theta = 90 + omega and delta = beta, F_T at h/3 on the back of the zone at delta - omega to the horizontal (p. 4-15, Fig. 4-5); internally Ka by Eq. 4-26 (p. 4-36; taken as Eqs. 4-2, 4-3 with delta = beta = 0, the printed bracket lacking its square, choices give both), and for geosynthetics the Coulomb failure plane of Fig. 4-9(b) (p. 4-34) through the toe; steel keeps 0.3 H1 from the face (Fig. 4-9(a) note). Refused under a broken backslope (no printed rule) and with an outward lean (below 0). The result's face_batter gives the basis. Aliases: wall_batter, batter, batter_angle, face_batter_deg. default: 0.0
phi_retainedfloatoptionalwall_type=mse: Friction angle (deg) of the retained fill behind the reinforced zone, for the external thrust. Left out: 30 deg, the assumed value GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-10 prints for the retained backfill ('recommended only for preliminary sizing'), stated in choices. | wall_type=mse_lrfd: Retained (behind-mass) fill friction angle (deg) for the external active thrust. Left out: 30 deg, the assumed value GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-10 prints for the retained backfill ('recommended only for preliminary sizing'), stated in choices.
gamma_retainedfloatoptionalwall_type=mse: Unit weight (kN/m3) of the retained fill behind the reinforced zone. Defaults to gamma_backfill. | wall_type=mse_lrfd: Retained fill unit weight (kN/m3). Defaults to gamma_backfill.
broken_backslope_heightfloatoptionalFor a broken backslope (GEC-11 Fig. 4-4): the height S (m) of the slope crest above the top of the wall, with level ground behind it. Omit for a slope that continues. Kab and the thrust inclination then use I, the angle from the top of the wall to the ground 2H behind the face, and h = H + min(L*tan(beta), S).
traffic_vertical_resistsbooloptionalBroken backslope with traffic (surcharge) behind the crest only: count the traffic thrust's vertical component F2*sin(I) as sliding and eccentricity resistance, as GEC-11 Example E1 does (Vol II pp. E1-7 to E1-9). Default false: the GEC-11 text counts loads that increase sliding resistance 'only if those loads are permanent' (Vol I p. 4-22). Bearing counts it either way (p. 4-26). The result's backslope.traffic_basis says which was used. default: false
rho_testedfloatoptionalwall_type=mse: For a geosynthetic at the lowest level, sliding is also checked along it. Sheet reinforcement (GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-21 Step 3(iii): 'For sheet type reinforcement, sliding along the weaker of the upper and lower soil-reinforcement interfaces'; Vol II Example E1 p. E1-7: 'sliding should also be checked at the elevation of the first layer of soil reinforcement'): the block above the lowest layer, its own weight and thrust, slides on tan rho, and the lesser of that and the base governs. The soil-reinforcement interface friction angle rho (deg) from interface direct shear tests, which p. 4-21 prefers ('should preferably be measured by means of interface direct shear tests'). Default 2/3 tan phi_backfill for tan rho ('In absence of testing, it may be taken as 2/3 tan phi'r'; Eq. 3-9, p. 3-21, 'for geotextiles, geogrids and geonet type drainage composites'). Refused when the lowest level's reinforcement is steel. | wall_type=mse_lrfd: With lowest_sheet_depth, sliding along the lowest sheet: The soil-reinforcement interface friction angle rho (deg) from interface direct shear tests, which p. 4-21 prefers ('should preferably be measured by means of interface direct shear tests'). Default 2/3 tan phi_backfill for tan rho ('In absence of testing, it may be taken as 2/3 tan phi'r'; Eq. 3-9, p. 3-21, 'for geotextiles, geogrids and geonet type drainage composites'). Needs lowest_sheet_depth.
live_loadfloatoptionalLive-load surcharge q (kPa) if different from surcharge.
bearing_resistance_strengthfloatoptionalFactored bearing resistance qR at the strength limit (kPa) = phi_b*qn; enables the strength/critical bearing CDR = qR/sigma_v. Give it or gamma_foundation, not both.
phi_bearingfloatoptionalBearing resistance factor phi_b for the qn worked out from gamma_foundation (GEC-11 Table 4-5: 0.65). default: 0.65
local_shear_possiblebooloptionalWith gamma_foundation: local or punching shear failure is possible under the wall, so qn takes the reduced strengths c* = 0.67 c_foundation and phi* = tan^-1(0.67 tan phi_foundation). GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-30: 'If local shear or punching shear failure is possible, Section 10.6.3.1.2b of AASHTO (2007) requires the use of reduced shear strength parameters for calculating the nominal bearing resistance'; local shear 'can occur in loose or compressible soils, in weak soils under slow (drained) loading'. Sliding keeps the strengths given. Default false (general shear). Refused without gamma_foundation: work a given bearing_resistance_strength out with c* and phi* instead. default: false
bearing_resistance_servicefloatoptionalService bearing resistance (kPa); enables the Service I bearing CDR.
lowest_sheet_depthfloatoptionalFor sheet (geosynthetic) reinforcement, the depth (m) below the top of the wall of its lowest layer: sliding is then also checked along it with the same load combinations. Sheet reinforcement (GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-21 Step 3(iii): 'For sheet type reinforcement, sliding along the weaker of the upper and lower soil-reinforcement interfaces'; Vol II Example E1 p. E1-7: 'sliding should also be checked at the elevation of the first layer of soil reinforcement'): the block above the lowest layer, its own weight and thrust, slides on tan rho, and the lesser of that and the base governs. Give it for geogrid or geotextile reinforcement; leave it out for steel strips or grids. Not given: sliding is checked at the base only.
gamma_EV_maxfloatoptionalMax vertical-earth (EV) load factor (AASHTO Strength I). default: 1.35
gamma_EV_minfloatoptionalMin vertical-earth (EV) load factor. default: 1.0
gamma_EH_maxfloatoptionalMax horizontal-earth (EH) load factor. default: 1.5
gamma_EH_minfloatoptionalMin horizontal-earth (EH) load factor. default: 0.9
gamma_LLfloatoptionalLive-load (LL) factor. default: 1.75
phi_slidingfloatoptionalSliding resistance factor (AASHTO 11.10.5.3). default: 1.0
ecc_limit_ratiofloatoptionalLimiting-eccentricity ratio e_max/L: 0.25 (L/4) on soil, 0.375 (3L/8) on rock. GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-23: the resultant 'within the middle one-half of the base width for soil foundations (i.e., emax = L / 4) and middle three-fourths of the base width for rock foundations (i.e., emax = 3/8 L)'. default: 0.25
ecc_limit_ratio_servicefloatoptionalLimiting-eccentricity ratio for the Service I resultant: 1/6 (L/6), as GEC-11 Vol II Examples E3, E4 and E5 check it (Tables E3-6.3, E4-6.3, E5-7.1: 'Limiting eccentricity, e = L/4 for strength limit states and e = L/6 for service limit state'). Each example is on soil and no page held prints the service limit on rock, so with ecc_limit_ratio above 0.25 and this left at L/6 the result warns. Must be in (0, 0.5]. default: 0.16666666666666666
key_distance_from_toefloatoptionalDistance from the toe to the front face of the shear key (m), for the wall section figure only: the sliding check takes the passive resistance on the plane below the toe over the key's depth, wherever the key is. Not given: the key is drawn under the stem, an assumption: UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-29 (p. 224, a gravity wall) and GEC-6 Fig. 5-22 (p. 101, a footing) print no key position for a cantilever wall. Set it here.
key_widthfloatoptionalWidth of the shear key (m), for the wall section figure only. Not given: the stem's thickness at its base, an assumption: no printed basis for a cantilever wall's key width.
project_namestroptionalProject name for header. default: "Project"
project_numberstroptionalProject number for header.
engineerstroptionalEngineer name for header.
checkerstroptionalChecker name for header.
companystroptionalCompany name for header.
datestroptionalDate string (auto-filled if empty).
