assumptionsdictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user did not give, as {input name: its basis}, e.g. {"unit_weight": "not given; typical of the soil described"}. An assumption that is not an input is its own row: {"drained": "long-term condition"}. The package lists them under Assumed Inputs with the analysis's own defaults, so no assumption reads as given. A misspelt input name is refused with a did-you-mean.
givenlist|dictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user gave, by the names you pass them under, e.g. ["width", "depth", "friction_angle"], or with the user's own words, {"friction_angle": "phi 32 deg from the boring logs"}. Only these print under Given Inputs. Every other input you pass prints under Assumed Inputs as passed, not stated as given (with its basis when it is in assumptions); left out, no input is the user's. A value you read off, worked out or chose is assumed, not given.
output_pathstroptionalFile path to save output. Auto-generated if omitted.
formatstroptionalOutput format: 'html' (recommended, self-contained with embedded CSS), 'latex' (raw .tex source), or 'pdf' (requires pdflatex installed). HTML is always available; PDF requires a LaTeX compiler on the system. allowed: html, latex, pdf default: "html"

ground_improvement_package — Run ground improvement analysis and generate calc package.

ParameterTypeDescription
methodstroptionalWhich method to analyse and report: the wick_drains, aggregate_piers, surcharge_preloading ('surcharge') or vibro_compaction ('vibro') tool. allowed: wick_drains, aggregate_piers, surcharge, vibro also read as: surcharge_preloading = surcharge, vibro_compaction = vibro default: "wick_drains"
spacingfloatoptionalRequired when method is wick_drains or aggregate_piers. method=wick_drains: Center-to-center drain spacing (m). | method=aggregate_piers: Center-to-center spacing (m). Alternatively give area_replacement_ratio (As/A, 0.1-0.35 typical) and spacing is back-calculated.
chfloatoptionalRequired when method is wick_drains. method=wick_drains: Horizontal coefficient of consolidation (m2/yr). | method=surcharge: Horizontal coefficient of consolidation (m2/yr). Give with drain_spacing to include wick drains.
cvfloatoptionalRequired when method is wick_drains or surcharge. Vertical coefficient of consolidation (m2/yr).
HdrfloatoptionalRequired when method is wick_drains or surcharge. Vertical drainage path (m).
timefloatoptionalRequired when method is wick_drains. Analysis time (years).
dwfloatoptionalmethod=wick_drains: Equivalent drain diameter (m). Default 2.5 in (0.0635 m), GEC-13 p. 2-35: 'Various diameters ranging from 1.5 inch to 5.5 inch have been used, but the most common is to use 2.5 inch.' A band drain's is 2(a + b)/pi (Eq. 2-3). | method=surcharge: Equivalent drain diameter (m). Default 2.5 in (0.0635 m), GEC-13 p. 2-35: 'Various diameters ranging from 1.5 inch to 5.5 inch have been used, but the most common is to use 2.5 inch.' A band drain's is 2(a + b)/pi (Eq. 2-3). With drains. default: 0.0635
patternstroptionalmethod=wick_drains: Installation pattern. | method=vibro: Probe pattern. GEC-13 p. 4-77: a square pattern 'requires 5 to 8 percent more points to achieve the same minimum densities in large areas'. allowed: triangular, square default: "triangular"
smear_ratiofloatoptionalmethod=wick_drains: Smear zone ratio s = ds/dw. Not given: smear ignored (F_s = 0), GEC-13 p. 2-35, 'The effects of both soil disturbance and well resistance are often ignored for typical projects.' Above 1, F_s = (kh/ks) ln(s) is added to F(n), as UFC 3-220-10 (2026) Eq. 5-25 prints it; GEC-13 prints no F_s formula, only 'a sample disturbance factor Fs ≈ 2 may be considered' in highly plastic, sensitive soils whose ch is accurately determined. | method=surcharge: Smear zone ratio s = ds/dw, with drains. Not given: smear ignored (F_s = 0), GEC-13 p. 2-35, 'The effects of both soil disturbance and well resistance are often ignored for typical projects.' Above 1, F_s = (kh/ks) ln(s) is added to F(n), as UFC 3-220-10 (2026) Eq. 5-25 prints it; GEC-13 prints no F_s formula, only 'a sample disturbance factor Fs ≈ 2 may be considered' in highly plastic, sensitive soils whose ch is accurately determined.
kh_ks_ratiofloatoptionalmethod=wick_drains: Permeability ratio kh/ks, used only with smear_ratio above 1 (UFC 3-220-10 Eq. 5-25). | method=surcharge: Permeability ratio kh/ks, with drains, used only with smear_ratio above 1 (UFC 3-220-10 Eq. 5-25). default: 1.0
n_time_pointsintoptionalPoints in the time-settlement curve. default: 50
column_diameterfloatoptionalRequired when method is aggregate_piers. Pier column diameter (m).
area_replacement_ratiofloatoptionalArea replacement ratio As/A (0.1-0.35 typical). Used to compute spacing when spacing is not given.
E_soilfloatoptionalSurrounding soil modulus (kPa). With settlement_method 'stress_ratio', used only for the composite modulus E_comp = E_soil*[1 + as*(n-1)]; the GEC-13 Fig. 5-21 methods need it given, for E_c/E_s. default: 5000.0
nfloatoptionalStress concentration ratio sigma_c/sigma_s; sets the improved bearing and, with settlement_method 'stress_ratio', the settlement reduction factor. GEC-13 for stone columns: measured 'between 2.0 and 5.0' (p. 5-31), and 'For preliminary design, a ratio of 2.5 is often conservatively used for stability and bearing resistance calculations' (p. 5-32); for rammed aggregate piers 5 to 10 under flexible embankment loading and 10 under rigid footings (p. 5-43); 'stress concentration ratios range from 4 to 45 for rigid footings' (p. 5-45). default: 5.0
settlement_methodstroptionalHow the settlement over the columns is worked out. 'stress_ratio' (default): SRF = 1/[1 + as*(n-1)] from n. The others give the settlement ratio (settlement without columns / with them; GEC-13 p. 5-36 prints it as 'n', which is not the stress ratio n) by E_c/E_s off GEC-13 Fig. 5-21, and need E_column and E_soil: 'weighted_modulus' (curve 2, settlement ratio = 1 + as*(E_c/E_s - 1), any E_c/E_s); 'balaam_rigid' (curves 5b, 5c: E_c/E_s 5 to 10, A/A_c 1.75 to 9); 'balaam_flexible' (curve 5a: E_c/E_s = 10, A/A_c 1.5 to 8.5). GEC-13 p. 5-37: the FHWA (1983) Equilibrium Method, 'roughly equivalent to the Balaam relationships', 'represents an average or lower bound estimate suitable for preliminary analyses'; the Priebe curve (priebe_improvement_factor) 'the upper bound effectiveness'. allowed: stress_ratio, weighted_modulus, balaam_rigid, balaam_flexible default: "stress_ratio"
E_columnfloatoptionalAggregate column modulus E_c (kPa), with E_soil, for the settlement_method 'weighted_modulus', 'balaam_rigid' or 'balaam_flexible' (E_c/E_s, GEC-13 Fig. 5-21). Refused with 'stress_ratio', which takes n instead. Alias: column_modulus.
q_unreinforcedfloatoptionalUnreinforced bearing capacity (kPa). 0 = not computed. default: 0.0
S_unreinforcedfloatoptionalUnreinforced settlement (mm). 0 = not computed. default: 0.0
S_ultimatefloatoptionalRequired when method is surcharge. Ultimate consolidation settlement under the surcharge (m). Compute first via the settlement module if unknown.
surcharge_kPafloatoptionalRequired when method is surcharge. Applied surcharge pressure (kPa).
target_UfloatoptionalTarget degree of consolidation (percent). default: 90.0
drain_spacingfloatoptionalWick drain spacing (m), if drains are used.
sigma_v0floatoptionalCurrent effective stress at layer center (kPa). default: 0.0
fines_contentfloatoptionalRequired when method is vibro. Percent passing #200 sieve (0-100). GEC-13 p. 4-65: 'proper densification generally cannot be achieved when the granular soil contains more than 12 to 15 percent silt OR more than 2 percent clay'; p. 4-67: fines below 10 percent ideally suited. Above 15 not feasible, 12 to 15 marginal.
initial_N_sptfloatoptionalRequired when method is vibro. Current SPT blow count (blows/ft), read as a density by GEC-13 Table 4-8 (normally consolidated sand). Very dense (N above 50, relative density 85 to 100 percent) is not feasible: p. 4-75, 'It is unlikely, even for heavy loading, that it will be necessary to achieve a relative density above 85 percent.'
target_relative_densityfloatoptionalTarget relative density (%), 55 to 90: the probe spacing is read off GEC-13 Fig. 4-34 (p. 4-77), relative density versus probe spacing for silty sands, the lower bound gradation (p. 4-76); refused outside 55 to 90, where the curve is not printed. GEC-13 p. 4-77: 60 percent for floor slabs, flat bottom tanks, embankments; 70 to 75 percent for column and bridge footings; 80 percent for machinery and mat foundations. Not given: no spacing. Alias: target_Dr.
project_namestroptionalProject name for header. default: "Project"
project_numberstroptionalProject number for header.
engineerstroptionalEngineer name for header.
checkerstroptionalChecker name for header.
companystroptionalCompany name for header.
datestroptionalDate string (auto-filled if empty).
assumptionsdictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user did not give, as {input name: its basis}, e.g. {"unit_weight": "not given; typical of the soil described"}. An assumption that is not an input is its own row: {"drained": "long-term condition"}. The package lists them under Assumed Inputs with the analysis's own defaults, so no assumption reads as given. A misspelt input name is refused with a did-you-mean.
givenlist|dictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user gave, by the names you pass them under, e.g. ["width", "depth", "friction_angle"], or with the user's own words, {"friction_angle": "phi 32 deg from the boring logs"}. Only these print under Given Inputs. Every other input you pass prints under Assumed Inputs as passed, not stated as given (with its basis when it is in assumptions); left out, no input is the user's. A value you read off, worked out or chose is assumed, not given.
output_pathstroptionalFile path to save output. Auto-generated if omitted.
formatstroptionalOutput format: 'html' (recommended, self-contained with embedded CSS), 'latex' (raw .tex source), or 'pdf' (requires pdflatex installed). HTML is always available; PDF requires a LaTeX compiler on the system. allowed: html, latex, pdf default: "html"

wave_equation_package — Run wave equation analysis and generate bearing graph calc package.

ParameterTypeDescription
hammer_namestroptionalHammer name (use list_available_hammers to see options).
pile_lengthfloatrequiredPile length (m).
pile_areafloatrequiredPile cross-sectional area (m2).
R_minfloatoptionalMin resistance (kN). default: 200.0
R_maxfloatoptionalMax resistance (kN). default: 2000.0
R_stepfloatoptionalResistance increment (kN). default: 200.0
skin_fractionfloatoptionalSkin friction fraction. default: 0.5
damping_modelstroptionalSmith damping form (UFC 3-220-20 (2025) Sec. 6-9.2, pp. 487-488): 'smith' (default), damping proportional to the mobilized static resistance, J x R_static x v, set 'in most instances' (GEC-12 Vol 2 p. 242); 'smith_viscous', proportional to the fully mobilized static resistance, J x R_ult x v, which GEC-12 Vol 2 (p. 242) selects for a residual stress analysis or a vibratory hammer, and sometimes for a refined analysis's match. allowed: smith, smith_viscous default: "smith"
quake_sidefloatoptionalShaft quake (m): 0.10 in (0.0025 m), usually satisfactory (GEC-12 Vol 2 Sec. 12.6.7, p. 211). default: 0.0025
quake_toefloatoptionalToe quake (m). Default 0.10 in (0.0025 m), GEC-12 Vol 2's toe quake for a non-displacement pile, e.g. an H-pile (p. 171). A displacement pile (closed end pipe, concrete): pile diameter or width D over 120 to D over 60 (p. 211), D/60 in medium or dense sand and D/120 in very dense soil (Examples 1, 3, 6, pp. 162, 170, 182); GEC-12 Vol 3 (p. 40) also gives H-piles D/60 and D/120. Hard rock: 0.04 in (0.001 m) (p. 212). Saturated or sensitive soils can reach well over D/60 (p. 211). default: 0.0025
damping_sidefloatoptionalShaft Smith damping (s/m), GEC-12 Vol 2 Sec. 12.6.7 (p. 211): 0.05 s/ft (0.16 s/m, the default) non-cohesive soils, 0.10 s/ft (0.33) silty sands, clayey sands and sandy silts, 0.15 s/ft (0.49) cohesive silts and sandy clays, 0.20 s/ft (0.66) cohesive soils. For restrike, perhaps twice as high (p. 211). default: 0.16
damping_toefloatoptionalToe Smith damping (s/m): about 0.15 s/ft (0.49 s/m) for most soils (GEC-12 Vol 2 p. 211); lower on hard rock, e.g. 0.05 s/ft (0.16 s/m) (p. 212). default: 0.49
embedded_lengthfloatoptionalThe pile's embedded length, its penetration below grade (m), at most pile_length: the shaft resistance acts only below grade, the pile above it standing free (GEC-12 Vol 2 p. 224: 'Penetration refers to the analyzed pile toe penetration below grade'; Example 1, p. 162, a 65 ft pile driven 62 ft; Example 6, p. 182, 66 ft with 'an embedded length of 52.5 feet'). Left out: pile_length, the pile embedded over its full length.
shaft_distributionstroptionalHow the shaft resistance (skin_fraction of R_ult) is spread over the embedded length, as GEC-12 Vol 2's examples print it: 'uniform' (default), the same per metre (Example 5, p. 179: '92% uniform shaft resistance'); 'triangular', rising linearly from none at grade to its largest at the pile toe (Example 1, p. 162, Fig. 12-3; Example 6, p. 182: 'distributed triangularly along the embedded portion of the pile shaft'). A distribution from a static analysis layer by layer (Example 4, Fig. 12-9) is not offered. GEC-12 Vol 2 p. 212: the stresses, tension above all, are sensitive to the distribution. allowed: uniform, triangular default: "uniform"
ram_weightfloatoptionalCustom hammer ram weight (kN) — used with stroke when hammer_name is omitted.
strokefloatoptionalCustom hammer stroke (m).
efficiencyfloatoptionalCustom hammer efficiency: the share of the potential ram energy (ram weight x stroke) that reaches the ram as kinetic energy at impact (GEC-12 Vol 2 (FHWA-NHI-16-010) Sec. 12.6.2, p. 205). GEC-12 Vol 2 prints 0.67 for an air hammer and 0.80 for an open end diesel (Example 6, p. 185), and say 0.95 for a hydraulic hammer whose ram kinetic energy is measured (p. 205). Default 0.67. default: 0.67
hammer_custom_namestroptionalCustom hammer label. default: "Custom"
hammer_typestroptionalCustom hammer type: a label in the result and calc package only. Every type is modelled as a rigid ram striking at v = sqrt(2 g stroke efficiency); a diesel hammer's combustion pressure is not modelled, and its result carries a warning (GEC-12 Vol 2 p. 206: its stroke rises with the resistance, and too high a stroke gives non-conservative nominal resistances). Give the type's losses through efficiency (GEC-12 Vol 2 (FHWA-NHI-16-010) Sec. 12.6.2, p. 205: relatively high, say 0.95, for a hydraulic hammer whose ram kinetic energy is measured and displayed). allowed: single_acting, diesel, hydraulic default: "single_acting"
segment_lengthfloatoptionalPile segment length (m): about 1 m (GEC-12 Vol 2 Sec. 12.3, p. 155; GRLWEAP's 3.3 ft, p. 213). Shorter segments for stiff, uncushioned driving systems (p. 210). default: 1.0
cushion_stiffnessfloatoptionalHammer cushion stiffness (kN/m), with cushion_cor and helmet_weight. Or give cushion_area + cushion_thickness + cushion_E: stiffness = E A / t (GEC-12 Vol 2 p. 155); two materials in series 1/k = 1/k1 + 1/k2 (p. 209). The model has one cushion spring, between the ram and the helmet (whose weight is lumped with the pile head); GEC-12 Vol 2 Fig. 12-2 (p. 157) has a hammer cushion and a pile cushion with the helmet between. Left out with no cushion properties: the hammer's printed driving system where a held reference prints one (hammer_name 'Vulcan 014', GEC-12 Vol 2 Table 12-2, p. 183), or the one named by driving_system; for any other hammer the call is refused and the error lists the printed options (GEC-12 prints no cushion by hammer otherwise; ideally the contractor's submittal, Vol II p. 226).
cushion_areafloatoptionalCushion area (m2) — with cushion_thickness and cushion_E.
cushion_thicknessfloatoptionalCushion thickness (m).
cushion_EfloatoptionalCushion elastic modulus (kPa), with the nominal (uncompressed) thickness. Plywood pile cushions 30 ksi (207,000 kPa) new and 75 ksi (517,000 kPa) used; oak boards 60 and 90 ksi (GEC-12 Vol 2 p. 209).
cushion_corfloatoptionalHammer cushion coefficient of restitution, required with a cushion given by stiffness or properties (no held reference prints one COR for every cushion). GEC-12 Vol 2: the hammer cushions of its examples 0.90 to 0.92 (pp. 174, 183); wood 0.50, a badly worn softwood cushion 0.25 (p. 156); a refined analysis adjusts it between 0.10 and 1.0 (p. 216). With a printed driving system and no cushion given: that system's COR unless given (Vulcan 014 0.91, ICE 42S 0.92, p. 183).
pile_EfloatoptionalPile elastic modulus (kPa). Default steel, 29,000 ksi (GEC-12 Vol 1 p. 317). Concrete: on the order of 4,000 ksi, varying with its strength (Vol 1 p. 317); its dynamic modulus is usually higher than the static (Vol 2 p. 213). default: 200000000.0
pile_unit_weightfloatoptionalPile material unit weight (kN/m3). Default steel, 492 lb/ft3 (GEC-12 Vol 2 p. 462). default: 77.3
helmet_weightfloatoptionalHelmet weight (kN): helmet, hammer cushion, striker plate and inserts (GEC-12 Vol 2 p. 226), lumped with the pile head; 0 with no helmet mass. Required with a cushion given. With a printed driving system and no cushion given: that system's helmet unless given (Vulcan 014 1.67 kips, 7.43 kN; ICE 42S 2.05 kips, 9.12 kN; p. 183). GEC-12's examples give 1.0 to 4.07 kips (4.4 to 18.1 kN; Vol II pp. 163, 167, 174, 179, 183).
driving_systemstroptionalA driving system (hammer cushion and helmet) as a held reference prints it, by its hammer: GEC-12 Vol 2 Example 6, Table 12-2 (p. 183), on a steel pipe pile. 'Vulcan 014': Nycast, 208 ksi, 234 in2, 6.0 in (1.42 million kN/m), COR 0.91, helmet 1.67 kips; 'ICE 42S': Blue Nylon, 175 ksi, 398 in2, 2.0 in (6.10 million kN/m), COR 0.92, helmet 2.05 kips. cushion_cor and helmet_weight, if given, replace the system's. Not with cushion_stiffness or cushion properties. Left out: the named hammer's own printed system, which only hammer_name 'Vulcan 014' has; any other hammer needs a cushion given. A run with another hammer says so in its choices. allowed: ICE 42S, Vulcan 014
project_namestroptionalProject name for header. default: "Project"
project_numberstroptionalProject number for header.
engineerstroptionalEngineer name for header.
checkerstroptionalChecker name for header.
companystroptionalCompany name for header.
datestroptionalDate string (auto-filled if empty).
assumptionsdictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user did not give, as {input name: its basis}, e.g. {"unit_weight": "not given; typical of the soil described"}. An assumption that is not an input is its own row: {"drained": "long-term condition"}. The package lists them under Assumed Inputs with the analysis's own defaults, so no assumption reads as given. A misspelt input name is refused with a did-you-mean.
givenlist|dictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user gave, by the names you pass them under, e.g. ["width", "depth", "friction_angle"], or with the user's own words, {"friction_angle": "phi 32 deg from the boring logs"}. Only these print under Given Inputs. Every other input you pass prints under Assumed Inputs as passed, not stated as given (with its basis when it is in assumptions); left out, no input is the user's. A value you read off, worked out or chose is assumed, not given.
output_pathstroptionalFile path to save output. Auto-generated if omitted.
formatstroptionalOutput format: 'html' (recommended, self-contained with embedded CSS), 'latex' (raw .tex source), or 'pdf' (requires pdflatex installed). HTML is always available; PDF requires a LaTeX compiler on the system. allowed: html, latex, pdf default: "html"

pile_group_package — Run rigid-cap pile group analysis (CPGA stiffness method) and generate calc package; with method_6dof, tables (CSV + printed) of the force and displacement at every pile head.

ParameterTypeDescription
method_6dofbooloptionalFalse: the pile_group_simple tool (vertical load and moments on a rigid cap); True: the pile_group_6dof tool (all six load components; needs the pile stiffnesses). allowed: False, True default: false
n_rowsintoptionalRows for rectangular layout.
n_colsintoptionalmethod_6dof=False: Columns for rectangular layout. | method_6dof=True: Columns.
spacing_xfloatoptionalX spacing (m). Or give a single 'spacing' for both directions.
spacing_yfloatoptionalY spacing (m). Or give a single 'spacing' for both directions.
spacingfloatoptionalUniform center-to-center spacing (m), used for both x and y.
pilesarrayoptionalmethod_6dof=False: Explicit pile list [{x, y, batter_x, batter_y, ...}] instead of n_rows/n_cols. | method_6dof=True: Explicit pile list [{x, y, batter_x, batter_y, axial_stiffness, lateral_stiffness, label}] instead of n_rows/n_cols.
VzfloatoptionalDefault: True 0.0 (method_6dof). Required when method_6dof is False. Vertical load (kN).
MxfloatoptionalMoment about x (kN-m). default: 0.0
MyfloatoptionalMoment about y (kN-m). default: 0.0
axial_capacity_compressionfloatoptionalPer-pile compression capacity (kN) for utilization checks (rectangular layout).
axial_capacity_tensionfloatoptionalPer-pile tension capacity (kN) (rectangular layout). Each pile's factored tension resistance. Where piles carry tension, also required for their sum in the group uplift check, as the group_uplift tool takes it; left out, the block alone, their resistance no more than the block's.
axial_stiffnessfloatoptionalRequired when method_6dof is True. Pile-head axial stiffness ka (kN/m), e.g. from a load test or E*A/L for an end-bearing pile. REQUIRED for every pile: give it here with n_rows/n_cols, or on each piles[] entry.
lateral_stiffnessfloatoptionalPile-head lateral stiffness kl (kN/m), here with n_rows/n_cols or on each piles[] entry. Needed for vertical piles to carry Vx/Vy (0 if omitted).
VxfloatoptionalLateral load x (kN). default: 0.0
VyfloatoptionalLateral load y (kN). default: 0.0
MzfloatoptionalTorsion about z (kN-m). default: 0.0
pile_diameterfloatoptionalPile diameter or width (m). With n_rows, n_cols, spacing and soil_type, the package adds the group efficiency factor eta_g, as the group_efficiency tool reads it (GEC-12 Sec. 7.2.2; UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-26). The plan view draws the piles to scale at it. Piles in tension are checked as a block as well (GEC-12 Vol. III checks the back row in tension of a group in compression), and a group in net tension (Vz < 0) as a whole, as the group_uplift tool checks it, with pile_length, soil_type and unit_weight (or layers; cu in clay): the block at the toes to the outer faces of the outer piles.
soil_typestroptionalFor the group efficiency factor eta_g, with pile_diameter and the spacing: the stratum giving most of the resistance, as the group_efficiency tool takes it. Not given: no eta_g, and the package says what it needs. Where piles carry tension, also the group uplift block's soil, as the group_uplift tool takes it. allowed: cohesionless, cohesive
cap_in_contactbooloptionalFor eta_g: whether the pile cap is in firm contact with the ground, as the group_efficiency tool takes it (left out where the row depends on it: not in contact, the lower eta_g, said in the choices).
cufloatoptionalFor eta_g with soil_type 'cohesive': the clay's undrained shear strength (kPa), set against 2 ksf, as the group_efficiency tool takes it; where piles carry tension in clay, the weighted average along the block's perimeter over the embedded length, as the group_uplift tool takes it.
pile_typestroptionalFor eta_g: the column of UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-26, as the group_efficiency tool takes it (driven piles when not given); where piles carry tension, the block's resistance factor phi_ug, as the group_uplift tool takes it. allowed: driven, drilled_shaft, cfa, ddp, micropile default: "driven"
north_degfloatoptionalDirection of north on the plan view, degrees clockwise from the cap's +y axis (up on the plan), -360 to 360, as the plan the layout came from shows it. Not given: north is drawn up and the figure says so.
cap_outlinearrayoptionalThe pile cap's outline on the plan view: its corners [[x, y], ...] in the cap's x, y axes (m, the axes the pile coordinates use), at least three, drawn closed. For the figure only. Not given: no cap is drawn and the figure says so.
property_linearrayoptionalThe property line on the plan view: its points [[x, y], ...] in the cap's x, y axes (m), at least two, drawn dash-dot as given (repeat the first point last to close it). For the figure only. Not given: none is drawn and the figure says so.
pile_lengthfloatoptionalRequired for the group uplift check where piles carry tension (left out, the package says what it needs), as the group_uplift tool takes it: Pile embedded length D (m), the block's height.
unit_weightfloatoptionalRequired for the group uplift check where piles carry tension (left out, the package says what it needs), as the group_uplift tool takes it: The soil's effective unit weight (kN/m3; below the water table the buoyant) over the embedded length. Or give layers.
layersarrayoptionalRequired for the group uplift check where piles carry tension (left out, the package says what it needs), as the group_uplift tool takes it: The soil from the top of the block down, [{thickness (m), unit_weight (effective, kN/m3)}, ...], to the toes at least, in place of one unit_weight (e.g. the water table inside the block). In cohesionless soil each layer's volume is taken between its bottom and top plan dimensions (UFC 3-220-20 p. 436; GEC-12 Vol. III Eq. D-1).
cap_weightfloatoptionalRequired for the group uplift check where piles carry tension (left out, the package says what it needs), as the group_uplift tool takes it: The pile cap's effective weight over the block (kN), part of the block (GEC-12 Eq. 7-41's W_g 'including pile cap weight'; UFC 3-220-20 p. 435); for the piles in tension of a group, the cap over them (GEC-12 Vol. III p. 207 takes the tributary area over the back row in tension). Leave it out (0, the safe side) where the uplift load already carries it. default: 0.0

project_numberstroptionalProject number for header.
engineerstroptionalEngineer name for header.
checkerstroptionalChecker name for header.
companystroptionalCompany name for header.
datestroptionalDate string (auto-filled if empty).
assumptionsdictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user did not give, as {input name: its basis}, e.g. {"unit_weight": "not given; typical of the soil described"}. An assumption that is not an input is its own row: {"drained": "long-term condition"}. The package lists them under Assumed Inputs with the analysis's own defaults, so no assumption reads as given. A misspelt input name is refused with a did-you-mean.
givenlist|dictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user gave, by the names you pass them under, e.g. ["width", "depth", "friction_angle"], or with the user's own words, {"friction_angle": "phi 32 deg from the boring logs"}. Only these print under Given Inputs. Every other input you pass prints under Assumed Inputs as passed, not stated as given (with its basis when it is in assumptions); left out, no input is the user's. A value you read off, worked out or chose is assumed, not given.

formatstroptionalOutput format: 'html' (recommended, self-contained with embedded CSS), 'latex' (raw .tex source), or 'pdf' (requires pdflatex installed). HTML is always available; PDF requires a LaTeX compiler on the system. allowed: html, latex, pdf default: "html"

sheet_pile_package — Run sheet pile wall analysis and generate calc package, with a table (CSV + printed) of pressure, shear and moment along the wall.

ParameterTypeDescription
wall_typestroptionalWhich wall to analyse and report: the cantilever_wall or anchored_wall tool. allowed: cantilever, anchored also read as: cantilever_wall = cantilever, anchored_wall = anchored default: "cantilever"
excavation_depthfloatrequiredExcavation depth (m).
layersarrayrequiredArray of soil-layer dicts, top down: {thickness (m, required), unit_weight (kN/m3, required; alias gamma), friction_angle (deg, default 30; alias phi), cohesion (kPa, default 0), wall_friction_deg (deg, 0 to friction_angle; alias delta), interface_soil (the soil against the steel, a row of the steel sheet pile wall friction table printed in UFC 3-220-20 Table 4-1, p. 184, EM 1110-2-2504 Table 3-3, p. 3-4, and the USS Steel Sheet Piling Design Manual Table 4, p. 13: 'clean_gravel' 22 deg (clean gravel, gravel-sand mixtures, well-graded rock fill with spalls), 'clean_sand' 17 (clean sand, silty sand-gravel mixture, single size hard rock fill), 'silty_sand' 14 (silty sand, gravel or sand mixed with silt or clay), 'fine_sandy_silt' 11 (fine sandy silt, nonplastic silt); at most friction_angle; not with wall_friction_deg)}. wall_friction_deg or interface_soil is used on both sides by pressure_method 'coulomb' and 'log_spiral'. A layer giving neither takes, with 'log_spiral', the clean_sand row (17 deg, at most its phi') on the passive side when it has no cohesion and no wall friction on the active side or in a layer with cohesion (UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-37 step 1, p. 237: 'Passive pressures for clean coarse grained soils include wall friction (see Table 4-1)'; it ignores wall friction in other soils, so give wall_friction_deg 0 in a silty sand or silt); with 'coulomb' none (UFC 3-220-20 p. 190: passive pressure 'should be calculated using the log spiral method and not the Coulomb method'). The result's choices give each layer's wall friction and its Kp at the other rows and at delta = 0, and where a layer took the clean sand row by default the embedment with none.
surchargefloatoptionalSurface surcharge (kPa). default: 0.0
FOS_passivefloatoptionalFOS applied to passive resistance. default: 1.5
gwt_depth_activefloatoptionalGroundwater depth on the active (retained) side, m below the top of the wall.
gwt_depth_passivefloatoptionalGroundwater depth on the passive (excavated) side, m below the top of the wall, the same datum as gwt_depth_active. A depth less than excavation_depth is water standing in front of the wall above the dredge line: its pressure, gamma_w times the depth below that level, acts on the wall from there down (UFC 3-220-20 Sec. 4-4.1, p. 199: 'Water applies a triangular pressure distribution equivalent to a soil with a unit weight of 62.4 pcf and an earth pressure coefficient of unity') and the soil below the dredge line is submerged (Fig. 4-41, p. 242: water levels can differ on the two sides; its example Fig. 4-43, p. 245, has water 5 ft below the top on both sides). The net water pressure is the retained side's less this side's (Figs. 4-5 and 4-6, p. 183: 'Net water pressure = u = gamma_w z2'), so the same depth on both sides (balanced water) gives none. Left out: the excavation level, or gwt_depth_active where that is deeper (no water on either side when gwt_depth_active is left out too), so no water stands in front of the wall.
pressure_methodstroptionalEarth pressure theory. 'log_spiral' uses Coulomb active + the log-spiral PASSIVE coefficient from log_spiral_source (avoids Coulomb's over-prediction of Kp at high delta/phi). 'coulomb' and 'log_spiral' take each layer's wall friction (layers: wall_friction_deg or interface_soil; what a layer giving neither takes is in the layers description). allowed: rankine, coulomb, log_spiral also read as: caquot_kerisel = log_spiral, logspiral = log_spiral default: "rankine"
log_spiral_sourcestroptionalWith pressure_method 'log_spiral', the printed source of the passive Kp. 'ufc_3_220_20' (default): UFC 3-220-20 (DM 7.2), the source the wall's geometry calls for (pp. 191-193); a sheet pile has a vertical face and the tool takes level ground in front of it, so that is Eq. 4-12 (p. 191), at each layer's wall_friction_deg. 'caquot_kerisel_1948': the Caquot and Kerisel (1948) chart, Kp at delta = phi times the printed reduction factor R(delta/phi), Caltrans Trenching and Shoring Manual Fig. 4-20 (p. 4-30), the method its Sec. 4-6 uses for passive pressure. 'dm7_2_fig_4_12', 'dm7_2_fig_4_13': UFC 3-220-20 Figs. 4-12 (p. 192, theta = 0 curve) and 4-13 (p. 193, beta = 0 row), Kerisel and Absi (1990), drawn for delta/phi' = 0.66 only, so every layer's wall_friction_deg must be 0.66 x its friction_angle; UFC 3-220-20 p. 260 says Kp for a tied-back wall 'should be obtained from Figure 4-12'. 'dm7_2_eq_4_12': Eq. 4-12 by name. They differ: at phi 30, delta/phi 0.66 the 1948 chart gives 5.4, the UFC charts 5.3 and Eq. 4-12 5.1. UFC 3-220-20 footnote 21 (p. 191): the 1982 DM 7.2 charts 'used delta/phi' = 1 along with reduction ratios', which 'were averages that introduced substantial inaccuracy for some cases'; the 1948 chart takes that form (Kp at delta = phi times R). UFC 3-220-20 Table 4-2 (p. 194) is not used: the log-spiral Kp in its row headed delta/phi' = 0.5, 5.3, 8.0, 12 and 20 at phi' = 30, 35, 40 and 45, are Fig. 4-13's values, drawn for delta/phi' = 0.66 (5.30, 8.00, 12.0, 20), and the Coulomb Kp printed beside them, 6.1, 9.8, 18 and 44, are Coulomb's at delta = 0.66 phi' (at 0.5 it gives 5.0, 7.4, 11.8 and 21.4). Eq. 4-12 at delta/phi' = 0.5 gives 4.46, 6.33, 9.33 and 14.3. The tool reads Fig. 4-13 at the 0.66 it is drawn for and Eq. 4-12 at the wall friction given. The result's choices give each layer's Kp from the source used and from the others. allowed: ufc_3_220_20, caquot_kerisel_1948, dm7_2_eq_4_12, dm7_2_fig_4_12, dm7_2_fig_4_13 default: "ufc_3_220_20"
embedment_increasefloatoptionalD / D0, the multiplier on the embedment from moment equilibrium: 1.2 (default), as the Caltrans Trenching and Shoring Manual (7-5.02 step 3, p. 7-11: 'The 20 percent increase is not a factor of safety'; its Example 7-3 takes it after FS 1.3 on the moments) and UFC 3-220-20 (Fig. 4-41 step 6, p. 242: 'Increase D by 20% to allow for dredging, scour, etc.'; its example Fig. 4-43 takes it after phi'allow = atan(tan 35 deg / 1.5) = 25 deg, Kp 3.6) both print it beside a factor of safety on the passive side. FOS_passive divides the passive pressure, UFC Fig. 4-41 step 2's alternative to phi'allow. Must be >= 1.0. default: 1.2
anchor_depthfloatoptionalRequired when wall_type is anchored. Anchor depth below surface (m).
project_namestroptionalProject name for header. default: "Project"
project_numberstroptionalProject number for header.
engineerstroptionalEngineer name for header.
checkerstroptionalChecker name for header.
companystroptionalCompany name for header.
datestroptionalDate string (auto-filled if empty).
assumptionsdictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user did not give, as {input name: its basis}, e.g. {"unit_weight": "not given; typical of the soil described"}. An assumption that is not an input is its own row: {"drained": "long-term condition"}. The package lists them under Assumed Inputs with the analysis's own defaults, so no assumption reads as given. A misspelt input name is refused with a did-you-mean.
givenlist|dictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user gave, by the names you pass them under, e.g. ["width", "depth", "friction_angle"], or with the user's own words, {"friction_angle": "phi 32 deg from the boring logs"}. Only these print under Given Inputs. Every other input you pass prints under Assumed Inputs as passed, not stated as given (with its basis when it is in assumptions); left out, no input is the user's. A value you read off, worked out or chose is assumed, not given.
output_pathstroptionalFile path to save output. Auto-generated if omitted.
formatstroptionalOutput format: 'html' (recommended, self-contained with embedded CSS), 'latex' (raw .tex source), or 'pdf' (requires pdflatex installed). HTML is always available; PDF requires a LaTeX compiler on the system. allowed: html, latex, pdf default: "html"

soe_package — Run a support-of-excavation wall analysis (cantilever, braced/anchored at support levels, or FHWA apparent-pressure anchored wall) and generate its calc package: earth pressures, embedment, moments and the strut or anchor loads, with tables (CSV + printed) of pressure, shear and moment along the wall.

ParameterTypeDescription
wall_typestroptionalThe excavation wall to analyse and report: 'cantilever' (the cantilever_excavation tool), 'braced' (braced_excavation: struts, rakers or anchors at given support levels) or 'fhwa_anchored' (fhwa_apparent_pressure_anchored_wall). allowed: cantilever, braced, fhwa_anchored also read as: cantilever_excavation = cantilever, braced_excavation = braced, fhwa = fhwa_anchored, fhwa_apparent_pressure_anchored_wall = fhwa_anchored default: "cantilever"
excavation_depthfloatoptionalRequired when wall_type is cantilever or braced. Excavation depth (m).
layersarrayoptionalRequired when wall_type is cantilever or braced. wall_type=cantilever: Array of soil-layer dicts, top down: {thickness (m, required), unit_weight (kN/m3, required), friction_angle (deg, default 30), cohesion (kPa, default 0), soil_type (optional and not read here: the cantilever analysis uses each layer's own phi and c; accepted so the same layers serve braced_excavation)}. The last layer continues below its thickness. | wall_type=braced: Array of soil-layer dicts, top down: {thickness (m, required), unit_weight (kN/m3, required), friction_angle (deg, default 30), cohesion (kPa, default 0), soil_type ('sand' or 'clay', also 'soft_clay' or 'stiff_clay'; REQUIRED on each layer above the excavation base, refused if missing)}. soil_type picks the Terzaghi-Peck apparent-pressure envelope: the one for sands where sand is the thicker over the excavation depth, else the one for clays, soft to medium or stiff fissured by the average N = gamma*H/cu over the excavation depth (> 4 soft). The embedment below the excavation uses each layer's own phi and c. The last layer continues below its thickness.
surchargefloatoptionalDefault: cantilever 10.0; braced 10.0; fhwa_anchored 0.0 (wall_type). wall_type=cantilever: Surface surcharge (kPa). | wall_type=braced: Surface surcharge (kPa); added to the envelope as Ka*q (sand) or q (clay). | wall_type=fhwa_anchored: Uniform surface surcharge q (kPa); adds ps = Ka*q.
gwt_depthfloatoptionalwall_type=cantilever: Groundwater depth behind the wall (m). | wall_type=braced: Groundwater depth behind the wall (m); water pressure is added for sand envelopes.
gwt_depth_excavationfloatoptionalGroundwater depth on the excavation side (m from top of wall), never above the excavation base. Default: same as gwt_depth.
FOS_passivefloatoptionalwall_type=cantilever: FOS on passive resistance. | wall_type=braced: Embedment FS, MR = FS*MD about the lowest support (Caltrans uses 1.3). default: 1.5
embedment_increasefloatoptionalDefault: cantilever 1.2; braced 1.0 (wall_type). wall_type=cantilever: D / D0 (Caltrans/AASHTO 1.2; use 1.0 to carry all safety on FOS_passive). | wall_type=braced: Multiplier on the free-earth-support embedment.
passive_theorystroptionalThe passive coefficient below the excavation: 'rankine' (default) = Rankine's Kp, no wall friction, as the Caltrans Trenching and Shoring Manual's examples take it where the wall friction is zero (pp. 7-18, 7-27), with its note that Rankine 'tends to underestimate the passive earth pressure' and Sec. 4-6 (p. 4-28): Rankine 'should not be used ... because it does not account for wall friction'; 'log_spiral' (or 'caquot_kerisel', the same) = the log-spiral Kp of log_spiral_source at passive_wall_friction_deg in each layer below the excavation. Choices give the other theory's Kp and embedment. allowed: rankine, log_spiral, caquot_kerisel also read as: logspiral = log_spiral, log-spiral = log_spiral default: "rankine"
log_spiral_sourcestroptionalWith passive_theory 'log_spiral', the printed source of Kp, as earth_pressure_coefficient takes it: 'ufc_3_220_20' (default) = UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 4-12 (p. 191), its log-spiral Kp for a vertical face and level ground at any wall friction; 'caquot_kerisel_1948' = the Caltrans Trenching and Shoring Manual Fig. 4-20 chart (its Example 8-1), and 'dm7_2_eq_4_12' = UFC Eq. 4-12 by name, both needing passive_wall_friction_deg given; 'dm7_2_fig_4_12' / 'dm7_2_fig_4_13' = UFC's charts, drawn for delta/phi' 0.66 only. allowed: ufc_3_220_20, caquot_kerisel_1948, dm7_2_eq_4_12, dm7_2_fig_4_12, dm7_2_fig_4_13 default: "ufc_3_220_20"
passive_wall_friction_degfloatoptionalWith passive_theory 'log_spiral', the wall friction delta (deg) in every layer below the excavation, at most its phi': the engineer's call (UFC 3-220-20 Table 4-1, p. 184; Caltrans Example 8-1 takes 15 deg on phi 30). Left out: delta/phi' = 0.66 (UFC p. 191, 'a common assumption') in a layer without cohesion, none in a layer with cohesion (UFC Fig. 4-37 step 1, p. 237: 'Passive pressures for clean coarse grained soils include wall friction'; in other soils it ignores wall friction); refused with 'caquot_kerisel_1948' or 'dm7_2_eq_4_12', which need it given (Caltrans p. 4-29: 'Given delta'). For soldier piles in coarse-grained soil UFC p. 249 takes KP 'without wall friction': give 0.
FyfloatoptionalSteel yield strength (MPa) for section sizing. default: 345.0
Fb_ratiofloatoptionalAllowable bending stress / Fy for the required section: 0.60 (default) as the Caltrans Trenching and Shoring Manual's examples take it (Example 7-3, p. 7-43; Example 8-1); GEC-4 (p. 81) recommends 0.55 for permanent walls and temporary walls that are critical; 0.66 the Caltrans railroad example (p. 9-20). Choices give the section at each. default: 0.6
supportsarrayoptionalSupport levels [{depth (m), support_type ('strut' or 'anchor'), spacing (m), angle_deg}].
support_load_methodstroptionalHow the support loads and span moments are taken: 'hinge' (default) = the Caltrans Trenching and Shoring Manual's hinge method (Sec. 8-4.02, Fig. 8-7, p. 8-10; Example 8-2): the load above the first support to it, its moment M1 there carried by the span below (T1L = P/2 + M1/L, T2U = P/2 - M1/L), simple spans between supports, and the lowest support's load from below by free earth support about it (FS = 1; one support: the whole wall about it); 'hinge_subgrade' = GEC-4's hinge method (Fig. 38, p. 79): the same above, simple spans down to the excavation base, which takes a subgrade reaction R; 'simple_spans' = UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-54 (p. 257): simple spans between supports, the span below the lowest support a cantilever on it (UFC's 80 % moment reduction not applied). Choices give the other methods' loads. allowed: hinge, hinge_subgrade, simple_spans default: "hinge"
stiff_clay_coefficientfloatoptionalThe stiff clay envelope's ordinate as a multiple of gamma H, 0.2 to 0.4: 0.4 (default) per UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-53 (p. 256, internally supported walls, N0 <= 4); 0.2 'when movements are minimal and the construction period is short' (UFC); the Caltrans Trenching and Shoring Manual (Eq. 8-3-2, p. 8-5) leaves it between 0.2 and 0.4 to judgment. Read for stiff fissured clay (N <= 4) and, for 4 < N < 6, as the ordinate soft clay must reach (Caltrans Sec. 8-3.02: the larger of the two). default: 0.4
HfloatoptionalRequired when wall_type is fhwa_anchored. Total wall height (m).
anchor_depthsarrayoptionalRequired when wall_type is fhwa_anchored. Depths of the anchor levels below the top of wall (m), e.g. [2.5, 6.25].
gammafloatoptionalRequired when wall_type is fhwa_anchored. Retained-soil unit weight (kN/m3).
phifloatoptionalRequired when wall_type is fhwa_anchored. Retained-soil friction angle (deg).
spacingfloatoptionalHorizontal anchor spacing (m) for the design loads. default: 1.0
inclination_degfloatoptionalAnchor inclination from horizontal (deg). default: 0.0
KafloatoptionalActive coefficient override (default Rankine Ka).
KpfloatoptionalPassive coefficient below the excavation, for the embedment (default Rankine; pass a log-spiral value).
FOS_embedmentfloatoptionalEmbedment FS, MR = FS*MD about the anchor, the lowest with two or more (Caltrans T&S Manual Secs. 8-4.01 and 8-4.02). default: 1.3
project_namestroptionalProject name for header. default: "Project"
project_numberstroptionalProject number for header.
engineerstroptionalEngineer name for header.
checkerstroptionalChecker name for header.
companystroptionalCompany name for header.
datestroptionalDate string (auto-filled if empty).
assumptionsdictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user did not give, as {input name: its basis}, e.g. {"unit_weight": "not given; typical of the soil described"}. An assumption that is not an input is its own row: {"drained": "long-term condition"}. The package lists them under Assumed Inputs with the analysis's own defaults, so no assumption reads as given. A misspelt input name is refused with a did-you-mean.
givenlist|dictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user gave, by the names you pass them under, e.g. ["width", "depth", "friction_angle"], or with the user's own words, {"friction_angle": "phi 32 deg from the boring logs"}. Only these print under Given Inputs. Every other input you pass prints under Assumed Inputs as passed, not stated as given (with its basis when it is in assumptions); left out, no input is the user's. A value you read off, worked out or chose is assumed, not given.
output_pathstroptionalFile path to save output. Auto-generated if omitted.
formatstroptionalOutput format: 'html' (recommended, self-contained with embedded CSS), 'latex' (raw .tex source), or 'pdf' (requires pdflatex installed). HTML is always available; PDF requires a LaTeX compiler on the system. allowed: html, latex, pdf default: "html"

reliability_package — Run a reliability analysis (FOSM, point estimates, Monte Carlo or FORM) on a performance function of random variables and generate its calc package: the variables and their distributions, the moments of g, the reliability index beta and the probability of failure, and which variable matters.

ParameterTypeDescription
enginestroptionalWhich reliability engine to run and report: 'fosm' (Taylor series), 'pem' (Rosenblueth point estimates), 'monte_carlo' or 'form' (the tool of that name). allowed: fosm, pem, monte_carlo, form also read as: mc = monte_carlo, monte carlo = monte_carlo, taylor = fosm default: "fosm"
variablesobjectrequiredRandom variables: {name: {mean, cov or std, dist, lower, upper}}. dist one of ['normal', 'lognormal', 'uniform', 'triangular'] (default normal). lower/upper truncate normal/lognormal or bound uniform/triangular. Example: {'su': {'mean': 50, 'cov': 0.3, 'dist': 'lognormal'}}.
g_expressionstrrequiredPerformance function of the variable names. With convention='fos' write a FACTOR OF SAFETY (failure at g<1), e.g. 'R/S'; with 'margin' a margin (failure at g<0), e.g. 'R - S'. Math functions allowed (sqrt, log, exp, tan, radians, ...).
conventionstroptional'fos': g is a factor of safety (failure g<1, lognormal beta reported). 'margin': g = R-S (failure g<0). allowed: fos, margin default: "fos"
correlationobjectoptionalPairwise correlations {'a,b': rho} or full matrix [[...]] in variable order. Omit for independent variables.
schemestroptional'full' = 2^n points; 'multiplicative' = Rosenblueth 2n+1 (uncorrelated only). allowed: full, multiplicative default: "full"
nintoptionalRealizations. Aim n >= 10/pf. default: 10000
seedintoptionalRNG seed for reproducibility.
samplingstroptional'lhs' = Latin Hypercube (variance reduction). allowed: random, lhs default: "random"
n_binsintoptionalHistogram bins. default: 30
max_iterationsintoptionalHL-RF iteration cap. default: 100
project_namestroptionalProject name for header. default: "Project"
project_numberstroptionalProject number for header.
engineerstroptionalEngineer name for header.
checkerstroptionalChecker name for header.
companystroptionalCompany name for header.
datestroptionalDate string (auto-filled if empty).
assumptionsdictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user did not give, as {input name: its basis}, e.g. {"unit_weight": "not given; typical of the soil described"}. An assumption that is not an input is its own row: {"drained": "long-term condition"}. The package lists them under Assumed Inputs with the analysis's own defaults, so no assumption reads as given. A misspelt input name is refused with a did-you-mean.
givenlist|dictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user gave, by the names you pass them under, e.g. ["width", "depth", "friction_angle"], or with the user's own words, {"friction_angle": "phi 32 deg from the boring logs"}. Only these print under Given Inputs. Every other input you pass prints under Assumed Inputs as passed, not stated as given (with its basis when it is in assumptions); left out, no input is the user's. A value you read off, worked out or chose is assumed, not given.
output_pathstroptionalFile path to save output. Auto-generated if omitted.
formatstroptionalOutput format: 'html' (recommended, self-contained with embedded CSS), 'latex' (raw .tex source), or 'pdf' (requires pdflatex installed). HTML is always available; PDF requires a LaTeX compiler on the system. allowed: html, latex, pdf default: "html"

10.1.33 drawing_ir — drawing_ir

digitize_drawing — Digitize a drawing (DXF / PDF-vector / raster image) into a unified intermediate representation. Caches the IR server-side under a 'handle' and returns a summary + stats (counts by type/layer, page metadata, extent, scale). Then use query_drawing / get_entities — the full IR is never returned by default.

ParameterTypeDescription
file_pathstrrequiredPath to the drawing file (.dxf, .pdf, or a raster image).
sourcestroptionalIngest leg. 'auto' picks by file extension. allowed: auto, dxf, pdf_vector, raster default: "auto"
pageintoptionalPDF page (0-indexed); pdf_vector only. default: 0
scalefloatoptionalModel units per page/drawing unit (m per PDF point, or m per pixel for raster). Promotes coordinates to model space (meters). Omit to stay in page/pixel units.
unitsstroptionalDXF drawing units override (default: the DXF $INSUNITS header, else meters). dxf only. allowed: m, mm, cm, ft, in
explode_blocksbooloptionalDXF only: explode block references (INSERTs) into IR primitives tagged style='block:<NAME>'. Default true — most annotation line-work on a real sheet is stamped from blocks and is otherwise invisible (n_block_entities reports how many entities came from blocks). Set false to see ONLY geometry drawn directly in model space, e.g. when a stamped title-block border outranks the section line-work you asked about. default: true
originstroptionalY-orientation for PDF/raster (bottom_left = engineering up-positive). allowed: bottom_left, top_left default: "bottom_left"
calibrationdictoptionalTwo-point PDF scale calibration {p1:[x,y], p2:[x,y], distance_m}. Alternative to scale.
detect_linesbooloptionalRaster: detect straight segments (Hough). default: true
detect_circlesbooloptionalRaster: detect circles (Hough gradient). default: true
detect_contoursbooloptionalRaster: trace closed shapes (contours). May overlap Hough lines on line-work. default: true
ocrbooloptionalRaster: attempt OCR text (needs pytesseract + Tesseract; skipped with a warning if absent). default: true
ocr_textbooloptionalPDF only: additionally OCR the rendered page and merge recognized text into the IR as confidence<1 text entities (source='ocr'). THE way to read SHX/stroked-lettering sheets (has_text=false) — needs planlens[ocr] (RapidOCR; auto-detects sideways plots). Adds seconds to a-minute-ish per page. SKIPPED, with a reason in the result, when the page already carries vector text: that text is exact and OCR could only add noisier copies. Check has_text/n_text in the summary first. default: false
ocr_forcebooloptionalRun the OCR pass even though the page already has a text layer (e.g. a sheet that is part vector text, part scanned inset). Expensive: a large sheet is a many-megapixel render, so prefer snipping the region and OCRing that. default: false

query_drawing — Request a SLICE of a cached drawing IR by handle. Returns compact entity references (id + small summary), not full coordinate dumps — follow up with get_entities for exact coordinates of a shortlist.

ParameterTypeDescription
handlestrrequiredHandle from digitize_drawing.
querystrrequiredWhich slice to compute. allowed: candidate_ground_surface, entities_by_color, entities_ending_near, entities_in_bbox, entities_on_layer, find_bubble_callouts, find_dimensions, find_leaders, find_revision_clouds, find_title_block, horizontal_lines, lines_by_angle, nearest_entity, polylines_longer_than, summary_stats, text_anchored_geometry, text_items, text_near, vertical_lines
paramsdictoptionalQuery params. entities_in_bbox: {x_min,y_min,x_max,y_max,mode?,entity_type?}; nearest_entity: {x,y,entity_type?,k?}; lines_by_angle: {min_deg,max_deg}; horizontal_lines/vertical_lines: {tol_deg?}; polylines_longer_than: {min_length}; text_items: {pattern?}; text_near: {entity_id,radius}; entities_ending_near: {x,y,radius,entity_types?} (what TERMINATES at a point — arrow tips, callout tails); text_anchored_geometry: {pattern,radius?,entity_types?} (find text X -> geometry ending at it -> the far point it points at; pattern is any runtime string); find_leaders: {min_confidence?,exclude_dimensions?,...}; find_dimensions/find_title_block/find_bubble_callouts/find_revision_clouds: {min_confidence?,...} (annotation-construct PROPOSALS with confidence + evidence — never asserted facts; confirm visually). On no-text-layer (SHX-stroked) sheets find_dimensions detects real plotted dims (split-shaft + continuous legs, 16/16 native defpoints on validation sheets; ends = arrow apexes) but some high-confidence hits may be other line-plus-arrows constructs — verify via snip_region before reporting values; entities_on_layer: {layer}; entities_by_color: {color}; candidate_ground_surface: {} — widest-horizontal-extent PROPOSAL; on a DXF digitized with the default explode_blocks=true it ranks over stamped block line-work too, so a title-block border can out-rank the drawn section surface (the reply echoes n_block_entities when the IR has any) — re-digitize with explode_blocks=false to rank over only directly drawn model-space work; summary_stats: {}.

get_entities — Fetch full, exact coordinates for specific entity ids from a cached drawing IR (the deterministic coordinates the LLM should trust over its own pixel reading).

ParameterTypeDescription
handlestrrequiredHandle from digitize_drawing.
idsarrayrequiredEntity ids to retrieve (e.g. ['e0','e5']).

snip_region — Render a zoomed-in crop of a PDF drawing page to a PNG file — the 'geometry says WHERE, vision says WHAT' primitive. Feed exact coordinates from query_drawing (e.g. a leader's tip_xy, a title block's region_bbox), then analyze the saved PNG with analyze_image (or use the one-step render_region tool).

ParameterTypeDescription
file_pathstrrequiredPath to the source PDF.
output_pathstrrequiredWhere to save the PNG crop.
pageintoptionalPDF page (0-indexed). default: 0
bboxarrayoptional[x0,y0,x1,y1] region of interest. Omit for the full page.
framestroptionalCoordinate frame of bbox/marks: 'ir' (bottom-left origin, y up — what digitize_drawing/query_drawing return, the default) or 'pdf' (top-left points, y down). allowed: ir, pdf default: "ir"
scalefloatoptionalModel units per PDF point, ONLY if the drawing was digitized with a scale (model-space IR coords are divided by this before the flip).
dpiintoptionalRender resolution. default: 300
pad_fracfloatoptionalFractional padding around bbox. default: 0.15
marksarrayoptional[[x,y,label], ...] numbered marker circles drawn at points of interest (set-of-marks: 'what is mark 1 pointing at?'). Same frame as bbox.

search_drawing_set — Search EVERY page of one or more drawing files (PDF/DXF) in one call: count/locate text matches ('how many times does X occur in this set') or annotation constructs (leaders, dimensions, title_block, bubble_callouts, revision_clouds — confidence-scored proposals). Returns per-file, per-page counts + compact match locations. Digitized pages are cached across calls (first pass on a dense sheet can take seconds).

ParameterTypeDescription
file_pathsarrayrequiredOne path or a list of paths (.pdf or .dxf).
patternstroptionalText to find (regex, else literal substring; case-insensitive). Any runtime string. With 'construct', filters constructs by their text (title blocks: matched against all contained text; revision clouds carry no text and never match a pattern). NOTE: sheets plotted with SHX/stroked lettering have NO text layer — such pages are flagged no_text_layer and a zero count is inconclusive; pass ocr_text=true to read them optically.
ocr_textbooloptionalOCR pages that have no text layer before the pattern search (planlens[ocr]; adds seconds per no-text page, cached across calls). default: false
constructstroptionalAnnotation construct to search for instead of (or as well as) raw text. allowed: leaders, dimensions, title_block, bubble_callouts, revision_clouds
pagesarrayoptionalPage numbers (0-indexed) to search; omit for ALL pages of each file.
min_confidencefloatoptionalConstruct proposals below this are dropped. default: 0.5

10.1.34 pavement_design — pavement_design

flexible_pavement_design — AASHTO 1993 flexible pavement design (Fig 3.1/3.2): required SN + layered D1/D2/D3 split with drainage m, Sec 3.1.4 minimums and forward check; or adequacy check of a given section. US customary units.

ParameterTypeDescription
w18numberrequiredDesign-lane 18-kip ESALs over the performance period (use design_traffic_esals to build it).
layersarrayrequiredList of layer dicts, TOP-DOWN; first must be layer_type 'asphalt'. Each: {layer_type: asphalt|granular_base|granular_subbase|cement_treated_base|bituminous_treated_base; modulus_psi (EAC/EBS/ESB -- required on granular layers below the surface in design mode); ucs_7day_psi (cement-treated, Fig 2.8 scale 200-1000 psi); marshall_stability_lb (bituminous-treated, Fig 2.9 scale 200-1800 lb); a (direct coefficient override); m (drainage, unbound layers) or drainage_quality + pct_saturation_time ('<1%'|'1-5%'|'5-25%'|'>25%'); thickness_in (set on EVERY layer for a check instead of a design); min_thickness_in (over a layer stiffer than 40,000 psi, e.g. a treated base, no SN is solved (II-37) and the layer above takes this or the Sec 3.1.4 minimum)}.
reliability_pctnumberoptionalReliability R % (50-99.99), Table 4.1 -> ZR. Or give zr.
zrnumberoptionalStandard normal deviate directly (overrides reliability_pct).
sonumberoptionalOverall standard deviation (flexible range 0.40-0.50). default: 0.45
mr_psinumberoptionalEffective roadbed resilient modulus, psi (or monthly_mr_psi).
monthly_mr_psiarrayoptionalSeasonal roadbed MR list (psi) -> Fig 2.3/2.4 effective MR.
ptnumberoptionalTerminal serviceability. default: 2.5
ponumberoptionalInitial serviceability. default: 4.2
delta_psinumberoptionalServiceability loss directly (else po - pt).
thickness_increment_innumberoptionalRound-UP increment. default: 0.5
enforce_minimumsbooleanoptionalApply Sec 3.1.4 minimum AC/base thicknesses. default: true
swellingobjectoptionalRoadbed swelling spec (Appendix G / Fig G.4): {vr_in: potential vertical rise (in), ps_pct: percent of area subject to swell, theta: swell rate constant (~0.04-0.20)}. Requires design_period_yr.
frostobjectoptionalFrost heave spec (Appendix G / Fig G.8): {phi_mm_day: heave rate, pf_pct: percent of area subject to heave, delta_psi_max: max loss (Fig G.7, from drainage quality x frost depth)}. Requires design_period_yr.
design_period_yrnumberoptionalAnalysis period (yr); required with swelling/frost -- their dPSI loss is subtracted from the design budget before the solve.

rigid_pavement_design — AASHTO 1993 rigid (PCC slab) design (Fig 3.7): required slab thickness D with k from direct value, MR/19.4, or the full Sec 3.2 composite-k worksheet (iterated with D); or adequacy check. US customary units.

ParameterTypeDescription
w18numberrequiredDesign-lane 18-kip ESALs.
sc_psinumberrequiredPCC modulus of rupture (28-day, third-point), psi.
ec_psinumberrequiredPCC elastic modulus, psi.
reliability_pctnumberoptionalReliability R % -> ZR (or give zr).
zrnumberoptionalStandard normal deviate directly.
sonumberoptionalOverall standard deviation (rigid 0.30-0.40). default: 0.35
ptnumberoptionalTerminal serviceability (also in the strength-term exponent). default: 2.5
ponumberoptionalInitial serviceability. default: 4.5
delta_psinumberoptionalServiceability loss directly.
jnumberoptionalLoad transfer coefficient J directly (else Table 2.6 midpoint from pavement_type/shoulder_type/load_transfer_devices).
pavement_typestringoptionalFor the Table 2.6 J lookup. allowed: plain_jointed_jrcp, crcp default: "plain_jointed_jrcp"
shoulder_typestringoptionalFor the Table 2.6 J lookup. allowed: asphalt, tied_pcc default: "asphalt"
load_transfer_devicesbooleanoptionalDowels present. default: true
cdnumberoptionalDrainage coefficient directly (else Table 2.5 midpoint from drainage_quality). default: 1.0
drainage_qualitystringoptionalFor the Table 2.5 Cd lookup. allowed: excellent, good, fair, poor, very_poor
pct_saturation_timestringoptionalMoisture exposure for the Cd lookup. allowed: <1%, 1-5%, 5-25%, >25%
k_pcinumberoptionalEffective modulus of subgrade reaction directly, pci. Give exactly one of k_pci / mr_psi / composite_k.
mr_psinumberoptionalRoadbed MR, psi -> simplified k = MR/19.4 (no subbase).
composite_kobjectoptionalSec 3.2 worksheet spec: {seasonal: [{mr_psi, ...}], dsb_in, esb_psi, dsg_ft, ls}; slab_d_in is iterated automatically. Fig 3.3 is read off the printed chart: dsb_in 6-18, esb_psi 15,000-1,000,000, mr_psi 1,000-20,000.
slab_thickness_innumberoptionalGive to CHECK a slab instead of designing.
thickness_increment_innumberoptionalRound-UP increment. default: 0.5
swellingobjectoptionalRoadbed swelling spec (Appendix G / Fig G.4): {vr_in: potential vertical rise (in), ps_pct: percent of area subject to swell, theta: swell rate constant (~0.04-0.20)}. Requires design_period_yr.
frostobjectoptionalFrost heave spec (Appendix G / Fig G.8): {phi_mm_day: heave rate, pf_pct: percent of area subject to heave, delta_psi_max: max loss (Fig G.7, from drainage quality x frost depth)}. Requires design_period_yr.
design_period_yrnumberoptionalAnalysis period (yr); required with swelling/frost -- their dPSI loss is subtracted from the design budget before the solve.

design_traffic_esals — Design-lane cumulative 18-kip ESALs: axle-load spectrum (Appendix D LEFs, single/tandem/triple), per-vehicle truck factors, or a base-year total; compound growth + directional DD + lane DL.

ParameterTypeDescription
axle_groupsarrayoptional[{axle_config: single|tandem|triple, load_kips, daily_count (two-way)}]; LEFs at the assumed sn/d_in/pt.
vehiclesarrayoptional[{description, daily_count, truck_factor (ESALs/pass)}].
base_year_w18_two_waynumberoptionalFirst-year two-way ESALs directly.
growth_rate_pctnumberoptionalAnnual growth rate %. default: 0
design_period_yrnumberoptionalPerformance period, yr. default: 20
pavement_typestringoptionalFor LEF selection. allowed: flexible, rigid default: "flexible"
snnumberoptionalAssumed SN for flexible LEFs. default: 5.0
d_innumberoptionalAssumed slab D for rigid LEFs. default: 9.0
ptnumberoptionalTerminal serviceability for LEFs. default: 2.5
directional_factornumberoptionalDD split (0.3-0.7). default: 0.5
num_lanes_per_directionintegeroptionalFor the DL table. default: 2
lane_factornumberoptionalDL fraction directly (else table midpoint).

effective_subgrade_modulus — Effective roadbed resilient modulus from seasonal (monthly) MR values via the Fig 2.3/2.4 relative-damage average (flexible design input).

ParameterTypeDescription
monthly_mr_psiarrayrequiredSeasonal roadbed MR values, psi (typically 12).

flexible_pavement_design_ufc — UFC 3-250-01 (DoD roads/parking) flexible design — the CBR-method ALTERNATIVE to AASHTO: Figure E-1 cover curves, Table 7-2 minimums, optional seasonal-frost reduced-subgrade-strength check. US customary.

ParameterTypeDescription
passes_18kipnumberrequiredDesign-life passes of the 18-kip single axle (design lane), 10 to 10,000,000 (the range Figure E-1 prints). NOT interchangeable with AASHTO W18 conceptually — same count, different damage model.
cbr_subgradenumberrequiredSubgrade design CBR (%), 1 or more.
cbr_basenumberoptionalBase course design CBR. default: 80
cbr_subbasenumberoptionalSubbase CBR (omit for a 2-layer section). A subbase is at least 4 in (UFC p. 20).
frostobjectoptional{uscs_class, finer_than_0_02mm_pct, frost_group} -> Ch 19 reduced-subgrade-strength frost check; governing section reported. frost_group (optional): the group a laboratory frost test set (Table 19-2 footnote ***); a soil Table 19-2 does not list is refused without it.
thickness_increment_innumberoptionalRound layer thicknesses up to this increment (in). default: 0.5

rigid_pavement_design_ufc — UFC 3-250-01 rigid (plain concrete) design — Figure F-1 (flexural strength x k x 18-kip passes) with the Eq 13-1 stabilized-foundation reduction. US customary.

ParameterTypeDescription
passes_18kipnumberrequired18-kip single-axle passes, 1,000 to 50,000,000 (Figure F-1's pass-level lines).
flexural_strength_psinumberrequiredConcrete 28-day flexural strength R (psi), 100-1,000. For a parking area para 13-3 enters R / 0.75.
k_pcinumberoptionalModulus of subgrade reaction, 25 pci or more; above 500 taken as 500 (Table 10-1 note 2). Or give subgrade for Table 10-1.
subgradeobjectoptional{uscs_group, moisture_pct} -> Table 10-1 k.
stabilized_foundationobjectoptional{ef_psi, hs_in} -> Eq 13-1 reduction.
thickness_increment_innumberoptionalRound the slab up to this increment (in). default: 0.5

compare_pavement_methods — Run AASHTO 1993 AND UFC 3-250-01 flexible designs on a shared 18-kip pass count and compare sections side by side, with every cross-guide assumption (CBR<->Mr correlation, AASHTO-only reliability) stated in notes.

ParameterTypeDescription
passes_18kipnumberrequired18-kip single-axle passes (= AASHTO W18; LEF 1.0 by definition).
cbr_subgradenumberoptionalSubgrade CBR (Mr derived via FHWA 2555*CBR^0.64). Give this OR mr_psi.
mr_psinumberoptionalSubgrade Mr (CBR derived by inversion).
reliability_pctnumberoptionalAASHTO-side reliability. default: 95
sonumberoptionalAASHTO overall standard deviation. default: 0.45
ptnumberoptionalAASHTO terminal serviceability. default: 2.5
cbr_basenumberoptionalBase CBR (both sides; AASHTO EBS read across the guide's Figure 2.6, CBR 20-100, unless ebs_psi given). default: 80
cbr_subbasenumberoptionalSubbase CBR (both sides; AASHTO ESB read across Figure 2.7, CBR about 9-100, unless esb_psi given). default: 30
eac_psinumberoptionalAASHTO asphalt modulus. default: 400000
ebs_psinumberoptionalAASHTO base modulus override.
esb_psinumberoptionalAASHTO subbase modulus override.

mixed_traffic_ufc — UFC 3-250-01 automated mixed-traffic reduction (Table G-1 procedure): per-vehicle thickness from the Appendix E curves at a representative CBR, controlling vehicle, allowable-passes inversion, equivalent-pass roll-up. Feeds flexible_pavement_design_ufc.

ParameterTypeDescription
vehiclesarrayrequired[{vehicle: E-1 (18-kip ESAL) or E-2..E-31 / registry slug, design_passes, name?}].
representative_cbrnumberrequiredTable 4-1 category CBR for the equivalency step (NOT the site CBR).

performance_period — Predicted performance period of a DESIGNED section under roadbed swelling / frost heave (the guide's Table 3.1 iteration): environmental dPSI shrinks the traffic budget until trial period and traffic-derived period converge.

ParameterTypeDescription
pavement_typestringrequiredWhich design equation gives the section's W18 capacity. allowed: flexible, rigid
delta_psi_designnumberrequiredTotal design dPSI (po - pt).
base_year_w18numberrequiredFirst-year design-lane ESALs.
growth_rate_pctnumberoptionalAnnual traffic growth %. default: 0
swellingobjectoptionalRoadbed swelling spec (Appendix G / Fig G.4): {vr_in: potential vertical rise (in), ps_pct: percent of area subject to swell, theta: swell rate constant (~0.04-0.20)}. Requires design_period_yr.
frostobjectoptionalFrost heave spec (Appendix G / Fig G.8): {phi_mm_day: heave rate, pf_pct: percent of area subject to heave, delta_psi_max: max loss (Fig G.7, from drainage quality x frost depth)}. Requires design_period_yr.
max_performance_period_yrnumberoptionalCap / default trial seed. default: 20
initial_trial_yrnumberoptionalFirst trial performance period (yr); default 0.9 x the cap.
snnumberoptionalFlexible: as-built structural number.

ec_psinumberoptionalRigid: PCC elastic modulus.
jnumberoptionalRigid: load transfer J.
cdnumberoptionalRigid: drainage Cd.
k_pcinumberoptionalRigid: design k.

10.1.35 profile_figure — profile_figure

subsurface_profile — Draw a subsurface profile schematic (PNG): soil layers with names/descriptions, water table, optional fill + surcharge, optional pile/micropile/drilled-shaft/footing/wall overlay, and callouts (e.g. neutral plane) at any elevation or depth. Saves the file and returns an <img> tag ready for a report.

ParameterTypeDescription
layersarrayrequiredStrata TOP-DOWN. Each dict: 'name' plus 'thickness' (m) — or a 'top_elevation'/'bottom_elevation' (or 'top_depth'/'bottom_depth') pair. Optional: 'description' (short properties string shown under the name, e.g. 'su = 25 kPa, N=8'), 'settling' (true marks a compressible layer with down-arrows — use it for downdrag/consolidation figures), 'color', 'hatch'. Layers must stack continuously; a gap or overlap is an error.
titlestroptionalFigure title (name the project/boring). default: "Subsurface Profile"
ground_elevationfloatoptionalOriginal ground surface (m). Defaults to the first layer's top_elevation, else 0.0 — with thickness-only layers the axis then reads as depth below ground.
water_elevationfloatoptionalWater-table elevation (m).
water_depthfloatoptionalWater-table depth below ground (m). Alternative to water_elevation.
fillobjectoptionalFill/embankment ABOVE existing grade: {'name', 'thickness'} (or 'top_elevation'), optional 'settling'. A bare number is read as a thickness.
surchargeobjectoptionalSurface surcharge drawn as load arrows: {'pressure': kPa, 'label'} — a bare number is the pressure.
foundationobjectoptionalFoundation overlay: {'type': 'pile'|'micropile'|'drilled_shaft'|'footing'|'wall', 'diameter' (or 'width' for a footing), 'tip_elevation' or 'tip_depth' or 'length', optional 'head_elevation'/'head_depth' (defaults to the top of the section), optional 'label'}. Drawn to true DEPTH; its width is exaggerated so it is visible, with the real dimension in the label.
annotationsarrayoptionalCallouts: [{'elevation' or 'depth', 'text', 'side': 'left'|'right'}] — the neutral plane, a sample depth, top of rock, a design assumption. Drawn as a dashed line across the section with a labelled leader.
axisstroptionalVertical-axis labelling. 'auto' = depth for thickness-only input, elevation once any elevation is given. Presentation only — geometry is unchanged. allowed: auto, elevation, depth default: "auto"
output_pathstroptionalPNG path. A bare filename lands in the working folder. Auto-generated if omitted.
dpiintoptionalRaster resolution; 150 suits a report page. default: 150
width_infloatoptionalFigure width (inches). default: 6.5
height_infloatoptionalFigure height (inches). default: 8.0
include_base64booloptionalAlso return the PNG as base64. Rarely needed and VERY large (tens of thousands of characters) — html_to_pdf embeds a local PNG path for you, so leave this off. default: false

plot_data — Generic data plot: one or more x/y series — an SPT or CPT profile against elevation, settlement vs time, load vs displacement, a parameter sweep or method comparison, the cases of a sensitivity study, a plan view of borings and a footprint drawn to scale. Shows in chat as an INTERACTIVE chart (zoom/hover) and saves a PNG for reports, with an <img> tag ready to paste.

ParameterTypeDescription
seriesarrayrequired[{'x': [...], 'y': [...], 'label': str, optional 'style': 'both'|'line'|'markers'|'step'|'polygon', 'color'}]. x and y are equal-length lists. Optional per series: 'marker' (circle, square, triangle, triangle-down, diamond, x, cross, star, hexagon), 'marker_size' (points), 'marker_edge' (outline colour), 'marker_open' (hollow), 'line_dash' (solid, dash, dot, dashdot), 'line_width', 'labels' (one name per point, written beside it, '' to skip one), 'hover' (one text per point, shown on hover in the interactive chart; '
' breaks a line), 'in_legend' (false hides it). Style 'polygon' closes the outline (a footprint, a site boundary, a zone); 'fill': true or a colour, 'fill_opacity' (default 0.2), 'hatch' ('/', '\', 'x', '-', '|', '+', '.') to mark a zone over what lies under it. x given as names (cases, scenarios, borings) puts them along the x axis in order: draw separate cases with style 'markers', since a line between unrelated cases shows a trend that is not there. Name points on the figure with 'labels' rather than a legend entry each.
annotationsarrayoptionalText placed where you put it: a note, the name of a zone or a line, a reading at a point. It is never moved (point names keep clear of it). [{'text', 'x', 'y'}] in data units (a case's name for x on a case axis), or with 'coords': 'axes' in fractions of the plot (0, 0 bottom left; 1, 1 top right). Optional: 'point': [x, y] in data units, the point the note marks, drawn as a leader arrow from the text; 'align': the side of the text that stands at x, y (center, left, right, top, bottom, or e.g. 'top left'); 'box': true for a plain white box behind the text (or a colour); 'halo': true for a thin ring of the background round the letters, so hatching or a grid behind them stops short (the PNG); 'color'; 'font_size' (pt). A new line or '
' breaks a line. The warnings say when a note overlaps other lettering, a line runs through it or it stands outside the plot.
equal_aspectbooloptionalDraw one unit across as long as one unit up: set it for every plan view, site map, footprint or section drawn to scale (x and y both lengths in the same unit). The figure takes the data's own proportions and the legend moves outside the map. default: false
plan_viewbooloptionalDraw a site plan as a drawing, not a chart: to scale, no axes, axis numbers or grid, a scale bar with xlabel (name the coordinate system there) under it, and a north arrow from north_deg. Use it for a plan of a site, compound or property; draw the property line as a polygon with line_dash 'dashdot'. default: false
north_degfloatoptionalDirection of north on the page, degrees clockwise from straight up, as the plan the data came from (or the project's other plans) shows it. Not given: drawn straight up, and the result says so.
scale_unitsstroptionalLength unit written on the scale bar: m, km, cm, mm, ft, in, yd, mi. default: "m"
xlimarrayoptional[start, end] of the x axis, kept in the order given: [100, 0.001] runs it from high to low (on a log axis too). Else fitted.
ylimarrayoptional[start, end] of the y axis, kept in the order given (with depth_axis, y runs downward whatever the order). Else fitted.
x_on_topbooloptionalPut the x axis along the top, as a boring log reads, on a profile against elevation (depth_axis does this by itself). default: false
legend_positionstroptionalWhere the legend goes; auto = outside a drawing to scale, inside otherwise. allowed: auto, inside, outside, below default: "auto"
titlestroptionalFigure title.
xlabelstroptionalX-axis label WITH units.
ylabelstroptionalY-axis label WITH units.
depth_axisbooloptionalA profile has elevation on y by default (leave this false, y = elevations): borings start at different ground levels. True when y is depth (only when no elevations are given; say so in ylabel) or settlement: y increases DOWNWARD and the x axis sits at the top (boring-log convention). default: false
logxbooloptionalLog-scale x axis. default: false
logybooloptionalLog-scale y axis. default: false
hlinesarrayoptionalHorizontal reference lines: [{'value': y, 'label': str}] — e.g. a water table or an allowable value.
vlinesarrayoptionalVertical reference lines: [{'value': x, 'label': str}].
gridbooloptionalDraw a light grid. default: true
legendbooloptionalShow the legend. Default: when more than one series is in it (reference lines are named on the line).
output_pathstroptionalPNG path. A bare filename lands in the working folder. Auto-generated if omitted.
interactivebooloptionalAlso write the interactive chart beside the PNG (<name>.plotly.json) — that is what the chat displays. Set false only when a static image is all you want. default: true
dpiintoptionalRaster resolution. default: 150
width_infloatoptionalFigure width (inches). default: 6.5
height_infloatoptionalFigure height (inches). Default 4.5, or the data's proportions with equal_aspect.
include_base64booloptionalAlso return the PNG as base64 — VERY large; html_to_pdf embeds the saved path for you, so leave this off. default: false
reference_chartstroptionalA standard chart's lines drawn under the data as the reference prints them, not from memory: 'uscs_plasticity' (the plasticity chart, UFS 3-220-10 Figure 1-2 as in ASTM D2487: the A-line, level at PI = 4 up to LL = 25.5 and then PI = 0.73(LL - 20); the U-line; LL = 50; PI = LL; the CL-ML zone, hatched as GEC 5 Figure 4-11 prints it; the zone names), 'aashto_plasticity' (GEC 5 Figure 4-12: LL = 40, PI = 10, PI = LL - 30 and the group names) or 'uscs_particle_sizes' (the sieve sizes that bound fines, sand, gravel, cobbles and boulders, on a log grain-size axis). The lines are grey and named on the line; the chart's own axis names and frame are used unless xlabel, ylabel, xlim or ylim are given. The result's reference_chart gives the source, page and each line's equation, for the caption.

10.1.36 worked_examples — worked_examples

find_worked_examples — Search validated worked examples from real published design reports (FHWA GEC, Caltrans, AASHTO, UFC, Slide2/FLAC verification). Returns compact summaries; fetch the full entry with get_worked_example. Consult BEFORE a nontrivial multi-step design or calc report — the entry shows the method calls, parameters, published answer, and what a good report presents.

ParameterTypeDescription
topicstrrequired
domainstroptional
limitintoptional default: 3

get_worked_example — Fetch one worked example by id: self-contained problem statement, ready-to-run dispatch calls with parameters, published vs computed results, and report-writing notes.

ParameterTypeDescription
example_idstrrequired
